items.title: Association of metabolic insulin resistance with white matter hyperintensity burden and plasma proteomic signatures in the UK Biobank.
items.abstract: Background Metabolic insulin resistance is closely related to cardiometabolic dysfunction and vascular injury. Its association with subclinical cerebral small vessel disease, and the circulating molecular signals that may accompany this association, remain incompletely characterised. Methods We analysed 59,826 UK Biobank participants with brain magnetic resonance imaging to examine the association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden. Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear regression and restricted cubic spline analysis, with spline models restricted to participants with complete covariate data. Proteomic data were available for 6,790 participants. Protein-wide association analyses, functional annotation and LASSO prioritisation explored circulating protein links between METS-IR and WMH burden, followed by exploratory mediation models in 1,309 participants with complete model data. Results Higher METS-IR was associated with greater WMH burden after adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle and vascular risk factors. Complete-case spline analysis suggested a nonlinear association, with steeper fitted slopes at higher METS-IR values. Proteomic screening identified 1,266 proteins associated with METS-IR and 122 proteins associated with WMH after false discovery rate correction, yielding 119 overlapping proteins. These proteins were enriched for immune-inflammatory processes and cell adhesion. LASSO prioritisation selected eight candidate proteins, and exploratory mediation models yielded indirect-effect estimates for selected proteins, with GAL showing the largest estimated proportion mediated. Conclusions METS-IR was associated with WMH burden after adjustment for measured covariates in this large UK Biobank analysis. Integrated plasma proteomic analyses identified immune-inflammatory and cell-adhesion signals that may help characterise molecular correlates of metabolic insulin resistance and cerebral small vessel disease burden.

items.title: Current perspectives in the pharmacological treatment of gambling disorder: psychedelics and beyond.
items.abstract: Introduction Gambling disorder (GD) is a heterogeneous behavioral addiction associated with dysregulated reward processing, impaired executive control, stress-system dysfunction, and maladaptive neuroplasticity. Despite its considerable clinical, social, and economic burden, no medication is currently approved specifically for GD, and available pharmacological strategies remain off label. Areas covered This narrative review examines established and emerging pharmacological approaches to GD. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language literature published between January 2010 and January 2026. Opioid antagonists show the most consistent, although still limited, therapeutic signal with potential benefits in selected patients with prominent gambling urges, whereas evidence for antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antiepileptic drugs, and antipsychotics remains heterogeneous. Glutamatergic, noradrenergic, endocannabinoid, and orexin-related interventions are biologically plausible but largely experimental. Psychedelic and neuroplasticity-oriented treatments, including psilocybin, ketamine/esketamine, and 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted interventions, may target cognitive inflexibility, compulsive behavior, and maladaptive reward learning. Expert opinion The available evidence supports a cautious, mechanism-informed approach to pharmacological research, while underscoring the need for adequately powered clinical trials and prospective evaluation of clinically relevant treatment-response indicators. Pharmacotherapy for GD should move toward phenotype-informed, multimodal treatment rather than a one-size-fits-all model. Emerging neuroplasticity-based interventions are promising, but adequately powered, controlled, and longitudinal trials are required before clinical implementation.

items.title: hilldiv3: a unified Hill-number framework for neutral, phylogenetic and functional diversity analysis in R
items.abstract: 1. Hill numbers provide a coherent family of diversity measures that can incorporate phylogenetic relatedness and functional trait dissimilarity, but applying them consistently across neutral, phylogenetic and functional diversity, and across measurement, partitioning and (dis)similarity, still requires combining several packages with incompatible conventions. 2. We present hilldiv3, an R package that provides per-sample diversity, nested multiplicative partitioning across scales for all three diversity types, bounded (dis)similarities and pairwise matrices, diversity profiles, evenness and redundancy, and the allocation of Hill power sums and dissimilarities to taxa or taxonomic sets. 3. hilldiv3 directly supported all twelve benchmarked combinations of operation and diversity type, and built pairwise (dis)similarity matrices 15-820 times faster than hilldiv2 and hillR, with up to two orders of magnitude less memory. We showcased the package by analysing Microflora Danica data (360 samples, 5,518 genomes, eight habitats), demonstrating that neutral, phylogenetic and functional diversity turned over at very different rates between habitats, and a near-constant Actinomycetota share concealed opposing shifts of two orders. 4. By deriving every metric from the same Hill-number formulation, hilldiv3 makes neutral, phylogenetic and functional results directly comparable, and lowers the barrier to rigorous diversity analysis of community-ecology and high-throughput sequencing data.

items.title: Marsupial fossil tracks reveal Eocene arboreal life in Antarctica.
items.abstract: Antarctica is the only continent where land mammals are extinct today. Before the Eocene-Oligocene boundary (>38 million years ago), however, the "white continent" had a much milder climate that sustained a diverse fauna of terrestrial mammals. Several discoveries of fragmentary Eocene fossils suggest that Antarctica acted as a land bridge connecting South America to Australia, most notably marsupials. However, fossil mammals are scarce and restricted to a single location-Seymour Island. Here we present two well-preserved fossil tracks which are the second Antarctic fossil mammal outside Seymour Island and the oldest fossil tracks assigned to an opossum-like animal in the Cenozoic. They were found in the Fossil Hill Formation on King George Island (lower-middle Eocene) and exhibit possible opposable thumbs, suggesting an arboreal behavior observable in microbiotheriid and some extant didelphid marsupials living in South America today. They further coincide in time with the rise of scansorial lifestyle in several mammalian lineages. This ichnologic record offers a more comprehensive look into the dispersion and ecology of mammals through the Early Cenozoic of Antarctica, evidencing that small arboreal marsupials inhabited the South Shetland Islands during the Eocene. In addition, the new finding indicates that Antarctica was not merely a corridor, but a rich habitat of dense and productive forest canopies during the middle Eocene.

items.title: Lessons in ecophysiology from the model sea anemone Nematostella vectensis: a review and future directions.
items.abstract: Ecophysiology seeks to understand how the environment affects organismal processes and shapes performance. Here, we synthesize >20 years of research that explores ecophysiology using a cnidarian model, the starlet sea anemone (Nematostella vectensis). Studies using N. vectensis as a model have employed field, laboratory and computational approaches, and have commonly entailed characterizing the responses of the anemones to biotic and abiotic environmental perturbations, including pathogens, heat, hypoxia, xenobiotics and more. These investigations have encompassed life stages from embryo through adult, with readouts spanning biological scales from gene to population. As a whole, this research has expanded our knowledge of how the environment influences processes such as phenotypic plasticity and stress acclimation, reproduction and early development, and immunity and host-microbe interactions. In this Review, we synthesize this knowledge and discuss major questions in each of these research areas, highlighting insights gained from studies using N. vectensis as a model organism. We also identify open questions for future research and discuss considerations for ecophysiology-focused laboratory experiments that are particularly relevant to the use of N. vectensis as a model. Overall, continued investigations in ecophysiology making use of N. vectensis hold promise to better equip society to meet the challenges of rapid environmental changes, pollution and emerging pathogen-based diseases.

items.title: A systematic review of EC number prediction algorithms based on reaction chemical structures.
items.abstract: Motivation Enzymes catalyse most of the metabolic reactions in living organisms. The functional characterization of enzymes is critical to understand the metabolic processes involved in different fields such as biotechnology, nutrition, ecology, and drug development. The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers provide a hierarchical framework for classifying enzymatic reactions, linking gene and protein sequences to biochemical transformations. However, the incomplete annotation of biochemical reaction databases limits the accurate representation of metabolism of living organisms. Results To address this gap, several computational methods have been developed to predict EC numbers from reaction chemical structures, broadly classified into reaction similarity-based and machine/deep learning approaches. We systematically review these tools, comparing their performance predicting EC numbers from different databases, and assessing their robustness across enzyme classes. We also apply these methods to predict EC numbers from drug metabolism reactions, highlighting their potential to improve functional annotation of uncharacterized metabolic pathways. Availability and implementation All the necessary data and code to reproduce the results of this manuscript are available within https://github.com/PlanesLab/ECNumberPrediction GitHub repository and in Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22957403. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: Recognizing and Mitigating Reference Bias in Population Genomics.
items.abstract: Most population genomic analyses require mapping sequence reads to a reference genome. Mapping to a single reference introduces reference bias, defined as either low-quality read mapping or downstream analytical distortions arising from biased mapping. Although reference bias has been repeatedly documented, its consequences remain insufficiently understood. Its impacts are particularly relevant in biodiversity genomics, where heterospecific references are commonly used to analyse entire clades. Here, we survey the literature to document where reference bias occurs, its sources, and its impacts, focusing on population and biodiversity genomics. We identify five major classes of reference-inference bias impacts: distortions in population genetic inference; alterations to phylogenetic inference; structural variant detection; RNA expression analyses; and gene presence-absence variation. Critically, the direction and magnitude of these impacts are inconsistent across studies, suggesting that generalisations are premature. Reference bias is primarily driven by evolutionary divergence between the reference genome and the mapped samples, and is further aggravated by analytical and biological factors. We suggest several mitigation strategies, including divergence-aware filtering, tool benchmarking, and standardised reporting of reference bias. In the longer term, we advocate expanding reference genome diversity and adopting pangenome-based alignment across taxa.

items.title: Seasonal differences in the sound detection ability of Arctic cod, Boreogadus saida.
items.abstract: Human activities are rapidly altering marine ecosystems, with increasing vessel traffic elevating underwater sound levels worldwide. Polar regions are particularly vulnerable, as declining sea ice has expanded access to the Arctic Ocean. Arctic cod (Boreogadus saida) is a key species that spawns under sea ice, yet its hearing ability remains entirely uncharacterised. Understanding how this species detects sound is essential for assessing the potential impacts of rising anthropogenic sound. Here, the detection sensitivity of spawning and non-spawning Arctic cod was evaluated using auditory evoked potentials (AEPs). Both groups were most sensitive to frequencies below 200 Hz when assessed using sound pressure. However, particle motion sensitivity differed markedly: spawning fish showed peak sensitivity at 400 Hz, whereas non-spawning fish were most sensitive near 90 Hz. Overall, Arctic cod exhibited significantly enhanced hearing sensitivity and an expanded detectable frequency range during spawning compared with non-spawning individuals. These results provide the first evidence of seasonal differences in auditory plasticity in a broadcast-spawning fish and highlight the potential vulnerability of Arctic cod spawning behaviour to increasing anthropogenic sound in a rapidly changing Arctic environment.

items.title: Statistical fragility in the meta-analytic evidence base of animal cognition: a meta-meta-analytic reappraisal.
items.abstract: How reliable is the meta-analytic evidence base in animal cognition? We conducted a pre-registered second-order meta-analysis of 28 published meta-analytical papers, comprising 48 eligible models and 5740 effect-size observations from primary studies. We assessed statistical power, Type M magnitude error, and Type S sign error at both primary-study and meta-analysis levels. Because these quantities depend on the assumed underlying effect, we compared the results based on uncorrected pooled effects, a regression-based bias correction, and a sensitivity analysis using a bias-robust fixed-effect model incorporating a within-study variance-covariance matrix (FE+VCV). At the primary-study level, estimated power was low under all three empirically estimated effect proxies: 17.4%, 9.0%, and 13.4%, respectively. Type M and Type S errors were also sensitive to the assumed effect and correction method. Power increased when larger externally specified effects were assumed, confirming that these quantities are conditional on the assumed effect. Meta-analysis-level results were generally more favourable but also sensitive to analytical choices. The evidence base was concentrated in experimental rodent studies of learning and memory, limiting field-wide generalisation. These findings support improving study design and reporting within the represented literature while expanding meta-analytic coverage across taxa and cognitive domains.

items.title: An interbehavioral account of culture can guide the formulation of therapeutic demands: the case of eating disorders
items.abstract: Abstract Behavior analysts frequently discuss the importance of addressing culture in psychotherapy, identifying demands such as gender-based violence, discrimination-related distress, and eating disorders as culturally loaded. A persistent epistemological tension accompanies these discussions: how to distinguish the psychological and cultural levels of analysis without severing the relation between them. This paper argues that interbehaviorism offers a way of addressing that tension, not by choosing between the two levels but by specifying what each consists of within a single field-theoretic logic. The argument is developed through eating disorders, a demand whose onset and course are well documented as sociocultural and which carries one of the highest mortality rates among mental disorders. Two complementary routes are examined. The first, following Kantor’s cultural psychology, locates culture within the psychological field by treating the foods, bodies, and evaluations to which clients respond as bearing institutional stimulus functions. The second treats the client–therapist interaction itself as a referential sociocultural event, in which both participants adjust to a shared referent through conventional forms of responding. Three implications for clinical practice follow: culture becomes identifiable within the session rather than inferred about it; the institutional functions operating for the therapist require analysis alongside the client’s; and therapeutic change can be described as the establishment of conventional functions between them.

items.title: Forty Years of The Legend of Zelda : A Scoping Review of Game Design, Computation, Culture, and Play
items.abstract: Over four decades, The Legend of Zelda has evolved from a landmark action-adventure series into a recurring object of research across game studies, computer science, musicology, cultural studies, psychology, education, and related fields. This article presents a scoping review and structured survey of Zelda-related research across the franchise’s 1986–2026 history, examining how the series has been studied as a designed system, cultural artifact, interactive narrative, audiovisual environment, player-community object, and computational testbed. Following a PRISMA-ScR-informed process with duplicate screening and full-text eligibility assessment, 93 studies were included in the final synthesis: 52 Core scholarly studies, 40 complementary scholarly/grey-literature studies, and one complementary critical/industry record. The literature is strongly recent and unevenly distributed: 65 included studies were published from 2020 onward, while 44 explicitly address either Ocarina of Time or Breath of the Wild. Narrative and worldbuilding constitute the largest thematic area, whereas technology remains comparatively underrepresented as a primary research topic. In contrast, Zelda dungeon structures have become established computational objects for procedural content generation, formal modeling, and mixed-initiative design research. A sensitivity analysis restricted to the 52-study Core scholarly corpus preserved the principal distributional patterns, indicating that the main mapping conclusions are not driven by complementary evidence. Across the reviewed traditions, a recurring pattern is the interaction among spatial design, player agency, audiovisual feedback, narrative, and increasingly interoperable game systems. The survey identifies gaps in longitudinal analysis, technical research, visual studies, localization, empirical player research, and computational models of modern three-dimensional Zelda environments, positioning the franchise as a distinctive longitudinal case for studying the relationships among game design, technology, culture, computation, and play.

items.title: Between theory and practice: Patients' experiences of payment in private psychotherapy.
items.abstract: Objective: This study explored how payment shapes patients' subjective experiences in private psychotherapy, including perceptions of commitment, treatment value, and relational dynamics with the therapist. Method: Semi-structured depth interviews were conducted with 28 adults in private therapy and analyzed using iterative thematic content analysis. Results: Five themes were identified: (i) payment shapes expectations for rapid results and therapist competence, licensing what patients feel entitled to expect; (ii) ambiguity in time-money rules creates perceived unfairness, transparency mattering more than strictness; (iii) value is weighed against alternatives and reinforced by therapist flexibility, patients constructing competing measures of worth; (iv) payment strengthens commitment and limits access, two outcomes of one ongoing calculation; and (v) discussing and handling money in-session triggers discomfort, exposing relational dynamics that usually remain implicit. Across themes, direct discussion of payment was typically confined to its practical logistics, and participants did not report instances in which its relational meaning was subsequently addressed and worked through in treatment. Conclusions: Despite theoretical recognition of money's relational significance, payment's relational meaning is rarely addressed directly in practice, generating misunderstandings, perceived unfairness, and frame violations-revealing a theory-practice gap and underscoring the need for greater attention to financial issues in training and supervision.

items.title: Short-term culture and hormone secretion analysis of prepubertal testicular tissue.
items.abstract: Lay summary Some boys with cancer or blood diseases may have a small piece of testicular tissue frozen before they start treatment, with the hope of preserving future fertility. In this study, testicular tissue from 59 boys aged 0.7 to 14.3 years was kept in a laboratory dish for a short time after biopsy. We measured whether the tissue could still release testosterone and other hormones that support germ cells that will make sperm in adulthood. The tissue of was able to release hormones after being transported from the operating room to the laboratory premises and, in some cases, even after previous chemotherapy. Hormone release was linked to the child's age and to previous treatment with a type of chemotherapy known to damage fertility. It was not clearly linked to the number of germ cells in the tissue. This suggests that hormone producing testicular cells may remain active even when germ cells are reduced. These tests may help assess tissue quality before future fertility treatments.

items.abstract: Introduction People with HIV (PWH) are at risk for functional decline and disability due to a complex interplay of factors, yet longitudinal studies of everyday functioning in this population are lacking. To select predictors of self-reported functional dependence, a binary logistic regression was performed using Akaike information criterion-guided backward stepwise selection. Model performance, discrimination, and calibration were assessed. The final model was internally validated by bootstrapping and optimism corrected. Risk index scores were generated using adjusted beta coefficients and a risk score cut-off was determined. Results Baseline predictors of functional dependence included elevated depressive symptoms, thrombocytopenia (platelets Conclusions A combination of demographics, fine motor skills, depression, and medical conditions predict functional decline. Additional studies examining external validity of the index in large, age-diverse samples of PWH with functional impairment are required before deployment in clinical settings.

items.title: 6- and 12-month test-retest score reliability and practice effects of the NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery in older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline.
items.abstract: Objective: The NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (NIHTB-CB) is increasingly used for cognitive assessment. However, its test-retest reliability estimates over clinically meaningful intervals are understudied in older Black adults. This study examined the reliability and practice effects of NIHTB-CB composite and subtest scores over 6- and 12-month intervals in older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline. Methods: Participants were 44 community-dwelling older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline ( M age = 71.4 years, SD = 4.9; M education = 16.1 years, SD = 2.1; 93% women) who completed baseline and 6-month testing and N = 29 participants (93% women) completed 12-month testing. Intraclass correlation coefficients evaluated the reliability of uncorrected standard scores and fully corrected T-scores. Paired-samples t tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction assessed mean-level change, and Bland-Altman plots evaluated agreement. Results: At 6 months, composite-level reliability was good for Total Cognition (ICC = .76-.78) and Crystallized Cognition scores (ICC = .82-.87), and moderate for Fluid Cognition scores (ICC = .69-.72). Subtest-level reliability was more variable, with lower reliability for List Sorting and Picture Sequence Memory scores. At 12 months, significant mean improvements were observed across several composites and subtest fully corrected scores. These changes demonstrated medium paired-samples effect sizes (| d z | = 0.51-0.58). 12-month follow-up reliability estimates remained strong for composite scores, particularly for Crystallized Cognition. Conclusion: NIHTB-CB composite scores showed generally good longitudinal reliability over 6-12 months among older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline. Variable subtest reliability and possible 12-month practice effects warrant cautious interpretation when monitoring change over time.

items.title: Musculoskeletal pain and coping mechanisms in older female rice farmers: a grounded theory study.
items.abstract: Objectives While ageing is often associated with retirement, many older women in northern Iran continue working in rice fields despite musculoskeletal pain. This study explored their pain experiences and how they cope with this condition. Methods Using a grounded theory approach developed by Strauss and Corbin, we conducted semi-structured interviews with twenty-two female rice farmers aged sixty years and older. Data analysis involved open, axial, and selective coding, with constant comparative analysis. Findings Analysis revealed five main categories: pain experience and disability, pain management and coping, social and economic factors, emotions and attitudes, and family impact. These categories informed a multilevel biosocial resilience model suggesting that resilience emerges through interactions across biocultural, socioeconomic, and structural domains. Conclusion The findings highlight areas for further consideration in occupational health, healthcare access, and social protection. They also draw attention to the need for policies and research that strengthen formal support systems and reduce structural constraints that compel continued work despite pain. Context-specific adaptation and further research are warranted before broader recommendations can be made.

items.title: Neuropsychiatric symptoms in MCI, AD, and healthy older adults: a network analysis perspective.
items.abstract: Objectives Alzheimer's Disease (AD), while traditionally classified as a cognitive disorder, is also characterized by neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS). Despite their clinical relevance, NPS are often under-assessed or rarely examined in conjunction with cognitive symptoms. Here, we aimed to explore the dynamic interplay between cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms across the AD continuum. Method We applied moderated Mixed Graphical Models (mMGMs) to a large sample from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), including Normal Controls (NC), individuals with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and patients with AD. Results Moderation analyses showed that diagnosis significantly influenced key relationships, such as those between visual hallucinations and visuoconstructive or memory functions, and between delusions and semantic fluency. Centrality analyses identified bridging symptoms-such as apathy, semantic fluency, and MMSE performance linking cognitive and psychiatric domains, highlighting their clinical relevance. In addition, diagnosis-specific patterns of symptom interaction were found, with AD patients displaying a denser and more interconnected network between cognitive and neuropsychiatric domains compared to the other groups. Conclusions These findings support a more integrated conceptualization of AD pathology, where cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms co-evolve. Early identification and treatment of NPS may therefore be critical to improve quality of life and for informing comprehensive diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Acute effect of moderate and higher cognitive demand HIIT on cognition in early adolescents: a cross-over trial.
items.abstract: Background High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is a potential physical activity opportunity to be integrated into educational settings for adolescents, yet little is known about the acute cognitive effects of varying cognitive load. We examined the effects of school-based HIIT involving moderate or higher cognitive demand on adolescents' acute cognitive performance. Methods Within-subject, crossover design with two HIIT conditions completed between 7-14 days apart. Adolescents (aged 11-14) completed two, four-minute HIIT bouts, designed with either moderate or higher cognitive demand. Before and after each condition, adolescents completed four brief cognitive tasks from the Mobile Monitoring of Cognitive Change platform to assess processing speed, visuospatial working memory, and response inhibition. Results Participants (N.=25) were a mean of 13.0 years-old (Standard deviation [SD] 0.8), 39% girls, and 39% overweight or obese. We observed significant time-by-condition interaction effects for visuospatial working memory (P=0.015) and processing speed (P=0.026). Visuospatial working memory worsened following higher cognitive demand HIIT (sum error distance of 18.2 pre to 28.5 post), while it improved following moderate cognitive demand HIIT (20.6 to 18.1). Processing speed reaction time improved more following moderate cognitive demand HIIT (765.7 milliseconds [ms] to 555.6 ms), compared with higher cognitive demand HIIT (716.9 ms to 703.8 ms). Conclusions The HIIT condition designed with moderate cognitive demand was associated with more favorable improvements in visuospatial working memory and processing speed compared with HIIT involving higher cognitive demand in this sample of adolescents. The overall results suggest that layering additional cognitive demands on top of HIIT exercises may attenuate acute cognitive benefits of higher-intensity physical activity, but additional studies are needed to confirm these preliminary findings.

items.title: Adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the long and short forms of the yearning in situations of loss scale in a Turkish sample.
items.abstract: Background: Yearning, the intense longing for the deceased loved one, is a hallmark symptom of prolonged grief disorder. Objective: The aim of this study was to adapt the Yearning in Situations of Loss Scale (YSL) into Turkish and to examine the psychometric properties of its long (YSL) and short forms (YSL-SF). Method: Data were collected from 500 participants used for exploratory factor analysis and an additional 445 participants for confirmatory analyses. In the data analyses, construct validity was evaluated through exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis, and convergent, discriminant, and incremental validity evidence was examined. Internal consistency was evaluated using item-total correlations and Cronbach's alpha coefficients. In addition, item analysis was conducted to evaluate item difficulty and discrimination parameters. Furthermore, measurement invariance of the YSL-SF was tested between Turkish ( N = 201) and American ( N = 95) samples using multigroup confirmatory factor analysis, and cross-cultural comparability of the construct was evaluated. Results: The findings provided evidence supporting the validity and internal consistency of the Turkish YSL and YSL-SF, both of which demonstrated a one-factor structure. The short form also showed measurement invariance across Turkish and American samples, supporting its suitability for cross-cultural comparisons. Conclusion: The Turkish versions of YSL and YSL-SF demonstrated good psychometric properties, supporting their use in the assessment of yearning following bereavement.

items.title: Internet-delivered self-help acceptance and commitment therapy for family carers of people with dementia (iACT4CARERS): a mixed-methods process evaluation of reach and recruitment.
items.abstract: Objectives A mixed-methods process evaluation was conducted alongside a randomised controlled trial of iACT4CARERS, an eight-session, online, self-help Acceptance and Commitment Therapy intervention with minimal therapist support for family carers of people with dementia. The study examined the reach of the intervention and factors influencing recruitment to inform equitable implementation. Methods Demographic data from 565 screened carers and interviews with 30 referrers across UK health services were analysed. Results The screened sample was predominantly aged 50-79 years (82.5%), female (77%), and White (91.7%). Five themes were identified: referrers' coordinated referrals, mutual motivation, and community outreach supported engagement; referrers' trust-building, tailored communication, and timely approaches facilitated participation; carers' time constraints and referrers' assumptions about older carers' digital skills influenced recruitment; proactive outreach was important for engaging ethnic minority carers; and cultural perceptions of mental health created barriers to participation. Conclusions The sample was broadly comparable with previous estimates of the UK dementia carer population. For the equitable implementation of interventions such as iACT4CARERS, coordinated recruitment across health, social care, and voluntary organisations, alongside centralised intervention delivery, may be critical. Outreach can be further strengthened by enhancing referrers' communication and empowerment skills, including challenging assumptions about older carers' digital abilities.

items.title: Moral Convictions on the Move: Abortion Ballot Outcomes and Migration Motivation.
items.abstract: Shifts in abortion policy can create or reinforce mismatches between local laws and personal values, disrupting people's sense of place. A corollary of the ideological migration hypothesis predicts that people are motivated to leave states whose laws conflict with their values to satisfy belonging needs. In Study 1 ( N = 1,227), pro-life and pro-choice residents of Florida and Missouri were surveyed before and after the 2024 U.S. presidential election, in which both states voted on abortion access. Missouri's measure passed; Florida's failed. Individuals whose attitudes conflicted with the outcome reported reduced belonging, lower life satisfaction, and greater migration desire. Study 2 experimentally replicated these effects among Arkansas residents ( N = 814), showing that envisioning a value-incongruent ballot outcome reduced belonging and increased migration consideration. Effects were strongest among participants who moralized abortion, suggesting that moral convictions may be important for the impact of policy outcomes on belonging and migration motivation.

items.title: Plasmodium vivax relapse reservoirs in Ethiopia: microhaplotype sequencing informs recurrent infection origins
items.abstract: Determining the origin of recurrent Plasmodium vivax infections is critical for quantifying the public health burden of the hypnozoite reservoir, understanding transmission potential, and evaluating anti-relapse antimalarial efficacy. In Ethiopia, P. vivax is a major contributor to malaria burden, but the relative contribution of relapse to recurrent infections remains poorly quantified. We performed microhaplotype genotyping using a panel of 93 genome-wide markers and applied a probabilistic recurrence classification framework to recurrent P. vivax samples collected in two Ethiopian radical cure trials (IMPROV and OPRA). Genotyping was conducted on parasite isolates collected at enrolment and subsequent recurrences, with participants monitored over a 12-month follow-up period (IMPROV: 604 samples from 444 participants; OPRA: 621 samples from 342 participants). Recurrent infections were classified using a Bayesian hierarchical model implemented in Pv3Rs , which estimated marginal posterior probabilities of relapse, reinfection, or recrudescence based on genotyping data and background population dynamics. Priors were structured across biologically motivated time windows reflecting the natural history of P. vivax infection in Ethiopia and anticipated drug efficacy. Recurrences with a probability of relapse (p(L)) ≥ 0.75 were classified as relapses. In the absence of primaquine, probable relapse was the dominant classification for primary recurrent infections in both trials (75.5%; 102/135) and for consecutive recurrent infections within individuals (75.2%; 204/271). Primaquine substantially reduced the proportion of participants experiencing recurrent infections attributable to probable relapse, from 57.3% to 1.7% in IMPROV and from 60.2% to 9.5% in OPRA. Polyclonal infection at enrolment was independently associated with increased odds of recurrence and a higher rate of probable relapse in OPRA, with a consistent but non-significant trend observed in IMPROV. These findings provide direct molecular evidence that the hypnozoite reservoir is the dominant driver of recurrent P. vivax infections in Ethiopia in the absence of radical cure. The marked reduction in probable relapse following primaquine treatment highlights the critical importance of expanding access to safe and effective radical cure strategies in Ethiopia and other comparable high-transmission settings.

items.title: Incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms: A nationwide population based longitudinal study
items.abstract: Background: Understanding the epidemiology of unruptured intracranial aneurysm (UIAs) is crucial for risk stratification, clinical decision making, and public health planning. The aim of this study was to perform a nationwide population-based analysis to examine the incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms in Sweden. Methods: Data were obtained from the Swedish National Patient Register for all persons, aged 18 years and older, diagnosed with an intracranial aneurysm (ICD-10: I67.1) between the years 2000 and 2020. Crude incidence was calculated for the total population and age- and gender-stratified groups. Age standardized incidence was assessed using the European standard population. The incidence of intracranial aneurysms diagnosed with concurrent subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) was also examined. Results: During the study period, 8681 patients were diagnosed with UIA. The median age of diagnosis was 63 years and 65.1% were women. The age-standardized incidence increased approximately 74% % between 2000 and its peak: from 4.6 (95% CI: 4,26-4.95) per 100,000 in the year 2000 to 7.99 (95% CI: 6.7-7.54) per 100,000 in the year 2019. The increase in incidence of UIAs was most pronounced among women and those aged above 60. During the study period, the number of cases with SAH decreased slightly. Conclusions: The increasing incidence of UIAs in Sweden might be due improved clinical detection rates, demographic changes, and changes in the prevalence of risk factors. These findings highlight the importance of enhanced surveillance, effective risk stratification, and targeted public health strategies to address the growing burden of UIAs.

items.title: Middle Temporal Gyrus Neurite Microstructure and Scam Susceptibility in Older Adults Without Dementia
items.abstract: Background: Financial exploitation is a prevalent public health concern among older adults, and emerging evidence links vulnerability to gray matter macrostructure and white matter microstructure, including within brain regions and networks implicated in early Alzheimer's disease. Although diffusion tensor imaging is sensitive to age-related variation in brain microstructure, its scalar metrics cannot distinguish among the tissue properties contributing to observed differences. Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) models distinct tissue compartments, yielding estimates of neurite density, dendritic complexity, and extracellular free water. Methods: This study examined associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics using ultra-high-field 7-Tesla imaging in 116 older adults without dementia. Neurite density index (NDI), orientation dispersion index (ODI), and free-water fraction were quantified within seven a priori regions of interest linked to early Alzheimer's disease. Multivariate regressions evaluated associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics, adjusting for age, sex, education, and global cognition, with multiple comparison correction within each metric. For significant regions, post-hoc hierarchical regression models tested whether NODDI metrics explained variance beyond regional cortical thickness, total gray matter, and total intracranial volume. Results: Greater scam susceptibility was associated with higher NDI (β=0.30, pFDR=.025) and lower ODI (β=-0.28, pFDR=.044) in the middle temporal gyrus (MTG). No other regions survived correction. Additionally, MTG NDI and ODI explained variance beyond macrostructure measures. Conclusions: These findings identify NODDI metrics as novel microstructural correlates of scam susceptibility beyond macrostructure, supporting investigation of their relevance to financial vulnerability in older age.

items.title: Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence During and After COVID-19 Social Distancing in Korea: A Nationwide 16-Year Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a rare but devastating event. However, the extent to which large-scale public health interventions, such as COVID-19 social distancing policies, affected the incidence of pediatric OHCA remains unclear. Methods We conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis using data from the Korea Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Registry (2008-2023). The primary outcome was the monthly incidence of OHCA among individuals aged 0-18 years. The study period was divided into three phases: pre-intervention (January 2008-February 2020), social distancing (March 2020-April 2022), and post-lifting (May 2022-December 2023). We used segmented Poisson regression, adjusted for population size and seasonal variation, to estimate changes in monthly incidence at each policy change and reported the results as incidence rate ratios (IRRs). To determine whether these changes differed by age, we compared children with adults (19-64 years) and elderly individuals (≥65 years). Results Of the 456,839 registry entries, 10,965 were pediatric OHCAs, of which 6,891 underwent resuscitation in the emergency department. The crude incidence was 7.04, 7.14, and 8.35 per 100,000 person-years in the three phases, respectively. Before the pandemic, incidence rose slightly (annual IRR 1.006 [95% CI 1.001-1.012]; P = 0.032). At the implementation of social distancing, incidence fell immediately (IRR 0.926 [95% CI 0.865-0.991]; P = 0.027), without a significant change in slope (P = 0.081). After restrictions were lifted, incidence rose immediately (IRR 1.138 [95% CI 1.048-1.235]; P = 0.002) and then declined gradually (monthly IRR 0.993 [95% CI 0.988-0.999]; P = 0.023). These changes were confined to children aged 1-11 years (implementation IRR 0.812 [95% CI 0.666-0.991]; post-lifting IRR 1.562 [95% CI 1.278-1.909]). The pattern of change differed significantly by age group (P < 0.001), mainly because incidence rose in children, but not in adults or elderly individuals, after restrictions were lifted. Conclusions Nationwide social distancing was associated with a transient decrease in pediatric OHCA incidence, which was concentrated among children aged 1-11 years and was followed by a rebound above the expected level after restrictions were lifted. Surveillance of pediatric OHCA should account for abrupt changes in children's daily environments, including the closure and reopening of schools and childcare facilities.

items.title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM 2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
items.abstract: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but few have focused on the most recent wildfire-intensive years, and jointly estimated both to quantify wildfire contributions to total PM2.5 exposure. This study developed a high-resolution machine learning framework to estimate daily 1-km concentrations of total and wildfire-related PM2.5 across the CONUS from 2018 to 2024. This framework incorporates chemical precursors and wildfire smoke density as predictors and relies on publicly accessible data sources enabling future updates. The model achieved high performance with cross-validated R2 of 0.72 and 0.89 for daily and annual estimates, respectively. Elevated total PM2.5 concentrations were observed along the west coast and in several metropolitan areas across the CONUS. Wildfire smoke contributed substantially to total PM2.5 concentrations during major wildfire years, accounting for approximately 35% of PM2.5 along the west coast in 2020, and over 25% in the eastern U.S. in 2023. Wildfire-related PM2.5 mortality accounted for 20% of PM2.5-attributable deaths along the west coast in 2020 (30 times that in 2019), and 24% in the northeastern U.S. in 2023 (14 times that in 2019). These findings highlight the growing role of wildfire smoke as a major driver of total PM2.5 exposure and associated health risks in both western and eastern U.S., underscoring the need for sustained nationwide public health interventions to reduce wildfire smoke exposure.

items.title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of a social media campaign to promote HPV vaccination in Bauchi state, Nigeria
items.abstract: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in women in 26 countries, including in sub‐Saharan African countries. Cervical and other cancer risks can be greatly reduced through timely HPV vaccination and early screening. But it continues to pose a significant public health challenge in LMICs such as Nigeria. This study reports on the implementation and evaluation of a pair of social media behavior change campaigns to increase HPV vaccination amongst girls ages 9-14 and reduce vaccine hesitancy amongst girls and their parents in Bauchi state, Nigeria. The primary objectives are to conduct a quasi-experimental evaluation of the social media campaign; to examine the effect of higher versus lower levels of campaign exposure on HPV vaccination and related outcomes; to determine whether the social media campaign followed its planned theory of change; and to identify which social media messages were most effective in promoting HPV vaccination. We implemented an HPV vaccination social media promotion campaign, using videos designed to encourage parents to vaccinate their daughters, at scale in Bauchi state on the Meta and TikTok social media platforms. We used a quasi-experimental design, a heavy-up approach, that experimentally manipulated the level of social media content delivered in Bauchi. We used the Virtual Lab platform, an open-source platform that uses social media to recruit participants using advertising and creates panels of respondents for data collection through an online survey, and also collected social media metrics including impressions and engagement. The campaign was effective in increasing HPV vaccination rates from 69% at baseline to 86% at endline over 2 campaign phases that spanned approximately 3 months. Based on GEE modeling, we found that higher levels of engagement with the campaign were associated with higher vaccination rates at midline and endline. Pro-vaccine attitudes and reduced vaccine hesitancy also predicted higher vaccination rates. Also, the campaign produced additional HPV vaccinations at low cost: Adjusted for campaign exposure cost of $0.81 per additional vax in campaign phase 1, $2.10 per vax in phase 2, and $2.40 for the total campaign period. Evidence from this study indicates that social media may be an effective strategy to promote HPV vaccination at low cost. Future rigorous trials using experimental methods are needed to further evaluate social media to promote HPV vaccination.

items.title: The Confidence – Information Quality Mismatch: Low Quality Posts Use More Confident Language
items.abstract: Misinformation on online platforms is of great concern for democracy, public health, and civic discourse. In fast-paced feeds, users often rely on heuristics when deciding what to attend to, believe, and share. One such heuristic is confidence, which, prior research shows, is treated as a cue of knowledge and credibility. Yet, we show that in over 4 million posts across seven social media platforms and one messaging app, confidence is negatively associated with information quality: posts written with greater confidence are more likely to link to lower-quality news domains and to contain false claims — even controlling for user baselines, toxicity, political lean, emotionality, and valence. Furthermore, we find that confident posts receive more engagement. Together, these results reveal a problematic asymmetry in online information environments: a widespread linguistic cue that is likely to be read as a signal of knowledge, and to attract engagement, is in fact associated with lower-quality information.

items.title: An Optimal Control Framework for Adaptive Virtual Reality Interventions in Substance Use Rehabilitation
items.abstract: Abstract Despite advances made over the years, substance use disorders are still a significant public health challenge, with relapse prevention continuing to be a major problem in rehabilitation. Traditional rehabilitation strategies often face barriers such as limited accessibility and difficulty recreating real-world environments that are associated with cravings. As a result, researchers have begun to study virtual reality (VR) as a tool for drug rehabilitation. I developed an Adaptive-Perturbed-Corrective-Relapse (APCR) compartmental model governed by differential equations that represent the transitions between stable recovery, cue-induced perturbation, corrective intervention, and relapse. The model incorporates a craving trigger parameterized using alcohol-related gaze data collected in a VR environment and a baseline recovery cue derived from physiological biomarkers. Transition rates were assigned based on literature-informed assumptions rather than clinical outcome data. To determine when and how strongly therapeutic interventions should be delivered, I formulated an optimal control problem in which intervention intensity is represented by a time-dependent control variable. Using Pontryagin’s Minimum Principle, I derived an intervention strategy that balances reducing the perturbed state with the control effort over 60 minutes. Using the forward–backward sweep method, I obtained an optimal control strategy that reduced the simulated peak proportion of individuals in the Perturbed state by 33.26% compared with the passive baseline, highlighting the potential of mathematical optimization for adaptive VR rehabilitation. This work supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing).

items.title: Biodegradability of Polyethylene Plastics by Individual and Co-cultured Bacterial Isolates
items.abstract: Abstract The extensive dependence on polyethylene-based products has contributed to their persistence in the environment, accounting for about 64% of global plastic waste and posing serious ecological and public health risks. Conventional disposal methods such as incineration and landfilling further intensify pollution, emphasizing the need for eco-friendly alternatives. This study explores the biodegradation of polyethylene plastics using bacteria isolates obtained from soil samples collected across three sites in Kumasi, Ghana. Degradation efficiency was assessed through weight loss analysis and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) to determine changes in the polymer functional groups. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was employed to evaluate the effect of pH, temperature, and incubation time on bacterial growth and degradation process. A total of eleven bacterial isolates were identified using Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization-Time of Flight Mass Spectrometry (MALDI-TOF), with Bacillus cereus being the most prevalent. Optimization analysis revealed that temperature, pH and incubation time significantly influenced degradation, with optimal conditions predicted at 25°C, pH 9- and 21-days incubation respectively. Co-cultures demonstrated higher degradation efficiency than single isolates, supported by elevated laccase activity indicating synergistic enzymatic interactions. FTIR analysis showed polymer modification, showing changes in asymmetric and symmetric C-H stretching peaks in all treatments except Bacillus cereus. In conclusion, the results demonstrate that co-cultured microbes enhance polyethylene degradation through metabolic cooperation and increased enzyme activity, highlighting the potential of microbial synergy as a sustainable strategy for plastic waste management.

items.title: Mapping corporate sustainability disclosures in the Indian food industry
items.abstract: Abstract Mandatory sustainability disclosure frameworks produce uneven compliance outcomes whose nature and drivers remain poorly understood in sector-specific contexts. This study applies a BRSR Disclosure Score - an equally-weighted, indicator-level index across 140 items drawn from India's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) framework - to a longitudinal panel of twenty listed food and beverage companies over 5 fiscal years (FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25). The food and beverage sector is particularly relevant due to its high environmental footprint, supply-chain complexity, and direct public health implications, making sustainability disclosure especially critical. Average disclosure scores rose from 19.3% of the maximum in FY21 to 86.7% in FY25, with over 60% of the gain concentrated in the single year coinciding with mandatory BRSR adoption. General and Process indicators converged to near-perfect coverage, while Leadership indicators - capturing voluntary, forward-looking commitments - remained persistently under-disclosed at 0.56 out of 1.0 in FY25. The Leadership gap was most acute for smaller mid-cap firms and subsections associated with policy advocacy and inclusive growth principles. These findings suggest that regulatory compulsion drives coverage breadth but does not generate values-driven disclosure depth, with implications for SEBI's phased adoption of Leadership indicators and for ESG-based investment screening in the Indian food sector.

items.title: Assessment of Knowledge, Attitude and Practice on Gum Disease among General Population in Bangladesh - A Cross-sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Gum diseases, encompassing gingivitis and periodontitis, remain a major yet under-recognized public health burden, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where population-level data on oral health behavior are scarce. This study assessed the knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) related to gum health among the general adult population of Bangladesh and identified sociodemographic determinants of each domain. Methods A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted between December 2025 and June 2026 across all eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. Using convenience sampling, 1,000 adults aged 18 years and above were interviewed with a pre-tested, semi-structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics and the four KAP components. Knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were each dichotomized using pre-defined cutoffs, and associations with sociodemographic variables were examined through chi-square tests, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and correlation analysis in STATA 17. items.title: Prevalence and factors associated with acute pesticide poisoning among pesticide handlers at a Macadamia Estate, Northern Malawi: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Acute pesticide poisoning (APP) remains a global public health concern. Although developing countries use only a fraction of the pesticides produced worldwide, they bear a disproportionately high burden of pesticide poisoning. Pesticide use improves agricultural productivity by reducing crop losses, but it also poses substantial risks to human health. This study determined the prevalence, symptom distribution, and exposure-related risk factors for APP among pesticide handlers at a macadamia estate in Northern Malawi. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 144 eligible participants were selected using stratified random sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a structured, pretested questionnaire after written informed consent had been obtained. The questionnaire captured: demographic characteristics, signs and symptoms of APP, and exposure-related risk factors. APP was defined using the World Health Organization APP case definition matrix. Associations between exposure-related risk factors and occupational APP were assessed using multivariable binary logistic regression. Results APP prevalence was 63.9% (95% CI: 56.1%–71.7%), and skin irritation was the most frequently reported symptom (58.5%). Exposure-related risk factors significantly associated with APP were secondary education (AOR = 11.56, 95% CI: 3.35–39.92, p p = 0.005), direct contact with pesticides (AOR = 5.84, 95% CI: 1.68–20.26, p = 0.005), and entering treated fields immediately after pesticide application (AOR = 5.13, 95% CI: 1.49–17.70, p = 0.01). Conclusions Nearly two-thirds of pesticide handlers at the estate met the case definition for APP, indicating a substantial occupational health burden. APP was significantly associated with secondary education, drinking water while handling pesticides, direct contact with pesticides, and entering treated fields immediately after pesticide application. To reduce occupational pesticide exposure, targeted behavioral safety interventions should strengthen safe pesticide-handling practices.

items.title: From Environmental Exposure to Compound Vulnerability: Reframing Public Health Governance in Environmental Planning
items.abstract: Abstract The effects of environmental determinants of public health have been investigated by individual pathways of exposure, including air pollution, unsafe water, climate stress, or waste exposure. This review discusses these risks in the light of the concept of compound vulnerabilities, which sees environmental health burdens as being not only determined by exposure, but also by governance, infrastructure, planning, social inequality and adaptive capacity. The study was carried out using a systematic review following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis. Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed were searched to identify peer-reviewed English language articles published between 2020 and 2025. 45 articles were included after screening. The results of the bibliometric analysis indicated an increasing attention to the intersection of environmental determinants and public health, and the major themes were public health, environmental health, air pollution, water pollution, urbanization, sustainable development and policy. Thematic synthesis resulted in the development of five interrelated pathways of air pollution and household energy related health burden; water contamination and WASH and public health risks; climate related stress, heat, flooding and water scarcity; waste, landfill, industrial contamination and spatial inequality; and governance, planning and the compound of vulnerabilities. The review includes recommendations for better environmental health governance that is integrated and equity driven by linking pollution control, WASH systems, waste management, climate change adaptation, land-use planning and vulnerable communities’ protection.

items.title: Nearly Universal Receipt of Desired Contraceptive Method in Two Districts of Rwanda
items.abstract: Abstract Background Research demonstrates that when contraceptive users receive their desired method, they are more likely to maintain contraceptive use, avoid pregnancy, and report satisfaction with family planning. Rwanda has increased family planning use dramatically in a short period of time, from 17% to 69% between 2005 and 2025. This study aims to investigate the role of client receipt of desired method during counseling with family planning nurses at public health clinics or posts in two districts of Rwanda. Methods This study involved data extraction in 2022 and 2023 from family planning records at a sample of public health facilities in two districts of Rwanda, the two districts with the highest and lowest contraceptive prevalence rates in the nation. Extraction from the family planning record included the family planning client’s desired method as stated and recorded prior to counseling as well as the client’s method received after counseling. Results Results show that 95%-97% of a sample of long-acting method users in these two districts received their desired method. Further, multilevel analysis examines correlates of not receiving desired method and finds that individual level client variables explain relatively little variation, while facility-level factors account for most differences in desired method provision in Rwanda. Conclusion Contraceptive users in Rwanda are obtaining their method desired nearly all of the time, meeting client’s method desires is integral to successful contraceptive use and providing human centered services for individuals, family planning programs, and nations.

items.title: Integrated One Health surveillance of canine visceral leishmaniasis in a military institutional kennel in Brazil: retrospective implementation analysis and international benchmarking
items.abstract: Abstract Canine visceral leishmaniasis surveillance in institutional kennels requires more than diagnostic testing because dogs, handlers, vectors, public-health services and institutional management interact within a shared environment. We conducted a retrospective implementation analysis of routine surveillance records from 2022 to 2026 in a military kennel in northeastern Brazil and benchmarked its surveillance architecture against selected international canine and One Health models. Institutional sources included health records, laboratory reports, technical communications and dual-path platform (DPP)-reactive screening episodes referred for enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) confirmation. Seven surveillance domains were predefined: working or institutional dog setting, repeated surveillance, Leishmania testing, prevention or control, environmental or vector component, human or public-health integration, and institutional management or governance integration. Comparator models comprised French military kennels, U.S. government working dogs, and integrated human-canine-sand-fly surveillance in Sicily. The kennel pathway introduced standardized records, sequential testing, deltamethrin-collar management, sanitary criteria for dog movement, environmental measures, staff education, municipal zoonosis-surveillance coordination and management communication. Thirteen DPP-reactive episodes were referred for confirmation; five were ELISA-reactive. Benchmarking showed complementary international emphases: long-term prevention in French military kennels, sentinel pathogen surveillance in U.S. working dogs, and human-canine-vector integration in Sicily. The Brazilian institutional pathway explicitly combined all seven predefined operational domains. This integrated architecture provides a practical One Health model for managed dog populations in endemic settings and links animal health, public health, environment and institutional governance.

items.title: The Impact of Unrestricted Transportation Passes on HIV Treatment and Service Outcomes: Results from a Randomized Controlled Trial among Unstably Housed People Living with HIV
items.abstract: Abstract Background Unstably housed people living with HIV (PLWH) face barriers to achieving and maintaining viral suppression. Transportation instability limits access to medical care and supportive services. Prior research has proposed transportation passes as a potential intervention. However, the effectiveness of this approach has not been evaluated. Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial recruited 146 unstably housed PLWH from a community-based organization serving PLWH in a Midwest city. Participants randomized to the intervention group received an unrestricted public transit pass for 6 months, while the control group retained their current benefits. Surveys administered at baseline and six-month follow-up assessed housing and transportation instability and quality of life. Viral load lab results and social service utilization were extracted from administrative databases. Results Logistic regression found no evidence of an effect of the intervention on the study’s primary outcome of viral suppression (OR .97; 95% CI: 0.47–2.01; p=.942) across multiple missing-data approaches. Models accounted for baseline indicators. Most secondary outcomes, including meals served, stable housing, employment, and quality-of-life scores, also showed no evidence of an effect. However, in a negative binomial model, the intervention affected the frequency of engagement with case management services, with the intervention arm having an estimated rate of recorded follow-up case management contacts 2.24 times that of the control arm (95% CI, 1.03 to 4.88; p = 0.042). Furthermore, stable housing and employment at follow-up clustered strongly in the intervention group (ratio of ORs: 48.9; p = .004). Conclusion Many supportive services are geared toward stabilizing PLWH experiencing homelessness to help them achieve and maintain viral suppression. However, transportation access is an oft-overlooked structural determinant of health. This study finds no evidence of a direct clinical effect of transportation passes during the follow-up period. Increased engagement with case management, though, is valuable and is associated with long-term health and stabilization benefits. The increased service engagement might warrant the relatively low cost of $16 per participant per month. The increased service engagement and exploratory stabilization findings suggest mechanisms by which transportation access might have clinical benefits at longer follow-up periods. Trial Registration The trial was prospectively registered with clinicaltrials.gov NCT06483152 on July 3, 2024.

items.title: “You cannot travel one hundred metres without finding such alcohol”: community perspectives on the availability of alternative alcohol products since the ban of alcohol sachets in Malawi and Uganda
items.abstract: Abstract Background Malawi and Uganda banned alcohol sachets in 2017 and 2019 respectively, to reduce alcohol availability and affordability and protect population health, particularly young people and the most vulnerable. However, the unintended consequences of those bans, particularly the use of alternative alcoholic products, is under-researched. Methods This qualitative study draws on 18 community focus group discussions conducted across both countries (nine per country; n = 159) between 2023 and 2024, in the districts of Wakiso and Gulu (Uganda), and Blantyre and Zomba (Malawi). Participants included adult men and women, in- and out-of-school young males and females, traditional leaders, teachers, and health workers. Data were analysed thematically. Results While participants considered the sachet bans effective, they perceived this effectiveness as temporary. All groups, from both countries, confirmed alternative products, which seem to be both newly emerging substitutes and existing products used as replacements. These included small bottles of recorded high-strength spirits (≤ 220ml) and unrecorded homebrews, sold by variable measures according to demand and purchasing power. Affordability of these products was mentioned in most groups. Community members expressed that these substitute products are widely available and sometimes sold without age verification. In both countries, this was viewed as leading to increased consumption and harm. Conclusion Sachet bans in Malawi and Uganda produced significant changes in the alcohol market rather than meaningful reductions in alcohol availability. Without understanding the market more fully and comprehensive legislation, banning a single product (such as sachets) is unlikely help to protect public health in the longer term.

items.title: Nutritional status and dietary adequacy among school-aged children living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy in Nsanje district, Malawi
items.abstract: Abstract Background HIV infection remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Children living with HIV are vulnerable to poor nutritional outcomes, particularly in rural settings affected by food insecurity and climate-related shocks. This study assessed the nutritional status and dietary adequacy of school-aged children living with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) in Nsanje District, Malawi. Methods A facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January to June 2026 among children aged 5–15 years attending Kalemba Mission Hospital. Of 111 children selected, 102 participated, giving a 91.9% recruitment rate. Nutritional status was measured using WHO anthropometric indicators, while dietary intake was assessed using 24-hour recalls, a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire, and dietary diversity analysis. The IBM™ SPSS Statistics version 29 was utilised for descriptive and inferential statistics. Results Among the 102 children, the mean height-for-age Z-score was − 1.74 and the mean BMI-for-age Z-score was − 1.21. Stunting affected 44.1% of participants, thinness 35.3%, and overweight 5.9%. Most children (70.6%) had adequate dietary diversity, but 29.4% had low dietary diversity. Energy and protein inadequacy were common, with 67.6% and 58.8% of children falling below the EAR, respectively. Mean NAR was highest for iron (0.91), and overall MAR was 0.783. Low dietary diversity (AOR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.15–5.08) and unsuppressed viral load (AOR = 3.48, 95% CI: 1.42–8.51) were associated with thinness, while children aged 11–15 years had lower odds of thinness than those aged 5–10 years (AOR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.30–0.99). Conclusion Poor nutritional status remained common despite ART, highlighting the need for routine nutritional screening, dietary counselling, and regular viral load monitoring.

items.title: Challenges in Collecting LGBT+ Health Data in Primary Health Care in Minas Gerais, Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Background: This study aimed to understand the obstacles involved in recording data on sexual orientation and gender identity in the individual registration form of the eSUS system in two municipalities in the central region of Minas Gerais, Brazil. Understanding these barriers is essential, as this registration process enables the identification, reception, and qualified follow-up of the LGBT+ population within Primary Health Care (PHC). Results: A qualitative, cross-sectional study was conducted, involving 42 semi-structured interviews with health professionals and administrative assistants working in PHC, analyzed using content analysis. The results revealed barriers related to three thematic axes: Professional Limitations, Lack of Institutional Integration, and Tensions Between the Family-Community Model and LGBT+ Identification. These axes unfold into issues such as lack of training and non-recognition of the importance of collecting this data. Conclusions: These findings show that the difficulty in collecting such information is not merely a technical problem, but a reflection of how LGBT+ people continue to be marginalized within health institutions, despite advances in public policies aimed at equity.

items.title: A WeChat-Based Platform Designed for Regional Home-Based Palliative Care in Advanced Cancer: Development and Formative Usability Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Home-based palliative care for people with advanced cancer requires accessible information, support for family caregivers, and continuity between specialist, community, and home services. Digital platforms may extend these resources, but their intended functions and the evidence from early user testing need to be reported separately. Objective This study aimed to develop a theory-informed WeChat-based platform intended to support regional home-based palliative care and to evaluate selected patient-facing functions in a formative usability study. Methods The HuYun Home-Based Palliative Care Platform was developed through multidisciplinary collaboration, clinical content preparation, iterative implementation, and internal expert review. Self-efficacy theory informed its educational and support functions. The design included patient, family caregiver, public, and health care provider interfaces. Ten patients with stage III or IV cancer were purposively recruited before discharge from a tertiary hospital in Shanghai, China. Following a brief introduction, they completed 5 tasks involving pain assessment, article reading, video viewing, feedback submission, and symptom search. Task completion, completion times, and System Usability Scale (SUS) scores were summarized descriptively. Results All 10 patients completed all 5 tasks (10/10, 100% per task; 50/50 task attempts). Mean task times were 61.92 (SD 11.80) seconds for pain assessment and feedback, 279.13 (SD 81.68) seconds for article reading, 117.00 (SD 47.55) seconds for video viewing, 11.05 (SD 7.36) seconds for feedback submission, and 25.40 (SD 19.97) seconds for symptom search. The mean SUS score was 61.25 (SD 9.88; range 42.50–75.00). Development outputs included 4 role-specific interfaces and a proposed hospital-community-home model; formal testing covered selected patient-facing functions. Conclusions Selected patient-facing functions of the platform were operable by 10 patients in a supervised setting, while perceived usability identified priorities for refinement. Further evaluation should include family caregivers and health care providers, independent use at home, and complete consultation, referral, and service-delivery pathways before regional service feasibility or clinical effectiveness can be established.

items.title: Pre-monsoon heatwave trends and ENSO-dryness associations in Rajshahi, Bangladesh
items.abstract: Abstract Pre-monsoon (March-May) heat extremes in the Barind Tract of northwestern Bangladesh threaten agriculture, water resources and public health. Using a 36-year record (1990–2025) from the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) station at Rajshahi, with satellite precipitation and ERA5/ERA5-Land reanalysis, this study assesses heatwave trends, hydroclimatic associations, circulation context and out-of-sample predictability. A heatwave day lies within a spell of at least two consecutive days with maximum temperature ≥ 36.0°C. Rajshahi averaged 31.0 ± 12.4 heatwave days per season (range 4–52). Heatwave days increased by + 4.8 days per decade (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.8–7.8; p = 0.008; false discovery rate [FDR] q = 0.016), whereas the trend in seasonal peak temperature (+ 0.28°C per decade) was not significant after FDR control (q = 0.056). Antecedent January-March root-zone (0–28 cm) soil moisture was inversely associated with heatwave days (Spearman’s ρ = −0.364; p = 0.029), but preceding-August El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region were not (ρ = 0.095; p = 0.58). An intercept-only Negative Binomial climatology had the lowest corrected Akaike Information Criterion, and rolling-origin hindcasts (2005–2025) produced negative Brier Skill Scores, indicating no skill beyond climatology. Severe seasons coincided with mid-tropospheric anticyclonic ridging, rainfall deficits and enhanced sensible heat flux. Because hindcast skill was absent, a 2027 El Niño-dryness scenario (mean 34.0 heatwave days; 95% prediction interval 14–60) is presented as a model-conditioned stress test, not a forecast. The pre-specified verification protocol offers a replicable standard for transparent heat-hazard assessment in data-sparse regions.

items.title: Heterogeneous Pathways to Rabies Prevention: Household-Level Determinants and Dog Owner Profiles of Vaccination Uptake
items.abstract: Abstract Dog-mediated rabies remains a persistent public health challenge in many low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective vaccines and global commitments to eliminate the disease through mass dog vaccination. Achieving and sustaining the recommended 70% vaccination coverage is complicated by substantial heterogeneity in dog ownership, management practices, and access to veterinary services, across urban and rural settings. This study investigates household-level determinants of dog vaccination and explores heterogeneity in rabies knowledge and vaccination behaviour among dog-owning households in Mzimba District, Malawi. Using secondary cross-sectional survey data from 682 households, the study combines count data regression and latent class analysis to examine factors influencing the number of dogs vaccinated per household and to identify distinct dog-owner typologies. The Negative Binomial Regression results indicate that urban residence, higher educational attainment, training in responsible dog ownership, larger dog ownership size, and prior vaccination behaviour significantly increase household vaccination uptake, whereas rabies knowledge alone does not independently predict vaccination. Latent Class Analysis revealed three distinct owner profiles: low-awareness moderate-prevention owners, prevention-oriented moderately aware owners , and high-awareness high-risk multidog owners . These clusters differ markedly in dog population structure, knowledge levels, and vaccination outcomes, highlighting mismatches between awareness and practice in some groups. In summary, the findings demonstrate that household-level configurations and behavioural patterns play a critical role in shaping vaccination outcomes. Tailored, context-sensitive rabies control strategies that integrate education, behaviour-focused training, and structural support are essential to improve vaccination coverage and advance dog-mediated rabies elimination.
