items.title: The Influence of Service Process Management Factors on Patient Satisfaction in Malaysia
items.abstract: Abstract The main objective of this research is studying the effects of process standardization, process efficiency, process flexibility, and process quality control on patient satisfaction in Malaysia's healthcare contexts. A quantitative cross-sectional design was adopted in this research, via a structured 5-point Likert-scale questionnaire to collect data from 400 adult patients across public and private healthcare institutions in urban and rural areas of Malaysia. Data was also examined using SPSS 26.0 through descriptive statistics, reliability and validity tests, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression as well. The findings indicate that all four service process management factors have a significant positive relationship with patient satisfaction in Malaysia. Process flexibility and process quality control demonstrated the strongest predictive effects, followed by process efficiency and process standardization. The regression model explained 87.3% of the variance in patient satisfaction (R² = 0.873). The findings featured importance of effective service process management in enhancing patient experiences within Malaysia's diverse healthcare environment. The study contributes to the literature by examining service process management in the Malaysian healthcare facilities and provides practical implications for healthcare institutions seeking to improve service delivery and patient satisfaction. This research is also related to the Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG 3) “Good Health and Well-being”, specifically Target 3.8, which stresses the importance of universal health coverage and access to essential healthcare services of high quality. Within this framework, the management of healthcare service processes can help achieve higher quality, efficiency, responsiveness, and consistency of healthcare service provision. Therefore, process standardization, process efficiency, process flexibility, and process quality control may be essential for improving patients’ experience and satisfaction with healthcare services.

items.title: Quality of Life Following Treatment for Cervical and Endometrial Cancer: A Patient-Reported EORTC Analysis from Slovakia
items.abstract: Background: Cervical and endometrial cancers remain major public health concerns, and their treatment can substantially affect quality of life (QoL) and survivorship outcomes. This study evaluated QoL among Slovak women after treatment for cervical and endometrial cancer and explored factors associated with post-treatment well-being. Methods: This cross-sectional patient-reported outcome study included 127 women: 74 with endometrial cancer and 53 with cervical cancer. Participants completed a one-time assessment using the EORTC QLQ-C30 together with the disease-specific QLQ-EN24 or QLQ-CX24 modules. Disease stages ranged from IA2 to IIIC1 in cervical cancer and IA to IIIC2ii in endometrial cancer. Eligible participants had histologically confirmed malignancy, ECOG 1–2, and had completed primary treatment 6–60 months before assessment. Analyses included Mann–Whitney U tests, Friedman’s ANOVA, and exploratory multiple linear regression; p-values were interpreted as nominal. Results: The mean age was 57.6 years for endometrial and 49.1 years for cervical cancer patients. All patients underwent surgery; 41.7% received no adjuvant chemotherapy or radiotherapy, 8.7% received adjuvant chemotherapy alone, 24.4% radiotherapy alone, and 25.2% combined chemoradiotherapy. In cervical cancer, cognitive and emotional functioning were relatively preserved, while fatigue, financial difficulties, and sexual/vaginal problems were prominent. In endometrial cancer, cognitive and physical functioning were relatively preserved, whereas social functioning was lower and insomnia and fatigue were frequently reported. Exploratory unadjusted treatment comparisons showed lower global health/QoL among endometrial cancer patients exposed to chemotherapy (r_rb = −0.688, 95% CI −0.950 to −0.387, p Conclusions: Women assessed 6–60 months after treatment reported difficulties particularly in fatigue, social functioning, and sexual-health domains. Treatment-related associations should be interpreted cautiously because of treatment-group heterogeneity, potential confounding by indication, and multiple testing. These preliminary findings support further evaluation of survivorship needs related to symptom management, psychosocial support, sexual health, and long-term QoL.

items.title: Mobile phone use while driving and associated factors: an observational study in Córdoba, Argentina.
items.abstract: Objective Mobile phone use while driving (MPWD) is a growing road safety concern. This observational study explores handheld MPWD and associated factors in the city of Córdoba, Argentina. Methods A total of 117,799 vehicle drivers were observed in different areas, road types, time slots, and days of the week. The data collection period spanned from June 2023 to June 2024. Data were collected on vehicle type, driver's sex, estimated age group, driving speed (measured via gun radar), and handheld mobile phone use. Factors associated with handheld mobile phone use (yes/not) were analyzed using a multiple logistic regression model. Results The observed percentage of mobile phone use was 4.6%. The logistic regression results indicate higher usage among young adult drivers (18-24 years), delivery motorcycle riders, and those driving light and heavy cargo vehicles. Additionally, mobile phone use was more prevalent on weekdays and during afternoon hours, compared to the morning. Greater use was also noted on major urban roads rather than local streets, and during periods of lower traffic count. On average, drivers using mobile phones traveled at lower speeds. Conclusions MPWD was linked to human, environmental, and situational factors. Drivers seem to regulate when and where they use their phones and exhibit risk-compensatory behaviors, such as reducing speed. Young drivers and those who drive for work should be priority targets for prevention campaigns.

items.title: Development of Monocarboxylate Transporter 4 Inhibitor/Docetaxel-Loaded Multilayer Nanoparticles for Prostate Cancer Combination Therapy.
items.abstract: The proposed work seeks to develop and characterize a smart, multilayer MCT4i/DXT-loaded polylactide-glycolic acid nanoparticle for combination therapy in prostate cancer. The core of the smart LBL NPs is prepared by nanoprecipitation, and the sodium acetate "freeze-coating" technique is used to construct the multilayer nanoparticle. The size, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, and nanoparticle surface chemistry are characterized by Malvern Panalytical Advanced Zeta Sizer. UV/VIS Spectrophotometer, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and Fourier Transform Infrared spectrometer (FT-IR). The cytotoxicity of the different nanoformulations is assessed in the C4-2 cell line by MTS assay, and the mechanism of cell death is assessed by flow cytometry using an apoptosis assay. The TEM shows a multi-layer spherical nanoparticle. The multilayer nanoparticle is 255.539 nm in size, with an entrapment efficiency of 89.56 ± 1. 70% and 91.55 ± 7.82% for compound AZD0095 and docetaxel, respectively. The FTIR confirms that sodium acetate coats all the nanoformulation. Low-dose combination therapy effectively inhibits C4-2 cell growth. Smart nanoparticles exhibit dose-dependent cytotoxicity in C4-2 cells. Cell death occurs via apoptosis with docetaxel alone and via secondary necrosis with the combination therapy. The multilayer nanoparticle is a promising nanomedicine for combination therapy in prostate cancer.

items.title: Causal Machine Learning for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity: Interpretation, Benchmarking, Validation.
items.abstract: Causal machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach for predicting individualized treatment effects and advancing precision medicine, moving beyond the limitations of conventional one-variable-at-a-time subgroup analyses of randomized trials. A recent benchmarking study by Chen and colleagues evaluated several causal ML learners across two large trials and concluded that current methods do not yet demonstrate reliable performance for clinical application. While such applied methodological investigations are valuable, this conclusion warrants a more nuanced examination. Multiple independent research groups have successfully applied causal ML across respiratory medicine and critical care, identifying clinically meaningful treatment effect heterogeneity that prior subgroup analyses had not resolved, although these applications have methodological limitations and do not yet establish that the detected heterogeneity is robust across internal and external validation. We outline four sequential and iterative dimensions central to credible causal ML analyses: choice of learner, model training with cross-fitting, internal validation using calibration-for-benefit and rank-weighted metrics, and external validation aligned with the original causal question. With careful methodological execution, causal ML holds considerable promise for personalized treatment decisions and warrants continued development; dismissing the field prematurely risks overlooking a powerful tool for personalized treatment decisions.

items.title: Preimplantation genetic testing in Italy: a single-cycle retrospective analysis.
items.abstract: Background Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) is a diagnostic procedure performed during assisted reproductive technology (ART) to detect chromosomal and monogenic abnormalities before embryo transfer. In Italy, the Italian ART Register (IARTR) monitors ART and PGT activity. Within a National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) project, entitled "Development of the Italian Preimplantation Genetic Testing (PGT) Network", we developed a monitoring system based on ART single-cycles in which PGT was performed. Methods Data on ART-PGT cycles performed in 2024 were collected from 24 Italian ART centers. A relational database was developed including cycle-level and embryo-level variables. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics, Version 29 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results Overall, 2181 ART-PGT cycles involving 1358 patients were analyzed. Genetic testing was performed in 1195 cycles during 2024, and next-generation sequencing was the most frequent technology (96.5%). PGT for aneuploidies (PGT-A) was the most frequent procedure (1065 cycles), followed by PGT for monogenic/single gene defects (PGT-M) (114 cycles) and PGT for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) (110 cycles). The main indication for PGT-A was advanced maternal age (59.4%), for PGT-M was beta-thalassemia (29.6%), for PGT-SR reciprocal chromosomal rearrangements (61.3%). A total of 3771 embryos were analyzed, of which 7% yielded no result. Most blastocysts were biopsied on day 5 or 6 and were classified as having good or optimal quality. Embryo transfer was performed in 761 cycles, most as single embryo transfer, resulting in a clinical pregnancy rate of 49.1%. Conclusions The single-cycle monitoring system for ART-PGT was feasible and effective in collecting detailed clinical and laboratory data. This approach represents an innovation in epidemiological surveillance and may be useful in quality assessment and standardization of ART-PGT practices in Italy.

items.title: Comparative effects of internal and external feedback during learning of a complex motor skill.
items.abstract: Background The influence of attentional focus on motor learning has been widely studied, yet evidence regarding how focus effects vary across learning stages and complex tasks remains inconclusive. The present study examined the impact of external vs. internal focus instructions on the acquisition and short-term retention of a complex manual skill task. Methods Sixteen healthy novice adults (8 males and 8 females; mean age: 26.3±3.8 years), with no prior experience in twirling or organized sports participation, were randomly assigned to either an external focus (EFA) or an internal focus (IFA) instructional group. Following an initial familiarization phase, participants completed three acquisition blocks of 15 trials each (45 practice trials in total) and a 15-trial retention test performed the following day. Performance was evaluated in terms of movement effectiveness and technical execution quality. Results Participants receiving EFA instructions exhibited superior performance improvements during acquisition and higher retention scores than those receiving IFA instructions. Between-group comparisons revealed significant differences favoring the EFA group across all execution categories (all P Conclusions These findings contribute to the understanding of how attentional focus manipulations influence motor behavior across learning stages, highlighting the potential utility of external focus strategies in complex motor tasks. Limitations related to sample size and instructional content are discussed, and implications for future research on attentional mechanisms in motor learning are considered.

items.title: Landfill microplastic research in Asia (2013-2025): Bibliometric insights into trends, contributors, and emerging hotspots.
items.abstract: Landfill-derived microplastics (MPs) are an emerging environmental concern in Asia. Although MP pollution has received increasing scientific attention, the regional knowledge structure, leading contributors, and emerging hotspots of landfill MP research in Asia remain limited and fragmented. This study addresses this gap through a bibliometric analysis of landfill MP research in Asia from 2013 to 2025. A total of 1992 records were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection using a fuzzy logic search strategy. Bibliometric indicators and network-based methods were employed to examine publication growth, document types, country and institutional contributions, subject area distribution, author collaboration, and keyword co-occurrence patterns. The results reveal a rapid expansion of this research field, with annual publication output increasing from 3 records in 2013 to 491 records in 2025. The compound annual growth rate was 52.53%, with a model fit of R 2 = 0.58. Research articles accounted for 38.56% of the dataset, whereas articles represented 37.76%, indicating a relatively narrow gap between empirical and synthesis-based studies. China, India, and Malaysia became the top contributor countries. Malaysia exhibited a high level of collaboration at the author level, whereas China published a high level of research at the institutional level. The largest subject area was environmental science with 1356 publications. Keyword analysis revealed the key emerging hotspots: landfill leachate, risk assessment, bioplastics, circular economy, and health risks. The novelty of the study is that it is the first study focused in Asia that considers publication tendencies, scientific contributors, thematic evolution, and research gaps in a single bibliometric context. Thus, this study serves as a regional evidence base to help facilitate collaboration, enhance field-based monitoring, and inform future risk assessments, management, and policy development for landfills in Asia.

We adjusted multivariable models for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. items.title: Beyond frictionless access: a testable downstream accountability framework for the WHO pathogen access and benefit-sharing annex.
items.abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement depends on a workable Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex that can reconcile rapid pathogen sharing with equitable access to pandemic-related benefits. This viewpoint presents a testable downstream accountability proposal rather than a description of agreed PABS rules. Article 12 already establishes the PABS system, requires the annex to address traceability, provides for legally binding contracts with participating manufacturers, and sets a target for WHO access to 20% of real-time production during a pandemic emergency. The proposal developed here adds an operational downstream trigger, persistent provenance identifiers, pass-through contractual duties, transparent compliance review, and pooled allocation. Routine public-health and non-commercial scientific access would remain rapid and low-friction, and obligations would arise when documented PABS use enters defined product-oriented, intellectual-property, regulatory, licensing, manufacturing, or commercial activity. Persistent identifiers would document provenance, not legal causation, while pooled benefit sharing would avoid sequence-by-sequence valuation. The model also acknowledges unresolved questions of legal authority, national access and benefit-sharing law, allocation governance, non-participating manufacturers, and political acceptability that require negotiation and prospective testing.

items.title: Investigating Incivility in Prelicensure Nursing Education: A Narrative Review of Faculty-to-Student Incivility.
items.abstract: Aim The aim of the study was threefold: 1) synthesize current research in undergraduate nursing education surrounding faculty-to-student incivility in the classroom setting, 2) construct a conceptual definition of faculty-to-student incivility, and 3) identify potential gaps in the current literature for future research purposes. Background Each dynamic of incivility in undergraduate nursing education has unique qualities that must be investigated. Faculty-to-student incivility can be identified in behaviors that negatively impact students' ability to progress through the program. Method A narrative review was performed on relevant articles from 2018 to the present across five databases. A thematic analysis was performed. Results Four key categories were identified in 14 articles: types of incivility, causes of incivility, consequences of incivility, and strategies to mitigate incivility. Conclusion Faculty-to-student incivility is an ongoing issue with profound consequences affecting student retention and the nursing profession. Addressing incivility through faculty education and institutional policies must be promoted.

items.title: Broadening global health knowledge: epistemic pluralism through Asian philosophical traditions.
items.abstract: Global health continues to operate largely within a biomedical epistemological framework that, while effective in addressing acute disease and advancing clinical care, remains limited in responding to complex challenges such as mental health, chronic illness, and persistent inequities. These limitations are not merely technical but reflect deeper epistemic constraints in how health and care are conceptualised. This article argues that selected Asian philosophical traditions, often interpreted through the lens of orientalism, offer an under-recognised resource for rethinking global health. Drawing selectively on Taoist, Confucian, and Buddhist traditions, we highlight how principles of relationality, adaptability, and compassion provide alternative foundations for understanding health beyond the absence of disease. These traditions offer distinctive conceptualisations of relationality, compassion and well-being that can be placed in dialogue with contemporary biomedical and public-health approaches. While contemporary global health systems have increasingly incorporated practices such as mindfulness-based interventions, this integration has often occurred without engagement with their broader philosophical and epistemological implications. Recognising these perspectives and their potential for integration has important implications for global health practice, including reorienting medical education toward reflective and relational competencies, strengthening person-centred and community-engaged care models, and addressing knowledge hierarchies that marginalise ancient philosophical traditions. Reimagining global health therefore requires moving beyond unidirectional knowledge transfer toward a more pluralistic and dialogic framework, in which diverse traditions contribute to more holistic, equitable, and contextually responsive health systems.

items.title: Probing a drug-drug based co-crystallization approach to study its impact on solubility, anti-leishmanial and anti-viral activities of Amphotericin B.
items.abstract: Background Leishmaniasis continues to pose a major growing global public health challenge including Pakistan and Yemen. Method In the present study, drug-drug co-crystallization approach successfully employed to modulate the physicochemical and biological properties of AmB without altering its molecular framework. Results All co-crystals revealed significant enhancement in solubility, showed potent anti-leishmanial potential against promastigotes of L. major, L. tropica and L. donovani except co-crystal 5 as well as anti-viral potential against SARS-CoV-2. Conclusion The initial promising results of the improved anti-leishmanial, potential demonstrated that drug-drug based pharmaceutical co-crystallization may be a promising strategy for improving the therapeutic performance of AmB and therefore, worth to be explored further via detailed in vivo and pharmacokinetic studies.

items.title: Dental solid waste management and associated environmental impacts in Australia: A mini-review.
items.abstract: Over the past century, global warming has become a major environmental issue. The healthcare sector, particularly the dental industry, has been responsible for generating significant amounts of solid waste, and consequently creating greenhouse gas emissions contributing to global warming. This mini-review collates evidence on the current global literature and Australian policy landscape on Australian dental solid waste management and associated environmental impacts. It involved a rapid literature review of global academic and grey literature and Australian policies on the management of dental solid waste. Seven academic articles, eight grey literature articles and three Australian policies were included for review. Key findings were tabulated and thematically coded into headings adapted from the 2018 Australian National Waste Policy framework for solid waste management. Solid waste generation should be reduced through actions such as oral health promotion and caries prevention activities, digitisation of dental administrative processes and streamlining of clinical processes. Waste management system design is important, including waste segregation and proper design of disposal and recycling systems. Knowledge sharing and staff education can help activate behavioural change towards the management of solid waste. Focusing on environmental sustainability, product stewardship and reducing single-use plastics and packaging can also improve solid waste management. Not all waste can be avoided in dentistry, and dental organisations should have alternative strategies to manage solid waste. Strong leadership and governance to support solid waste management strategies can ensure that organisations approach solid waste management at the highest level possible, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and their impact on climate change.

items.title: Toward a Definition and Differentiation of Secondary Traumatic Stress, Vicarious Trauma, Post-Traumatic Stress, and Compassion Fatigue in Relation to First Responders: An Integrative Literature Review.
items.abstract: This integrative review focuses on the psychological effects of direct and indirect exposure to trauma among first responders (firefighters, police investigators, police officers, paramedics, ambulance workers). The aim of this study is to provide conceptual clarification of the various terms used: secondary traumatic stress, vicarious trauma, compassion fatigue, and post-traumatic stress disorder. For this study, six databases were consulted: PsycINFO/ARTICLE; PubMed/Medline; Web of Science; Cochrane; Cairn; ScienceDirect, up to January 2026. To be included, articles had to be published in peer-reviewed scientific journals and concern an adult and professional population. Data extraction followed PRISMA guidelines, and 76 studies were included. Two researchers participated in data extraction and ensured the quality of the articles. The main results revealed conceptual porosity maintained by symptomatic overlaps and the limitations of measurement tools, often designed for other professional categories. The analysis also highlights the central role of organizational constraints in the emergence of trauma, the importance of considering the nature of exposure, cumulative burden, personal experience, and professional role in the study of traumatic responses. Finally, this review calls for exposure to trauma among first responders to be viewed as a public health issue.

items.title: An interactive Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (iPBPK) Model for Predicting Florfenicol and Florfenicol Amine Residues in Edible Tissues and Estimating Withdrawal Intervals in Market-Age Sheep.
items.abstract: Florfenicol (FF) is an antibiotic used for treating respiratory disease in food animals. Extralabel use of FF may lead to violative residues of FF and its major metabolite florfenicol amine (FFA) in edible tissues. This study aimed to develop a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to predict FF and FFA concentrations in edible tissues of sheep to estimate extralabel withdrawal intervals (WDIs). The model consisted of two flow-limited sub-models for FF and FFA. The model was calibrated with FF plasma and FFA tissue concentration data. Upon calibration, the model was evaluated with independent datasets from the Food Animal Residue Avoidance Databank (FARAD). The determination coefficient (R2) values for the goodness-of-fit analysis were 0.97 and 0.93 for model calibration and evaluation datasets, respectively. Furthermore, a population PBPK model was developed using Monte Carlo sampling to estimate the time required for 99th percentile concentration estimates to decline to levels below a given threshold tolerance level associated with safe consumption. Finally, the model was converted into an interactive PBPK (iPBPK) web interface using R Shiny to facilitate the model application. This modeling framework provides a useful tool for predicting WDIs for FF after extralabel use in sheep to support food safety assessment.

items.title: How Can Local Food Environment Policies Reduce Socioeconomic Inequalities in Diet?
items.abstract: This commentary discusses the role of local municipal policies in addressing socioeconomic inequalities in diet and preventing diet-related noncommunicable diseases (NCDs). While national legal and fiscal instruments are essential, local governments possess unique tools, such as spatial planning and public procurement, to improve daily food environments. However, published examples do not establish the comparative effectiveness of municipal-level interventions or their effects on dietary inequalities. Improving physical access or relying on informational tools, like menu labelling, should not be assumed sufficient to reduce dietary inequalities. Direct financial incentives are promising, but the cited observational evidence does not establish causal effectiveness. Interventions combining availability, affordability and demand may address multiple barriers, without necessarily outperforming single structural measures. To reduce dietary disparities, local policies should form part of a coherent multilevel strategy, address economic as well as physical access, and be durably funded, coupled with rigorous, equity-focused evaluation of implementation, dietary outcomes and, where feasible, longer-term health outcomes.

Results Within-person transitions into preparation were associated with a 1.02-point lower CES-D score and a 0.11-point higher life-satisfaction score on a 5-point scale (both p Discussion Old-age financial preparation appears to function as a within-person psychosocial resource related to both evaluative and affective dimensions of well-being. items.title: Analyzing epigenetic modifications at sample-specific CpG loci in long-read data using a likelihood-based framework in bsseq.
items.abstract: Summary DNA in CpG context is often epigenetically modified in vertebrate genomes which increases their mutation rate. However, it remains challenging to identify sample-specific CpG loci for analysis of epigenetic modifications. Here, we present a read-based likelihood framework for identifying reference and non-reference CpG loci with high precision and sensitivity in single-molecule long-read sequencing data from Nanopore and PacBio platforms. Including all sample-specific CpG loci increases the number of analyzable loci and reduces bias in modification level estimates, both critical factors for accurate analyses of epigenetic modifications. Availability and implementation The likelihood framework is implemented in the R package bsseq with the source code available on github https://github.com/hansenlab/bsseq. Installation instructions and a user guide for long-read analysis and likelihood-based filtering of CpG loci are available on Bioconductor https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/bsseq.html. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: Racial cuts: Explanations of race inequities in cesarean births in U.S. government and medical discourse.
items.abstract: Cesarean births are increasingly common worldwide, constituting what some experts call a cesarean epidemic and attracting public health initiatives to reduce cesarean rates. The U.S. cesarean epidemic is racialized, consisting of cesarean overuse in low-risk contexts and underuse in high-risk contexts for Black birthing people. Research shows health initiatives portray Black women as non-compliant with health directives, justifying inequitable outcomes in reproductive contexts, including birth, breastfeeding, and pre-pregnancy health. However, research has not examined initiatives to reduce cesareans, which are distinct because they occur within hospitals and are authorized by medical professionals. This study used critical discourse analysis to investigate constructions of race inequities in cesareans across 59 documents published between 2010 and 2025 by U.S. government agencies and medical organizations. Findings revealed cesareans are constructed as lifesaving procedures that carry inherent risks of detrimental outcomes, including death. Documents acknowledged race inequities in cesareans, but associated them with comorbidities (e.g. hypertension) rather than structural or obstetric racism; explaining and eradicating race inequities was rarely addressed. By centering behavioral and biomedical risk factors, discourses reproduce Black birthing people as inherently "high-risk," thereby legitimizing cesarean overuse. Centering cesareans as a discursive site of racialization, this study shows how surgical intervention is justified through language that marks Black bodies as pathologically susceptible to "risk." These findings illustrate that cesarean birth functions not only as a medical intervention but also as a site of racialized reproductive governance.

items.title: Two Decades of Cardiovascular Prevention Science at CDC: A Bibliometric Analysis, 2006-2025.
items.abstract: Background The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Division for Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention (DHDSP) provides national leadership for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, including efforts to improve hypertension control. Scientific publications document surveillance, program implementation, evaluation, and dissemination of evidence-based strategies. This study describes DHDSP's scientific productivity, focus, and reach across two decades of CVD prevention work. Methods We conducted a bibliometric analysis of publications authored or coauthored by DHDSP staff during 2006-2025. Publications were identified from internal records and PubMed searches, verified for eligibility, and categorized by condition and topic area. Citation metrics, Relative Citation Ratio (RCR), Altmetric Attention Scores, policy and guideline mentions, authorship role, and collaboration indicators were summarized descriptively. Results DHDSP contributed to 841 publications ranging annually from 12 in 2006 to 67 in 2017. Publications accrued 88,636 citations (median: 19; 25-75 percentiles: 7;48). Median RCR was 1.15 (25-75 percentiles: 0.50-2.53), and median Altmetric Attention Score was 6.0 (25-75 percentiles: 0.5-23.5). DHDSP publications were cited or mentioned in 637 policy documents and 410 guidelines indexed by Altmetric. Most focused on core DHDSP conditions, including hypertension, with surveillance and epidemiology the most common topic. Overall, 240 publications (28.5%) included a focus on hypertension. Conclusions DHDSP's publication portfolio demonstrates sustained scientific productivity and broad dissemination across two decades of CVD prevention. Hypertension was an important component, alongside research addressing heart disease, stroke, and other cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes. The portfolio documents the evolution of public health science and contributes to the evidence base for cardiovascular disease prevention and control.

items.title: Estimated Usual Nutrient Intakes and Nutrient Inadequacy Among Schoolchildren in Rural Communities in the Philippines.

Estimated usual intakes and the prevalence of inadequacy were calculated using the National Cancer Institute 1-day method with external variance ratios (between-person and within-person) from the 2018 Filipino National Nutrition Survey. items.title: Real-world data to support clinical evidence generation in oncology: considerations for biomarker-based cohort selection, end point assessment and other methodological issues.
items.abstract: Randomized clinical trials remain the evidentiary gold standard for oncology, but they are often insufficient to fully characterize benefit-risk in rare cancers, biomarker-defined subgroups, and other settings where trial evidence is limited. As precision oncology advances, real-world data and real-world evidence (RWE) offer an increasingly important opportunity to address evidentiary gaps outside traditional trial populations. Yet the use of RWE in oncology requires more than access to data; it requires fit-for-purpose methods that account for the distinctive challenges of biomarker-based cohort selection, end point definition and bias mitigation. This paper reviews methodological considerations for oncology RWE generation and synthesizes selected use cases to illustrate their application in practice. We highlight unique issues arising in oncology RWE research, including incomplete or delayed biomarker ascertainment, heterogeneity in testing platforms and thresholds, misclassification of molecularly defined cohorts, variability in line-of-therapy assignment and time-related biases that can compromise interpretability. We also examine real-world end point ascertainment and discuss considerations for assessing end point validity, completeness and translatability. In addition, we outline how common oncology clinical trial end points can be operationalized as approximate real-world constructs, recognizing that differences in assessment schedule, measurement method and available data may affect comparability and performance. By integrating these methodological challenges with practical design considerations, this paper provides timely guidance to support generation of credible RWE for clinical development in oncology.

items.title: Heart Failure in Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity: From Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
items.abstract: Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone therapy for haematological malignancies and solid tumours, but their use is limited by cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to overt heart failure (HF). The risk increases with cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent exposure exceeding 250-300 mg/m2, although susceptibility varies substantially according to patient characteristics, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, genetic predisposition, and modifiable risk factors. Clinically overt HF occurs in ∼6-9% of patients, while subclinical cardiac dysfunction develops in up to 18%. The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving interconnected mechanisms that disrupt cardiomyocyte homeostasis and promote endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and adverse remodelling. Yet evidence connecting molecular mechanisms with long-term HF outcomes in humans remains incomplete. Risk stratification, incorporating clinical variables, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and, when appropriate, cardiac magnetic resonance enables earlier recognition of cardiac dysfunction. Trials of preventive neurohormonal treatment and statins have produced heterogeneous results, often relying on imaging rather than clinical HF endpoints. Once cardiac dysfunction develops, prompt initiation of foundational HF treatment and multidisciplinary decisions on cancer therapy are essential. Early detection and prompt initiation of HF therapies may reverse myocardial dysfunction, whereas delayed recognition is associated with a poorer treatment response and prognosis. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the mechanisms, risk stratification, surveillance, prevention, and management of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and HF, while highlighting gaps in knowledge, emerging therapeutic strategies, and future directions for clinically meaningful, risk-guided research.

items.title: Implementing social health insurance scheme for universal health coverage: A multiple case study in three health districts in Benin.
items.abstract: To improve access to health services for the entire population, the Beninese government launched in 2019 a new social health insurance (SHI) programme specifically targeted to the poorest population. This study presents an assessment of SHI programme implementation in different contexts and examines how stakeholders perceive it. The design of study was a multiple and contrasted case studies conducted in three health districts in Benin. Empirical data were collected through documentary analysis, interviews (n= 140), focus group discussions (15) and non-participate observations with the SHI programme's beneficiaries, health workers, community leaders, and non-beneficiaries of the programme. Data analysis was based on the main components "SHI's programme theory" using deductive and inductive thematic approaches with NVivo software 14. Findings of this study revealed a relatively faithful implementation in relation to the planned design. However, several implementation gaps, issues and challenges were observed: targeting of the poor faced inclusion and exclusion errors; community awareness efforts did not result in sufficient knowledge of the benefits package by beneficiaries; some health workers were insufficiently trained; a multitude of additional forms, including treatment records, hospitalization forms, and healthcare invoices, must be completed by healthcare facilities to substantiate reimbursement claims; delays were observed in the reimbursement of healthcare facilities. The SHI's objectives were widely appreciated and positively received. Nevertheless, feelings of demotivation and dissatisfaction emerged, along with strained relationships between healthcare providers and beneficiaries. This study highlighted the challenges of implementing social health insurance in Benin. It also confirms the importance of conducting implementation studies to ease bottlenecks on the path towards universal health coverage.

items.title: Association of subjective workload on burnout in village midwives: A NASA TLX-based investigation.
items.abstract: BackgroundVillage midwives play a central role in delivering maternal and primary healthcare services in rural Indonesia, where professional demands are extensive and resources are limited. Understanding the relationship between subjective workload and burnout is essential to support their occupational well-being.ObjectiveThis study examined the association between multidimensional subjective workload and burnout among village midwives using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX).MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 209 village midwives in Kediri District, Indonesia, selected through simple random sampling from the official registry. Subjective workload was assessed using the six NASA-TLX dimensions: mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, performance, effort, and frustration. Burnout was measured using the Maslach Burnout Inventory. Ordinal logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between workload dimensions and burnout levels.ResultsMost respondents reported moderate workload and moderate burnout. Mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, performance pressure, and effort were significantly associated with higher burnout levels, whereas frustration was not statistically significant.ConclusionsMultiple dimensions of subjective workload were associated with burnout among village midwives. These findings support systematic workload assessment to identify occupational strain and inform institutional strategies to promote midwives' well-being in rural healthcare settings. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

items.title: Work-Caregiving strain among family caregivers of burn survivors: Occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.
items.abstract: BackgroundFamily caregivers are often working adults whose unpaid care responsibilities can disrupt paid work, yet occupational impact is rarely examined beyond employment status or financial burden. Burn caregiving provides a high-demand traumatic-injury context in which prolonged rehabilitation, family reorganization, and support needs may conflict with caregivers' work lives.ObjectiveTo examine the occupational impact of burn caregiving over a 24-month recovery period and characterize two theory-informed patterns of caregiver occupational experience: occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.MethodsWe analyzed baseline and 24-month occupational follow-up data from 256 family caregivers in a burn survivor-caregiver cohort. Follow-up outcomes captured work participation, job change, caregiving-attributed workforce detachment, perceived career impact, and work-related barriers and facilitators post-baseline. Occupational sacrifice was operationalized as caregiving-attributed workforce detachment or adverse career appraisal among employed caregivers; positive occupational appraisal was defined as favorable perceived career impact. Baseline demographic, survivor-injury, and psychosocial characteristics were examined descriptively and in logistic regression models.ResultsAt 24 months, 71.5% reported ongoing work participation, 20.7% caregiving-attributed workforce detachment, and 7.8% other changes. Among employed caregivers, 32.2% reported job change, of whom 42.4% reported negative career appraisal. Occupational sacrifice was identified in 35.2% and was accompanied by functional, appearance-related, family-caregiving, workplace, rehabilitation-support, and financial barriers. Positive occupational appraisal was reported by 31.3% and was associated with lower baseline distress and higher posttraumatic growth.ConclusionsThese findings extend injury-related occupational health to family caregivers and support a theory-informed framework for studying work-caregiving strain, occupational sacrifice, and positive appraisal prospectively.

items.title: From Isolated Work to a Team-Based Approach in Home Care Services: Impact on Labor Conditions and Physical Health.
items.abstract: Background Barcelona's municipal Home Care Services (HCS) have undergone a teamwork- and proximity-based reorganization aimed, among other goals, at improving workers' labor conditions. Although team-based home care has been commonly studied in relation to job satisfaction and autonomy, evidence on workers' physical health is limited. Objective To assess the impact of HCS reorganization on workers' employment conditions, ergonomic hazards, and physical health outcomes. Methods Mixed-method quasi-experimental pre-post design (2022-2024). Quantitative data included 1288 survey observations from intervention and comparison groups across three waves (pre: 550 workers; post1: 397 workers; post2: 341 workers). Qualitative data comprised 27 longitudinal interviews with intervention group workers at two time points, with one participant lost to follow-up. Results Quantitative descriptive results showed increased full-time employment and shorter travel times between users' homes in the intervention group. Ergonomic risk exposure was high across groups, but lifting or moving people augmented only among intervention workers. These workers also reported higher levels of fatigue and poorer self-rated health over time. Multivariable analyses confirmed results on travel times, exposure to lifting or moving people, and fatigue. Qualitative findings suggest sustained exposure to ergonomic hazards and indirect effects of the reorganization as potential mechanisms behind fatigue. Conclusions Among intervention workers, three main changes were associated with the HCS reorganization: shorter travel times between users' homes, more frequent lifting or moving people, and higher fatigue levels. Further strategies are needed to reduce physical strain and safeguard workers' health in this essential care sector.

items.title: Preconception Mycoplasma genitalium Seropositivity and Risk of Impaired Fecundity.
items.abstract: Background Mycoplasma genitalium (MG) is an emerging sexually transmitted infection (STI) associated with pelvic inflammatory disease. Its relationship with impaired fecundity remains unclear and is rarely examined in the context of co-seropositivity with other STIs. Methods We conducted a secondary analysis of the Effects of Aspirin in Gestation and Reproduction (EAGeR) trial, a prospective preconception cohort of women with proven fecundity and prior pregnancy loss. MG serostatus was determined using Western blot-based IgG assays on 1146 stored serum specimens. Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) and other STIs were also measured. Associations between MG seropositivity and measures of impaired fecundity were assessed.Pregnancy loss and live birth were modeled using inverse-probability weighted quasi-Poisson and unweighted log-binomial models to calculate relative risks (RR). Fecundability-odds-ratio (FOR) was estimated using a discrete Cox proportional hazards model accounting for left truncation and right censoring. Propensity score (PS) weighted versions of these models assessed risks associated with CT co-seropositivity. Analyses were adjusted for demographic and reproductive history variables. Results Overall, 17.1% (n=210) of participants were MG seropositive, with 27.6% (n=58) co-seropositive with CT. Compared to STI-seronegative women, MG seropositivity was not associated with any outcome, although trends were observed for reduced fecundability (FORadj: 0.87, 95% CI 0.70-1.08) and live birth (RRadj: 0.94, 95% CI 0.79-1.11). Co-seropositivity with CT was associated with lower likelihood of live birth [RRPS-weighted: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.70-0.96]. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of these findings. Conclusions Being co-seropositive for MG and CT preconception was associated with impaired fecundity.

items.title: Evaluating the availability and quality of online resources for Australian injured workers finalizing workers' compensation claims.
items.abstract: BackgroundThe negative impacts of a compensation claim on injured workers, may continue beyond the end point of a claim and limited resources exist to facilitate this transition.ObjectiveTo identify and evaluate online resources that are currently available for injured workers finalizing a workers' compensation claim in Australia, and to synthesize the information within the resources.MethodsA descriptive research design was utilized. A Community Advisory Group (CAG) appraised the resources for usefulness and readability. The resources were also evaluated independently by two researchers, utilizing the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) Benchmark Criteria, evaluating 4 core standards for web sites: authorship, attribution, disclosure, and currency. Information within the resources was synthesized into categories.Results109 resources were screened for inclusion, with 15 online resources meeting inclusion criteria included in analysis. The median CAG appraisal for usefulness ranged from 5 to 8.5 out of 10 and the median CAG appraisal for readability ranged from 5.5 to 10 out of 10. 2 of the 15 resources were considered to contain completely sufficient data following JAMA evaluation. Synthesis of information presented in the resources identified 4 categories related to insurance, financial, legal and healthcare recommendations for injured workers.ConclusionA novel view on resources currently available to injured workers exiting a workers' compensation claim environment in Australia is presented. Limitations are reported and a synthesis of information within the resources and future recommendations to facilitate development of resources for this population are provided.

items.title: Child grant receipt and birth registration in Nepal: evidence from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey.
items.abstract: Background In Nepal, a child grant program was introduced in 2009 to improve education and nutrition among disadvantaged children under the age of five while linking grant eligibility to birth registration as part of efforts to strengthen civil registration and vital statistics systems. Objective This study examined whether child grant receipt was associated with birth registration. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey. The outcome was whether a child's birth had ever been registered with civil authorities. The main explanatory variable was whether the child had ever received a child grant. Child age, sex, maternal education, ethnicity, household wealth quintile, and province were included as covariates in multivariable logistic regression models. Results Among 5,064 included children, 72.8% had a reported registered birth. Registration was higher among children reported to have received a grant than among nonrecipients (93.6% versus 65.9%). Children reported to have received a grant had higher adjusted odds of registration than nonrecipients (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.75; 95% CI 5.14 to 8.85). Registration was 71.8% among children whose mothers had no education, 68.3% for grades 1 to 8, and 77.0% for education above grade 8. Conclusions Child grant receipt was strongly associated with reported birth registration. Links between social protection and birth registration should be accompanied by accessible registration services and support for families facing documentation barriers.

items.title: Photovoice as contributing to resiliency among trans women experiencing individual and intersecting HIV and anti-trans stigma in madhesh province, Nepal.
items.abstract: Trans women in low-income countries face high risk for HIV and poor care outcomes, often due to pervasive anti-trans and HIV-related stigma. We implemented a Photovoice intervention to explore how intersecting forms of stigma shape the lives of trans women in one of the Terai districts of Nepal and to examine how participation in the project influenced social support and community connectedness. Using a participatory mixed-methods design, fourteen trans women participated in two Photovoice workshops, completed pre- and post-intervention surveys, and engaged in photo documentation, journaling, group discussion, and interviews. Participants described experiences of internalised and familial stigma, economic exclusion, diminished family support, and social marginalisation, with photographs illustrating how stigma influenced daily life, livelihood, mobility and well-being. Following the intervention, most participants reported greater community connectedness, defined as increased feelings of interpersonal connection, emotional support, and engagement with other trans women and peer networks. These changes were reflected in participants reporting greater outreach to peers, increased emotional openness, and stronger support from relationships developed during the project. Photovoice effectively fostered social support and collective resilience, highlighting the need for structural interventions to improve HIV prevention, treatment, and wellbeing outcomes.

items.title: Explaining Human Psychology Evolutionarily
items.abstract: Abstract Evolutionary psychology aims to fulfil Darwin’s vision—articulated towards the end of The Origin of Species— of providing a new foundation for the scientific study of human psychology. The field holds that human behavior should be explained using the same biological principles and empirical approaches applied to non-human animals, emphasizing how different evolutionary forces have influenced the functioning of their psychological mechanisms. Scholarly debate has long centered on issues such as adaptationism, testability, cognitive modularity, and the role of culture. More recently, however, evolutionary psychology has faced a new wave of critiques. These include that it presupposes, but cannot support, that human psychological mechanisms are “vertically homologous” with those of their ancestors; that it neglects several important evolutionary processes; that it relies on an outdated computationalist view of the mind; and that it does not yet satisfy the criteria for a mature, normal science. This article aims to present a balanced account of these emerging critiques, along with a set of original responses that, to date, have not been fully articulated in the literature. In general, we argue that the critiques involve unsound argumentation with false premises, attack a straw man position, are vulnerable to reductios , or rely on an implausible philosophical model of how scientific works ought to be evaluated.

items.title: Probable post-traumatic stress disorder after miscarriage: psychological, social, and healthcare-related factors in a mixed-methods study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Miscarriage is commonly managed as a short-term obstetric condition, yet its psychological consequences may extend beyond physical recovery. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after miscarriage and to examine psychological, social, and healthcare-related factors shaping PTSD symptom severity and recovery experiences. Methods: A theory-informed sequential mixed-methods study was conducted at the Post Abortion Care clinic of a tertiary Grade-A women’s and children’s hospital in Sichuan Province, China. In the quantitative phase, 293 women who had experienced miscarriage before 20 completed weeks of gestation completed a digital survey assessing PTSD symptoms, psychological resilience, perceived social support, rumination, coping style, distress disclosure, self-efficacy, anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic growth. Probable PTSD was defined as a Post-traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist–Civilian Version score of 38 or higher. Between-group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and hierarchical multivariable linear regression models were used. In the qualitative phase, nine women participated in semi-structured interviews, which were analyzed thematically and integrated with quantitative findings. Results: The mean PCL-C score was 33.5 ± 12.1, and 95 women (32.4%) screened positive for probable PTSD. Women with probable PTSD had lower psychological resilience than those without probable PTSD (55.4 ± 12.7 vs. 66.4 ± 16.4) and lower perceived social support (59.3 ± 14.0 vs. 66.3 ± 13.8). Higher resilience and perceived social support were associated with lower PTSD symptom severity, while intrusive rumination showed the strongest positive association. Hierarchical regression showed that sociodemographic and reproductive variables alone explained little variance in PTSD symptom severity (adjusted R² = 0.007), whereas adding healthcare-related, psychosocial, and psychological process variables increased explanatory power (adjusted R² = 0.161 and 0.538). Qualitative interviews identified four themes: self-regulation after miscarriage, partner and family support, social safety and stigma, and healthcare communication and care-process burden. These findings contextualized the quantitative associations and highlighted modifiable family, social, and health-service factors. Conclusions: Probable PTSD was common after miscarriage and was shaped by more than individual psychological vulnerability. Post-miscarriage care should move beyond procedure-centered management toward trauma-informed, partner- and family-sensitive, and patient-centered support that includes psychological screening, clear communication, stigma reduction, and attention to care-process burden.

items.title: Efektivitas Pengelolaan Sumber Daya Alam dalam Memenuhi Kebutuhan Ekonomi Masyarakat
items.abstract: Natural resource management is often assumed to improve community welfare, yet empirical evidence shows mixed outcomes. This article synthesizes research on natural resource management in forestry, fisheries, mangroves, and related sectors, internationally and in Indonesia, to assess how far such management meets the economic needs of communities. Using a library research approach, it synthesizes 29 scholarly journal articles through thematic grouping and interprets the findings with economic concepts such as property rights, scarcity, opportunity cost, externalities, and benefit distribution. The findings show that natural resources contribute roughly 22–38% of rural and coastal household income, and that various management schemes are reported to raise income or food security by 18–45%. However, Indonesian studies indicate that abundant resources do not automatically generate stable income, owing to land tenure problems, weak coordination and regulatory enforcement, pollution, and technological constraints. Management effectiveness should be assessed across four dimensions: economic, ecological, equity, and institutional. Policies should recognize community management rights, strengthen regulatory implementation, and provide alternative livelihoods when resource use is restricted

items.title: From intracellular force maps to organelle and organism physiology.
items.abstract: The mechanical properties of the cell interior are heterogeneous, varying across components and compartments according to function, location and time. However, many current mechanical models of the cell do not fully reflect this, either treating the cell as a simplified isotropic mechanical continuum or focusing on complex mechanics of isolated cellular structures, leaving the integration of mechanical features at cellular-to-tissue levels unresolved. To link mechanics with biological function, complete, spatially and temporally resolved maps of subcellular to mesoscopic mechanical properties in living systems and organisms are needed. Despite major technical advances in mechanobiology over the past decade, only snapshots of these heterogenous material properties have been obtained. Crucially, the integration of quantitative force measurements with microscopy approaches remains a challenge in connecting cell mechanics with biological structure and function. This limitation underlines the urgent need for novel imaging methods to visualize how different organelles, cells and organisms respond to forces and how their mechanical properties are coupled to function and physiology. In this Review, we outline recent developments in this rapidly advancing field and discuss what lays ahead in order to bring spatially and temporally resolved imaging of subcellular mechanics into a quantitative and broadly accessible framework for cell biology.

items.title: The Cylinder Test: Development and clinical validation of a tool for assessing hand opening.
items.abstract: Background Impaired hand opening following neurological injury can limit functional grasp and object handling. Existing upper limb assessments do not specifically evaluate functional hand opening or distinguish between active and passive components. Purpose To describe the development of the Cylinder Test (CyT) and evaluate its preliminary face validity, manual clarity, feasibility, and perceived clinical relevance among clinicians and individuals with neurological upper limb impairment. Study design Clinical measurement, cross-sectional study. Methods The CyT was developed through iterative clinical refinement and literature review. The final CyT version comprises 14 plastic cylinders (20-150 mm diameter) and four subtests assessing active and passive functional hand opening. Face validity was evaluated in 33 individuals with neurological upper limb impairments due to cervical spinal cord injuries (cSCI) or spasticity and 31 clinicians experienced in neurological upper limb rehabilitation. Clinicians reviewed the CyT manual and completed a study-specific questionnaire assessing clarity, perceived clinical usefulness, relevance of the subtests, and scoring criteria. Participants performed the CyT and subsequently rated its relevance and perceived effort. Data were summarized descriptively. Results All clinicians (31/31, 100%) reported that the manual provided sufficient guidance for independent administration, and all considered the CyT potentially useful in clinical practice. The purpose of the CyT was rated as clear or very clear by 26/31 clinicians (84%), and no clinician rated any subtest or scoring criterion as inappropriate. All participants (33/33, 100%) rated the overall CyT as relevant or very relevant, and ratings of the individual subtests were predominantly relevant or very relevant. Six of 15 participants with spasticity rated the test as demanding compared with 2/18 participants with cSCI. Conclusions Preliminary evaluation supports the face validity, manual clarity, feasibility, and perceived clinical relevance of the CyT for assessing functional hand opening in neurological upper limb rehabilitation. The CyT may provide hand therapists with a clinically feasible approach to assessing active and passive hand opening. Further evaluation of reliability, construct validity, and responsiveness is required.

items.title: Molecular detection of Borrelia puertoricensis and a Coxiella endosymbiont in Ornithodoros puertoricensis from northern Veracruz, Mexico.
items.abstract: Tick-borne relapsing fever (TBRF) is a neglected zoonosis caused by Borrelia spp. and transmitted by soft ticks of the genus Ornithodoros. Although Mexico has a long history of human TBRF, the current distribution of relapsing fever borreliae and their associated vectors remains poorly understood, particularly in the Mexican Gulf Coast region. This study investigated the presence of tick-borne bacteria in ticks collected at a​ veterinary clinic in northern Veracruz, Mexico. A total of 164 Ornithodoros puertoricensis ticks were identified using morphological characteristics and 16 S mitochondrial ribosomal RNA sequencing. DNA extracts were screened by conventional PCR for Borrelia, Rickettsia, Bartonella, Coxiella, and Ehrlichia/Anaplasma, followed by DNA sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of positive samples. Borrelia puertoricensis DNA was detected in six ticks (3.66%), in four nymphs and two females. Phylogenetic analyses of the flaB gene confirmed that all sequences clustered within the B. puertoricensis clade with strong bootstrap support. In addition, a Coxiella endosymbiont was detected and assigned to clade B based on 16 S rRNA phylogenetic reconstruction, representing the first molecular evidence of this lineage in O. puertoricensis. None of the DNA samples were positive for Rickettsia, Bartonella, Ehrlichia, or Anaplasma. These findings provide the first molecular evidence of B. puertoricensis and a Coxiella clade B endosymbiont in O. puertoricensis from Veracruz, extending the known distribution of both microorganisms in Mexico. The detection of these bacteria in ticks collected at a veterinary clinic capable of treating wild animals highlights the importance of integrated acarological and molecular surveillance at wildlife-domestic animal-human interfaces to improve understanding of the ecology and public health significance of neglected tick-borne zoonoses.

items.title: The wild avian resistome: metagenomic insights into antimicrobial resistance ecology.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in wild birds is increasingly studied as an ecological component of the wider One Health resistome, yet the evidentiary meaning of a resistance gene detected in avian material varies markedly with study design. This review synthesizes culture-based, whole-genome and metagenomic evidence with emphasis on what modern sequencing can and cannot establish about acquisition, persistence, mobility and transmission. Wild birds encounter antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) through wastewater, landfills, livestock-associated environments, surface waters, sediments and food webs; resident synanthropic species can be as informative as long-distance migrants. Shotgun and genome-resolved metagenomics have expanded the known avian resistome, enabled host assignment and revealed links with mobile genetic elements and viromes, but DNA detection alone does not demonstrate viable carriage or directional dissemination. We therefore organize the evidence through an evidence-to-inference framework of five complementary domains: ARG detection, microbial-host assignment, genomic mobility, viable carriage and persistence, and transmission, the last separated into sharing between compartments and direction of movement. Applying the framework to published sequencing studies shows that most reach only detection or host assignment, rely on relative abundance, rarely report negative controls and come predominantly from China. The framework clarifies why wild birds are often best regarded as ecological sentinels unless persistence, viable hosts and directionality are shown. Combining metagenomics with long-read sequencing, targeted culture, isolate genomics, environmental sampling and movement ecology offers the strongest route toward biologically meaningful One Health surveillance.

items.title: From subjects to experts: Methodological reflections on interviewing preschool-aged children about sensitive topics.
items.abstract: Preschool-aged children remain underrepresented in research on illness, death, and bereavement, reflecting ethical concern and the fit between conventional interview methods and children's developmental and communicative capacities. This article draws on three Danish studies. These were a home-based sand tray interview with parentally bereaved children, a laboratory timeline task on understanding death, and a practice-based evaluation of a family bereavement network. Across the three studies, participants were aged three to eight at data collection. We use preschool-aged children throughout to refer to this broad group, recognizing that the term is defined more narrowly in some national systems, and we note where age-related differences within the group mattered for participation. Together the three studies show how children can be included in sensitive research. Participation depended less on simpler questions than on designing encounters that gave children ways to engage, supported distance from difficult material, and visible opportunities to continue, pause, or stop. Setting, interviewer judgment, and infrastructure shaped the ethics of participation and the knowledge produced. Recognizing children's expertise means broadening what counts as data, including play, gesture, objects, silence, and advice. The task is not to make children speak like adults, but to build methods that recognize what they communicate.

items.title: Measurement properties of instruments assessing self-stigma and help-seeking stigma in youth: a systematic review protocol.
items.abstract: Objective This systematic review will evaluate the measurement properties and methodological rigor of self-report instruments assessing internalized self-stigma and self-stigma of seeking help among youth and emerging adults (aged 12-25 years). The review will map global evidence to identify geographical gaps in psychometric equity, focusing on instruments validated for Arabic-speaking youth as a critical test of cross-cultural validity and measurement invariance. Introduction The transition between ages 12 and 25 years represents a critical period for mental health. Internalized self-stigma is a significant proximal barrier to professional help-seeking; however, existing tools often lack sufficient evidence of cross-cultural validity. Without psychometric equity, particularly in collectivist, Arabic-speaking contexts, current instruments may contain measurement bias. Eligibility criteria We will include original peer-reviewed primary research and academic dissertations reporting the development, translation, cross-cultural adaptation, or validation of self-report instruments measuring internalized self-stigma or the self-stigma of help-seeking in youth (aged 12 to 25 years) across any cultural context, with a secondary focus on Arabic-speaking populations (including regional dialects). Studies published in English, Arabic, or French published from January 1, 1996, to the date of the final search, will be eligible. Methods This review will follow the COSMIN framework. We will search PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Citation Index, and the Index Medicus for the Eastern Mediterranean Region. Two independent reviewers will screen studies for eligibility, assess methodological quality using the COSMIN Risk of Bias checklist v.3.0, and extract data using a standardized tool. Findings will be synthesized following COSMIN guidance, and certainty of evidence will be evaluated using the modified GRADE approach tailored for measurement properties. Review registration PROSPERO CRD420261290064.

items.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
items.abstract: Purpose The present study aimed to evaluate associations between resistance training and binge drinking in relation to musculoskeletal composition, physical fitness, cognitive function, and psychological wellness in young adult females. Methods Participants were categorized into four groups: sedentary low alcohol consumers (SL; n=12), sedentary binge drinkers (SB; n=12), resistance-trained low alcohol consumers (RTL; n=12), and resistance-trained binge drinkers (RTB; n=12). Measurements included body composition via DEXA scan, muscle quality via ultrasonography, and insulin sensitivity via oral glucose tolerance test. Physical performance was assessed using maximum chair stand power, vertical jump, broad jump, knee extensor torque, grip strength, and push-ups to failure. Tests and questionnaires were used to assess cognitive function and psychological wellness. Results Resistance-trained females had lower body fat than sedentary females (RTL = 29.28±4.27%; RTB = 29.03±3.67%; SL = 37.18±5.32%; SB = 34.83±3.54%; p Conclusions The results suggest that ≥1 year of binge drinking is associated with poorer metabolic health without differences in performance in young females. Further, frequent RT may mitigate the effects of binge drinking on body composition.

items.title: Supporting Males with Suicidal Ideation: Evaluation of an E-Learning for Healthcare Providers.
items.abstract: Suicide remains an important public health issue. Males are at increased risk for suicide, yet display reduced help-seeking, increased drop-out and less lasting engagement. Despite calls for more gender-responsive care, practical training for healthcare providers (HCPs) remains scarce. To address this gap, a training module (e-learning) was developed to support HCPs in offering gender-responsive suicide prevention care to males. This study aimed to evaluate changes in HCPs' self-efficacy and gender-responsive competencies, and their satisfaction with the training. This pre-post trial has been registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06810713). A single-group pre-post design was used. HCPs completed questionnaires before and after completing the 30-60 minute e-learning module. The surveys assessed self-efficacy and gender-responsive competencies in supporting males experiencing suicidal ideation. In addition, participants evaluated the e-learning using Likert-scale items. A total of 109 HCPs participated, of whom 75 completed the posttest. Results showed statistically significant improvements in both self-efficacy and gender-responsive competencies with moderate to large effect sizes of d = 0.55 and d = 1.98. Participants evaluated the module positively (M = 8.0/10), with good evaluations of its content and format. The psychoeducational model on gender socialization and suicidality, as well as the downloadable summary sheets, were well received. The e-learning module significantly improved HCPs' confidence and gender-responsive competencies in working with males experiencing suicidal ideation. Given its self-paced, freely accessible online format, the training appears feasible and acceptable. Further research is needed to examine its long-term impact, behavioral outcomes in clinical practice, and applicability to more diverse male populations.

items.title: Contribution of risk factors to racial/ethnic disparities in tuberculosis among US-born persons.
items.abstract: In the United States, tuberculosis (TB) incidence rates are substantially higher among racial/ethnic minorities compared with non-Hispanic White persons. However, few analyses have investigated the mechanisms driving these disparities. To assess the contribution of geographic factors and individual TB risk factors to racial/ethnic disparities in TB incidence among U.S.-born individuals. We analyzed TB case data for 2012-2019 from the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System, stratified by race/ethnicity, age, sex, and Public Use Microdata Area (PUMA). Age-sex standardized incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were calculated to quantify disparities across racial/ethnic groups. We decomposed these IRRs to quantify the contribution of differences within and between PUMAs to overall disparities. We also estimated the contributions of racial/ethnic differences in the prevalence of established TB risk factors-diagnosed diabetes, current smoking, HIV infection, and excess alcohol use-to TB disparities. Non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native and non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander persons had the highest TB incidence rates compared to non-Hispanic White persons (IRR: 15.3 (95% CI: 12.5, 18.6) and 18.1 (12.3, 26.2) respectively). Within-PUMA TB incidence differences accounted for most of the differences in incidence by race/ethnicity, representing 52-96% of total IRRs for each racial/ethnic population. Racial/ethnic differences in the prevalence of individual risk factors had minimal impact on total TB incidence disparities. Eliminating racial/ethnic disparities in TB will require more than addressing individual risk factors. Combatting structural or community-level determinants of TB, including treating infection to prevent disease, will be important for accelerating TB elimination.

items.title: Multiparametric ultrasound characterizes pediatric cystic fibrosis hepatobiliary involvement.
items.abstract: The contemporary European Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN)/North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) framework broadens the definition of cystic fibrosis hepatobiliary involvement (CFHBI), but the biological interpretation of individual multiparametric ultrasound parameters within this framework remains unclear. We evaluated the biological associations of shear wave elastography (SWE), shear wave dispersion (SWD), and attenuation imaging (ATI) with histopathological phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis (CF). In this ambispective cohort study, 119 children with CF underwent hepatobiliary assessment, including SWE, SWD, ATI, Doppler ultrasonography, clinical and laboratory evaluation. Histopathological assessment was performed when clinically indicated. CFHBI was classified according to the ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN framework, with the Debray criteria used as a secondary exploratory comparison. Exploratory phenotype-oriented analyses evaluated ultrasound parameters according to corresponding histopathological phenotypes. Exploratory phenotype-oriented analyses demonstrated significantly higher ATI values in histopathologically defined steatosis (p < 0.001), with good discriminatory performance (AUC 0.813) and an optimal threshold of 0.655 dB/cm/MHz. In contrast, SWE was not associated with histopathologically defined fibrosis (p = 0.151), whereas SWD showed no significant phenotype-specific associations. Secondary exploratory analyses demonstrated significant overall CFHBI discrimination by all three ultrasound parameters, with the highest AUC observed for SWD. The ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN and Debray classifications demonstrated significant disagreement (McNemar p < 0.001), with 22.7% of patients classified as Debray-negative but ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN-positive. Multiparametric ultrasound should be interpreted within the contemporary ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN CFHBI framework rather than as a single diagnostic tool for hepatobiliary involvement. The distinct biological associations of SWE, ATI, and SWD support a phenotype-oriented interpretation of individual ultrasound parameters, whereas overall CFHBI discrimination should be interpreted as a secondary exploratory finding requiring prospective multicenter validation.
