items.title: A Novel Extreme Weather Risk Insurance System for Kenya (NEWRISK): Encouraging preparedness, planning, community co-design, and protection of Kenya’s health system from the effects of extreme weather
items.abstract: Kenya is a frontline country for extreme weather and faces long droughts, flooding and heat waves. This study will focus on the broader, pervasive health risks associated with the reduction or catastrophic withdrawal of health services. Our aim is to determine what extreme weather hazards Kenya faces, and how resulting impacts on the population and health service can be mitigated, creating scalable tools that inform planning. This study will be carried out in four counties, selected to represent the different climatic regions of Kenya. We will conduct a mixed methods study drawing on qualitative participatory approaches, climate modelling, health facility surveys and health economic modelling. We will conduct a policy document review; non-participant observations of key county budgeting and planning events; in-depth interviews with health managers; and stakeholder dialogue workshops to co-create a framework for developing extreme weather mitigation plans. We will use the latest climate analysis techniques to provide high resolution data on heat and precipitation for the whole of Kenya. Drawing on secondary data, we will then create a population vulnerability index to spatially represent vulnerable populations. We will create a tool to assess the readiness of public health facilities across four counties. We will map this data to understand the interactions between extreme weather, population vulnerability, and the health system. We will present this information during community consultation and stakeholder workshops to get input and co-develop mitigation plans. Finally, we will use health economics methods to estimate the costs of doing nothing versus various protective strategies. We will create a set of tools and methods that can be combined to analyse the extreme weather threats posed to health systems or inform a climate risk insurance product. We expect to provide policymakers with practical approaches to protect their health systems and populations.

items.title: Cu-Doped Intercalation-Engineered 2D ZIF-8/alk-MXene Heterostructure: A High-Performance Synergistic Adsorbent for Efficient Tetracycline Removal from Wastewater
items.abstract: Abstract The safe disposal of high-concentration antibiotic wastewater from medical, livestock and aquaculture sectors is critical to ecological security and public health. Herein, a Cu-doped ZIF-8/alk-MXene heterostructure with a well-defined intercalation structure and ultrahigh adsorption capacity for tetracycline in aquaculture wastewater was rationally fabricated via in-situ growth and post-modification. This heterostructured material (Cu-ZIF-8/alk-MXene) was fabricated via in-situ growth of two-dimensional ZIF-8 nanosheets within the intercalated structure of alkalized MXene (alk-MXene) followed by Cu doping, which synergized the electron-metal-support interactions (EMSI) induced by Cu dopants and the inherent structural merits of alk-MXene. Impressively, the Cu-ZIF-8/alk-MXene adsorbent achieves a remarkably boosted TC adsorption capacity in wastewater through the synergy of electrostatic attraction, metal coordination and π-π interaction. The Pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir isotherm fitting further verify that the adsorption process is mainly controlled by chemical adsorption and follows a monolayer adsorption pattern. The composite delivers a Langmuir maximum TC adsorption capacity of 1631.1 mg·g -1 , with stable performance across pH 4-10 and initial TC concentrations of 10-200 mg·L -1 . It also shows excellent reusability: after five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, the adsorbent retains approximately 1283 mg·g -1 of TC uptake, corresponding to ~78.7% of its initial capacity, and exhibits strong anti-interference ability against coexisting ions in complex water matrices. DFT calculations further verify that the synergistic TC adsorption arises from the combined effects of metal coordination, electrostatic attraction and π-π interaction. This work demonstrates the great application potential of the as-designed heterostructure for practical tetracycline-contaminated water remediation.

items.title: knowledge–practice gap in junk food consumption among secondary school students in Nepal
items.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a period of increasing independence in food choices. During these years, dietary behaviour may be influenced by peers, media exposure, and the availability of different types of food. Junk food consumption among adolescents in Nepal has emerged as a public health concern due to its potential long-term effects on health. Frequent consumption of such foods may increase the risk of obesity and dental caries during adolescence and may also contribute to the development of chronic conditions such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease later in life. Studies in Nepal using the knowledge–attitude–practice approach have generally examined knowledge and dietary practices as separate aspects and have often assumed that greater knowledge results in healthier food choices. However, having knowledge about the health effects of junk food does not necessarily mean that students will avoid or reduce its consumption. This study therefore examined the level of knowledge and patterns of junk food consumption among secondary-level students in Pokhara. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was carried out among 290 students enrolled in grades 9 and 10 in six public schools in Pokhara Metropolitan City. Participants were selected through a multistage sampling procedure. Data were gathered using a pretested, self-administered questionnaire. Students’ knowledge of junk food was measured using 21 items for which objectively verifiable answers were available, with an overall reliability coefficient of KR-20 = 0.634. Knowledge levels were categorised using Bloom’s cut-off criteria. Practice was assessed mainly in terms of the number of times students consumed junk food during a typical week, with consumption three or more times per week considered frequent. In addition, a four-component index was developed to provide a broader assessment of dietary practices. Relationships between the study variables were examined using independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, chi-square tests with Cramér’s V, correlation analysis, and binary logistic regression. Results The mean knowledge score was 15.41 ± 2.99 out of 21, corresponding to 73.4% of the items answered correctly. Overall, 33.4% of students had high knowledge, 51.0% had moderate knowledge, and 15.5% had low knowledge. Most students correctly recognised common characteristics of junk food. However, fewer students were able to explain why processed junk food has a long shelf life (37.9%) or identify the nutrient that is generally lacking in such foods (42.4%). Junk food consumption was almost universal, with 97.2% of students reporting consumption, and 59.3% consuming it frequently. Taste was the most commonly reported reason for consumption (61.0%). Grocery stores were the main source of junk food (83.8%), while only 6.6% of students reported obtaining it from school canteens. Mother's education was the only socio-demographic factor significantly associated with knowledge (F = 3.387, p = 0.010). Daily pocket money was the only factor associated with frequent junk food consumption (χ² = 10.150, p = 0.017), indicating a threshold effect rather than a gradual increase in consumption with increasing pocket money. However, the results demonstrated that students with higher knowledge scores reported more frequent junk food consumption. The mean knowledge score was 13.12 among students who did not consume junk food and 16.01 among those who consumed it five or more times per week (F = 3.310, p = 0.021). After adjustment for other variables, knowledge remained the only independent predictor of frequent junk food consumption. For each one-standard-deviation increase in the knowledge score, the odds of frequent consumption increased by 35.9% (adjusted OR = 1.359, 95% CI: 1.057–1.746, p = 0.017). Conclusions Students at the secondary level in Pokhara demonstrated a generally good understanding of junk food; however, greater knowledge was not accompanied by lower consumption. Rather, students with higher knowledge scores reported consuming junk food more frequently. This finding suggests that knowledge about the health effects of junk food, by itself, may not be sufficient to bring about changes in adolescents’ dietary practices. Strategies aimed at reducing frequent junk food consumption should therefore address the wider factors that shape students’ food choices. The availability and affordability of these foods, their prices and portion sizes, exposure to food marketing, and the amount of pocket money available to students may all play a role in consumption patterns. Restricting or regulating the sale and availability of junk food in and around schools could also be considered as part of a broader intervention. Nutrition education should remain an important component of such efforts, but it could place greater emphasis on helping students understand food processing and acquire practical skills for reading and interpreting food labels.

items.title: Cross-border health care seeking among Somali nationals: a multi-country rapid evidence synthesis of determinants, outcome domains, economic burden and health-system implications, 2014–2026
items.abstract: Abstract Background Somali nationals travel abroad for care that the domestic health system cannot supply, yet the scale, clinical drivers, costs and outcomes of this movement have not been synthesised. We aimed to consolidate the available evidence on outbound medical travel from Somalia to India, Türkiye, Ethiopia and Egypt, to distinguish what is measured from what is not, and to draw implications for health financing and governance. Methods We conducted a rapid evidence synthesis of evidence from 2014 to 2026. Sources were Indian parliamentary and ministerial series, peer-reviewed studies, country-of-origin reports, health-financing documents and consular guidance. Synthesis was narrative because heterogeneity precluded pooling. Every statement was assigned to one of three evidence tiers: directly measured, credibly inferred or unquantifiable. Movement indicators count episodes, not unique patients, and expenditure envelopes are planning scenarios, not accounts. Results India is the only corridor with a nationality-specific public series: 13,585 medical-purpose arrivals in 2015–2017 and 47,880 medical visas in 2019–2024 (2018 unavailable), a minimum of 61,465 episodes. Medical visas peaked at 16,411 in 2023, 4.8 times the 2019 level, and fell to 12,261 in 2024. Türkiye offers a single anchor (2,742 Somali patients in 2019); Ethiopia and Egypt lack nationality-specific series. Demand concentrates in oncology, cardiovascular and renal disease, advanced diagnostics, reproductive medicine and orthopaedics. A snowball survey of 106 medical travellers in Garowe reported a mean direct cost of US$8,543 per episode. Out-of-pocket payments met 30.8% of current health expenditure in 2023. Applying published per-patient benchmarks to Indian visas gives US$88–105 million for 2024; a four-corridor central scenario gives approximately US$219 million, about 1.8% of projected gross domestic product. No pooled morbidity, complication or mortality rate can be derived, because outbound episodes are not linked to treatment or outcome. Conclusions Outbound travel functions as an unregulated, privately financed parallel tertiary-care system that is substantial in scale, financially consequential and largely unmeasured in outcome. We propose a minimum outbound-referral dataset, pooled catastrophic-illness protection linked to authorised referral, facilitator licensing, bilateral referral compacts and sequenced domestic investment in oncology diagnostics, chemotherapy, dialysis and imaging.

items.title: Narrative Inquiry on the Innovation Journeys of Biomedical and Health Technology Startup Founders in the Philippines
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Research on biomedical and health technology startups in the Philippines has documented regulatory, financial, and market barriers, but little is known about how founders themselves experience, interpret, and manage the journey from ideation to commercialization. This study examines how biomedical and health technology startup founders narrate that journey in the Philippines, a resource-constrained, lower-middle-income country. Methodology: Guided by a constructivist-interpretivist paradigm, the study used narrative inquiry with eight purposively selected founders representing medical devices, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, and digital health. The study conducted semi-structured narrative interviews, re-storied them into individual narrative profiles, member-checked them, manually coded them, and compared them through cross-narrative synthesis, retaining negative cases. Findings: The journeys were organized around five non-linear narrative thresholds: arrival or entry; building and validation under constraint; regulatory qualification; procurement and adoption; and relational reconfiguration with the systemic environment as well as, resilience and identity reconstruction. Entry was relational and often serendipitous. A problem-led orientation and commitment to identifiable beneficiaries sustained the founders. Founders validated functioning technologies through improvisation and resource combination. Regulatory qualification varied by product and venture. Founders sought clear product categorization, proportionate requirements, and predictable timelines rather than deregulation. The sharpest divergence occurred after validation, when procurement and institutional adoption enabled movement or produced delays, redirection, withdrawal, or re-entry. Financing and adoption were mutually constraining. Resilience and narrative identity formed an adaptive architecture. Resilience was characterized as individualized, team-distributed, or organizational, while identity was reconstructed in sequential, layered accumulation or continuity deepening modes. Implications: The study qualifies effectuation, resilience, narrative identity, and diffusion of innovations for resource-constrained biomedical settings. For policy, it points to aligning development funding with public procurement, proportionate regulatory pathways, pre-revenue financing, simplified administrative processes, and entrepreneurial capability building. Originality/Value: This is among the first founder-centered narrative studies of biomedical and health technology commercialization in the Philippines. It shows that the decisive challenge is not invention itself but moving viable technologies into institutional adoption and sustained public benefit. JEL codes: L26, O31, O32, I11, I18, O53.

items.title: Job satisfaction and self-efficacy as mediators of organizational support and job competency: a cross- sectional study among Shanghai community health personnel
items.abstract: Abstract Background Job competency among public health personnel is essential for delivering quality community health services. This study examined the relationships among job competency, perceived organizational support, job satisfaction, and self-efficacy among public health personnel in Shanghai. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 3,809 public health personnel from 249 community health service centers across 16 districts in Shanghai. Multiple linear regression examined demographic differences in job competency. Spearman correlation analysis assessed relationships among the four core variables. A multiple mediation model was tested using structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Harman’s single-factor test assessed common method bias. Results Job competency was associated with gender, marital status, professional title, number of professional training sessions, regular exercise, and sleep. The final mediation model showed good fit (χ² = 5.383, df = 2, p = 0.068, CFI = 0.999, TLI = 0.998, NFI = 0.999, RMSEA = 0.021, SRMR = 0.007). The total indirect effect from perceived organizational support to job competency was 0.747 (95% CI [0.662, 0.834]). The indirect effect via job satisfaction was 0.426 (95% CI [0.350, 0.511]), and the sequential indirect effect via job satisfaction and self-efficacy was 0.320 (95% CI [0.270, 0.372]). Common method bias was not a serious concern. Conclusions Perceived organizational support was associated with job competency through job satisfaction and sequentially via self-efficacy. Community health service centers should strengthen organizational support, monitor job satisfaction, and provide self-efficacy training to improve workforce competency and public health service delivery.

items.title: Factors Associated with Zero-Dose Status Among Children Aged 12–23 Months in the Mobayi-Mbongo Health Zone, North Ubangi Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, from January to December 2024: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Zero-dose children—those who have not received any dose of the first dose of pentavalent vaccine (Penta1), remain a major public health concern in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Understanding the determinants of zero-dose status is essential for improving immunization coverage and reducing vaccine-preventable diseases. Methods An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2024. A three-stage cluster sampling technique was used to select 203 children aged 12–23 months across six health areas. Data were collected through structured electronic questionnaires (KoboCollect), direct observation, and vaccination card review. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25, with bivariate and multivariate logistic regression to identify associated factors. Results The prevalence of zero-dose children was 28.6% when combining vaccination card data and maternal declarations. Multivariate analysis revealed that Central African nationality of mothers/caregivers (AOR = 5.9; 95% CI : 3.01–11.58), lack of knowledge of vaccine-preventable diseases (AOR = 16.09; 95% CI : 3.35–77.29), young maternal age ( 5 km (AOR = 4.22; 95% CI : 2.21–8.05) were significantly associated with zero-dose status. Conclusion Zero-dose prevalence remains high in the Mobayi-Mbongo Health Zone, driven by sociodemographic, knowledge-related, and geographic barriers. Targeted interventions focusing on refugee populations, health education, improved geographic accessibility, and support for young mothers are urgently needed to reduce inequities in immunization coverage.

items.title: Category learning drives cortical attentional gain to diagnostic dimensions of perceptual information
items.abstract: Humans and other animals develop remarkable perceptual and cognitive specializations for identifying, differentiating, and acting on classes of ecologically important signals. This expertise is flexible enough to support diverse perceptual judgments: a voice, for example, simultaneously conveys what a talker says, as well as myriad cues about her identity and state. Expert perception across complex signals thus involves discovering and learning regularities that best inform diverse perceptual judgments, as well as weighting this information flexibly as task demands change. Here, we test whether this process may involve attentional gain. We use two prospective auditory category learning tasks to relate a complex, entirely novel soundscape to four classes of ‘alien identity’ and two classes of ‘alien size.’ Identity, but not size, categorization requires discovery and learning of patterned acoustic input situated in one of two simultaneous, non-overlapping frequency bands. This allows us to capitalize on the coarsely segregated, frequency-band-specific channels tiling auditory cortex. We use fMRI to ask whether category-relevant perceptual information present in one frequency band is prioritized relative to simultaneous, uninformative information in the other frequency band. Only among participants expert at alien identity categorization do we observe neural prioritization of the identity-diagnostic frequency band. This prioritization persists even when the diagnostic information becomes irrelevant in the size categorization task. Tellingly, the neural selectivity evoked implicitly in the identity categorization task aligns with that in an independent task, where activation is driven by explicit and sustained selective attention to pure tones in one or the other frequency band. Additionally, the learning trajectories taken to achieve expert-level categorization leave fingerprints on the patterns of neural activity associated with the diagnostic dimension. In all, this indicates that learning categories can drive attentional gain to category-diagnostic input dimensions.

items.title: A Survey on LLMs from a Human-Centric Perspective
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) has positioned them as powerful computational instruments for human-centered research and applications, spanning tasks involving cognition, decision-making, and social interaction. This survey examines LLMs from a human-centric perspective organized around individual and collective levels. We first review LLM competencies across perception, analysis, integration, execution, and social interaction, highlighting both their demonstrated capabilities and the evaluation conditions under which these capabilities are observed. We then explore how LLMs are used across behavioral science, psychology, linguistics, political science, economics, and sociology as research tools, behavioral simulators, and objects of inquiry, covering both individual behavior and collective social processes. Finally, we identify challenges and future research directions, such as improving LLM adaptability, affective-to-behavior evaluation, and cultural sensitivity, while addressing inherent biases and enhancing frameworks for human-AI collaboration. This survey aims to provide a foundational understanding of LLMs from a human-centric perspective, offering insights into their current capabilities and potential for future development.

items.title: Cognitive and physiological responses to prolonged video viewing: Activities of the autonomic nervous system and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis in relation to video interest
items.abstract: In recent years, online lectures and conferences have become widespread, but prolonged video viewing has been suggested to affect psychological state and physiological regulation. However, few studies have objectively examined how such viewing influences autonomic and endocrine activity. This study aimed to evaluate changes in autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity during the viewing of high- and low-interest videos. Twenty-six university students (10 males, 16 females; aged 21–24 years) watched high-interest (comedy) and low-interest (lecture) videos (90 minutes each). After viewing each video, they recorded subjective ratings of concentration, comprehension, interest, and fatigue. To assess autonomic nervous system activity, heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) analyses, including the low-frequency (LF)/high-frequency (HF) ratio (LF/HF), LF and HF power, and very low-frequency (VLF) power, were performed. As stress markers, saliva samples were collected before, during, and after video viewing to measure cortisol, amylase, and chromogranin A (CgA). Subjective ratings showed that scores for concentration, comprehension, and interest were significantly higher, and fatigue was lower during the high-interest video. Regarding physiological indicators, significant main effects of time were observed for heart rate, LF/HF, LF, HF, and VLF, with overall patterns of lower heart rate and LF/HF and higher LF, HF, and VLF power during viewing. Salivary cortisol also decreased over time during both videos, demonstrating a significant main effect of time. However, no significant changes were observed in salivary amylase or chromogranin A. Furthermore, a significant interest × time interaction was observed for HR, but not for the other physiological indicators. A significant main effect of interest was observed only for LF. These findings indicate that the video conditions differed in subjective cognitive evaluation, with condition-dependent temporal changes detected for HR, whereas no significant interest × time interactions were detected for the other physiological indicators.

items.title: Individual differences in sequential decision-making
items.abstract: People differ widely in how they make decisions in uncertain environments. While many studies leverage this variability to measure differences in specific cognitive processes and parameters, the key dimension(s) of individual variability in uncertain decision-making tasks has not been identified. Here, we analyzed behavioral data from 1001 participants performing a restless three-armed bandit task, where reward probabilities fluctuated unpredictably over time. Using a novel analytical approach that controlled for the stochasticity in this tasks, we identified a dominant nonlinear axis of individual variability. We found that this primary axis of variability was strongly and selectively correlated with the probability of exploration, as inferred by latent state modeling. This suggests that the major factor shaping individual differences in bandit task performance is the tendency to explore (versus exploit), rather than personality characteristics, reinforcement learning model parameters, or low-level strategies. Certain demographic characteristics also predicted variance along this principle axis: participants at the exploratory end tended to be younger than participants at the exploitative end, and self-identified men were overrepresented at both extremes. Together, these findings offer a principled framework for understanding individual differences in task behavior while highlighting the cognitive and demographic factors that shape individual differences in decision-making under uncertainty.

items.title: Development and validation of a scale assessing perceived trustworthiness in large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly part of everyday life, yet there is no established way to measure how users evaluate their trustworthiness. This study introduces the Perceived Trustworthiness of LLMs scale (PT-LLM-8), a self-report psychometric instrument measuring users’ perceived trustworthiness of their primary LLM. PT-LLM-8 is developed from the TrustLLM framework and adapted as a human-centred measure. The PT-LLM-8 comprises eight items representing truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, transparency, accountability, and compliance with laws. Psychometric properties of the scale were tested with 752 LLM users in the United Kingdom (Mean age = 28.58, SD = 6.11, 50.3% males, 48.8% females). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a one-factor structure, with high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.90, Composite Reliability = 0.91, strong item-total correlations (ranged between 0.62 and 0.75), and measurement invariance across gender. The total score measures overall perceived trustworthiness, while individual item responses may also be examined descriptively for information about the content represented by each item. For researchers, practitioners, and developers, the PT-LLM-8 offers a practical instrument for evaluating interventions, comparing groups and contexts, and examining whether technical safeguards are reflected in users’ perceived trustworthiness of LLM. The scale can also be applied to guide system design, support policy development, and help organisations monitor shifts in user trust toward LLMs over time, making it applicable across research, practice, and governance.

items.title: Not one size fits all: model-specific effects of reasoning on emotion recognition from body-gesture videos
items.abstract: Background The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in mental-health contexts underscores the need to evaluate its emotion-recognition capacity. Objective This study examined whether a reasoning-oriented model or structured Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improved recognition of emotions conveyed through bodily gestures. Methods Four Gemini models were evaluated using 36 silent videos depicting 18 emotions. Each model completed 20 trials per video under Zero-Shot and CoT prompting, yielding 5,760 responses. Population-averaged generalized estimating equation models compared accuracy across models, prompts, emotional groups, and the human benchmark. Results Gemini 2.0 Pro showed higher accuracy than the other models following multiplicity adjustment, whereas Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking did not outperform the general-purpose models. The marginal CoT-versus-Zero-Shot contrast was not statistically significant. However, the Model × Prompt Type interaction was significant. Accuracy was higher under the tested CoT condition than under Zero-Shot prompting for Gemini 2.0 Pro and lower under the tested CoT condition for Gemini 2.0 Flash. The Model × Prompt Type × Emotional Group interaction was not significant. The Performer × Emotional Group interaction was significant, although within-model differences between positive and negative emotions did not survive adjustment. Three models showed lower accuracy than humans for negative emotions, whereas no significant model–human differences were found for positive emotions. Conclusion The data did not support a general improvement in emotion recognition under CoT prompting. Prompt-condition differences varied across models. This pattern underscores the need to evaluate reasoning prompts for specific models and tasks before application in mental-health contexts.

items.title: "Tab, Tab, Bug": Security Pitfalls of Next Edit Suggestions in AI-Integrated IDEs
items.abstract: Modern AI-integrated IDEs are shifting from passive code completion to proactive Next Edit Suggestions (NES). Unlike traditional autocompletion, NES is designed to construct a richer context from both recent user interactions and the broader codebase to suggest multi-line, cross-line, or even cross-file modifications. This evolution significantly streamlines the programming workflow into a tab-by-tab interaction and enhances developer productivity. Consequently, NES introduces a more complex context retrieval mechanism and sophisticated interaction patterns. However, existing studies focus almost exclusively on the security implications of standalone LLM-based code generation, ignoring the potential attack vectors posed by NES in modern AI-integrated IDEs. The underlying mechanisms of NES remain under-explored, and their security implications are not yet fully understood. In this paper, we conduct the first systematic security study of NES systems. First, we perform an in-depth dissection of the NES mechanisms to understand the newly introduced threat vectors. It is found that NES retrieves a significantly expanded context, including inputs from imperceptible user actions and global codebase retrieval, which increases the attack surfaces. Second, we conduct a comprehensive in-lab study to evaluate the security implications of NES. The evaluation results reveal that NES is susceptible to context poisoning and is sensitive to transactional edits and human-IDE interactions. Third, we perform a large-scale online survey involving over 200 professional developers to assess the perceptions of NES security risks in real-world development workflows. The survey results indicate a general lack of awareness regarding the potential security pitfalls associated with NES, highlighting the need for increased education and improved security countermeasures in AI-integrated IDEs.

items.title: Integrating psychosocial factors with geospatial analytics to assess community climate resilience
items.abstract: Abstract Conventional climate adaptation strategies emphasize infrastructure, hazard modelling, and ecosystem management while underestimating psychological processes that shape how communities perceive and respond to climatic risks. Cognitive appraisal, emotional attachment, and behavioural engagement fundamentally influence preparedness, adaptation, and recovery. This study introduces GeoPsyche Futures , an interdisciplinary framework that integrates psychological indicators with geospatial analytics to map community resilience in a holistic, human-centered way. A cross-sectional study among 648 residents in a flood-prone coastal neighbourhood of Visakhapatnam, India, combined validated psychosocial measures with participatory GIS mapping, exploratory factor analysis, spatial autocorrelation, and OLS/GWR modelling. Three resilience dimensions—cognitive, emotional, and behavioural—explained 83.2% of the variance (KMO = 0.84). Spatial patterns (Moran’s I = 0.36, p < 0.01) revealed clustered resilience dynamics, and regression analyses demonstrated that emotional and behavioural factors were stronger predictors of preparedness behaviours (R² = 0.64) than cognitive variables. The GeoPsyche Resilience Index (GPRI) further illuminated stratified resilience zones. These findings highlight the urgent need to integrate psychological insights into climate adaptation planning and contribute directly to SDGs 3, 11, and 13.

items.title: Investigating designers’ perceptions of thermal comfort: a Q-methodology study in residential design
items.abstract: Abstract This study employs a robust mixed methods approach—anchored in Q-methodology and semi-structured interviews—to explore how architects in Ilam, Iran, conceptualize thermal comfort as both technical and cultural discourse. A concourse of 78 statements, refined to 43, was sorted by 20 senior designers. Factor analysis using PQMethod revealed four distinct perception types: (1) passive climate responsiveness, (2) reliance on smart HVAC systems, (3) prioritization of insulation materials, and (4) management of natural light and solar exposure. These viewpoints highlight methodological hybridity, combining subjective discourse with analytical rigor, and reveal how cultural and professional logics shape design priorities. Findings indicate that thermal comfort is a cultural and cognitive construct, shaped by professional judgment, local climate, and social expectations. Q-methodology integrates qualitative interpretation with quantitative categorization to reveal subjective viewpoints with analytical rigor. By situating comfort within cultural and cognitive frameworks, this study demonstrates how Q-methodology enriches sustainability research, guiding climate-responsive design and fostering critical dialogue on energy efficiency and occupant well-being.

items.title: Navigating young-onset dementia caregiving: a qualitative study of unmet needs, support, and resilience
items.abstract: Abstract Aim To explore the unmet needs, support experiences, and resilience strategies of informal caregivers of persons with young-onset dementia (YOD) in Singapore. Background YOD is defined by symptom onset before 65 years of age and presents caregiving challenges distinct from later-onset dementia. Despite these distinct challenges, evidence on the experiences and support needs of young-onset dementia caregivers in Singapore remains limited. Design: A descriptive qualitative study. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 11 informal caregivers of persons with YOD recruited through a neurocognitive service in Singapore between October and December 2024. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Caregivers described YOD caregiving as emotionally and physically demanding, socially isolating, and financially disruptive. Their experiences were shaped by limited access to age-appropriate services, poor visibility of resources, and stigma surrounding dementia in younger persons. While caregivers drew on resilience strategies including self-care, meaning-making, humour, faith, and support from family, peers, and community networks, these efforts were insufficient. Overall, the findings highlight a mismatch between the complex realities of YOD caregiving and the services currently available to support caregivers. Conclusion Although caregivers demonstrated resilience and adaptive coping, YOD caregiving in Singapore remained constrained by limited access to visible, tailored, and age-appropriate support. More coordinated support is needed to address caregivers’ life-stage, psychosocial, and practical needs. Impact: This study extends understanding of YOD caregiving in an underexamined Asian context and highlights the need for healthcare and community services that better address caregivers’ needs. The findings can inform the development of more responsive models of caregiver support and future intervention research. items.title: Designing Critical Human–AI Learning in Higher Education: The SC-AIM–FAVIC Framework for Analytical and Logical Reasoning
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now routine in university study, yet unstructured use risks cognitive offloading, surface learning, and uncritical acceptance of fluent but unreliable output. This article aimed to develop and specify the Symbiotic Critical Human–AI Learning Model (SC-AIM), operationalised through the five-stage FAVIC framework (Formulation, Augmentation, Verification, Integration, Creation), and to set out the assessment instruments and evaluation design that accompany it. Following the Analysis and Design phases of the ADDIE research-and-development approach, we synthesised recent experimental, meta-analytic, and survey evidence to derive design requirements, translated them into a stage-by-stage instructional specification, built a process-sensitive assessment rubric, and defined a quasi-experimental and qualitative validation plan for Indonesian higher education. The results are the model and its components: an evidence-to-design mapping, the FAVIC stage specification, a three-level process-sensitive rubric, and an evaluation design with hypotheses. Conclusion: SC-AIM offers lecturers a concrete, theory-grounded sequence that places human reasoning before and after AI assistance and makes verification an assessed activity, giving higher education a ready-to-use pedagogical model for developing analytical and logical reasoning in the age of generative AI.

items.title: African lungfish secrete a complex living cocoon during prolonged periods of suspended animation in the laboratory
items.abstract: Abstract One of the most exceptional adaptations to extreme drought is found in the sister group to tetrapods, the lungfishes (Dipnoi), which can aestivate inside a mucus cocoon for multiple years at reduced metabolic rates with complete cessation of ingestion and excretion. However, the function of the cocoon tissue is not fully understood. Here we describe a new more natural laboratory protocol for inducing aestivation in the West African lungfish, Protopterus annectens , and investigate the structure and function of the cocoon. We used electron microscopy and imaging to discover that the inner and outer layers of the paper-thin cocoon are composed primarily of living cells. We report for the first time that living cells are found on the outside of the cocoon, confirming a living shell surrounds the lungfish during aestivation, and a novel honeycomb pattern of nuclei organization within the cocoon. However, we also repeatedly observed extensive bacterial and fungal growth covering the cocoon. We completed successful aestivation trials for up to one year in the laboratory, confirming a robust laboratory protocol for investigating suspended animation in vertebrates.

items.title: Spatial ecology, relative abundance and threats to the Indian pangolin (Manis crassicaudata) in Abbottabad District, Lesser Himalayas
items.abstract: Abstract The Indian pangolin ( Manis crassicaudata ) is an endangered and poorly studied mammal in Pakistan, where limited ecological information constrains effective conservation planning. This study assessed its spatial distribution, relative abundance, habitat characteristics, and anthropogenic pressures in Abbottabad District, Lesser Himalayas, Pakistan, from October 2024 to September 2025. A stratified, spatially explicit sampling framework comprised 30 intensively surveyed 2 × 2 km raster sampling units (RSUs), representing approximately 120 km² of landscape across four tehsils. Three 1-km belt transects were surveyed per RSU, providing 90 transects and 90 transect-km of standardized effort. Active living burrows were used as indirect indicators of current occurrence and relative abundance rather than individual population density. In total, 91 burrows were recorded, comprising 9 active living, 55 feeding, and 27 inactive burrows. The active burrows yielded a relative abundance index of 0.075 active burrows km⁻² of represented landscape and an encounter rate of 1.00 active burrows per 10 transect-km. Active burrows occurred between 700 and 1,361 m, primarily in low- to moderate-elevation scrub, agricultural-edge, and forest-transition habitats. Inactive and feeding burrows differed significantly in elevation, canopy cover, undergrowth density, distance to water, and burrow dimensions ( p < 0.05). Field observations and community information identified illegal hunting, habitat modification, agricultural expansion, domestic-dog interactions, and road mortality as conservation pressures. These findings establish a district-level ecological baseline for M. crassicaudata and support standardized long-term monitoring, targeted habitat management, threat mitigation, and community-based conservation.

items.title: Prediction of ephemeral plant diversity patterns and identification of conservation priority areas in the Gurbantunggut Desert
items.abstract: Abstract Background Ephemeral plants are a key functional group in the Gurbantunggut Desert, contributing to windbreak, sand fixation, and biodiversity maintenance, while being highly sensitive to climate change. Understanding their spatial diversity patterns can reveal desert ecosystem adaptation mechanisms and inform conservation planning. This study examined 35 dominant ephemeral plant species in the Gurbantunggut Desert, Xinjiang. Using species occurrence data and 12 environmental variables, an ensemble species distribution model was applied to simulate spatial patterns of species richness and migration under current and future (2050s) climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5). Climate velocity was calculated using the KNN algorithm. The Zonation model, integrating species richness, species loss, and climate velocity, was used to identify and optimize priority conservation areas. Results This study show that: (1) species richness declines under all scenarios toward the 2050s, with greater losses under higher emission pathways; the central southern margin consistently remains a biodiversity hotspot. (2) Climate velocity of temperature variables is higher in eastern and western regions, while precipitation variables show higher values in the east; overall, precipitation velocity exceeds temperature velocity. (3) Current conservation areas (2.103 × 10⁴ km²) are mainly in southern, western, and eastern regions. By the 2050s, conservation areas shrink (≈ 1.48–1.58 × 10⁴ km²) and shift, with higher-priority areas increasingly concentrated in the central southern margin and western desert under higher emission scenarios. Conclusion Future climate change will reduce ephemeral plant diversity and shift priority conservation areas, highlighting the need to protect the central southern margin and western desert.

items.title: Soil and host-tree associations with Tuber aestivum's ITS abundance in productive Istrian oak forests
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding the ecological drivers of Tuber aestivum productivity in natural oak forests remains limited despite the species’ broad ecological niche and rising economic value. We characterised 65 productive plots of T. aestivum associated with Quercus pubescens and Q. cerris in forest stands of the Istrian peninsula, Croatia. At each plot, we applied a paired sampling design consisting of two systematically collected soil samples: one taken beneath the harvested ascocarp and the other taken 5 m outside the visible brûlé or tree crown area, yielding a total of 130 samples. We quantified soil physical–chemical properties (pH and texture), macronutrients (C, Ca, K, N and P), and mycelial abundance by qPCR (ITS2 copies g⁻¹ soil). Across the study area, a positive relationship between clay content and mycelial abundance emerged as the most consistent, highlighting the importance of soil water retention in T. aestivum mycelial development. In contrast, higher N levels and imbalanced K: Ca ratios were associated with lower mycelial abundance, particularly in Q. pubescens stands, whereas P showed a marginal, host‑dependent positive trend detectable only in Q. pubescens . Trends of increasing and decreasing median pH and nutrient values were detected between paired samples, with these patterns differing between host tree species. Altogether, our results indicate that T. aestivum mycelial development is promoted by clay-rich soils in oak forests and demonstrate the value of paired sampling for disentangling host- and soil‑driven processes in wild T. aestivum ecosystems.

items.title: A climate-driven environmental sustainability indicator for assessing future Phlebotomus expansion risk in semi-arid Iran
items.abstract: Climate change can redistribute environmentally suitable conditions for Phlebotomus vectors in semi-arid regions, but conventional habitat-suitability models provide limited information on the broader environmental dimensions of future expansion. This study developed a Climate-Driven Environmental Sustainability Indicator (ESI) to assess spatial patterns of future Phlebotomus expansion risk in semi-arid Iran. We analyzed 312 spatially filtered occurrence records and environmental predictors using MaxEnt. Future suitability was projected for 2041–2060 under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 using an ensemble of five CMIP6 climate models. The ESI integrated habitat suitability, climate exposure, habitat expansion potential, and environmental vulnerability. Model performance, spatial validation, inter-model variability, and predictor sensitivity were assessed. The model showed strong predictive performance (mean test AUC: 0.942 ± 0.018). Mean Temperature of the Driest Quarter was the largest relative contributor (38.4%). Suitable habitat increased by 25,400 km 2 under SSP2-4.5 and 51,200 km 2 under SSP5-8.5, with northward and elevational shifts. High-to-Very-High ESI areas increased from 20.7% at baseline to 28.0% and 38.9%, respectively. Expansion was concentrated mainly in northern and transitional environments, whereas contraction occurred in hyper-arid southern areas. The ESI provides a transparent framework for translating climate-driven suitability changes into multidimensional environmental expansion-risk assessment while incorporating uncertainty. It does not represent disease transmission probability.

items.title: Vertical distribution, optical characterization and automated classification of airborne pollen from in situ measurements
items.abstract: Bioaerosols, such as pollen grains, play an important role in air quality, human health and atmospheric processes. However, their vertical distribution within the boundary layer remains insufficiently researched. In this study, we investigate the vertical profiles of pollen concentrations between 4–272 ma.g.l. at the Vehmasmäki station in Eastern Finland. In situ measurements with optical pollen sensors at 4, 115, and 272 m were conducted simultaneously with ground-based observations from a Hirst–type volumetric air sampler and a Cloud Droplet Analyzer. Multiple campaigns were conducted during pollen seasons between 2021–2024, focusing on the dominant pollen types, i.e. birch and pine pollen. The three optical pollen sensors showed strong agreement during the intercomparison period ( R 2 ≥0.91), demonstrating good consistency among the instruments. The Cloud Droplet Analyzer measurements in the 20–100 µm size range showed that pollen dominated the measured concentrations of coarse particles during the intensive pollen periods. Polarization scatter plots for birch and pine pollen revealed distinct optical signatures, during predefined intensive pollen periods between 2021–2023, consistent with laboratory results. Furthermore, we assess how background fine-mode aerosol influences these signatures. During a major birch pollen episode in May 2024, pollen concentrations decreased with height. These vertical profiles were compared with predictions from the System for Integrated modeLling of Atmospheric coMposition (SILAM), which reproduced the vertical distribution from the observations, but systematically overestimated pollen concentrations at all heights. Moreover, a machine–learning classification approach combining optical pollen sensor measurements and meteorological variables demonstrated the possibility of identification of dominant pollen types. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of optical pollen sensors for continuous, real–time monitoring of dominant pollen taxa in boreal regions, from measurements in Vehmasmäki.

items.title: Fishers’ local ecological knowledge recovers information about the recent-past existence of a Caribbean coastal shark and ray nursery area
items.abstract: Abstract Elasmobranchs have declined sharply due to overfishing and habitat destruction. Nursery-areas are crucial for the recruitment and sustainability of elasmobranch populations; however, they have been scarcely studied globally and in Mexico. We used fishers’ Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) to investigate whether Bahía de la Ascensión was an elasmobranch nursery-area 30 + years-ago, and for which species. Shark nursery-areas are defined by three criteria that we evaluated using semi-structured interviews covering 90% of the target population (local fishers aged 40+). Several elasmobranchs met all criteria, supporting that this bay served as a communal elasmobranch nursery-area 30 + years-ago for Carcharhinus leucas , C. limbatus, Ginglymostoma cirratum , Negaprion brevirostris, Hypanus americanus and Styracura schmardae. Additionally, fishers reported changes in early-offspring elasmobranch abundance –including declines and increases– between our study-period and the present. This is the first study showing that LEK can be used to reconstruct the former existence of elasmobranch nursery-areas, highlighting its value to rescue past information in data-poor contexts, in support of conservation. This approach can and should be widely-applied for similar purposes. Our study is part of a trans-disciplinary project examining past-and-present elasmobranch nurseries in the Mexican Caribbean, providing a baseline to evaluate changes while preventing misinterpretation based solely on present-day data.

items.title: Automated Identification of Parasitoid Wasps for Biological Control Monitoring Using an Optimized Single-Stage Detector
items.abstract: Parasitoid wasps are important biological control agents, but their small size and subtle morphological differences hinder rapid identification and require taxonomic expertise. This study developed a computer vision framework for recognizing parasitoid wasps from single-plane microscopy images. A dataset of 3420 images representing 36 parasitoid taxa and 38 terminal biological classes was assembled. Five YOLO detector generations and six CNN- and ViT-based classifiers were evaluated across three dataset sizes. YOLO11m was selected for further optimization. The optimized model integrated multiscale feature processing, attention mechanisms, a modified bounding-box regression loss, and tuned training settings. On an independent set, the baseline YOLO11m achieved an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.867 at 640 × 640 pixels. At 960 × 960 pixels under untuned settings, YOLO11m and YOLO11m-opt achieved 0.873 and 0.917, respectively. After applying the selected training configuration, YOLO11m-opt achieved a precision of 0.985, recall of 0.989, mAP@0.5 of 0.995, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.933 across all 105 detection labels. Eigen-CAM visualizations showed spatial feature activations overlapping with potentially informative morphological structures. A Windows application supported batch analysis, offering a basis for computer-assisted specimen screening under laboratory conditions.

items.title: Reef resilience and demise on the NW shelf of Australia during the warm Miocene
items.abstract: Abstract During the Miocene, sea surface temperature (SSTs) and CO 2 exceeded modern levels. Given the current decline of coral reefs due to rising summer temperatures, it is unclear how extensive reef systems developed and thrived in a warm Miocene world. This problem is exacerbated by a lack of SST reconstructions. Here, we use TEX 86 H to reconstruct summer SSTs between 5.0 and 17.4 Ma from a sediment core (IODP Site U1464) within the Miocene NW Australian shelf Barrier Reef system. During the Miocene Climate Optimum, summer SSTs reached up to 34 °C. However, stable arid conditions and low subsidence rates allowed the reef to expand. Around 6 Ma, SSTs were ideal for coral reef growth, but increased terrestrial input and subsidence caused the relatively rapid collapse of almost all reefs. Multiple environmental stressors culminated in reef drowning. Therefore, a barrier reef system formed at > 30 °C SSTs, but this was only possible under otherwise ideal conditions.

items.title: Is the professionalization of forest management cooperatives the solution to all the problems? A qualitative SWOT analysis in Bavaria
items.abstract: Forest management cooperatives (FMCs) are key intermediaries in consolidating small, fragmented private forest holdings and implementing forest policy. Building on an earlier study of their professionalization, this study examines the strategic self-perception of Bavarian FMCs through a qualitative SWOT analysis. It draws on a full survey of all state-recognized FMCs in Bavaria conducted in 2016 ( N = 136; 63% response rate), in which managing directors and honorary board members were asked to complete the questionnaire jointly. Responses on strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats were coded through qualitative content analysis, assigned to internal factors (resources, competencies, structures, processes) and external dimensions (political-institutional, economic, ecological, social), and combined within each case into SO, ST, WO, and WT configurations. Key strengths are qualified staff, efficient operations, and strong regional roots. Weaknesses include staffing shortages, limited process and logistics capacities, financial insecurity, and a heterogeneous ownership and membership structure. Opportunities arise above all from structural change in ownership and changing service needs, followed by the energy transition and institutional networking. Risks stem above all from competition and market volatility, followed by regulatory pressure, including nature conservation requirements, possible funding cuts, and climate hazards. The WT configurations point to clusters of vulnerability where external stressors coincide with internal capacity limits. The findings are consistent with the proposition that professionalization is necessary but not sufficient for the future viability of FMCs. Organizational development needs to be combined with reliable institutional frameworks and with forest policy that targets transaction-cost reduction and capacity building.

items.title: The evolution of the marine ’nitrostat’ across the Great Oxidation Event
items.abstract: The bioavailability of nitrogen and phosphorus is tightly coupled in the modern ocean, a concept known as the ’nitrostat’. Phosphorus is considered the ultimate limiting nutrient on geological timescales, while nitrogen supply is biologically modulated via nitrogen fixation and denitrification. This balance maintains relatively constant N:P ratios in seawater. However, the strong redox dependence of both N and P cycling, as well as the dependence on specific enzymes, suggest that the balance of the marine ‘nitrostat’ may have evolved over Earth’s history in response to oxygenation and biological innovation. Here, we review what is known about N and P biogeochemistry across the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and discuss cause-effect relationships between the evolving N:P balance and primary production. A key remaining uncertainty is when exactly life transitioned from energy- to nutrient-limitation. However, it is likely that a marine ‘nitrostat’ was established at least locally or temporarily from the Neoarchean onwards. This implies increasing biological control over water chemistry, which may in turn have contributed to stabilizing O 2 -producing ecosystems and thus acted as a positive feedback for the GOE.

items.title: Experimental addition of branch and stone piles increases reptile abundance in agricultural landscapes
items.abstract: Agricultural intensification has reduced farmland habitat heterogeneity, contributing to biodiversity decline. Small structural elements such as stone and branch piles are widely recommended to mitigate this loss, yet their effectiveness for promoting biodiversity in high-intensity farmland has not been tested experimentally. We evaluated the effects of adding small structures along agricultural field margins on reptile abundance across 14 regions of the Swiss Plateau. Using a replicated randomized block design, we applied two experimental treatments (branch and stone piles) and compared them with untreated control sites. Reptiles were surveyed repeatedly using two complementary methods and analysed within a hierarchical modelling framework that accounted for imperfect detection. Results showed that small structures substantially increased reptile abundance relative to controls. Branch piles produced strong, consistent positive effects across all focal species, with abundances ca. 4–13 times higher than in controls. Stone piles also showed positive effects, with estimated abundances approximately 2–6 times higher than in controls, although posterior support for positive effects was generally weaker and varied among species. The whole reptile assemblage benefitted from these structures, including the sand lizard Lacerta agilis , a species of particular conservation concern across Europe. Our findings provide robust experimental evidence that adding small structural elements enhances reptile abundance in otherwise intensively managed farmland. Given their low implementation costs, minimal space requirements and compatibility with existing farming practices, small structures represent a practical and scalable conservation measure for restoring fine-scale habitat heterogeneity in agricultural landscapes.

items.title: Scalability Scope and Limitations of Potential Innovations and Renewable Energy Sources to Sustain Small Holder Farming Families and Various Ecosystems in India-Local to Global Relevance
items.abstract: The soil, water and air pollution are posing a huge threat to soil, underground water aquifers, oceans, various ecosystems, food chain, human, animals (land, aquatic both), various species health and our environment. Efficiently recapturing carbon emissions through agroforestry, increasing area under forests along with increasing the use of renewable sources in hybrid mode can put a halt on this pattern. Biogas/Biofuels along with necessary engine changes, can control vehicular carbon emissions to a great extent. There is need to increase use of vermi-compost, in-situ crop residue management techniques, green manuring, farm yard/poultry manures, pulse-cereal intercropping/diversification, eco-friendly integrated pest management techniques, biodegradable plastic, jute bags and use of crop residue biochar, sunflower seed husk and its biochar as a bioremediation to treat industrial waste with heavy metals. A new and innovative eco-friendly Parkash Bioherbal water reservoir is proposed. Neem, Moringa oleifera and seaweed products can be used as biopesticides, bioinsecticides, biofertilizers to enhance crop growth in an organic way. The technologies and implementation to minimize and treat industrial/domestic waste at source before discharge into the marine system are urgently required so as to enhance the oceans’ capacity to maintain carbon cycle.

items.title: Microbial colonisation patterns are more affected by plant substrate compositions than termite modulated environments
items.abstract: Abstract Background Termites are dominant plant biomass decomposers and important ecosystem engineers that modify soil properties and microbial communities. In fungus-farming termites, mound building contribute to distinctions between three environments: fungal gardens, mound walls, and outside soil away from mounds. Here we determined the properties of these environments for 10 colonies of Macrotermes bellicosus termites and tested their consequences for fungal and bacterial colonisation of two novel substrates presented as compositionally-different types of tea. Lastly, capitalising on the mass loss of tea bags, we evaluated the decomposition rates in these environments across habitats (forest patch, woody savanna, and teak plantation) in central Côte d’Ivoire. Results We confirmed that M. bellicosus termite colonies create distinct local environments that are markedly different in both elemental (e.g., carbon and nitrogen content) and bacterial and fungal community compositions. Fungal colonisation of tea bags in outside soils, and to a lesser extent mound soil, reflected community compositions of soil sources, with dominant colonisers being opportunistic spore-forming saprophytes. Similar communities colonised tea bags within mounds, resulting in poor reflection of the termite gut and fungal comb source communities. Bacterial colonisation was also comparable across environments, but overall poorly reflected source communities, underlining that tea bag properties strongly select for coloniser taxa. Although decomposition rates were more consistent in mound walls and fungal gardens than outside soils, we did not detect significant differences between either of the three environments. Conclusions Our findings point to contrasting tea bag properties strongly selecting for opportunistic colonisers that are not necessarily abundant in source environments and across habitats. This canalisation was most prominent for fungi and likely contributed to the comparable decomposition rates across environments. The omnipresence of fast-colonising fungi to novel substrates in all three environments imply that they remain present and potentially threat termite farms, while termites actively suppress their proliferation within combs. Colonisation here thus best exemplified competitive release owing to reduced suppression of non- Termitomyces fungi. Even so, termite activities markedly shape environmental properties, demonstrating the importance of mound building in generating heterogeneous microbial niches in savannah ecosystems.

items.title: Seasonal Dynamics of diarrheagenic Escherichia coli pollution in black clam Villorita cyprinoides and its harvesting habitats of Vembanad Lake, India
items.abstract: Abstract Microbial contamination of estuarine ecosystems is a major public health concern, particularly in the shellfish-harvesting areas where the accumulation of potential pathogens pose severe health risks for consumers. The study investigated the occurrence, seasonal dynamics, pathogroup distribution, and virulence gene profiles of Escherichia coli in black clams ( Villorita cyprinoides ), harvesting waters, and sediment at five major harvesting locations in Vembanad Lake, India. Samples were collected monthly over one year from February 2023 to January 2024. The Most Probable Number (MPN) method was implemented for the enumeration of faecal coliforms and E. coli , followed by biochemical identification and PCR-based confirmation targeting the uidA gene and 11 virulence-associated markers. Elevated faecal indicator bacterial loads were detected across the sampling period, with significant seasonal variation, characterised by increased prevalence during the monsoon period, suggesting enhanced land-based runoff and anthropogenic inputs. Elevated MPN levels were recorded during the monsoon (MON) and post-monsoon (PSMON) seasons compared to the pre-monsoon (PRMON) period, indicating persistent faecal contamination and bacterial accumulation beyond the monsoon season. Among 313 confirmed E. coli isolates, 68.05% harboured at least one virulence gene. The prevalence of virulence associated gene was highest in water samples (72.72%) followed by clam (66.94%) and sediment (60%) samples. Of the 213 virulent isolates, 51.17% belonged to the enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC) pathogroup, indicating dominance of toxigenic strains. A total of 47 distinct serotypes were detected, demonstrating considerable diversity among isolates. Prevalence of pathogenic E. coli in these different samples shows persistent faecal pollution, which is a potential threat to public health through consumption of contaminated shellfish. These findings further stress the importance of microbial surveillance and improved pollution management in tropical estuarine systems where shellfish harvesting occurs.

items.title: Towards biodiversity-relevant chemical risk assessment: insights from SETAC Europe 2025
items.abstract: A special session entitled “ Biodiversity and chemical hazard/risk assessment: regulatory frameworks, integrative approaches and research for a sustainable future ” was held at the SETAC Europe 2025 Annual Meeting. The session explored how environmental risk assessment (ERA) of chemicals can better support biodiversity protection, drawing on presentations, panel discussions and a live survey of over 100 participants. While existing prospective ERAs were recognised as providing a foundational framework for regulatory decision-making, the discussions highlighted persistent limitations in ecological realism. Key concerns included limited taxonomic coverage, insufficient consideration of indirect effects, and lack of integration of chemical mixtures and multiple stressors, alongside ongoing difficulties in translating laboratory findings into meaningful biodiversity-relevant outcomes in real-world ecosystems. Participants identified 105 barriers and proposed 95 solutions, leading to a set of strategic recommendations. Recommendations emerging from the discussions call for: (1) operationalising biodiversity protection goals into measurable endpoints aligned across policy frameworks; (2) increasing ecological realism and predictive capacity through modelling and integrative approaches; (3) embedding routine assessment of chemical mixtures and multiple stressors; (4) strengthening links between ERA and environmental monitoring (covering biota biodiversity, and chemicals), supported by findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable (FAIR) data infrastructures; and (5) improving governance and implementation to enable preventive and protective actions. Together, these priorities outline a pathway for advancing biodiversity-focused ERA that better reflects real-world complexity and supports sustainable chemical management.

items.title: Biodiversity and wilderness sustainability in environmental ethics: What can Yoruba eco-philosophy offer?
items.abstract: This work interrogates some theories of environmental ethics. It identifies biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation as pivotal environmental problems facing our world today. This is because the local and global environment is presently experiencing biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation, traceable to destructive anthropogenic activities such as deforestation, pollution, hunting, urbanisation and uncontrolled capitalist-inspired agricultural practices. Using relationalism as a theoretical framework, the work examines the practice of Igbo oro in Yoruba eco-philosophy and untangles the inherent similarity and the point of divergence between Yoruba eco-philosophy and deep ecology of the western philosophical tradition. It argues that the practice of Igbo oro among the Yoruba people embodies and goes beyond what deep ecology stands for. The work goes further to demonstrate how the practice of Igbo oro pragmatically shows respect for nature, thereby constituting an indigenous African paradigm for environmental sustainability. This argument is significant since it debunks the position held in certain quarters that the practice of Igbo oro in Yorubaland is only for the fulfilment of religious aspirations of the Yoruba people.

items.title: Modeling the distribution of bryophytes threatened according to the European Red List in Türkiye under climate change
items.abstract: Introduction Climate change is expected to become one of the greatest threats to bryophyte diversity; therefore, predicting the future distributions of species is vital for effective conservation planning. However, the absence of a national bryophyte Red List and threat assessments in Türkiye represents a major shortcoming in terms of biodiversity conservation. To address this gap, we modeled the current and future potential distributions of bryophyte taxa naturally occurring in Türkiye that are classified as “Vulnerable” (VU), “Endangered” (EN), or “Critically Endangered” (CR) on the European Red List. Methods From among the 73 threatened taxa identified in Türkiye, 36 species with at least five (≥5) recorded occurrences were selected for modeling. Species distribution models were developed using MaxEnt v3.4.4 under current climate conditions and projected to 2021–2040 and 2081–2100 under two climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5) and two global climate models with contrasting climate sensitivities (HadGEM3-GC31-LL and MIROC6). Results Precipitation-related variables, particularly precipitation seasonality (BIO15), were the most important predictors for most species, whereas temperature-related variables predominated for the species of the continental interior and mountain regions. Projections for 2081–2100 under the SSP5-8.5 scenario indicate that 15 bryophyte taxa (14 mosses and one liverwort (Scapania verrucosa)) will experience substantial reductions in their climatically suitable areas, consistently under both climate models, and some species are projected to lose nearly all of their climatically suitable areas. The moss species at highest risk of extinction were predominantly acrocarps and small taxa (with the exception of Brachythecium geheebii and Palamocladium euchloron). Discussion Our findings present the first climate-based conservation assessment for threatened bryophytes in Türkiye and provide a scientific foundation for the creation of a National Bryophyte Red List, the identification of priority bryophyte conservation areas, and the development of evidence-based conservation planning under future climate change conditions.

items.title: Chronic Wasting Disease in Wild and Farmed Cervids: Global Epidemiology, Economic Consequences and Future Challenges—A Conceptual Narrative Review
items.abstract: Chronic Wasting Disease (CWD) has evolved from a geographically restricted transmissible spongiform encephalopathy of cervids into an international wildlife health challenge with documented population-level impact and potential broader consequences for biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, captive cervid production, and wildlife management. Despite advances in prion biology, transmission, diagnostics, and surveillance, knowledge remains fragmented across epidemiological, ecological, economic, and management disciplines, limiting integrated understanding of disease persistence, spread, and long-term consequences. This conceptual review synthesizes current evidence on CWD epidemiology in wild and farmed cervids and develops a systems-based framework integrating these perspectives. We examine its distribution, biological, environmental, and anthropogenic transmission drivers, and human-mediated spread. We further evaluate population- and ecosystem-level consequences, economic impacts on wildlife-based economies and captive cervid production, surveillance and management strategies, and priorities for future preparedness. Our synthesis identifies distinct regional epidemiological systems and shows that CWD dynamics are shaped by reciprocal interactions among host ecology, environmental contamination, human activities, economic responses, and management interventions. Ecological changes may modify transmission opportunities, while economic and societal responses influence surveillance capacity, stakeholder behaviour, management feasibility, and preparedness. This integration clarifies CWD dynamics, identification of knowledge gaps, and development of adaptive, evidence-based surveillance, management, and preparedness strategies.

items.title: An autonomous imaging system for reef fish monitoring in the southern Gulf of Mexico
items.abstract: Introduction Reef fish assemblages are widely used as indicators of coral reef condition. Yet, diver-based surveys provide limited temporal resolution and are constrained by logistical demands. We evaluated an autonomous underwater imaging system based on cameras programmed for unattended image acquisition to monitor reef fish assemblages in the southern Gulf of Mexico. Methods Five terrestrial trail cameras adapted for underwater deployment were operated at Bajo de Diez reef during two seasonal deployments in 2024 and 2025, yielding 191,758 valid underwater images at a nominal 3-min interval. Image quality, camera view, species diversity, and daily assemblage dynamics were evaluated using expert annotations of 27,471 images, iNEXT-4steps, multivariate analyses, and an RF-DETR Medium object-detection model applied to the complete valid underwater record. Results Across the expert-sampled record, the mean daily proportion of images containing at least one fish was 17%, and 65 species were recorded. Laplacian variance distinguished lower- from higher-quality images. Assemblage composition differed clearly between the two deployment contexts and showed smaller but statistically detectable heterogeneity among fixed camera views within each deployment, while daily observations revealed structured temporal variation. On the held-out image-level test set, RF-DETR Medium achieved mAP@50 = 0.741, mAP@50:95 = 0.545, precision = 0.794, and recall = 0.650. Across 68 dates shared by the expert and CV analyses, expert- and CV-derived Bray–Curtis temporal structure was positively correlated (ρ = 0.63; Mantel permutation test, p ≤ 0.0001), with similar concordance for daily richness and the image-based relative abundance index. Applied to nearly seven times the number of manually annotated images, RF-DETR expanded temporal support from 68 to 110 dates. Discussion Autonomous imaging can extend reef fish monitoring beyond discrete surveys through repeated acquisition, while computer vision can reduce manual processing within a human-supervised workflow. Within the site and deployment periods evaluated, combining sustained fixed imaging, expert annotation, and computer vision made fuller use of the image archive and provided daily information on reef fish assemblage structure and its variation through time.
