items.title: Occurrence, environmental associations, and screening-level ecological risks of legacy and emerging PFASs in Hangzhou Bay.
items.abstract: The resistance of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) to environmental degradation, together with their potential adverse effects, has raised concern about their occurrence in aquatic ecosystems. This study investigated the occurrence, source indications, environmental associations, and ecological risks of dissolved PFASs in surface seawater from 30 stations in Hangzhou Bay, China. Summed target PFAS concentrations (ΣPFASs) ranged from 2.47 to 109.35 ng/L, with a median concentration of 14.85 ng/L. Among the 45 target PFASs, 11 were detected. PFOA and PFHxA occurred at all stations, while 10:2 FTCA had the highest mean concentration (11.693 ng/L). Emerging PFASs accounted for 55.4% of ΣPFASs, with 10:2 FTCA and HFPO-TA as the principal contributors. Elevated concentrations occurred mainly at northern stations. Diagnostic ratios and PCA indicated a widespread PFCA background with spatially variable contributions from PFBS and emerging PFASs. Associations with NO 3 -N and Cd were consistent with coupled land-based inputs and estuarine redistribution. Most compound-station combinations indicated negligible or low ecological risks, but 10:2 FTCA presented high risk at five stations and PFHxDA presented medium risk at two stations. Cumulative mixture risk reached the high category at six stations. These findings improve understanding of PFAS composition and ecological risks in Hangzhou Bay and provide a basis for targeted monitoring and risk management in highly dynamic estuarine waters.

items.title: Metastable retention of cadmium in karst carbonates: Internal cycling and its environmental implications.
items.abstract: Elucidating Cd release and fate in karst areas with high geological background is critical for constraining source-to-sink dynamics and underpinning geogenic risk management. This study integrated dissolution experiments, compositional analysis, mineral characterization, and monitoring of natural waters (drip water, pool water, and spring water) to systematically elucidate the source-to-sink migration and partitioning mechanisms of Cd. The results demonstrate that: (1) differential dissolution of bedrock released 65-82% of Cd into the solution phase, representing an upper-bound estimate of the mobilizable Cd inventory, while the remaining 18-35% was retained in insoluble residues that evolved in situ via weathering into Cd-enriched soil parent materials; (2) Cd 2+ released from parent rock dissolution is partly retained by soil parent materials, exhibiting stable occurrence with high content and low activity, while another fraction is incorporated into the lattice of secondary carbonates (stalagmites and stalactites), forming metastable Cd-bearing calcite whose stability is governed by the susceptibility of the carbonate host to dissolution rather than by the bonding form of Cd; (3) hydrological export is not a dominant pathway for net Cd loss, and Cd in karst systems follows an internal cycling path of "lattice fixation, differential dissolution, resorption by the soil parent material, and secondary calcite" with the initial weathering stage as the critical ecological risk period. Accordingly, the management strategy should focus on preserving natural buffering capacity and preventing acidification disturbance.

items.title: Elucidating organ-specific and cross-organ toxic effects of 6PPDQ in mice via integrated network toxicology and multi-omics analysis.
items.abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPDQ) is an emerging pollutant generated via environmental oxidation of tire-derived 6PPD. Although concerns have been raised about its potential toxicity, the organ-specific and cross-organ toxicological mechanisms in mammalian liver and kidney remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the toxic mechanisms of 6PPDQ in the liver and kidney of mice, with a focus on elucidating both organ-specific damage and correlations in cross-organ toxicity. By integrating network toxicology with molecular docking, we identified potential targets associated with 6PPDQ-induced liver and kidney toxicity. In vivo assessments confirmed concurrent hepatic inflammation, redox imbalance, and renal edema. Multi-omics analysis revealed that 6PPDQ selectively disrupts hepatic arachidonic acid pathways as well as renal arginine metabolism and osmoregulation. Molecular and in vitro functional validations identified p53 and c-Fos as key transcriptional regulators coordinating these interconnected metabolic dysfunctions across organs. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms of 6PPDQ-induced liver and kidney injury and contributes to the development of organ-specific and cross-organ biomarkers for toxicity caused by environmental pollutants.

items.title: Extreme dust deposition disrupts diatom carbon allocation under CO<sub>2</sub>-elevated ocean conditions.
items.abstract: Extreme dust deposition and ocean acidification are intensifying environmental stressors under climate change, yet their combined impacts on marine phytoplankton physiology and carbon cycling remain poorly understood. Here, we explored the responses of the cosmopolitan diatom Skeletonema costatum to present-day (420 ppm) and future (1000 ppm) CO 2 conditions under low (2 mg L -1 ) and high (10 mg L -1 ) dust deposition scenarios. Elevated CO 2 alone promoted sustained growth by reducing investment in carbon-concentrating mechanisms and enhancing dissolved organic nitrogen utilization. In contrast, high dust addition under elevated CO 2 triggered a metabolic reallocation: although cell density remained high, cellular particulate organic carbon and nitrogen quotas declined by more than 50% relative to the elevated CO 2 alone. Transcriptomic analyses revealed that a dust-derived ammonium pulse disrupted coordinated nitrogen metabolism, redirecting cellular resources toward rapid proliferation at the expense of lipid biosynthesis and carbon storage. This shift decoupled population growth from carbon accumulation, resulting in a 65.2% reduction in per-cell carbon uptake efficiency relative to the elevated CO 2 control. Although transient dissolved inorganic carbon drawdown and pH elevation occurred during dust-stimulated growth, the production of carbon-depleted biomass may reduce carbon export efficiency by increasing the likelihood of upper-ocean remineralization. These findings suggest that extreme dust deposition under future ocean acidification may reduce the efficiency of the biological carbon pump rather than enhance carbon sequestration, representing a potential environmental risk to this critical marine ecosystem service.

items.title: Impacts of traditional and industrial approaches to oil palm cultivation on bird biodiversity and conservation in a West African rainforest landscape.
items.abstract: Agricultural expansion threatens tropical ecosystems worldwide. Oil palm is cultivated primarily in Southeast Asia, but production in West Africa (its native range) is increasing rapidly. Here, oil palm is cultivated under traditional and industrial management, and the impacts on native West African ecosystems are poorly understood. Working within the framework of the Sustainable Oil Palm in West Africa (SOPWA) Project in Sinoe County, Liberia, we derived bird occurrence data using point count surveys across 54 plots in January-February 2023, spanning rainforest ('forest'), traditionally managed oil palm ('country palm'), and industrial oil palm systems, to investigate differences in bird species richness, community composition and community-level trait associations. Forest and country palm had comparable species richness, which was significantly higher than industrial oil palm. Taxonomic community composition differed across systems, with assemblages in country palm representing a mix of those in forest and industrial oil palm. Further, communities in forest and country palm were more associated with foraging in high strata, ant-associated behaviour, and an invertebrate diet. We detected four species of conservation concern in all systems, showing no consistent collective response to any specific system. Our findings show that country palm offers a promising option to preserve relatively high biodiversity as well as traditional cultivation practices in Liberia's managed landscape, although country palm is likely less productive than industrial oil palm. Oil palm systems are no replacement for rainforest ecosystems, and protection and designation of reserves and remnant forest patches are critical for wider bird conservation across West Africa.

items.title: Crystallinity-dependent dual role of iron oxides in regulating SOC mineralization and sequestration in paddy soil.
items.abstract: Improving soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration and reducing CO 2 emissions are essential for sustaining agricultural production in intensive farming regions worldwide. This study investigated the effect of iron oxide on SOC mineralization and sequestration in paddy soil because of its high redox reactivity and adsorption capacity. Soils were collected from an 11-year field experiment with two treatments: NPK fertilization and NPK fertilization combined with green manure (Chinese milk vetch) return. An incubation experiment was conducted with four treatments: no addition, 13 C-glucose, 13 C-glucose + low-crystallinity iron oxide (Fe 3 O 4 ), and 13 C-glucose + high-crystallinity iron oxide (α-Fe 2 O 3 ). Compared to the 13 C-glucose treatment, iron oxide addition reduced total CO 2 emissions by 3.5-10.0%, with the reduction being significant for α-Fe 2 O 3 . Source tracing revealed that soil-derived CO 2 decreased by 13-23% and 17-26% with Fe 3 O 4 and α-Fe 2 O 3 addition, respectively, while glucose-derived CO 2 increased by 26-45% and 12-48%. Both Fe 3 O 4 and α-Fe 2 O 3 induced a negative priming effect (-49 to -129 mg C kg -1 dry soil) and increased the 13 C content in SOC by 11.5-19.8%. The iron-bound carbon content was significantly increased by the iron oxide treatments, and its aromaticity was decreased by Fe 3 O 4 while increased by α-Fe 2 O 3 . This research concludes that iron oxides facilitate SOC sequestration by suppressing native SOC mineralization and promoting the storage of exogenous carbon, illustrating their potential role in improving soil fertility and enhancing environmental sustainability.

items.title: Behind Closed Doors: Caregiving Burden in Exclusive Two-Person Living Arrangements.
items.abstract: This study examined caregiving burden among primary family caregivers in two-person households, consisting solely of home-based Long-Term Care Insurance recipients and their caregivers in South Korea. By analyzing 1,068 caregivers from the 2019 and 2022 Korean Long-Term Care Surveys (717 spouses; 351 adult children), we assessed burden across emotional support, IADL, housekeeping, and physical ADL domains. Spousal caregivers showed higher odds of IADL and physical ADL burden, and caregiving frequency was positively associated with their emotional support and housekeeping burden. Adult child caregivers were more likely to experience burden when caring for male or dementia-affected recipients. These findings suggest that burden was linked to caregiving frequency among spouses and to recipient characteristics among adult children. Spousal caregivers may face greater strain from age-related limitations and continuous care demands. Recipient-centered policies may not adequately address their needs; caregiver-inclusive assessments and targeted support merit consideration.

items.title: Setting the Pace of Epigenetic Aging in Mammals: A Hierarchy from Species to Individual.
items.abstract: Epigenetic clocks have transformed aging research by providing accurate molecular measures of biological age, but the factors regulating their pace across mammals remain unclear. This review proposes a hierarchy of regulation: species-level determinants that set intrinsic aging rate and lifespan, as well as individual-level modifiers acting within species. Comparative analyses show developmental tempo, rather than body mass, anchors species differences. Across individuals, caloric restriction and other perturbations of the insulin-like growth factor 1 nutrient-sensing axis alter epigenetic aging rate, whereas torpor models suggest body temperature, rather than metabolic rate per se, acts as the pacemaker. Gonadal hormones, reproduction, social environment, and ecology also contribute, with applications in livestock and wildlife conservation highlighted as means to capitalize on age-associated traits and exposures. Together, this work shows epigenetic clocks are far more than a yardstick for biological time; they reveal the multifaceted biology, and its hierarchy, that sets the pace of aging in mammals.

items.title: Sex Differences in Biological Responses: Mechanisms, Evolution, and Environmental Interactions.
items.abstract: Sex-specific phenotypes arise from complex interactions among genetic, epigenetic, hormonal, and environmental factors throughout development and across the lifespan. Although sex-determination mechanisms establish gonadal identity, they also initiate differences in sex-specific responses beyond reproductive tissues. Here, we review the diverse genetic and environmental sex-determination systems, highlighting how these mechanisms regulate sex-specific gene expression. We further examine the roles of hormones, epigenetic modifications, and environmental factors in shaping physiological, behavioral, and life-history differences between the sexes. Early-life conditions, social environments, and reproductive strategies further modify these trajectories, producing substantial within- and among-species variations in sex-specific phenotypes during development and aging. By integrating evidence across vertebrates and invertebrates, we propose a unified framework in which sex-specific phenotypes emerge from dynamic interactions between genomes, epigenomes, and environments. This comparative perspective discusses conserved and lineage-specific principles underlying the evolution, phenotypic plasticity, and adaptive significance of sex differences across diverse taxa.

items.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants.
items.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

items.title: Transcriptomic characterization of obligate winter diapause in the emerald ash borer (Agrilus planipennis).
items.abstract: Wood-boring insects pose serious threats to trees, and even when living inside their hosts, they remain exposed to adverse conditions such as extreme low temperatures. Diapause is a critical strategy that enables certain pests to survive such environments and sustain their populations. Characterizing the molecular changes associated with diapause may therefore improve our understanding of their overwintering biology and environmental responses. However, transcriptomic studies of diapause in wood-boring insects remain relatively limited, partly because of their long life cycles, cryptic habits, and difficulties in sampling and observation. In this study, we focused on the emerald ash borer (EAB, Agrilus planipennis), an obligate diapausing pest that causes severe damage in both its native and invaded ranges. Using a comparative transcriptomic approach, we sequenced samples from three developmental stages: pre-diapause, diapause, and post-diapause. Compared to the other developmental stages, 1,147 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified as showing diapause-stage-associated expression patterns, with up-regulated genes outnumbering down-regulated genes by approximately 1.88-fold. By integrating exploratory GO/KEGG analyses, expression profiles, and previously reported diapause-associated pathways, we identified 47 candidate diapause-associated genes. Among these, 35 were upregulated (1.24- to 807.71-fold) and 12 were downregulated (0.04- to 0.74-fold) relative to the pre- and post-diapausing stages. KEGG Mapper further indicated that several candidates were associated with the Wnt, circadian rhythm, and FOXO signaling pathways. Collectively, these results characterize diapause-associated transcriptional changes in EAB and provide candidate genes and pathways for further investigation of overwintering responses in EAB and other winter-diapausing wood-boring insects.

items.title: Feeding type and microplastic particle concentration drive the ingestion of polystyrene beads in a natural zooplankton community.
items.abstract: The mismanagement of plastic waste in recent decades has led to global plastic pollution problem. Much of this plastic waste in the environment degrades into small particles, forming microplastics and increasing their abundance in ecosystems. These microplastics can be ingested by various microinvertebrates such as zooplankton. Using a microcosm experiment with a near-natural zooplankton community, we tested whether microplastics particle size and concentration affect the proportion of individuals ingesting polystyrene beads. Zooplankton were exposed to three bead sizes (1, 3, and 6 µm) at two concentrations (10 3 and 10 6 particles mL⁻ 1 ). Ingestion was assessed as the presence or absence of beads within individual organisms. As all beads sizes were within the ingestible range, the experiment was designed to evaluate size-dependent differences in ingestion probability rather than physical ingestion limit. At low concentrations, 40% of the cladocerans ingested microplastics, which was a higher percentage than copepods, rotifers and ostracods; suggesting that their unselective filter-feeding mode facilitates ingestion. At high microplastics concentrations, these were ingested by more than 70% of the organisms across all experimental groups, with only moderate differences in the proportion of individuals ingesting microplastics among rotifers, cladocerans, ostracods and copepods. These high percentages indicate that even raptorial feeders cannot avoid ingesting plastic at elevated concentrations. The size of the microplastics had no effect on their ingestibility. Overall, our near-natural experiment demonstrated that both feeding type and beads concentration significantly influenced microplastics ingestion by zooplankton.

items.title: Organization and remodeling of olfactory subsystems across development in the brilliant-thighed poison frog Allobates femoralis.
items.abstract: Olfaction is important for many ecological and social behaviors, but the development, organization, and molecular features of the olfactory system remain poorly understood in most anuran amphibians. Understanding developmental changes is particularly important because, during metamorphosis, the olfactory system must adapt to the very different conditions encountered by aquatic larvae and mainly terrestrial adults. In the brilliant-thighed poison frog Allobates femoralis, chemical cues influence behavior during both aquatic and terrestrial life stages, but the organization of its olfactory system has not yet been described. Here, we examined the anatomy and molecular features of the olfactory system of A. femoralis during development. We identified a main olfactory epithelium and a vomeronasal organ, together with a distinct buccal-exposed olfactory epithelium that is present only in larvae. We also found an additional larval sensory epithelium that is in close connection to the main olfactory epithelium. The different sensory epithelia showed distinct anatomical features and projected to defined regions of the main and accessory olfactory bulb. Immunohistochemistry revealed Gαo-expressing receptor neurons in all these epithelia, together with Gαo-positive axonal projections to the main and accessory olfactory bulb. Our study provides the first detailed description of the developing olfactory system of A. femoralis. These findings provide a basis for future studies linking the organization and function of the olfactory system to the olfaction-guided behaviors of this species.

items.title: Phylogenomic analysis of Dendrothele nivosa, a bark-inhabiting and host-specific crust fungus with an enigmatic ecological role.
items.abstract: Fungi in the genus Dendrothele (Basidiomycota, Russulales) are known for their obligate associations with the bark of living trees. However, the genus as it is currently defined is polyphyletic, and the phylogenetic placement and ecological roles of many of its species are poorly understood. We focused on Dendrothele nivosa , a common species in eastern North America associated with the bark of living Juniperus species. The taxonomic placement of D. nivosa has shifted among different orders and families since the 19th century. This species is found exclusively on the bark of living Juniperus , and its ecological niche remains unclear, as it is not associated with the bark of dead trees and thus may function as something other than a primary decomposer. Using Illumina short-read technology, we generated the first highquality genome assembly of D. nivosa (71 Mb length; BUSCO completeness of 97.5%, N50: 9572, L50: 1618). We determined its phylogenetic placement by building a whole genome-based phylogeny using publicly available data for the order Russulales. D. nivosa represents a distinct clade separate from its most closely related families, Bondarzewiaceae and Stereaceae. To better understand its ecological niche, we analyzed gene families of D. nivosa and closely related relatives, with an emphasis on carbohydrateassociated enzymes (CAZymes). The CAZyme profile in our assembly suggests that D. nivosa may function primarily as a bark/wood decay fungus, despite its exclusive association with living trees. In contrast to other close relatives, nearly half of the D. nivosa genome consists of transposable elements (TEs) caused by a massive invasion of long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons, suggesting that TEs have played an important role in shaping D. nivosa 's evolution. The clarified phylogenetic position of D. nivosa and robust genomic data serve as a starting point for future work to determine the evolution and ecology of the diverse species of corticioid fungi associated with the bark of living trees.

items.title: Botulinum neurotoxin type a exposure and executive functioning: A multinational web-based survey.
items.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin A (BoNT-A) injections have revolutionized both cosmetic and therapeutic interventions, gaining recognition for their positive physical and psychological effects. However, potential psychological correlates and safety concerns have received comparatively less attention. This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the association between BoNT-A exposure and executive function (EF) in a global sample. We collected data from participants across 155 countries using an online survey translated into 28 languages and distributed via web-based platforms. Chi-square tests and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) were employed to assess bivariate associations, while multivariable linear regression models using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) were employed to examine the association between BoNT-A exposure and EF scores, accounting for within-country clustering across the 155 countries while adjusting for sociodemographic and behavioral confounders. A total of 46,611 participants were screened, of whom 1,088 were excluded based on predefined criteria, leaving a primary eligible analytic cohort of N = 45,523. Among BoNT-A recipients, Self-Organization/Problem-Solving deficit scores varied significantly by injection frequency (p = 0.008), with the annual-injection group reporting a slightly higher mean score (42.3 ± 12.9), indicating a higher level of reported difficulties in this domain compared to other groups. However, the magnitude of this difference was small. No, clinically or statistically significant differences were observed across the remaining four executive function subscales (p > 0.05). In adjusted multivariable linear regression analysis controlling for sociodemographic and behavioral factors, BoNT-A injection was very small, albeit statistically significant, positive associations with higher scores for Self-Control/Inhibition (β = 0.508, 95% CI: 0.131-0.886, p = 0.008), self-regulation of emotion (β = 0.508, 95% CI: 0.238-0.778, p < 0.001), and Self-Motivation (β = 0.226, 95% CI: 0.023-0.428, p = 0.028), whereas no significant association was observed with Self-Organization/Problem-Solving, and self-management of time. Sensitivity analyses yielded a largely similar pattern across most domains but showed attenuation and loss of statistical significance for the Self-Organization/Problem-Solving association, highlighting domain-specific variability and the modest magnitude of the original estimate. These cross-sectional findings identify subtle, domain-specific observational associations. Because the Self-Organization/Problem-Solving association was attenuated in sensitivity analyses and residual confounding by indication is possible, these results should not be interpreted as evidence of toxin-induced neurocognitive changes or a causal effect. Prospective longitudinal cohort studies that incorporate comprehensive assessments of clinical indications and other potential confounders are warranted to further investigate these associations.

items.title: Assessing the viability of monospaced fonts for eye-movement paradigms in Arabic reading.
items.abstract: Monospaced (fixed-width) fonts such as Courier, where each character occupies an identical unit of horizontal space, are widely used in eye-movement research in Latinate languages (Slattery, 2016). The uniformity of monospaced fonts is methodologically advantageous, allowing researchers to match the spatial width of words containing equal numbers of letters. However, their use has been avoided in Arabic research due to their rarity and perceived unnatural appearance, which changes the natural cursive interconnection between letters (Hermena et al., 2017). This imposes difficulties for researchers of Arabic reading, particularly when employing gaze-contingent change techniques, creating restrictions that impede progress to close the gap in knowledge about cursive languages. While it has been hypothesized that monospacing may interfere with cognitive processing, this has not been directly investigated. In two experiments, we examined whether monospaced and proportional fonts modulate lexical frequency effects and parafoveal preview effects during Arabic sentence reading. Fixation time measures showed similar patterns in both font types. Lexical frequency influenced word identification similarly across most measures in the two font types (Experiment 1), while a manipulation of parafoveal preview validity produced comparable effects on fixation times for target words (Experiment 2). Across experiments, monospaced fonts produced shorter but more frequent fixations than proportional fonts: a trade-off that mirrors effects previously reported in Latinate languages. Given the methodological advantages for gaze-contingent paradigms, these findings establish monospaced fonts as a readable and suitable option for Arabic reading research, facilitating tighter spatial control and cross-script comparability.

items.title: Internalized and Externalized Symptoms: A Qualitative Analysis of Discussion Threads from Femcel Forums.
items.abstract: The terms incels and femcels, respectively, designate men and women who identify as involuntary celibates. Incels and femcels share frustration linked to their inability to obtain love and sex, along with a deep sense of marginalization in their social, sexual, and romantic lives. Studies carried out on incels suggest the presence of internalizing and externalizing symptoms. However, because research on femcels is very limited, it is not known whether they encounter the same problems. The present study sought to fill this gap by identifying the types of internalizing and externalizing symptoms experienced by femcels, as observed in the forums where they voice themselves. A deductive content analysis of exchanges on two public forums where femcels post showed a high prevalence of internalizing symptoms. Most of these symptoms concerned loneliness, low self-esteem, depressed and anxious mood, and even suicidal ideation. Externalizing symptoms were far less frequent and mainly involved aggressive affects toward men. These findings echo those of Brix Rasmussen (2023), who reported that the dominant themes in femcel exchanges concerned their psychological distress, particularly depressive and anxious symptoms. They also highlight the need for future research on the psychological and relational difficulties associated with involuntary celibacy among women.

items.title: The first wave of macro-level nature connectedness research: Convergent insights and emerging directions.
items.abstract: The human-nature relationship is increasingly recognised as a fundamental driver of environmental issues. This article synthesises and reflects on an emerging "first wave" of quantitative macro-level research on nature connectedness, revealing how the human-nature relationship is shaped not only by individual experiences but by slow-moving cultural, socioeconomic, and historical forces. Drawing on multinational surveys, machine-learning analyses, and agent-based models spanning two centuries, the paper identifies consistent drivers of declining nature connectedness, including urbanisation, economic development, secularisation, and intergenerational transmission. It shows that these macro-factors explain both long-term declines and contemporary global variation, reframing nature connectedness as a societal property rather than an individual trait. This perspective paper synthesises these emergent insights, highlights the conceptual foundations of an integrated science of nature connectedness, and outlines priorities for future research into systemic, multi-level interventions capable of informing policy and societal transformation of the human-nature relationship.

items.title: Norms for gender-inclusive role nouns in Italian: The GIRN-I database.
items.abstract: Understanding how linguistic alternatives to gender-binary forms are perceived is particularly relevant in languages that encode gendered categorisations through specific linguistic markers, such as Italian. Indeed, gender-diverse individuals face additional distress associated with perceived invisibility arising from the absence of adequate linguistic forms. To date, substantial research has been devoted to identifying demographic and socio-political factors underlying preferences for gender-inclusive language. However, far less is known about the cognitive mechanisms that underlie these attitudes. Here, we provide the first Italian psycholinguistic database of role nouns (e.g., nurse, carpenter, teacher) encompassing both gendered (i.e., feminine and masculine) and gender-inclusive (i.e., asterisk and schwa) desinences. Remarkably, this is the first contribution explicitly assessing Italian participants' dispositions towards gender-inclusive desinences. We asked participants to rate role nouns on nine semantic dimensions, including classic dimensions like familiarity and sensibility and less conventional ones like psychological distance and political relevance. Our findings suggest no clear preference for either of the two inclusive alternatives, both of which are perceived as less familiar and less pleasant than their corresponding gendered forms. We suggest that processing components related to linguistic fluency may also contribute to explaining observed preference patterns. Taken together, our findings underscore the importance of considering semantic and linguistic processing factors, alongside ideological and social variables, when investigating attitudes towards gender-inclusive language.

items.title: A practical guide to self-organising maps in psychological research.
items.abstract: Identifying shared and distinct profiles, whether of symptoms, personality traits, or cognitive abilities, is essential for understanding psychological phenomena, yet doing so requires navigating interrelated theoretical, conceptual, and technical complexities. First, most psychological phenomena typically exist along continuous spectra rather than discrete categories, complicating the characterisation of inherently heterogeneous constructs. Second, studying individual differences requires balancing population-level generalisation with person-level interpretability, which is critical for applied science and clinical practice. Third, psychological data often contain missing values, non-linear relationships, and high-dimensional patterns that violate standard statistical assumptions. Commonly used approaches for profile detection often fall short of these demands, producing oversimplified or difficult-to-interpret results that are hard to map back to the individual. In contrast, self-organising maps (SOMs) offer a powerful, visual, and intuitive solution that addresses these challenges. Despite growing interest, SOMs remain underutilised in psychology, likely due to a lack of accessible tutorials and clear guidelines tailored to the field. This tutorial introduces SOMs to psychologists without technical backgrounds, emphasising practical implementation. We provide evidence-based recommendations for key methodological decisions, accompanied by annotated R code. Using a dataset of depressive symptoms as an illustrative case, we present a complete workflow covering data preprocessing, map initialisation, parameter optimisation, and interpretation. We further discuss advanced SOM extensions relevant to psychological research and highlight key limitations of the method. By making SOMs accessible, this tutorial supports nuanced, person-centred analyses that preserve the complexity of psychological phenomena.

items.title: Comparative effects of various exercise types and doses to improve executive function in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses.
items.abstract: Exercise interventions have been demonstrated to effectively improve executive function (EF) in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, evidence comparing effects of different exercise types and doses is limited, and the optimal exercise type and dose that improve EF remain unclear. This study aims to compare the effects of different exercise types and doses on EF improvement in children and adolescents with ADHD. Seven databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, SPORT Discus via EBSCO, PsycINFO, and CNKI) were systematically searched up to February 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing the effects of exercise interventions on EF in children and adolescents with ADHD were included. The outcomes included working memory (WM), inhibitory control (IC), and cognitive flexibility (CF). Pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses using random-effects models were conducted to assess the effects of exercise on EF. Forty RCTs (n = 1563) were included. Network meta-analysis indicated that, among children and adolescents with ADHD, mind-body exercise had the highest probability (SUCRA = 94.9) of being the most effective intervention for improving WM. Combat sports demonstrated the highest probability of being the most effective intervention for enhancing IC (SUCRA = 93.4) and CF (SUCRA = 92.5) in this population. Furthermore, a significant positive non-linear dose-response relationship was identified between total exercise and all EF domains among children and adolescents with ADHD. The minimum effective dose was estimated at approximately 1200 METs-min/week for WM, 340 METs-min/week for IC, and 280 METs-min/week for CF, respectively.

items.title: Understanding the exposome across the life course to promote healthy aging: consensus recommendations from the Gateway Exposome Coordinating Center.
items.abstract: Healthy aging is shaped by the exposome-the accumulation of exposures experienced across the life course arising from intersections of the natural, physical, social, community and policy environments in which people age. This Consensus Statement reports recommendations from the Gateway Exposome Coordinating Center to accelerate life-course research on the exposome's impacts on healthy aging, including Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Recommendations centered on five themes are presented: the promotion of interdisciplinary collaboration; the integration of life-course perspectives on the timing, accumulation and sequencing of exposures; systematically quantifying and incorporating broader contexts of time and place into health research; the adoption of mechanistic thinking to develop pathway-relevant exposure metrics; and leveraging new data streams, including wearable sensors, administrative records and remote sensing, to improve exposure measurement. These priorities emphasize harmonized measures, transparent methods and attention to bias, with the goal of identifying actionable intervention and policy targets across diverse populations that can shape individuals' exposures, lived experiences, behaviors and, ultimately, health as they age.

items.title: Medication burden among adults with cystic fibrosis prescribed CFTR Modulators: a cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: Background While CFTR modulators (CFTRm) have transformed clinical outcomes in CF, their impact on perceived medicines-related burden is not fully understood. This study aimed to quantify medicines-related burden in adults with CF prescribed CFTRm. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted between September and December 2022 in two adult CF centres in the North of England. Subjects >16 years and receiving CFTR modulator therapy were recruited in both inpatient and outpatient settings. Medicines-related burden was assessed using the validated Living with Medicines Questionnaire version 3 (LMQ-3). Data on use of pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT), insulin, number of daily medicines, and self-reported lung function (ppFEV₁%) was also captured. Results Of 577 eligible participants, 346 completed the survey (60%). The mean (SD) age was 33.6 (±12) years, with 190 (54.9%) male. The mean LMQ-3 score was 83.01 (SD 18.8; range 42-127). Minimal, moderate and high burden was experienced in 58.4%, 32.9% and 8.7% of subjects respectively. Higher burden was significantly associated with receiving help in managing medicines, greater number of daily medicines, lower educational attainment, and unemployment. No significant associations were observed for age, sex, lung function, pancreatic or diabetic status. Conclusion Despite the introduction of CFTRm therapy, medicines-related burden remains prevalent. Greater burden is associated with polypharmacy, need for support, and socioeconomic factors. The LMQ-3 may be a useful screening tool to identify individuals requiring targeted interventions to reduce treatment burden.

items.title: Aphantasia in Healthy Relationships: Visual Imagery in Attachment styles, Dyadic bonding, Social Networks & Loneliness.
items.abstract: This study explores the role of mental imagery in relationship functioning, attachment styles, loneliness and social networks, with a focus on individuals with aphantasia-a rare trait characterised by weak or absent mental imagery. We compared 82 participants (44 with aphantasia and 38 without) using psychological scales including the State Adult Attachment Measure, Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised scale, UCLA Loneliness Scale, Social Network Index, Dyadic Adjustment Scale, and Dyadic Coping Inventory. Results revealed that individuals with aphantasia reported significantly lower anxious attachment compared to controls, supporting the notion that lower mental imagery offers a protective effect against relationship anxiety. There were no penalties for aphantasics in the size of their social networks, in secure and avoidant attachment, or in dyadic adjustment within romantic relationships (with evidence to support these null effects). This suggests no necessary role for imagery in these domains, and/or compensatory mechanisms employed by aphantasics. Finally, we also investigated loneliness, network diversity and dyadic coping under stress but found insufficient evidence to draw conclusions. Overall our findings challenge assumptions about the universality of mental imagery in social and romantic relationship social processes, highlighting the variability of human cognition. Our study also contributes to understanding the cognitive and emotional nuances of aphantasia, with implications for therapeutic practices that consider individual imagery differences.

items.title: Cue modality modulates dynamic functional network organization during motor imagery: Evidence from EEG functional connectivity and spatiotemporal decoding.
items.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) is typically guided by external sensory cues; however, how cue modality and imagery type jointly influence functional connectivity during post-cue MI remains unclear. This study combined functional connectivity analysis with a CNN-TemporalConv-MLP spatiotemporal decoding model to investigate phase-locking value (PLV) differences across visual versus auditory cues and kinesthetic (KMI) versus visual (VMI) motor imagery. Functional connectivity analyses revealed that all connections with significant cue-modality effects in the early theta band showed higher PLV following visual cues. In the beta band, PLV was higher under visual cues in the earlier significant time window, whereas it was higher under auditory cues in the later significant time window. In contrast, differences between KMI and VMI were primarily localized to connections in the theta and alpha bands, while interactions between cue modality and imagery type emerged selectively in the theta, beta, and gamma bands. Decoding analyses showed that PLV functional connectivity features contained discriminative information about both factors. Overall cue-modality decoding achieved moderate performance, and performance improved when KMI and VMI conditions were held constant. By contrast, overall imagery-type classification showed relatively low discriminability. However, KMI versus VMI classification improved within specific cueing backgrounds, with better performance under fixed visual or auditory cues than under mixed cue-modality conditions. These findings indicate that the influence of cue modality can extend into subsequent MI, with functional connectivity differences showing selectivity across time, frequency, and connections. Condition-related differences were evident in both connection-specific PLV effects and deep learning decoding of PLV features.

items.title: Caregiver Stress and Coping during Pediatric Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant: Perspectives of Caregivers and Healthcare Providers.
items.abstract: Background Although pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) is potentially curative, it also carries risks and challenges, including lengthy hospitalizations, a risk of life-threatening complications, and demanding medical regimens. Thus, there are high levels of burden and psychological distress among caregivers of children who undergo HCT. However, limited research has explored healthcare provider perspectives on caregivers' pediatric HCT experiences, nor integrated those perspectives with those of caregivers. As healthcare providers partner with caregivers throughout the HCT process, they may be uniquely positioned to identify needs and provide additional support for caregivers during pediatric HCT. Objective(s) The objective of this paper was to explore caregiver and HCT healthcare provider perspectives of caregiver and family experiences across the pediatric HCT process, as identifying areas of agreement and disagreement may inform targeted interventions to support caregiver wellbeing during pediatric HCT. Study design This cross-sectional, qualitative pilot study recruited caregivers (n=12) of children 6-24 months post-HCT for individual semi-structured interviews, as well as HCT healthcare providers (i.e., nurses, psychosocial providers, physicians; n=13 in 3 focus groups) from a large freestanding children's hospital in the Midwestern United States. Interviews were coded via inductive qualitative content analysis. Results Caregivers and healthcare providers exhibited high agreement regarding caregivers' HCT experiences, which tended to broadly fall into HCT-related stress and coping. Both groups described high levels of caregiver stress; this included causes of stress, such as the child's medical course and balancing competing demands, as well as the expression of heightened emotional distress. Both groups also described caregivers' coping; this included caregiver use of social or relational support, a reliance on private coping, and employing acceptance, adaptive disengagement, and active coping methods. Caregivers and healthcare providers presented some differing foci, with healthcare providers focusing most on symptom-related stress and caregivers emphasizing multiple stressors, including their child's medical course, symptoms, and social isolation. Conclusion(s) There was significant overlap in caregiver and HCT healthcare provider perspectives, as well as areas of divergence, identifying potential opportunities for increased support during care. Findings may inform points of intervention or additional integrated clinical care to ultimately support optimal caregiver and family experiences during pediatric HCT. In particular, additional psychosocial support is needed to mitigate caregiver stress and support caregiver coping during pediatric HCT.

items.title: Influence of Stimulation Parameters on the Analgesic Effect of High-Frequency Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation on Neuropathic Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Background There is a need for novel analgesic treatments in patients with chronic neuropathic pain. High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) may have a clinically significant pain reducing effect. The aim of this study was to evaluate the therapeutic effects of HF-rTMS on chronic neuropathic pain and to investigate the influence of different stimulation parameters. Methods A systematic search in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science was performed. Thirty-one studies were included. Results HF-rTMS delivered to the precentral cortex (PreCC) with a focal F8-coil showed a significant analgesic effect (SMD = -0.86, 95% CI [-1.34, -0.37] and SMD = -0.80, 95% CI [-1.39, -0.20], for 3-5-session and >5-session datasets, respectively). HF-rTMS delivered to the PreCC with a larger H-coil also showed a significant effect (SMD = -0.36, 95% CI [-0.65, -0.08]), whereas HF-rTMS delivered to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex did not (SMD = -0.29, 95% CI [-0.93, 0.34]). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not show statistically significant differences between levels of stimulation frequency, intensity, number of pulses per session, or number of sessions, except for stimulation intensity in the >5-session dataset with the largest effect observed at 80% of the resting motor threshold. Regarding the effects of HF-rTMS of the PreCC, some parameters reached statistical significance at individual level: stimulation frequency (10 Hz in both datasets; 20 Hz in the 3-5-session dataset only), stimulation intensity (80% of the resting motor threshold), and number of pulses per session (1200-1600 in the >5-session dataset; 2000-2500 in the 3-5-session dataset). However, these individual-level significances do not formally establish a difference between subgroups, given that the corresponding comparison tests were not statistically significant. Conclusion This meta-analysis supports the overall efficacy of HF-rTMS of the PreCC for relieving chronic neuropathic pain. However, given substantial study heterogeneity, statistical limitations, reliance on few or influential studies for several parameter levels, and correlation between parameters across studies, parameter-specific findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of established parameter-response relationships. These results underscore the need for well-powered, systematically designed trials that directly compare stimulation protocols before optimal strategies can be established.

items.title: Oxygen concentration modulates cortical excitability in humans.
items.abstract: Cortical excitability is fundamental to neuroplasticity, particularly relevant in conditions like stroke and neurodegeneration. Although oxygen is essential for brain metabolism, its effects on cortical excitability remain poorly understood, representing a fundamental gap in neuromodulation research. This study is the first to directly examine the effects of both hypoxia and hyperoxia on corticospinal excitability (CSE) in humans, utilising non-linear analysis of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) recruitment curves. In a single-blinded, randomised, within-subjects design, 37 participants were exposed to hypoxia (10.5% O 2 ), normoxia (21% O 2 ), and hyperoxia (100% O 2 ). TMS was applied at varying intensities to generate motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), using a Boltzmann Sigmoidal Curve (BSC) approach to optimise estimation of CSE from recruitment curves. Hypoxia enhanced CSE sensitivity at lower intensities, whereas responsiveness was attenuated at higher intensities within the sampled range, potentially due to metabolic constraints. Hyperoxia increased CSE at higher intensities within the sampled range, while saturation could not be accurately estimated with the current sampling. Recruitment curves demonstrated distinct mechanisms, with hypoxia lowering the half-maximal intensity and hyperoxia increasing maximum excitability and slope steepness. These findings show that oxygen levels can modulate CSE in humans, revealing a critical mechanism for enhancing plasticity. Oxygen-based interventions may offer a promising route for improving neurorehabilitation outcomes in clinical populations.

items.title: Stimulus prior and reward probability differentially affect response bias in perceptual decision making.
items.abstract: Signal detection theory posits that subjects in two-stimulus, two-choice discrimination tasks decide by comparing random samples of an evidence variable to a static decision criterion. While the core assumptions of the theory have received ample experimental support, it has become evident that the decision criterion is not static but subject to trial-by-trial fluctuations and can be influenced by experimental manipulations. The mechanisms governing the trial-by-trial criterion changes are however not well understood. Here, we report results from five experiments in which we subjected rats to a two-stimulus, two-choice auditory discrimination task. In the first three experiments, we investigated the effects of stimulus presentation ratios and reward ratios and provide clear evidence that the effects of changing reward ratios are more pronounced than those of stimulus presentation ratios. A model-based analysis revealed that this effect was due to more than tenfold higher learning rates when reward ratios were manipulated. In two separate experiments, we investigated the effect of reward density (i.e., global reward rate) on criterion learning but failed to find consistent effects. A systematic comparison of three different trial-by-trial criterion learning models based on detection theory, the matching law, and reinforcement learning showed that no model was able to capture the differential effects of stimulus presentation and reward ratios. We conclude that subjects explicitly represent either prior stimulus probabilities or entire stimulus distributions, and accordingly future models need to represent these factors as well.

items.title: Ask, don't assume: Editorial and Data Integrity Triage (EDIT), an editor's practice-based checklist for screening manuscripts at submission.
items.abstract: As an editor, I regularly find problems in submitted manuscripts that need explaining before peer review can begin. A reference cannot be found, participant numbers in the abstract differ from those in the tables, or the methods do not explain the results. Most have an honest explanation, but some do not, and paper mills and text produced by artificial intelligence (AI) add to the pressure on editors. My message in this paper is simple. When something does not add up, editors should ask the authors a specific question before assuming anything, and they should judge the work itself and leave aside who wrote it. I describe Editorial and Data Integrity Triage (EDIT), a checklist I developed from my editorial work at the Journal of Hospital Infection and from academic integrity practice. EDIT has 20 checks in five domains covering reporting, methods and data, references, authorship and declarations, and submission files. Ten core checks can be applied to every submission and the others when they are relevant. Each finding leads to routine handling, a request for clarification or a pause for senior assessment. Writing style, a free email account, an incomplete author profile, the authors' country and unusually tidy data are not treated as evidence of a problem. A fictional example follows one submission from the first checks to an editorial decision, and I identify the checks that peer reviewers can use. EDIT reflects one editor's practice, and independent review and testing are needed before it is used routinely.

items.title: Acute aerobic exercise and orbitofrontal cortex reactivity during positive emotion processing in obesity: An exploratory fNIRS study.
items.abstract: Objective This exploratory functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) study examined positive emotional processing in obese college students and pre-post associations of affect and prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation with acute aerobic exercise. Methods Thirty-six students (18 obese, 18 normal body mass index [BMI]) were recruited; two normal-BMI controls were excluded after fNIRS quality control. The Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS) assessed affect. PFC activation was measured during passive emotional picture viewing and active picture description. The obese group completed 30-min moderate-intensity cycling (70.5±1.6% age-predicted maximum heart rate; 82.8±13.6% time in target zone) and was reassessed after standardized recovery. Results At baseline, obese participants reported lower positive affect (PA; Cohen's d=0.71) and lower right orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) activation during picture description (d=0.97, false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected p=0.040); left OFC and bilateral dorsolateral PFC (dlPFC) differences were non-significant (FDR-corrected p ≥ 0.220), and no passive-viewing comparison survived correction. Post-exercise, PA was higher (d=0.74) with greater right OFC activation in the same task (d=0.66, FDR-corrected p=0.040); no other region changed. With n=18, minimum detectable paired effect was d≈0.71; null dlPFC findings are inconclusive. Conclusion Obese students showed lower baseline PA and right OFC activation during active positive elaboration; post-exercise PA and right OFC activation were higher in the same context. These single-arm associations cannot be attributed to exercise; right OFC is a preliminary trial signal, dlPFC involvement cannot be excluded, and effect estimates can inform randomized controlled trials.

items.title: Effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on post-task heart rate variability and visual attention during an empathy-for-pain task.
items.abstract: Empathy for pain enables individuals to understand others' suffering and can promote prosocial behavior, yet how transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) modulates this process remains unclear. The relationship between interoception and empathy is also complex. This study therefore investigated the effects of taVNS on empathy for pain and explored the potential contribution of interoception. Participants were randomly assigned to a taVNS group receiving stimulation at the cymba conchae or a sham group receiving stimulation at the earlobe. Before and after stimulation, participants completed questionnaires assessing interoception and empathy, performed an empathy-for-pain task with concurrent eye-tracking, and underwent resting-state electrocardiographic (ECG) recording. Two group × time interactions emerged as the primary findings. Low-to-high frequency ratio (LF/HF) of heart rate variability increased from pretest to posttest in the sham group but remained relatively stable in the taVNS group. For eye-tracking metrics, duration of first fixation increased from pretest to posttest in the taVNS group but not in the sham group. These findings suggest that taVNS may modulate early visual attentional processing during empathy for pain, potentially promoting greater initial attentional engagement. These results provide preliminary evidence that vagal stimulation may influence attentional processes involved in empathy for pain.

items.title: Childhood coercive control and suicide: An under-recognised pathway via entrapment.
items.abstract: Childhood experiences of domestic violence (also referred to as domestic abuse, in the context of parental intimate partner violence/abuse) is a well-established risk factor for adverse mental health outcomes, including suicidality. However, dominant measurement approaches continue to prioritise discrete incidents of physical violence, obscuring coercive control as a pervasive and chronic pattern of harm. This narrow framing limits understanding of how children's experiences of parental domestic violence create risk for suicide. This article reconceptualises childhood experiences of coercive control as a distinct and underexamined risk factor for suicidality. We advance the understanding of entrapment as a central mechanism through which coercive control may contribute to suicidality and identify critical gaps in current evidence and measurement approaches. Coercive control operates across the family unit and frequently persists following parental separation, creating developmental environments characterised by chronic fear, enforced dependency, and constrained autonomy. We argue that these conditions may give rise to a sustained sense of entrapment, a risk factor for suicidality, positioning childhood experiences of coercive control as an under-recognised pathway to suicide-related outcomes among children and young people. Childhood experiences of coercive control are inadequately measured in research, with suicidality largely overlooked as an outcome, obscuring the true extent and impact of the problem. Better pattern-based measurement and recognition across research, clinical practice and family courts could improve identification of abuse and strengthen safeguarding.

items.title: Disruptions in mentalizing trauma across the prenatal and postnatal periods: Stability and associations with environmental stressors and infant development.
items.abstract: Disruptions in trauma-specific reflective functioning (T-RF) among parents are linked to poorer mental health and parental functioning, whereas effective T-RF is a key protective factor. However, the natural trajectory of T-RF and its association with infant development remain unclear. This longitudinal study examined trait- and state-like features of disruptions in T-RF from pregnancy to postpartum, and its associations with infant development. A sample of 185 pregnant women were recruited during the second trimester (T1) and followed up in the third trimester (T2), as well as between five and 14 months postpartum (T3). Self-report questionnaires were used to assess T-RF at all three time points and stressful life events and infant development at T3. Latent growth curve analyses showed significant interindividual variability at baseline (M = 22.82, p < 0.001; s2 = 135.59, p < 0.001), but overall stability across time (M = -0.33, p = 0.49; s2 = 6.40, p = 0.57), supporting its trait-like features. Greater exposure to prenatal stressful life events was associated with greater prenatal disruptions in T-RF (β = 0.17, p = 0.03), a finding that is consistent with, but does not establish, the possibility that T-RF may exhibit state-like characteristic. Higher disruptions in prenatal T-RF prospectively predicted infant developmental difficulties (β = -0.23, p = 0.01). This study suggests that T-RF primarily reflects stable individual differences and is associated with infant development. Future research should examine whether enhancing prenatal T-RF through psychological interventions can promote infant development.

items.title: Acculturation and adjustment: Factors affecting acculturation and psychosocial adjustment among international students in China.
items.abstract: Most acculturation research has focused on Western societies, leaving limited evidence from non-Western contexts such as China. This cross-sectional study addressed that gap by examining the associations of integration and contextual factors with international students' psychosocial adjustment in China. Using a bidimensional framework, we assessed mainstream and heritage cultural orientations, a derived integration index, and contextual variables including English and Chinese proficiency, perceived cultural distance, and anticipated acceptance. A total of 461 international students enrolled in Chinese universities, predominantly Pakistani (70.5%), completed measures of depression, sociocultural difficulties, and acculturative stress. Hierarchical regression analyses revealed that integration was associated with fewer sociocultural difficulties (β = - 0.22, p = .043), lower acculturative stress (β = -0.34, p = .001), and better overall adjustment (β = 0.26, p = .011). Integration accounted for modest additional variance in these outcomes (ΔR 2 = 0.008-0.023). Neither mainstream nor heritage orientation was significantly associated with overall adjustment in the final model. Anticipated acceptance (β = 0.13, p = .010) and English proficiency (β = 0.11, p = .020) were positively associated with overall adjustment, whereas Chinese proficiency (β = - 0.25, p < .001) and perceived cultural distance (β = - 0.16, p = .001) showed negative adjusted associations. The unexpected association with Chinese proficiency warrants further investigation. These findings provide context specific evidence on acculturation and adjustment, while the cross sectional design and sample composition limit causal inference and generalizability.

items.title: Those with graft length of 25 mm or more inside the femoral tunnel were not at lower risk of graft tear in soccer players submitted to anatomical anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
items.abstract: Introduction/objectives Anatomical anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction can lead to shorter femoral tunnels, which can have decreased load capacity to failure. How much graft needs to be inside the femoral tunnel to allow proper graft integration and protect against graft tears remains unclear. The primary aim was to compare the rate of graft tear after ACL reconstruction in high-level soccer players between those with 25 mm or more of length of graft within the femoral tunnel (vs 20-24 mm). Methods A total of 63 soccer players (mean age 22 ± 5.2 years, male-to-female ratio of 6:1) with a Tegner score ≥9 who underwent anatomical ACL reconstruction using the arthroscopic antero-medial technique with hamstrings autograft between January 2021 and May 2024 were included. The primary outcomes were the incidence of graft tear and the length of graft within the femoral tunnel. The secondary outcomes included graft diameter and femoral tunnel length. Patients were followed for 24 months to evaluate new knee injuries, graft tear, and return-to-sports (RTS) rates. RTS was defined as rejoining previous competitive sports. Results Seven athletes (11.1%) suffered a graft tear. The overall RTS rate was 71% (45/63, secondary outcome), while the new knee injury rate was 19.1% (12/63) (secondary outcome). Graft length within the femoral tunnel was 24.3 ± 2.3 mm (20-28 mm) and was not significantly different between those with and without graft tear (23.8 mm vs 24.4 mm, p = 0.08). Similarly, total femoral tunnel length (p = 0.47), concomitant knee injuries (p = 0.32) and graft diameter (p = 0.67) were not statistically significantly different between those with and without graft tear. Conclusions The ACL graft length inside the femoral tunnel was not different between those with and without graft tear in a limited sample of 63 high-level soccer players undergoing anatomical ACL reconstruction with hamstrings autograft and followed for 2 years. Aiming for 25 mm or more of graft inside the femoral tunnel does not seem to provide an advantage in reducing the risk of graft tears as compared to 20-24 mm. Level of evidence III.

items.title: When told what to do, girls persist less: Ineffective instruction selectively lowers preschool girls' exploratory behavior and subsequent persistence.
items.abstract: Children's persistence is associated with future success, such as academic achievement. Therefore, researchers have examined individual differences that influence persistence. One factor that shapes persistence is how children respond to ineffective instructions. Previous research using a challenging, self-terminated task in which children attempted to open an unsolvable box showed that children who divested from ineffective instructions and used self-generated strategies persisted longer. As girls are socialized to follow instructions more closely than boys, they also may be less likely to divest from ineffective instructions. This reduced divestment limits girls' opportunities to use self-generated strategies, which, in turn, may lower their persistence. To examine this possibility, we conducted a secondary analysis of data collected between 2020 and 2024 from 157 Japanese 4-5-year-olds. The children were divided into two conditions: one that received ineffective instructions and one that did not. We found gender differences in responses to ineffective instructions and persistence only under the instruction condition. When ineffective instructions were provided, girls showed, on average, less divestment from ineffective instructions and the diversity of self-generated strategies, and lower persistence than boys. However, when no ineffective instructions were provided, these gender differences were not observed. These findings suggest that average gender differences in responses to ineffective instructions and persistence emerge in early childhood.

items.title: Communication about color over the life span.
items.abstract: Color communication is more than a naming game where the informant names each color: the color terms must also be understood by the listener. Here, we studied how participants' productive and receptive vocabularies affect communication about color over the life span. Human participants, 3-72 years old, played a color communication game. As "senders", participants named 15 or 30 color samples presented singly. Then, as "receivers", they selected from their palette of 15 or 30 colors the sample that corresponded to color term "messages," which were either their own color terms (self-communication) or another participant's color terms (interpersonal communication). The number of color terms in participants' vocabularies, their fraction correct performance for self-communication, and their fraction correct for interpersonal communication, all matured continuously until at least age 21, and were highly correlated with each other. Simulations using a quantitative model of the communication task showed that performance for self-communication was determined by the number of color terms the participant provided in the color-naming phase (color term production), with some forgetting of how they had previously named the samples. The simulation predicted no association between participant age and performance on the interpersonal communication task. Contrary to that prediction, interpersonal communication improved throughout the age range. Further analysis showed that performance for interpersonal communication was independently controlled by life-long improvement in participants' ability to understand terms provided by others (color term comprehension). Therefore, color term production and color term comprehension are distinct abilities, which mature independently across the life span.

items.title: Influence of psychobiological predictors on the outcome of patients after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
items.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is a standard treatment for hematologic diseases. While biological predictors of transplant success are well established, psychobiological factors such as depression and physical activity remain underexplored. This study investigates their influence on clinical outcomes and quality of life after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In this prospective study, 42 patients undergoing transplantation (December 2020- December 2021) were assessed at four time points (T0-T3). Depression was assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, physical activity using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire, and quality of life using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Leukemia and its Trial Outcome Index subscore. Bivariate correlations (p-value <0.05) were used to examine associations with clinical endpoints (leukocyte engraftment, GVHD, adverse events ≥ Grade III, relapse, mortality, and quality of life at six months). Higher depression at T0 (Mean: 6.53; SD: 4.98) predicted lower global quality of life at T3 (r = -0.46; p = 0.04), but not clinical outcomes. Physical activity at T0 (Mean: 4290.3; SD: 4242.7) showed no significant associations. Older age (Mean: 57.7; SD: 10.2) was linked to a better Trial Outcome Index (r = 0.5; p = 0.02), higher global quality of life (r = 0.45; p = 0.04), and lower depression (r = -0.56; p = 0.005) at T3. Complications had no effect on quality of life or depression. Depression before allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may predict poorer quality of life afterward. Older age was associated with better outcomes, suggesting rigid age limits for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation should be re-evaluated.

items.title: Family Structure Theory: Understanding the Role of Childhood Household Composition on Life Outcomes.
items.abstract: Family Structure Theory (FST) provides a conceptual framework for understanding the higher rate of incarceration observed in children from single-mother families without significant co-parenting arrangements, or extended and multigenerational family support. Persistent inequities have been observed in social, financial, educational, legal, and health outcomes amongst this cohort compared to their two-or-more caregiver peers. Empirical research consistently demonstrates that, on average, children nurtured in this context suffer more disadvantaged outcomes than their peers, yet traditional explanations-such as socioeconomic deprivation, parental education, historical oppression, and current systemic discrimination-fail to fully account for the observed differences after adjustment. FST posits that household composition exerts an independent and measurable effect on child development, functioning as an independent determinant rather than merely a correlate. Drawing upon interdisciplinary evidence from sociology, developmental psychology, public health, criminology, and public policy, the theory identifies three principal pathways - time and attention, economic resources, and social capital -through which family structure shapes lifelong trajectories. Importantly, these mechanisms operate beyond traditional socioeconomic, structural, and environmental variables, suggesting that interventions must address more than material deprivation or location of habitation. FST underscores the importance of replicating or substituting the protective and developmental functions of multi-caregiver households in social programs targeting single-mother families. By centering the family unit as a foundational determinant of measurable outcomes, Family Structure Theory provides a more comprehensive model for explaining life course disparities and guiding future policy, research, and interventions designed to help remove these inequities.

items.title: Investigating 24-Hour Movement Behaviors in Young People With Learning Disabilities: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Study.
items.abstract: Background Physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep play a key role in the health and development of young people. This has led to the development of guidelines on PA, SB, and sleep for children and young people aged 5 to 17 years. Adherence to these integrated guidelines is associated with favorable physical, mental, and cognitive health outcomes. However, evidence regarding 24-hour movement behaviors (MBs) among young people with learning disabilities is scarce, particularly in the United Kingdom, where no studies have comprehensively examined adherence to all guideline components or explored the factors influencing these behaviors in this population. Objective This study aims to investigate 24-hour MBs among young people with learning disabilities in Scotland, United Kingdom; determine adherence to PA, SB, screen time, and sleep recommendations; assess the feasibility and acceptability of measuring 24-hour MBs in this population; and explore individual, social, and environmental barriers to and facilitators of MBs. Methods This mixed methods study recruited young people aged 11 to 17 years who attended secondary schools for children with additional support needs (ASN) in Scotland. Participants were asked to wear an ActiGraph GT3X accelerometer continuously for 7 consecutive days to objectively assess PA, SB, and sleep. Parent- and youth-completed diaries captured sleep schedules, screen time, and monitored nonwear periods. Individualized activity profiles were produced to summarize participants' daily MBs and support engagement in the qualitative phase. A purposive subsample participated in semistructured interviews exploring experiences, barriers, and facilitators associated with MBs. Quantitative data will be analyzed descriptively to determine MB patterns and guideline adherence, while qualitative data will undergo thematic analysis informed by the capability, opportunity, and motivation-behavior (COM-B) model, the theoretical domains framework and the behavior change wheel. Results The study was funded by the Baily Thomas Charitable Fund from April 2025 to July 2026. Ethics approval was granted by the University of Strathclyde Ethics Committee (UEC25/10). Recruitment and data collection were completed in June 2026 across participating ASN schools in Scotland. This manuscript describes the study protocol and planned analyses; however, data cleaning and analysis were ongoing at the time of submission. Quantitative and qualitative findings are expected to be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations during 2027. Conclusions This study is among the first in the United Kingdom to comprehensively examine all components of the 24-hour MB framework in young people with learning disabilities using objective measurement and qualitative inquiry. The findings will provide important evidence on MB patterns, guideline adherence, and modifiable determinants of behavior, informing the development of theory-informed, inclusive interventions designed to improve health and well-being among young people with learning disabilities. items.title: Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Panic Disorder Among Arabic-Speaking Patients: Case Series.
items.abstract: Background Internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (ICBT) has shown promise for the treatment of panic disorder (PD), but little is known about its feasibility and use across cultures and languages. Objective This study examines the feasibility and preliminary outcomes of an Arabic-translated ICBT program for PD and describes how patients experienced the program. Methods Six Arabic-speaking women (aged 21-50 years, mean 35, SD 10 years) with a primary diagnosis of PD underwent a 16-week guided ICBT program using an Arabic-translated protocol. PD symptoms (Panic Disorder Severity Scale-Self-Report [PDSS-SR]), anxiety sensitivity (Anxiety Sensitivity Index-3 [ASI-3]), and agoraphobic avoidance (Mobility Inventory [MI]) were assessed pretreatment, posttreatment, and 3 months later. The outcomes were analyzed descriptively. Four patients also participated in individual, semistructured posttreatment interviews about their experience of the program, which are reported descriptively as the patient-perspective component of the case series. Results The program was completed by 4 of the 6 (67%) patients. Among completers, PDSS-SR scores decreased from 11-18 pretreatment to 0-7 posttreatment, ASI-3 scores decreased from 18-59 to 0-4, and MI scores decreased from 1.44-3.82 to 0.00-1.60, indicating reduced agoraphobic avoidance. Follow-up data were available for 3 of the 4 (75%) completers: 2 maintained their gains, and 1 showed a partial return of symptoms. The fourth reported a recurrence of symptoms posttreatment but could not be reached for follow-up. During the interviews, all 4 patients expressed positive views of the program. Conclusions Arabic-translated ICBT appeared feasible and was associated with reductions in panic symptoms and anxiety sensitivity among Arabic-speaking patients with mild-to-moderate PD. These preliminary findings support further investigation with larger samples.
