items.title: Mobile Health Apps for Individuals Who Are Blind or Have Low Vision: Systematic Review of Evidence, Accessibility, and App Quality.
items.abstract: Background Individuals who are blind or have low vision experience disproportionate burdens in both physical and psychological functioning, and mobile health apps may help address some of these needs. However, their availability, accessibility, and empirical support for this population remain unclear. Objective This systematic review aimed to identify mobile health apps relevant to supporting physical and psychological functioning in individuals who are blind or have low vision, summarize the empirical evidence available for these apps, and examine their accessibility and quality. Methods We used a multicomponent approach that combined (1) identification of apps through organizational recommendations; (2) a systematic search of the scientific literature, conducted and reported in accordance with PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines; and (3) an exploratory accessibility and app quality appraisal using the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 and the Mobile App Development and Assessment Guide. Results A total of 19 unique mobile health apps were identified after combining and deduplicating apps identified through organizational recommendations and scientific literature. Fifteen apps were identified through organizational recommendations, and 14 empirical studies evaluating 11 apps were included in the qualitative synthesis. Only a subset of these studies specifically involved blind or low-vision participants; several evaluated apps in broader clinical or general populations where visual impairment status was not reported. The identified apps focused primarily on physical functioning, particularly medication management, glucose monitoring, pharmaceutical information access, and health care access. No apps primarily designed to support psychological functioning in individuals who are blind or have low vision were identified. Of 14 studies, 6 (43%) were rated as being of good methodological quality. The exploratory user-informed accessibility appraisal showed variability across apps: MyPills received the most favorable accessibility profile, with "High" ratings across all 4 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines principles, whereas several organizationally recommended apps received low ratings across most principles. Mobile App Development and Assessment Guide scores ranged from 8/39 to 34/39, with Medisafe scoring highest. Conclusions The current landscape of mobile health apps for individuals who are blind or have low vision remains limited, uneven in accessibility and quality, and supported by a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. The absence of identified apps targeting psychological functioning represents a particularly important gap. Improving the development and implementation of mobile health apps for individuals who are blind or have low vision will require more than increasing the number of available apps; it will require apps that are accessible from the outset, rigorously evaluated, and developed with the people they are intended to serve.

items.title: Text Psychometrics: Assessing psychological constructs in text using natural language processing.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language processing (NLP). Yet when used to assess psychological constructs in text, they are generally not evaluated for the types of validity, reliability, and standardization typically expected from traditional questionnaires with rating scales. This study bridges that gap by proposing a framework for evaluating the psychometric properties of NLP-based psychological assessments (including LLMs-based ones), an area of research we refer to as Text Psychometrics. We first review different NLP methods, compare their ability to address key challenges in psychological research such as explainability, and outline ways of evaluating them on many desirable psychometric properties. Our goal is to describe most psychometric properties that may be of interest, especially for psychology and NLP researchers who are less familiar with psychometrics or psychometricians who are less familiar with NLP. We then illustrate the tradeoffs of different NLP methods through two empirical studies. Study 1 classifies thousands of crisis counseling conversations and Reddit posts into different types of mental health issues and introduces a novel method to evaluate text models for content validity-the extent to which a test captures the full range of expressions of a single construct. Study 2 examines prospective criterion validity by estimating how 49 known suicide risk factors predict imminent risk in crisis counseling conversations. We find that mentioning lethal means for suicide, the police, depressed mood, and anxiety in text as well as the texter writing more than the counselor characterize the conversations that end up needing an emergency service intervention for imminent suicide risk, which showcases the interpretability of the method that was used. In sum, NLP studies in psychology often rely on only a few validation metrics; here, we demonstrate the need for broader psychometric evaluation and, as a step towards Text Psychometrics, provide practical examples and future directions that can help researchers evaluate these models.

items.title: When shifts matter for hybrid teams: The moderating role of location predictability.
items.abstract: In recent years, changes to the nature of work and evolving employee preferences have led to the rise of hybrid teams. In contrast to traditional teams, hybrid teams frequently shift between remote and face-to-face interaction. This structure raises new questions about how such dynamism impacts team engagement, an emergent state typically thought to develop under long periods of stability and face-to-face interaction. Drawing on the boundary transition theory of dynamic teamwork, we theorize that weekly downshifts in face-to-face interaction (i.e., relative decreases from the prior week) harm weekly team engagement and performance, but only for teams with lower levels of location predictability-an important yet understudied differentiator of hybrid team functioning. To test these ideas, we use a within-team, repeated-measures field survey design with a sample of hybrid sales teams at a large alcohol distributor in China. We surveyed 164 hybrid teams and their supervisors across 6 weeks (648 team-level weekly responses) to capture shifts in team work locations and examine their impact on weekly team engagement and performance. Results supported our hypotheses. By focusing on the role of weekly fluctuations in team structures and how location predictability shapes these effects, we advance our understanding of the unique and dynamic nature of hybrid teams. items.title: From patient to purpose: How a cancer diagnosis creates existential liminality to motivate crafting for work-related generativity.
items.abstract: The life-threatening nature of cancer makes it a unique work-life shock event with distinctive implications for one's work and life. Drawing on inductive analysis of 50 employees with cancer, we theorize how this life-threatening, dynamic work-life shock event forces a reckoning with mortality that existing theory has not captured. This occurs through a process we label existential liminality, where people grapple with tensions of time and meaning, reflecting on what is meaningful in paid and unpaid work within an unknowable mortal timeline. When people have the cognitive space to engage in this process (i.e., when demands are manageable and resources are sufficient), existential liminality can catalyze crafting for generativity across paid and unpaid work. This work extends work-life shock events theory by revealing existential liminality as a unique sensemaking process that differs meaningfully from the identity-focused processes this theory describes. We also challenge the dominant death anxiety-based paradigm in the death awareness research by centering death reflection, a positive but undertheorized pathway with significant consequences for how people invest in work activities. Confronting death, we find, can prompt people to pursue a positive, lasting impact on others through work-related crafting for generativity. items.title: Cultural variability in the link between affect and meaning in life: Evidence from 69 countries.
items.abstract: People tend to evaluate their lives as more meaningful when they experience more positive affect and less negative affect. However, most evidence for this association comes from Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic societies, which are culturally distinctive in their strong emphasis on happiness. To assess the cross-cultural generality of the affect-meaning link, we conducted the largest cross-cultural investigation of this association to date. Between 2022 and 2024, we collected data from 18,672 individuals across 69 countries spanning all inhabited continents. Across cultures, the association between affect and meaning was largely robust: Positive affect was positively related to meaning in life in 62 countries, and negative affect was negatively related to meaning in 57 countries. At the same time, substantial cross-cultural variation emerged. Multilevel analyses indicated that both associations were, on average, somewhat stronger in Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic countries than in most other regions. Moreover, a cross-level interaction showed that the links between affect (both positive and negative) and meaning were stronger in countries that more strongly idealize happiness, even after accounting for national differences in wealth, religiosity, and life satisfaction. Cross-cultural differences were more pronounced for the association between negative affect and meaning than for the association involving positive affect. Meaning was consistently associated with all eight discrete emotions. However, cultural valuation of happiness moderated only the associations with fear, shame, sadness, anger, and gratitude, with weaker evidence for relaxedness and excitement and no moderation observed for love. Together, these findings suggest that while affective experiences are a widespread basis for evaluating meaning in life, their psychological significance is amplified in Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic cultural contexts that place greater emphasis on happiness. items.title: Emotional reactivity, emotion perception, and emotional empathy.
items.abstract: Neuropsychological models of emotion posit that we simulate the feelings of others in ourselves as a means to understand them. Accordingly, people who are more emotionally reactive may be better at simulation and responding to the emotions of others. This study aimed to examine the relationship between emotional responsivity and emotion perception in normal adults and to determine whether these factors change with age. A trait measure of emotional reactivity (Perth Emotional Reactivity Scale), a naturalistic video measure of emotion perception (Complex Audio-Visual Emotion Assessment Task-Short), and a trait measure of emotional empathy (Balanced Emotional Empathy Scale) were administered to 369 normal healthy adults 24-83 years of age using a digital research platform. People high in negative reactivity (and low in positive reactivity) were more accurate recognizing negative emotional expressions (small to medium effects: r = -.130 to -.203). People high in positive reactivity tended to self-report greater emotional empathy (r = .441-.443). There were no differences across age groups, although there was an indication that older adults self-reported fewer negative mood states (Depression Anxiety Stress Scale). We found a relationship between responsivity and emotion perception, consistent with the simulation model of emotion processing, but specifically for negative reactivity. The results suggest that high positive reactivity, likely reflecting good emotion regulation, is aligned with empathy. Older adults do not show a decrement if we use naturalistic video materials to assess emotion perception. These findings require replication in a more culturally diverse sample but have interesting implications for rehabilitation. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Examining the gender-equality paradox in values using a new measure of value-based gender typicality.
items.abstract: This study examined changes in gender differences in human values as a function of country-level gender equality (GE) and time. We used a novel gender-typicality approach and data from the European Social Survey collected between 2002 and 2023 (34 countries, N = 439,389). We assess whether gender differences in values are associated with countries' levels of GE; whether these differences diverge, converge, or remain stable over time; and whether increases in GE predict changes in gender gaps in values. Preregistered confirmatory analyses showed that men and women both reported, on average, significantly lower male value-based typicality in countries with higher GE. Results using single-value types showed similar patterns, that is, men and women's values shifted in the same directions as a function of GE. Additional exploratory country-specific analyses using single-value types and younger respondents also supported this pattern. Trends also varied by region, with Nordic and Western European countries generally showing decreases in male typicality, while post-Communist countries showed increases. Regarding time, the overall gender difference in the multivariate gender value typicality composite was smaller in 2023 than in 2002, though the effect of time on values was nonsignificant for both genders. In sum, while we found small gender differences in the relationship between country-level GE and values, the results overall did not support the gender-equality paradox in the domain of values. The real paradox may involve methodological confusion between cross-level and country-level relationships. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: A systematic investigation of age-gender intersectional stereotypes and their consequences.
items.abstract: Research on age and gender stereotypes has largely examined these dimensions in isolation or reduced their intersection to broad perceptions of warmth and competence. To foster a more nuanced understanding of age-gender intersecting stereotypes, the present research offers a systematic, inductive-deductive investigation of stereotype content toward individuals with intersecting age and gender identities. Using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, Study 1 inductively develops and validates six target-specific stereotype measurement models comprising 22 stereotype dimensions capturing mixed-valence content of younger, middle-aged, and older women and men. Study 2 uses a deductive approach to categorize these dimensions into a framework distinguishing interactive, additive, age-based, and gender-based stereotypes, with multiple interactive or additive stereotypes emerging for each age-gender target. Study 3 establishes the convergent and discriminant validity of these dimensions and finds evidence that some dimensions predict attitudes beyond established models of person perception. Finally, Study 4 demonstrates that age-gender targets are differentially assigned to organizational roles that align with stereotype content associated with their groups and that role-relevant stereotype dimensions predict hiring decisions beyond broader perceptions of warmth and competence. Overall, the present studies highlight the complex interplay between age and gender in shaping stereotype content, show the consequences of these stereotypes in real-world contexts, contribute to ongoing social-psychological arguments for going beyond warmth and competence in stereotype models, and ultimately, lay essential groundwork for further empirical investigations on an increasingly timely topic. items.title: Navigating divorce and partner bereavement: Personality and trajectories of change in life satisfaction and mental health.
items.abstract: Dissolutions of romantic relationships can elicit diverse reactions across various aspects of well-being, but they also offer an opportunity to examine which factors promote resilience and identify individuals at risk. In this preregistered multisample longitudinal study, we examined the heterogeneity in life satisfaction and mental health changes around and during divorce or partner bereavement and whether personality (i.e., traits and resilient vs. nonresilient personality profiles) may explain individual differences in change trajectories. Data from 1,306 divorcees and 1,150 bereaved partners were drawn from nationally representative panel studies in the Netherlands (N = 12,551), Germany (N = 10,830), and China (N = 28,628) and analyzed using growth mixture modeling. Four life satisfaction trajectories and three mental health trajectories were identified for each event. Recovery and resilience emerged as the most common trajectories across events, outcomes, and samples. Among personality factors, neuroticism was the most consistent predictor of a lower likelihood of belonging to a resilience trajectory. This study advanced the generalizability of findings across diverse loss-based events, populations, and aspects of well-being. The findings further underscore the influence of neuroticism in shaping, and potentially complicating, psychological adjustment surrounding divorce and partner bereavement. items.title: The structure and history of English words that describe people.
items.abstract: The English language is filled with words that are used to describe people, such as "nice," "skilled," "conservative," and "attractive." This broad trait space includes words that describe personality but also words that describe people's physical, sociodemographic, and ideological differences. Here we define trait space as the sum of stable, comparative, and socially meaningful descriptors and map this space by combining large language models, human ratings, and historical text analyses. Across four studies, we (a) introduce a comprehensive trait list (2,847 trait words); (b) establish normative human ratings of these words (3,070 English speakers) along 24 dimensions drawn from prior literature; (c) identify a four-factor structure of fitness, agency, communion, and traditionalism from these dimensions, which covers 95.4% of trait words; and (d) reveal systematic differences in the coherence, valence, and evolution of these factors. Specifically, these four factors differ in their coherence (e.g., communion is the most semantically coherent while traditionalism the least), valence (e.g., communion and agency show more alignment between their semantic direction and valence than traditionalism and fitness; communion has more negative words while agency and traditionalism more positive ones), and historical usage (e.g., fitness and communion are older than traditionalism; communion is converging in semantic space while agency diverging). These findings showcase new large language model-based methods for discovering and analyzing trait words. We close by motivating a functional constructionist view: The meaning, structure, and use of traits constitute a culturally constructed toolkit that represents socially relevant individual differences to help navigate recurring interaction problems. items.title: Understanding the impact of racism in Canada using the Racial Trauma Scale.
items.abstract: Equitable and inclusive mental health care requires the ability to identify/measure symptoms to inform client diagnosis and care, regardless of race. Yet, due to unfamiliarity, a skills deficit, discomfort, and an absence of appropriate tools, many clinicians fail to identify racial trauma. The Racial Trauma Scale (RTS) is a novel self-assessment measure for quantifying distress symptoms due to racism. Using the RTS, this study aimed to understand the impact of racial trauma among racialized individuals residing in Canada. A sample of 756 racially diverse participants from across Canada completed a battery of measures, RTS included, to establish the validity of the scale and better understand racial trauma in racialized Canadians. RTS scores were positively correlated (large effect) with measures of depression, anxiety, posttraumatic stress disorder, and posttraumatic cognitions. Reliability was excellent in both English and French versions of the scale (Cronbach α = .98) and in the nine-item short version (α = .95 and α = .93, respectively). Among racialized groups, racial trauma severity was highest in Black (M = 62.11; SD = 23.19) and lowest in Asian respondents (M = 51.32; SD = 22.04). White respondents reported notably lower racial trauma severity (M = 36.36; SD = 15.16). There were also significant differences in RTS scores across provinces, with the highest scores in the Atlantic region. Findings indicate that clinicians can use the RTS to identify racism-related distress and symptoms to target for intervention. Results highlight the need for culturally informed assessment and intervention of this prevalent and debilitating condition. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Posttraumatic stress disorder and racism-based traumatic stress: Not one and the same.
items.abstract: It remains unclear the extent to which symptoms of racism-based traumatic stress (RBTS) and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) reflect distinguishable experiential profiles or are better characterized by a general traumatic stress construct. The present study sought to address this gap by utilizing bifactor modeling to disambiguate shared and unique variance between RBTS and PTSD. Participants were a national sample of 651 ethnoracially minoritized adolescents living in the United States (51.61% male; 44.24% Black; Mage = 14.54, SDage = 1.63). Participants completed the Child PTSD Symptom Scale for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition-Self-Report and the Youth Racism-Based Traumatic Stress Symptom Scale. Findings indicate little evidence of a reliable and valid global factor comprising general and racism-specific traumatic stress symptoms. Rather, PTSD and RBTS emerged as moderately correlated but distinguishable constructs that demonstrate independent and discriminant validity with racism-related measures. Findings suggest that RBTS and PTSD are not reducible to a single traumatic stress construct among ethnoracially minoritized youth. Results underscore the importance of assessing RBTS with measures designed to specifically capture traumatic stress responses to racism. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Differentiating risk and maintaining factors of posttraumatic stress and prolonged grief in the aftermath of death: A longitudinal study on traumatic loss.
items.abstract: Traumatic losses can lead to posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and prolonged grief disorder (PGD). This study is the first to examine both constructs longitudinally immediately following traumatic losses, focusing on risk and maintaining factors. Data were collected immediately after the loss (Time Point 1, N = 126) and 6 months later (Time Point 2, N = 42). Participants were recruited by psychosocial crisis intervention teams. Variables assessed included sociodemographic and loss-related characteristics, PTSD, PGD, depression, generalized anxiety, life satisfaction, posttraumatic cognitions, social acknowledgment, and self-disclosure. Linear regression analyses identified common and specific predictors for symptom severity of PTSD and PGD at Time Points 1 and 2. Cross-lagged regression analyses investigated longitudinal associations between PTSD and PGD. Maintaining factors and comorbidities of PTSD and PGD symptomatology were explored at Time Point 2. Participants were significantly impacted by violent or sudden death circumstances, close relationships with the deceased, and high exposure levels. Dissociation predicted immediate and long-term PTSD symptom severity. A close relationship with the deceased was a distinct risk factor for PGD symptoms in the short and long term. Posttraumatic cognitions and generalized anxiety were maintaining factors for both disorders. Findings do not support a bidirectional longitudinal relationship between PTSD and PGD symptoms. The results are consistent with previous literature and, for the first time, extend these findings to the immediate aftermath of a loss. Dissociation and the relationship to the deceased should be considered in future research and practice regarding early screening, triage, and intervention, as well as posttraumatic cognitions for transdiagnostic treatment. items.title: Does perceiving immigration policy as unstable reduce immigrants' felt inclusion in the United States?
items.abstract: The instability of U.S. immigration policies has had deleterious consequences for the material and mental well-being of immigrants. Changes in policies serve as a powerful source of information about social norms, with downstream consequences for attitudes and beliefs. We examined whether perceiving immigration policy as unstable and harsh would have similar consequences for reducing immigrants' felt inclusion in the United States. Across two experiments with a general sample of immigrants and a sample of first- and second-generation immigrants with origins in Mexico, Central America, South America, or the Caribbean (N = 1,511), we manipulated immigrants' perceptions of immigration policy instability and punitiveness and examined their feelings of inclusion in the United States. Across experiments, immigrants' felt inclusion remained unchanged across conditions even when participants reported higher perceived immigration policy instability and punitiveness in the experimental condition. This consistent pattern suggests that immigrants' felt inclusion is resilient to heightened perceptions of immigration policy instability and punitiveness, potentially reflecting desensitization. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Linear and nonlinear associations between children's sleep-wake patterns and harsh parenting.
items.abstract: Harsh parenting is a consistent predictor of children's development, including their sleep. Yet little work has considered how school-age children's sleep may also influence parenting. Addressing this gap, we examined the prospective linear and nonlinear effects of children's sleep on change in harsh parenting over 1 year. Children (N = 298, 46% female, 63% White/European American, 37% Black/African American) and their parents from socioeconomically diverse backgrounds participated in two data collection waves (ages 10 and 11, respectively). Children's sleep was assessed at age 10 utilizing seven nights of actigraphy to derive measures of sleep duration (minutes), sleep quality (efficiency, activity), and chronobiology (sleep midpoint). Parents reported on harsh parenting at ages 10 and 11. Results from latent change score modeling supported a linear dose-response association between sleep activity and change in harsh parenting such that greater sleep activity predicted increases in harsh parenting, and lower sleep activity predicted declines or less steep increases in harsh parenting (β = 0.13). Sleep duration (β = -0.12) and sleep midpoint (β = -0.10) predicted change in harsh parenting in a nonlinear manner. Consistent with a threshold-acceleration model, shorter sleep duration and later sleep midpoint were weakly associated with increases in harsh parenting. After surpassing a critical threshold, beneficial associations emerged such that longer sleep duration and earlier sleep midpoint were progressively linked to declines in harsh parenting. Novel findings build on the literature by considering nonlinear predictors of parenting and applying nonlinear models of sleep to associations beyond developmental outcomes. items.title: Life satisfaction and motives for postponing parenthood among Polish women: A sequential indirect association model of depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination.
items.abstract: Postponed parenthood is an increasingly common feature of reproductive patterns in high- and middle-income societies. Although previous research has examined factors associated with delayed parenthood, less is known about the psychological characteristics linked to self-reported motives for postponement. The present study examined the relationship between life satisfaction and motives for postponing parenthood and tested a theoretically ordered cross-sectional model involving depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination. Participants were 201 childless Polish women aged 20-44 years (M = 32.75, SD = 6.91). They completed the Satisfaction with Life Scale, the Multidimensional Scale of Motives for Postponing Parenthood, the Brief Screen for Depression, the Dark Future Scale, and the Pure Procrastination Scale. Higher life satisfaction was negatively related to some, but not all, motive-specific outcomes and to depressive symptoms. Depressive symptoms were positively associated with future anxiety, which was, in turn, positively related to procrastination. Higher procrastination was linked to higher motive-specific and overall postponement scores. The hypothesized specific sequential indirect association of life satisfaction with motives through depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination was statistically supported for uncertainty and incompetence (B = -.0083, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0214, - .0007]), fear of change (B = -.0054, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0148, - .0003]), financial security concern (B = -.0095, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0229, - .0012]), and the overall motives score (B = -.0324, 95% bootstrap CI [-.0818, - .0027]). The corresponding sequential indirect associations were not supported for self-focus, parenthood as a burden, or worry about a child's future, indicating that the pattern differed across motives. Sensitivity analyses indicated that some outcome-specific sequential associations were not robust to the exclusion of potential multivariate outliers. Overall, the findings suggest that life satisfaction, depressive symptoms, future anxiety, and procrastination show distinct associations with self-reported reasons for postponing parenthood. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed sequential indirect associations should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal psychological mechanisms.

items.title: Problem-solving and social support appraisals in the cross-sectional association between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity.
items.abstract: The present study investigated the relationship between social media integration and PTSD-consistent symptomatology among South African university students, with a specific focus on the roles of problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support. Participants were 491 students who completed the Social Media Use Integration Scale, the Problem-Solving Inventory-20, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses with PROCESS. Social media integration was positively associated with overall PTSD-consistent symptomatology and all symptom clusters measured by the PCL-5. Problem-solving appraisal was negatively associated with PCL-5 symptom severity. It partially mediated the relationship between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity. Perceived social support showed a more selective pattern of association, with higher support linked to lower negative alterations in cognition and mood, as well as hyperarousal. In addition, social support moderated the relationship between social media use and PCL-5 symptom severity, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and hyperarousal. These findings suggest that greater social media integration is associated with higher PCL-5 symptom severity, whereas problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support serve as important protective factors. Interventions aimed at strengthening coping appraisals and supportive social networks may help reduce trauma-related distress among young adults in the context of frequent social media use.

items.title: Color-Blind Racial Attitudes and Clinician Evaluations of Patients in Clinical Trial Recruitment.
items.abstract: Across two studies, we examined whether endorsement of color-blind racial attitudes (color-blindness) impact perceptions of patient fit for clinical trials. Study 1 provided correlational evidence from a field sample of clinical research professionals indicating that, while patient race itself showed limited direct effects on perceptions of understandability, adherence, and suitability, color-blindness was consistently and negatively associated with evaluations of patient fit. Notably, color-blindness was specifically associated with lower perceived adherence for Black patients, a pattern not observed for other racial and ethnic groups. This suggests adherence perceptions as a potential mechanism linking color-blindness to referral disparities for Black patients. Study 2 extended the findings from Study 1 using a vignette-based experimental design among general healthcare providers, testing whether perceptions of a patient's ability to understand study protocols and to adhere to study requirements shape overall suitability judgments, and whether these pathways operate uniformly across patient racial groups. Using a serial mediation framework, we tested whether color-blindness priming influenced perceptions of suitability through perceptions of patients' ability to understand the protocol and their ability to adhere to study requirements. While results did not provide support for a robust effect of color-blind priming on perceptions of understandability, we did find that the inferential pathways linking patient information to study suitability judgments differed markedly by race and ethnicity. Specifically, the serial pathway from understandability to adherence to suitability held only for White patients. For Asian, Black, and Latino patients, understandability predicted suitability directly, without adherence serving as an intermediate step - suggesting that patients of color were evaluated through a qualitatively different pathway than White patients. These race and ethnicity-contingent pathways suggest that evaluators apply different implicit standards when integrating information depending on the patient's racial and ethnic group. The findings advance understanding of mechanisms that could influence healthcare providers' decisions to refer patients to clinical trial studies, highlighting evaluator-level decision processes as critical intervention targets for improving racial representation in clinical research.

items.title: Treatment Engagement and Facial Emotion Recognition among Adolescent Males and Females with Conduct Problems.
items.abstract: Few studies have empirically tested whether facial emotion recognition (FER) is related to treatment engagement (TE), which is unfortunate since TE is crucial for treatment success. This study investigated whether FER abilities were associated with TE among adolescent males and females who have (allegedly) committed crimes and/or exhibited conduct problems. Participants were 16- to 17-year-old males (n = 321; 42.1% of Belgian origin) and females (n = 105; 54.2% of Belgian origin) residing in Flemish youth detention centers or residential (secured) care institutions. TE dimensions (i.e., readiness to change, bond with staff, collaboration on goals and tasks, and therapeutic engagement) were measured using a self-report questionnaire. FER (i.e., accuracy and processing speed) was assessed using two computerized tasks, one including static and the other dynamic facial expressions as stimuli. Callous-unemotional (CU) traits and conduct disorder (CD) symptoms were included as control variables, assessed via a self-report questionnaire and a diagnostic interview, respectively. A series of multiple linear regressions was performed, with accuracy scores or reaction times as independent variables, CU traits and the number of CD symptoms as control variables, and TE dimensions as dependent variables. Emotion recognition accuracy and processing speed were predominantly not significantly associated with TE. In contrast, elevated CU traits remained robustly negatively linked to TE, even after controlling for FER. These findings suggest that FER may not be a primary determinant of TE, whereas CU traits appear to be a more informative predictor of individual differences in TE and may hold greater practical relevance for clinicians. Interventions aimed at reducing CU traits may represent a promising approach to enhancing TE and, ultimately, improving treatment outcomes.

items.title: Broadening the Indications for the SPING Block in Palliative Care: A Case Discussion.
items.abstract: The Spinal Phenol IN Glycerol (SPING) block is an intrathecal neurolytic technique developed to provide sustained unilateral analgesia in frail patients with nonoperative hip fractures. Its potential role in other palliative care populations remains unexplored. Two cases are described with refractory unilateral lower-limb pain: a 76-year-old male with metastatic esophageal cancer and acetabular metastasis, and an 86-year-old female with advanced dementia and critical limb ischemia. In both cases, systemic opioids failed and were associated with significant adverse effects. Both patients experienced rapid and clinically assessed sustained pain relief, reduced opioid requirements, and improved comfort until death. These two case reports suggest that SPING may provide effective palliative analgesia with opioid reduction in patients with refractory unilateral lower-limb pain caused by metastatic bone disease and critical limb ischemia. These findings support consideration of SPING as a proportionate palliative intervention beyond its current use for hip fractures when comfort is the primary goal.

items.title: Health Literacy of Mental Health Workers: A Latent Profile Analysis.
items.abstract: Low health literacy is linked to poorer outcomes. Individuals with mental illness often have lower health literacy and engage in less healthy behaviours. Healthcare workers play an important role in supporting consumers' health literacy, but they may also have gaps in their own health literacy skills. This study aims to (a) explore the multidimensional health literacy profiles of mental health workers, (b) compare their health literacy to the Australian general population and (c) examine health behaviours within health literacy profiles. Participants were 338 mental health workers employed at an Australian community-based mental health treatment service. Multidimensional health literacy was measured using the Health Literacy Questionnaire. Latent profile analysis was used to identify multidimensional health literacy profiles. Three health literacy profiles were identified: lowest (23%), moderate (65%) and highest (12%). Workers in the lowest health literacy profile had significantly lower health literacy compared with the general population of Australia and were less likely to engage in physical activity and consume vegetables. Improving the health literacy of workers could improve their well-being and promote healthier behaviours among consumers. Workers with lower health literacy would benefit from greater support from education providers, services and the wider system prioritising health literacy improvements and training.

items.title: What makes people seeking asylum and refugees well? A qualitative scoping review using an asset-based approach.
items.abstract: People seeking asylum and with refugee status (ASR) often face worse health outcomes compared to host populations. Despite this, ASR are underserved in healthcare and research, resulting in a knowledge gap about what promotes their health and resilience. The aim of this review is to define what ASR communities express makes them well despite adversity by looking at the assets of individuals and communities identified in community-based research. A scoping review of peer-reviewed papers and grey literature documenting patient-centred holistic health, wellbeing and social outcomes in community-based research with ASR. In total, 24 papers met the inclusion criteria. Wellbeing was primarily defined by safety, empowerment and a sense of purpose. Three things matter most for wellbeing: gaining knowledge and skills (like language and education), having meaningful things to do (like work or volunteering) and access to connections you care deeply about (like family, culture and faith). The study demonstrates that wellbeing for ASR is multifaceted, encompassing psychological, social and cultural dimensions. Asset-based approaches support holistic wellbeing in underserved populations by shifting the focus from identifying problems and deficits to recognising and building upon strengths, capabilities and existing resources. Although there are challenges in measurement, qualitative and participatory research approaches are proving effective in capturing the complex needs and outcomes for this population.

items.title: An Overlooked Critical Factor in Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Transmission in Türkiye: Direct Contact with Livestock.
items.abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) prevention in Türkiye focuses predominantly on tick attachments, often neglecting transmission via direct contact with viremic livestock. Field observations from an endemic province were synthesized with a comparative review of official Ministry of Health educational materials. Direct animal transmission is minimized within professional training slides and omitted from public awareness posters, despite high livestock seroprevalence and documented cases without tick exposure. Additionally, training materials fail to emphasize that viremic animals are clinically asymptomatic. Public health strategies must move beyond a tick-exclusive focus by integrating animal-contact warnings into public posters, mandating protective equipment during slaughter, and introducing targeted campaigns during Eid al-Adha.

items.title: Prevalence and Determinants of Underweight Among Children Aged 6-10 Years in Urban and Rural Areas of Central Ethiopia: A Community-Based Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: ObjectivesThe evidence revealed that underweight is a major public health concern affecting school-aged children in low and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Underweight affects children aged 6-10 years, growth and development, which leads to poor physical, cognitive, and social performance. Thus, this study aimed to assess the prevalence and determinants of underweight among children aged 6-10 years old in urban and rural areas of Central Ethiopia.MethodsA community-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 541 children from January 2 to May 2, 2023. Participants were selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and anthropometric measurements. Children's nutritional status was assessed using weight-for-age z-scores calculated with WHO AnthroPlus software. Factors associated with underweight were identified using binary logistic regression analysis. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05, and associations were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).ResultsIn this study, 501 children were enrolled, yielding a response rate of 92.6%. Underweight was more common in rural areas than in urban areas, with prevalence rates of 24.9% (95% CI: 21.2, 26.3) and 17.5% (95% CI: 14.0, 19.0), respectively. Among urban children, maternal age at first birth (AOR = 4.4; 95% CI: 1.63, 12.2), handwashing after latrine use (AOR = 0.16; 95% CI: 0.12, 0.46), use of treated drinking water (AOR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.18, 0.51), and family planning use (AOR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.10, 0.47) were determinants of underweight. In contrast, among rural children, maternal age at first birth (AOR = 2.4; 95% CI: 1.34, 8.91), no antenatal care (ANC) follow-up (AOR = 2.3; 95% CI: 1.27, 6.53), diarrhea in the previous month (AOR = 2.8; 95% CI: 1.63, 9.35), dietary diversity (AOR = 6.0; 95% CI: 2.79, 13.2), and a history of illness in the preceding two weeks (AOR = 3.4; 95% CI: 1.91, 7.23) were identified as determinants of underweight.ConclusionUnderweight was more prevalent among rural children (24.9%) than among urban children (17.5%), highlighting the need for context-specific nutritional interventions. Interventions addressing the identified factors should be strengthened to improve the nutritional status of school-age children in both rural and urban settings.

items.title: Cluster of vitamin C deficiency in prisoners referred to a tertiary hospital in Northwest Ethiopia: a case report.
items.abstract: Vitamin C deficiency, though rare, can reemerge in high-risk settings with poor dietary intake. We report three cases of vitamin C deficiency in male prisoners referred from Shedie Prison to the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital (UoG CSH), Ethiopia. Three Ethiopian male prisoners aged 23-25 years developed progressive bilateral lower limb stiffness, gingival bleeding, weight loss, and signs of anemia after 9 months of incarceration. Their diet consisted mainly of bread and cooked legume (kik wot in Amharic) without fruits or vegetables. On arrival at UoG CSH, all had signs and symptoms of nutritional anemia and scurvy. Although serum vitamin C measurement was not available, the diagnosis was supported by the characteristic clinical feature, the shared dietary exposure among affected prisoners and the rapid clinical improvement following ascorbic acid supplementation. This case series highlights an important public health concern in prison settings. Two had bicytopenia or pancytopenia. All were treated with ascorbic acid, folate, iron, nutritional support, and physiotherapy. They improved significantly and were discharged. Although 40 inmates reportedly had similar symptoms at the prison, only these three were referred and evaluated at UoG CSH. These cases illustrate the persistence of micronutrient deficiency syndromes in confined populations. Tertiary care institutions must remain vigilant for preventable nutritional diseases among vulnerable groups.

items.title: A lens on salutogenic concepts as resources for oral health among adults: a scoping review.
items.abstract: To effectively address the global burden of oral health disease, a broader and more sustainable approach focusing of health factors is suggested. The salutogenic approach, which emphasizes psychosocial health resources, offers a promising framework for health promotion. However, there is currently a lack of synthesized evidence on how salutogenic concepts are applied in adult oral health. This scoping review therefore aims to identify and map the existing scientific research on the use of salutogenic concepts as oral health resources among adults. This scoping view followed established guidelines. A systematic search was conducted across four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, PsycInfo, and CINAHL) using a search string strategy based on three key elements: Population (adults aged 18-59), Concept (salutogenic concepts), and Context (oral health). The outcomes of interest included dental caries, periodontitis, and self-reported oral health. A total of 2,503 articles were identified and screened for eligibility, followed by data extraction from the relevant studies. A total of 28 studies were included in the review, most of which were cross-sectional and published between 1996 and 2025. The studies were conducted across multiple regions worldwide. Based on the salutogenic umbrella framework, 12 key concepts were identified: self-efficacy, sense of coherence, social capital, coping, locus of control, social support, optimism, emotional intelligence, motivation, positive emotionality, resilience, and well-being. These studies varied in how these concepts were defined, the instruments used, the populations studied, and the settings in which the research was conducted. There is a growing research interest in applying salutogenic approaches to adult oral health, although concentrated on a few salutogenic constructs and inconsistent in measurement. The findings highlight the relevance of salutogenic concepts for oral health promotion research. Future research using well-defined concepts and robust methodological designs is needed to strengthen the evidence base.

items.title: Suicide Among Indigenous Peoples in Brazil: Ecological Study and Geospatial Mapping of Cases, 2013-2022.
items.abstract: This retrospective ecological study analyzes the temporal trend of suicides among Indigenous men and women in Brazilian cities between 2013 and 2022. Suicide mortality data were obtained from the Ministry of Health's Mortality Information System (Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade, SIM). Records were classified according to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10), focusing on intentional self-harm (X60-X84). There was a significant increase in suicides among Indigenous men (41%) and women (42.9%). The highest absolute numbers occurred in the North, for men (n = 547) and women (n = 195). The Central-West showed the highest suicide rates for men (30.5/100,000) and women (8.8/100,000). The most affected age group among men was 20-29 years (37.3%), while among women it was 15-19 years (36%). Findings highlight the urgency of suicide prevention public policies for Indigenous peoples, particularly youth and young adults. Investment in culturally sensitive mental health strategies is essential to address Indigenous community contexts and expand access to psychosocial support services.

items.title: The anti-misinformation movement must not become anti-science.
items.abstract: Communities of experts have an indispensable role to play in addressing misinformation. However, some of these efforts have weaponized the term "misinformation" to suppress dissenting viewpoints, risking inadvertently turning the anti-misinformation movement into an anti-science one. The scientific community should instead be asking: how can we cultivate forums that promote discourse according to scientific values and incentivize broad participation in them? Here, we diagnose this problem and propose a number of remedies. Operationalizing precise definitions of misinformation can help curate information in public forums. Certification of trusted organizations by scientific societies can help ensure trustworthy information is incorporated and up-ranked in AI and search algorithms. Professional societies can champion shared principles of scientific debate in public with clear, transparent professional guidelines. Stronger incentives for producing high-quality science communication are also needed. Ensuring inclusive participation by diverse stakeholders is a pre-requisite for legitimate scientific debate and policy-making in a democratic society.

items.title: U.S. state-level variation in caregiver-reported provider recommendation of HPV vaccination to 13-to-17-year-old adolescents.
items.abstract: Although regional differences in provider recommendation of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine have been documented, limited research has examined variation at the state level. Therefore, this study examined state-level differences in caregiver-reported health care provider recommendation of HPV vaccines among 13-to-17-year-old adolescents in the United States. Using a cross-sectional design to examine data from the National Immunization Survey-Teen (2023), multivariable logistic regression was used to model state-specific variations in provider recommendation of HPV vaccine. Proportion estimation was used to examine state-specific prevalence. Provider recommendation varied considerably across states. For example, the odds of reporting a recommendation were lower among caregivers of adolescents in Arkansas (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 0.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.33 to 0.96), Georgia (AOR = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.26 to 0.93), and Mississippi (AOR = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.24 to 0.74), and higher among caregivers in New Hampshire (AOR = 2.40, 95% CI = 1.23 to 4.68) compared with adolescents in California. Greater heterogeneity was observed in the South compared with other regions. For example, the prevalence of not receiving a recommendation was 16% in Maryland and 41% in Mississippi. The findings underscore the need to improve HPV vaccine recommendation in some states in the United States. In particular, states with low rates should be targeted for focused interventions.

items.title: Spirituality and death anxiety in cancer caregivers: the mediating role of quality of life.
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationships among spirituality levels, death anxiety, and quality of life in family caregivers of cancer patients, and to determine the mediating role of quality of life in the relationship between spiritual orientation and death anxiety. This descriptive study was conducted at the Erzurum Regional Training and Research Hospital between June and December 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews with 322 family caregivers of cancer patients, determined by power analysis. The Personal Information Form (22 items), Spiritual Orientation Scale (16 items, 7-point Likert, range 16-112; Cronbach's α = 0.88), Death Anxiety Scale (15 items, yes/no format, range 0-15, scores ≥ 7 indicating death anxiety; Cronbach's α = 0.90), and Caregiver Quality of Life Index-Cancer (CQOLC; 35 items, 5-point Likert, range 0-140; Cronbach's α = 0.87) were used. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and Hayes Process Macro (Model 4) with 5000 bootstrap resampling were employed for data analysis. The mean spiritual orientation score was 72.18 ± 5.88, the death anxiety score was 7.46 ± 2.78, and the CQOLC score was 64.28 ± 7.52. Spiritual orientation was positively correlated with quality of life (r = 0.422) and negatively correlated with death anxiety (r =-0.361). Mediation analysis revealed that quality of life partially mediated the relationship between spiritual orientation and death anxiety (indirect effect B = -0.1063, 95% CI [-0.1584, -0.0603]). Spiritual orientation explained 15% of the variance in quality of life, and the model explained 28% of the variance in death anxiety. The mediation effect reached a medium effect size (standardized effect = - 0.1134). Spiritual orientation improves quality of life and reduces death anxiety among cancer caregivers. Quality of life partially mediates this relationship. Integrating spiritual support into psychosocial care programs for caregivers may enhance quality of life and reduce death anxiety.

items.title: PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases.
items.abstract: Diseases affect multiple cell types within tissues, but the overall landscape of the multicellular responses in human diseases remains largely unexplored. Here we categorize the multicellular responses of human diseases based on a remapped atlas of human cells, PANGEA, incorporating 12.6 million cells acquired from a pipeline that automatically processes raw sequence files from public repositories. We constructed a hierarchical cell classification framework comprising 32 major cell types and 165 cellular subtypes. On the basis of this annotation framework, we explored an extensive atlas of human cells containing 46.5 million cells from 160 diseases across 48 organs and revealed core archetypes of human diseases repeatedly found across organs. We show that this cell atlas could also serve as a reference for unbiased analysis in spatial transcriptomics, revealing spatial features associated with immunotherapy responses. Collectively, our study provides foundational resources for cell ontologies, enabling cross-tissue comparisons of cellular features in human diseases.

items.title: Insomnia versus daytime sleepiness: distinct behavioural phenotypes of mood and binge eating in adults with clinical obesity.
items.abstract: Insomnia and excessive daytime sleepiness are common in adults with obesity but typically examined in isolation. We tested whether, jointly, they identify behavioural phenotypes with distinct eating and mood profiles. Cross-sectional analysis of 2016 adults seeking specialist obesity care (76% women; mean BMI 37.1 kg/m²). Participants completed the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Binge Eating Scale (BES), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Perceived Stress Scale, and Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2). Four phenotypes were defined a priori using ISI ≥ 15 and ESS ≥ 11: good sleeper, isolated insomnia, isolated sleepiness, combined. Multivariable regressions were adjusted for age, sex and BMI. Phenotype distribution was 53.6% good sleeper, 18.2% isolated insomnia, 13.8% isolated sleepiness, 14.4% combined. ISI and ESS were only moderately correlated (ρ = 0.30). Isolated insomnia was most strongly associated with anxiety (HAD-A ≥ 11: adjusted OR [aOR] 4.48, 95% CI 3.41-5.89, p < 0.001) and depression (aOR 3.09, 2.20-4.33, p < 0.001); isolated sleepiness was most strongly associated with severe binge eating (BES ≥ 27: aOR 2.55, 1.69-3.83, p < 0.001) and lower intuitive eating (IES-2 β = -0.24, -0.33 to -0.15, p < 0.001). The combined phenotype carried the highest risk overall. BMI did not differ across phenotypes. Findings were robust to OSA exclusion and to alternative insomnia thresholds. Insomnia and daytime sleepiness identify distinct behavioural phenotypes in clinical obesity, independently of BMI. Joint screening at intake may help personalise behavioural obesity management.

items.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus and risk of long-term cardiometabolic disease.
items.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), or hyperglycaemia first diagnosed during pregnancy, is associated with adverse outcomes for the mother and offspring. In this narrative review, we first summarize the epidemiological evidence regarding long-term maternal and offspring cardiometabolic consequences of GDM, including the role of heterogeneity in the aetiology of GDM in shaping the long-term effects of GDM exposure. Next, we discuss established mechanistic processes, such as β-cell stress, vascular dysfunction and developmental programming, that link GDM to long-term maternal and offspring outcomes and, accordingly, hold potential to be therapeutic targets. We also discuss emerging evidence for connections between other processes, such as placental signalling, and cardiometabolic risk after GDM. Finally, we discuss the role of potential avenues for cardiometabolic risk mitigation following GDM exposure, including lactation and breastfeeding, postpartum monitoring and lifestyle interventions.

items.title: Cardiovascular risk, evaluation and management in patients with hypertriglyceridaemia: a Consensus Statement from the International Atherosclerosis Society.
items.abstract: The prevalence of hypertriglyceridaemia is increasing globally owing to high rates of obesity and diabetes mellitus. Hypertriglyceridaemia is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, mediated through the cholesterol content of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnant particles rather than through triglycerides per se. Although plasma levels of triglycerides can be measured with a simple blood test, hypertriglyceridaemia remains underdiagnosed and undertreated. Hypertriglyceridaemia can result from various primary or secondary aetiologies, the identification and management of which is an important first step. Hypertriglyceridaemia can be managed with lifestyle measures, lipid-lowering therapy with statins in indicated patients to reduce cholesterol levels and, in refractory situations, with the addition of triglyceride-specific pharmacological therapies. Emerging therapies with considerable promise for the management of hypertriglyceridaemia include those targeting apolipoprotein C-III, angiopoietin-related protein 3 or fibroblast growth factor 21. However, so far, there is no evidence from randomized clinical trials that pharmacotherapies targeting triglycerides can reduce the occurrence of cardiovascular events, suggesting that elevated levels of triglycerides serve as a marker of atherosclerotic risk that should prompt optimization of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. In this Consensus Statement, we provide clinical context and evidence for the evaluation, diagnosis and management of hypertriglyceridaemia.

items.title: Environmental health resilience and exposure reduction for healthy aging and longevity.
items.abstract: Population aging has widened the gap between life expectancy and healthspan. Yet aging trajectories remain strikingly heterogeneous even among populations facing comparable harmful environmental exposures, including air pollution, extreme temperatures, toxic metals, unsafe water and sanitation, noise and poor housing. Why similar environmental risks produce divergent patterns of multimorbidity, disability and functional decline is a central research question. This Review proposes environmental health resilience factors, features of physical, social, ecological and built environments that act as protective effect modifiers, flattening the exposure-response curve and attenuating the biological translation of adverse exposures into harm rather than reducing exposure itself. Drawing on longitudinal cohorts, natural experiments and policy evaluations, we show that green and natural environments, age-friendly urban design, climate-resilient infrastructure and social connectivity flatten exposure-response curves and help to explain divergent aging trajectories under comparable urban environmental conditions. We propose both building resilience and reducing exposure are complementary strategies to compress morbidity and advance healthspan equity in aging societies.

items.title: Understanding the social determinants of healthy aging across the lifecourse with social policy experiments.
items.abstract: Social and economic conditions shape healthy aging, but it remains unclear whether policies that modify these conditions change aging-related biomarkers or later-life functional trajectories. The growing availability of biomarker data in longitudinal cohorts, together with the wider use of experimental and quasi-experimental designs in social policy research, creates new opportunities to evaluate how social conditions become biologically embedded. We argue that policy experiments can strengthen research on the biology of aging by specifying the exposure modified by policy, the populations affected and the life-course stage at which intervention occurs. Using education and cognitive aging as an example, and drawing on emerging evidence on policy effects on biomarkers, we show how causal evidence can diverge from observational associations. We propose a research agenda that integrates social policy evaluation with biomarker research, functional decline, resilience and healthy aging trajectories across the life course.

items.title: Personalised mobile health coaching from early pregnancy to 12-months postpartum for females at risk of gestational diabetes (Bump2Baby and Me): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Maternal overweight and obesity increase the risk of gestational diabetes and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Digital health interventions offer scalable, personalised support, but evidence for interventions spanning both pregnancy and postpartum remains scarce. We evaluated the effectiveness of a personalised mobile health (mHealth) coaching intervention for females at increased risk of gestational diabetes. This multicentre, randomised controlled trial conducted in Australia, Ireland, Spain, and the UK enrolled pregnant females aged 18 years and older between 12-24 weeks of gestation with increased risk of gestational diabetes (Monash GDM risk tool score ≥3; tool risk factors were maternal age, BMI, ethnicity, family history of diabetes, and past history of gestational diabetes). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using computer-generated block randomisation (block size 200; stratified by site) to receive either personalised mHealth coaching via smartphone providing synchronous and asynchronous support through pregnancy to 12 months postpartum alongside usual maternity care, or usual maternity care alone. Usual maternity care, including gestational diabetes screening and management, continued unchanged in both groups, and both groups received Bluetooth-enabled scales. Participants and health coaches could not be masked to allocation; clinical staff providing usual care, laboratory staff, and trial statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was the between-group mean difference in BMI at 12 months postpartum among females at risk of gestational diabetes. The trial was registered at Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Register, ACTRN12620001240932. Between Feb 9, 2021, and Oct 22, 2023, 4386 females were screened, 3521 were excluded, and 865 were randomly assigned (437 to the mHealth intervention group and 428 to the control group). The mean age of participants was 35·2 years (SD 4·3), and most participants were White (588 [73%] of 804). Mean BMI change did not differ between groups (intervention, -0·04 kg/m2 [SE 0·12] vs control, 0·04 kg/m2 [0·13]). Adverse events were recorded in 18% (79 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 25% (106 of 428) of participants in the control group; serious adverse events occurred in 6% (28 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 9% (40 of 428) of participants in the control group. No adverse or serious adverse events were considered related to the intervention. Personalised mHealth coaching spanning pregnancy and an extended postpartum support period did not reduce mean maternal BMI at 12 months compared with usual care. Findings suggest that mHealth interventions targeting at-risk females might benefit from addressing a broader range of maternal health outcomes beyond weight management. items.title: Helicobacter pylori antibiotic resistance in Egypt exceeds eradication thresholds: systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Eradicating Helicobacter pylori in Egypt is severely hindered by escalating antibiotic resistance. Comprehensive national resistance data are essential for optimizing failing treatment protocols. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the pooled prevalence of Helicobacter pylori resistance to key antibiotics in Egypt to inform national treatment guidelines. Data sources: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Egyptian Knowledge Bank (EKB). Primary studies published between 2000 and 2025 reporting H. pylori antibiotic resistance prevalence in Egypt were included. Human subjects with documented H. pylori infection. Resistance was assessed for metronidazole, amoxicillin, clarithromycin, tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones. Assessment of risk of bias: The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Prevalence Studies was used. Methods of data synthesis: Pooled prevalence and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. Thirty studies comprising 5019 observations were included. The resistance rate for clarithromycin was 42.8% (95% CI: 34.7-51.1%), nearly tripling the 15% Maastricht clinical threshold for abandoning empirical clarithromycin-containing regimens. Rates for other primary antibiotics were also critically high: metronidazole 79.1% (95% CI: 64.7-90.8%) and amoxicillin 45.8% (95% CI: 29.1-62.9%), both far exceeding rates typical for standard empirical therapies. Resistance to tetracycline (23.4%), ciprofloxacin (20.0%), and levofloxacin (18.8%) also surpassed clinical cutoffs. Significant geographic disparities were observed across governorates, with metronidazole resistance reaching 100% in some regions. Meta-regression indicated that these high resistance levels have remained stable over the past two decades. Egypt Delta and the Cairo metropolitan areas face a critical burden of Helicobacter pylori resistance, rendering standard empirical triple therapies suboptimal. National guidelines should prioritise quadruple therapy or susceptibility-guided treatments to improve eradication outcomes. PROSPERO (CRD420251249967).

items.title: Dangerous and High-Risk Offender Frameworks in Canada, the United States, and England and Wales.
items.abstract: Dangerous and high-risk offender regimes sit at the intersection of psychiatry, criminal law, and human rights. This article compares Canada's dangerous and long-term offender provisions, the United States's sexually violent predator laws, and the dangerousness framework in England and Wales. We review their historical development, statutory foundations, leading cases, and the role of forensic psychiatric evidence in assessments of future risk, manageability, and treatability. Across jurisdictions, psychiatry remains central to decisions with profound liberty consequences, yet each system resolves the tension between public protection and proportionality differently: Canada embeds dangerousness within criminal sentencing, the United States relies primarily on civil commitment, and England and Wales has moved from imprisonment for public protection toward a more graduated sentencing structure. We also examine contemporary Canadian trends, including growth in dangerous offender designations, regional variation, and persistent Indigenous overrepresentation. Despite doctrinal differences, all three regimes face common challenges: the limits of risk prediction, the cultural validity of assessment tools, and the ethics implications of preventive confinement. We argue that forensic psychiatrists and psychologists contribute most effectively when their opinions are transparent, evidence-based, culturally informed, and attentive to proportionality.

items.title: What cannabis sales data can and cannot tell us about young adult risk: a critical commentary on retail trends and clinical practice.
items.abstract: Cannabis retail sales data from legalized markets provide a valuable but incomplete view of young adult consumption patterns. Recent analyses of California's commercial cannabis transactions show that, although flower accounts for the largest share of spending, young adults allocate a greater proportion of cannabis expenditure to vapor pens and concentrates than older adults. These trends raise important clinical and public health concerns. This commentary critically evaluates the strengths and limitations of retail analytics using established appraisal frameworks and considers the implications for clinical assessment, harm reduction, and policy development. Retail datasets have inherent limitations that restrict their usefulness as indicators of individual risk. Transaction logs cannot capture frequency of use, dosage, motivations, psychosocial influences, or associated harms, and they exclude illicit market activity, which represents a substantial proportion of young adult consumption. Retail data should be interpreted as macro-level indicators rather than direct proxies for personal use. Effective risk assessment requires integrating commercial analytics with qualitative insight, epidemiological surveillance, and updated clinical screening approaches that reflect modern high-potency cannabis modalities. The commentary also considers how these findings translate to international contexts, including the United Kingdom, where unregulated markets and product mislabeling present additional challenges for frontline practitioners.

items.title: Quality Assessment of and User Engagement With Short Videos About Breast Cancer Screening on Douyin, Kuaishou, and TikTok: Cross-Sectional Content Analysis Study.
items.abstract: Breast cancer screening plays a critical role in early detection and mortality reduction. Short video platforms have become widely used channels for patient education, but the quality and reliability of breast cancer screening information on short video platforms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore and compare the source, content characteristics, and quality of short videos on breast cancer screening across 2 major Chinese-language platforms (Douyin and Kuaishou) and the English-language platform TikTok. Using the keyword "breast cancer screening," this study retrieved and screened the top 100 short videos from each of the 3 platforms-Douyin, Kuaishou, and TikTok-resulting in a final sample of 258 eligible videos. Basic video information, user engagement metrics, and uploader characteristics were collected. A total of 3 breast disease specialists independently evaluated the content using 4 tools: the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Audiovisual Materials (PEMAT-A/V), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), Global Quality Score (GQS), and Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark criteria (JAMA-BC), which assess understandability and actionability, overall quality, educational value, and reliability, respectively. Statistical analyses included Kruskal-Wallis tests, Dunn-Bonferroni tests, chi-square tests, and Spearman correlation analysis. Videos on TikTok had significantly lower scores on the mDISCERN, GQS, and JAMA-BC than those on Douyin and Kuaishou, indicating poorer overall quality and reliability. The median mDISCERN scores were 1.50 (IQR 1.00-2.00) for TikTok compared to 3.00 (IQR 2.00-3.00) for both Douyin and Kuaishou (P<.001), the median GQS scores were 2.00 (IQR 2.00-3.00) for TikTok compared to 3.00 (IQR 2.50-4.00) (P<.001) for Douyin and 3.00 (IQR 3.00-3.50) (P<.001) for Kuaishou, and the median JAMA-BC scores were 10.00 (IQR 8.25-12.00) for TikTok compared to 12.00 (IQR 10.00-12.00) (P<.001) for Douyin and 12.00 (IQR 10.00-14.00) (P<.001) for Kuaishou. The PEMAT-A scores of Douyin and Kuaishou were also significantly lower on TikTok (Douyin vs TikTok: P=.002; Kuaishou vs TikTok: P=.02). Health care professionals were the main content creators on Douyin (49/66, 74.2%) and Kuaishou (56/69, 81.1%), while individual content creators dominated TikTok (33/72, 45.8%). Authentication rates were significantly lower on TikTok (9/72, 12.5%) than on Kuaishou (35/69, 50.7%) and Douyin (58/66, 87.9%). Viewer engagement metrics, including likes, comments, and collections, were nonsignificant or negatively correlated with video quality. For example, mDISCERN scores were negatively correlated with the number of likes per 30 days (P<.001). This study reveals that high-quality videos on breast cancer screening tend to attract lower viewer engagement, highlighting platform-specific disparities and challenges in dissemination. It is recommended that short video platforms implement stricter review processes for health-related videos and uploaders. Additionally, governmental or related agencies should provide media training for health care professionals in public science communication to enhance the impact and effectiveness of health education via short videos.

items.title: Positive pressure ventilation in newborns at birth: a systematic review of recipient characteristics and temporal trends.
items.abstract: To synthesise evidence on temporal trends, recipient characteristics and variation in the use of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) at birth. This systematic review was registered (CRD42024487025) and followed a condition-context-population framework. Five electronic databases and grey literature were searched to 25 June 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI checklist, and reporting followed PRISMA 2020. Forty-two studies from 34 countries (27 from high-income countries), reporting 269 to 10,696,831 livebirths per study (1984-2024), were included. Heterogeneity in whether continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was distinguished from PPV, interface definitions and eligibility criteria precluded meta-analysis. Fifteen studies included only preterm infants and 19 excluded congenital anomalies. Nine population-based and large multicentre studies that excluded CPAP and included all age groups reported PPV incidence ranging from 3.0% to 8.0%. Rates were much higher among very and extremely preterm infants. Temporal trends suggested increasing PPV incidence overall and via facemask, whereas tracheal-tube PPV was stable or declining. Lower PPV incidence was reported in low-resource and lower-level birthing centres. Few studies reported indications for or timing of PPV initiation, and reported data items were inconsistent. PPV remains common in neonatal resuscitation, with higher use at lower gestational ages and higher-level birthing services. Limited and heterogeneous reporting of indications and PPV timelines constrains interpretation and comparison. Standardised, neonatal Utstein-aligned reporting, including PPV indications and time intervals and separate reporting of airway interfaces and CPAP, is needed. Further population-based studies, particularly in low-and middle-income countries, are warranted.
