items.title: Cycle-to-Cycle Prediction of Return of Spontaneous Circulation Using End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide Dynamics in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
items.abstract: Prognostication in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) commonly relies on static pre-resuscitation variables, although resuscitation is a rapidly evolving physiologic process. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is continuously available during cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but its sequential information has not been fully used for real-time prediction. We aim to develop and internally validate a cycle-to-cycle time-updated prediction model using sequential EtCO2 values to estimate the probability of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in the subsequent 2-minute resuscitation cycle. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adult OHCA patients from the NTUH-HYCARD database between 2016 and 2023. Event-level EtCO2 sequences were extracted from resuscitation records and standardized into 2-minute intervals for up to 30 minutes, consistent with Advanced Cardiac Life Support reassessment cycles. At each prediction time point, the model used EtCO2 values available from event onset to the current time point, without using future values. A two-layer long short-term memory model estimated the probability of ROSC in the subsequent cycle. Performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation at two levels: the event level (one prediction per event) and the cycle level (one prediction per 2-minute cycle). The final analysis included 1,651 event-level EtCO2 sequences from 1,480 patients; 583 events ended with ROSC. At the event level, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.876 (95% CI, 0.863-0.890) and a Brier score of 0.140 (95% CI, 0.131-0.149). When applied to every 2-minute cycle (17,029 prediction points; ROSC prevalence, 3.4%), the AUROC was 0.685 (95% CI, 0.664-0.706), and the model systematically overestimated ROSC probability (Brier score, 0.285; 95% CI, 0.268-0.303). Sequential EtCO2 dynamics showed good event-level discrimination for predicting ROSC in the subsequent cycle. When applied at each cycle, the model retained modest discrimination but overestimated ROSC probability, indicating that recalibration is required before cycle-to-cycle use.

items.title: Prognostic Value of Tissue Doppler Late Diastolic Velocity (TDI-a') in Patients with Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
items.abstract: Risk stratification after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains suboptimal. Beyond valvular hemodynamics, a number of standard echocardiographic parameters of function are associated to outcome. Mitral annular late diastolic velocity (TDI-a') is proven to have prognostic value in multiple clinical settings, but its role after TAVI is unresolved. In a single-center retrospective observational study we included adult patients with isolated severe AS (aortic valve area < 1.0 cm²) undergoing TAVI, between December 2013 and August 2025. Pre-procedural transthoracic echocardiography was reviewed offline by blinded investigators to measure TDI-a' velocities. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and ROC analysis were performed. A total of 805 patients (median age 81 years; 44.8% male) were included. During a median follow-up of 36.5 months, 196 deaths (24.3%) occurred. On univariable analysis, left ventricular ejection fraction, E/e' ratio, left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI), and TDI-a' were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, average TDI-a' remained the only independent echocardiographic predictor of mortality in both logistic regression (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.821-0.944; p < 0.001) and Cox analysis (HR 0.934, 95% CI 0.881-0.991; p = 0.023). ROC analysis showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.585), with an optimal cut-off ≤ 8.4 cm/s (sensitivity 65%, specificity 49%). Reduced TDI-a' is independently associated with mortality after TAVI, beyond conventional echocardiographic predictors. Despite modest discrimination, it is a simple prognostic marker that may improve pre-procedural risk stratification and warrants further prospective validation.

items.title: County-Level Poverty, Primary Care Availability, and Trends in Adult Preventable Hospitalizations: A Multi-State Analysis, 2013-2023.
items.abstract: To examine trends in preventable hospitalizations (PH) across multiple states and evaluate associations between county-level poverty and primary care physician (PCP) availability and rates of preventable hospitalizations in US counties. A repeated cross-sectional analysis was conducted to examine county-level adult PH rates overall and by subtype (acute, chronic, diabetes-related), as well as trends in PHs over time. Data from Health Care Utilization Project (HCUP) State Inpatient Databases from 13 states from 2013-2023 were analyzed in 2025 and yielded 9,691 county-year observations from 881 counties. Negative binomial models were used to estimate associations between PCP availability, poverty rate, and PH outcomes while controlling for county demographics, rurality, and year. From 2013-2023, age-adjusted acute PH rates decreased substantially, and chronic PH rates declined moderately, while diabetes-related PH increased significantly through 2019 before declining modestly. In adjusted models, high-poverty counties experienced 79% higher PH rates versus low-poverty counties (IRR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.38-2.31), and the highest PCP tertile counties had 14% lower PH rates than the lowest tertile (IRR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.80-0.93). Higher county-level poverty and lower PCP availability were associated with increased adult PH rates, particularly chronic and diabetes-related hospitalizations. These findings highlight the importance of structural socioeconomic conditions and local primary care resources in understanding variation in potentially avoidable hospitalizations.

items.title: Loss of Macrophage-Derived Wnt Signaling Coupled with mTORC1-Mediated Inhibition of β-Catenin Activation Drives Acute Liver Injury in Severe Ehrlichiosis.
items.abstract: Severe ehrlichiosis is characterized by fulminant acute liver injury that frequently culminates in multi-organ failure, yet the mechanisms governing defective hepatic regeneration remain poorly understood. Using complementary in vitro systems and established murine models of mild (Ehrlichia muris) and severe (Ehrlichia japonica) infection, we identified differential regulation of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway as a central determinant of disease outcome. Mild E. muris infection elicited robust activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling through macrophage-derived Wnt ligands, promoting β-catenin nuclear translocation in hepatocytes, transcription of regenerative target genes, and marked hepatocyte proliferation. In contrast, severe E. japonica infection profoundly suppressed Wnt/β-catenin signaling despite extensive hepatic macrophage accumulation, resulting in impaired liver regeneration, progressive liver injury, and fatal disease. Mechanistically, this suppression was driven by diminished macrophage-derived Wnt ligand production, aberrant hepatocyte mTORC1 activation that inhibited β-catenin signaling, and potentially the absence of a Wnt-mimetic Ehrlichia effector capable of engaging Frizzled receptors and sustaining regenerative signaling. Therapeutically, pharmacologic activation of β-catenin combined with doxycycline treatment of E. japonica infected mice restored canonical Wnt signaling, reduced bacterial burden and hepatic injury, and significantly improved survival. Collectively, these findings establish impaired Wnt/β-catenin signaling as a pivotal mechanism underlying impaired liver regeneration during severe ehrlichiosis and identify restoration of this pathway as a promising host-directed therapeutic strategy that complements antimicrobial therapy by simultaneously promoting pathogen clearance and hepatic repair.

items.title: Disruptions in U.S. Heart Transplantation: When Innovation Outpaces Evidence.
items.abstract: For nearly four decades, heart transplantation was defined by a stable, predictable paradigm: brain-dead donors, ice-cooler transport, uniform three-drug immunosuppression, and biopsy-based surveillance. Within a few years, that paradigm has been upended. In this perspective, we examine the disruptions now reshaping heart transplantation in the United States. Some are desirable: new preservation platforms and the rapid growth of donation after circulatory death, which now accounts for nearly a quarter of U.S. heart transplants, have expanded the donor pool, and cardiac xenotransplantation has reached clinical testing. Others remain controversial: the 2018 allocation policy has altered listing and support practices, normothermic regional perfusion raises unresolved questions about the determination of death, and inconsistent definitions of ischemic intervals undermine comparisons across DCD studies. Still others are troubling: OPTN restructuring, uneven OPO performance, outsourced procurement, rising costs, and press reports of donors showing signs of life have strained public trust. Underlying all of these is a data gap: national registries capture few DCD procurement and preservation variables, and little about recipients' long-term health beyond survival. Innovation has outpaced our ability to evaluate its consequences. We propose a shared DCD clock built on fixed timestamps, national ethical standards for normothermic regional perfusion, transparency in procurement and its costs, longitudinal outcome reporting, and accountability shared by OPOs and transplant centers. The challenge facing the field is no longer simply how to transplant more hearts, but how to ensure that more transplantation becomes better transplantation.

items.title: Burden of Child Growth Failure across countries in Eastern Africa Region: A systematic analysis of Global Burden of Diseases study 2010-2023.
items.abstract: Child growth failure remains a major contributor to child morbidity and mortality in Eastern Africa. Long-term evidence is essential for priority setting and monitoring progress toward child nutrition and survival targets. Therefore, this study aimed at assessing the burden of deaths and DALYs attributable to Child growth failure. This study was a systematic analysis conducted using estimates from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2023 for countries in the Eastern Africa region. Child growth failure was analyzed as a risk factor for DALYS and death among children under five years of age. Trends were assessed across selected years, and cause-specific contributions of child growth failure to major childhood diseases were examined. The analysis indicated that, under-five deaths of 245,334 in 2010 and 120,217 in 2023 and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of 21.9 million in 2010 and 10.8 million in 2023 were attributed to child growth failure in East Africa region. Regarding the components of child growth failure, underweight remained the leading contributor to mortality and health loss, followed by wasting and stunting. CGF burden was highest in low socio-demographic index (SDI) countries. The number of deaths and DALYs attributed to Child growth failure (CGF) substantially declined in Eastern Africa between 2010 and 2023. However, it remains a major cause of preventable child mortality, especially in low-SDI and fragile countries. These findings highlight the need to scale up nutrition-specific interventions, particularly for wasting and underweight, while integrating them with child health and disease control programs.

items.title: Medicare beneficiaries have less follow-up imaging and more invasive procedures than NLST participants following lung screening.
items.abstract: To determine if the proportion of patients receiving thoracic imaging, invasive diagnostic, or surgical procedures following community lung cancer screening (LCS) differed from that in the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). We compared the proportion of NLST participants and 2018 Medicare beneficiaries receiving imaging, invasive, or surgical procedures in the six months and one year following LCS, as well as lung cancer incidence and all-cause mortality. To create comparable cohorts, we used NLST chart abstraction data to impute information on procedures for participants with no abstraction. Within six months and one-year of LCS, NLST participants were significantly more likely to have at least one imaging test than Medicare beneficiaries (21.4 versus 16.5%); (difference=4.97%; 95% confidence limits (CL) 1.85%, 8.09) and 26.6% versus 22.3% (difference=4.28; 95% CL: 0.55, 8.02) respectively. NLST participants were significantly less likely to have an invasive or surgical procedure within six months of LCS (0.60 versus 4.64%; difference: -4.04% ; 95% CL: -5.23%, -2.84%) and (0.28 versus 1.51%; difference: -1.22% ; 95% CL: -1.80%, -0.65%) respectively, but neither differed significantly at one year. NLST had more cases of lung cancer diagnosed (3.83% [95% CL: 3.33,4.33] versus Medicare 2.26% [95%CL:1.51,3.01]). Mortality was not significantly different. Medicare beneficiaries were less likely to have follow-up imaging within six months and one year of LCS, and they were more likely to undergo invasive diagnostic or surgical procedures at six months, but were not statistically significant at one year following LCS.

items.title: Fluorochloridone Impairs Sertoli Cell Junctional Integrity and F-Actin Organization via p-FAK-Tyr407.
items.abstract: Fluorochloridone (FLC), a commonly used selective herbicide, caused male reproductive toxicity. However, the impacts of FLC on Sertoli cell junctional integrity and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate FLC-induced cytotoxicity on Sertoli cell barrier integrity and the cytoskeleton organization. To explore potential mechanism, we evaluated the effect of overexpressing a "phosphomimetic" mutant form of focal adhesion kinase (FAK), FAK Y407E, against FLC-induced damage. The viability of the mouse Sertoli cell line TM4 was assessed using the CCK8 assay. The integrity of the in vitro Sertoli cell monolayer barrier was evaluated using the sulfo-NHS-LC-biotin permeability assay. TM4 cells were transfected with a plasmid containing FAK Y407E. Subsequently, the actin filaments (F-actin) were fluorescence-labeled to observe the cytoskeletal structure. The expression and distribution of relevant proteins, as well as changes in their levels, were detected using immunofluorescence assays and Western blotting, respectively. The results revealed that FLC significantly reduced TM4 cell viability and downregulated the expression of blood-testis barrier (BTB) -associated cell adhesion proteins, including Connexin 43, N-cadherin, and Zonula Occludens-1, affecting intercellular adhesion. Furthermore, the expression of actin-related regulatory proteins (Arp3 and Eps8) was reduced, thereby disrupting F-actin reorganization. Concurrently, FLC exposure downregulated FAK-Tyr407 phosphorylation and altered the expression of the related signaling proteins in TM4 cells. Overexpression of FAK Y407E partially reversed FLC-induced cytoskeletal disassembly and junctional disruptions, suggesting FLC-induced impairment of Sertoli cell junctional integrity and the cytoskeleton organization is mediated by p-FAK-Tyr407. In conclusion, our findings showed that FLC could disrupt F-actin organization and cellular adhesion by decreasing p-FAK-Tyr407 and associated regulatory proteins.

items.title: Metal mixtures, industrial proximity, and child IQ: A cross-sectional biomarkers and longitudinal tooth analysis in schoolchildren from Taranto, Italy.
items.abstract: Children living near industrial sources may experience simultaneous exposure to multiple neurotoxic metals, with risks shaped by proximity, socioeconomic conditions, and developmental timing. We investigated associations among metal exposures, residential proximity to industrial sites and intelligence quotient (IQ) in 610 schoolchildren aged 6-15 years from Taranto, Italy. Child cognition was assessed using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children, Fourth Edition ( WISC-IV) IQ and parental cognitive ability using Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (SPM). Blood, hair, and urine biomarkers of cadmium, mercury, arsenic, lead, and manganese were analyzed cross-sectionally (n=437), while deciduous teeth reconstructed exposure across 22 time points (n=173). Analyses included regression, Spearman correlations, BKMR, BKMR-DLM, and TDLMM, adjusting for age, sex, SES, parental SPM, and proximity. Residence within 500m captured the strongest spatial signal for manganese and mercury. Urine cadmium (β=-3.12, p=0.001) and hair manganese (β=-0.0051, p=0.003) were inversely associated with IQ, and BKMR ranked cadmium as the dominant mixture contributor (PIP=0.98). Time-resolved models identified no robust metal-specific critical windows, while residence within 500m was consistently associated with lower IQ. Parental SPM was associated with child IQ and SES, while lower SES was associated with shorter residential distance from the industrial site. Near-source residence captured proximity-related metal elevations and cognitive disadvantage, while cadmium showed an IQ association without a clear spatial pattern. These findings highlight the sensitivity of metal-IQ associations to sample selection and covariate adjustment and underscore the importance of accounting for socioeconomic and residential factors when evaluating environmental metal exposures.

items.title: Ligand/receptor-based chimeric antigen receptors: a promising alternative to conventional scFv designs in cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Engineering immune cells, particularly T lymphocytes, with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) has become one of the most successful modalities of cancer immunotherapy, as evidenced by the approval and clinical use of multiple CAR-T cell products. Current CAR platforms predominantly rely on monoclonal antibody-derived single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) for target recognition. While scFv-based CARs have achieved remarkable clinical successes, they also exhibit notable limitations, including the potential to elicit anti-CAR immune responses, tonic signaling that contributes to CAR-T cell exhaustion, tumor escape via antigen loss or downregulation, and on-target, off-tumor toxicities. In response, researchers have explored alternative binding moieties for CAR architectures. Natural ligands and receptors represent one such class of alternatives. These approaches may offer advantages over conventional scFv-based CARs, such as potentially lower immunogenicity with fully human-derived domains, the ability to engage multiple targets or ligands, access to antigens that are challenging for scFvs, and the use of protein-protein interfaces shaped by evolution within human physiology. However, these benefits are not absolute. CAR junctions, non-native orientations, expression levels, modifications, and the cellular context can still generate immunogenic epitopes or dysfunctional products. Additionally, natural ligand/receptor pairs may transmit unwanted agonistic or regulatory signals that require careful engineering to mitigate. This review discusses recent advances in ligand/receptor-based CARs from a translational perspective. It also provides a critical overview of their inherent limitations, alongside potential solutions to support the rational design of next-generation constructs.

items.title: Health-related quality of life in early-stage type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study within the SMARTEST trial.
items.abstract: Normative health-related quality of life (HRQoL) data for people with early-stage, well-controlled type 2 diabetes are lacking. We aimed to describe the HRQoL profile of SMARTEST trial participants, contextualised against general population benchmarks. Baseline RAND-36 data (n = 1,501; domain scores range 0-100) were compared with population-based reference data using multiple linear regression adjusted for sex, age and education. Participants with 65 years, HRQoL exceeded reference population levels across several domains, particularly physical role functioning (β = 9.8, 95% CI 5.6; 13.9). Participants included during the pandemic reported a lower mental composite score (β = -2.5, 95% CI -4.5; -0.6). HRQoL in this early-stage type 2 diabetes cohort showed a distinct age-related pattern relative to general population benchmarks. Mental HRQoL during periods of societal disruptions merits further study.

items.title: Effects of Sauna Bathing on NMR-Based Metabolomic Profiles.
items.abstract: Frequent sauna bathing is associated with reduced risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, the biochemical pathways through which sauna bathing may exert its cardiovascular health effects remain unclear. We therefore investigated the effects of Finnish sauna bathing on various blood-based cardiometabolic biomarkers. Specifically, this study investigated how a single 30-minute Finnish sauna session (AS) and an 8-week exercise-plus-sauna intervention (ESS) influence circulating metabolomic biomarkers related to lipid and amino acid metabolism. The study included two complementary populations: (1) an acute sauna exposure study including 63 habitual sauna users with at least one cardiovascular risk factor, and (2) an 8-week randomized controlled trial (RCT) including 47 sedentary non-regular sauna users randomized to exercise, exercise plus sauna, and control arms. The exercise intervention consisted of concurrent training three times per week, with the sauna group additionally completing 15 min of post-exercise sauna bathing. Circulating metabolites were quantified using high-throughput 1H-NMR spectroscopy at multiple time points in the acute study and at baseline and post-intervention in the RCT. AS produced consistent metabolic shifts, including significant reductions in concentrations of plasma triglycerides and VLDL particles, decreases in branched-chain and aromatic amino acids, and increases in ketone bodies, suggesting a metabolic pattern compatible with enhanced lipid utilization and a transient metabolic stress response. ESS resulted in additional improvements beyond exercise alone, including reductions in LDL particle number and concentration, greater decreases in VLDL subclasses, and increases in HDL particle size, suggesting additional metabolic effects when heat exposure is added to exercise training. Sauna bathing, as an example of heat exposure, induces favorable alterations in lipid and amino acid metabolism and when combined with regular exercise, augments longer-term improvements in lipoprotein profiles.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Cabotegravir Long-Acting HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP): A Systematic Review of Modelling Studies.
items.abstract: Cabotegravir long-acting injectable (CAB-LA) is a promising non-oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention, especially where daily oral adherence is poor. Despite superior efficacy, CAB-LA's high price raises concerns about economic value and implementation across settings. This study reviewed modelling studies on CAB-LA's cost-effectiveness as PrEP across diverse populations and settings. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and Cochrane Library (2015-2025), assessing CAB-LA's cost-effectiveness versus oral PrEP or no PrEP. Eligible studies reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, cost per HIV infection averted, or cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) or disability-adjusted life year gained. Reporting quality was assessed using the CHEERS 2022 checklist. Results were narratively synthesized due to heterogeneity. Eleven modelling studies across sub-Saharan Africa, the United States, and Asia-Pacific showed that CAB-LA averted more HIV infections than oral PrEP, especially in high-incidence, low-adherence populations. In high-risk U.S. populations, CAB-LA averted about 71,000 infections and gained 4.65 million QALYs. In Africa, CAB-LA became economically favourable under lower acquisition-cost assumptions, although cost-effective prices varied across models, populations, price years and thresholds. U.S. and Asia-Pacific models found CAB-LA not cost-effective at current prices, requiring 24-88% price reductions. Sensitivity and scenario analyses showed that cost-effectiveness estimates were responsive to CAB-LA price, HIV incidence, ART coverage, adherence, persistence, and programme-delivery assumptions. CAB-LA cost-effectiveness is context dependent and generally more favourable at lower prices, higher-incidence populations, and poor oral PrEP adherence. Wider adoption may require strategies to improve economic value, equitable access, and implementation, especially in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Acinetobacter baumannii: An 11-Year Longitudinal Study at a Tertiary Hospital in Northern China.
items.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is a critical-priority pathogen. We investigated the epidemiological characteristics and clinical outcomes of Acinetobacter baumannii infections over an 11-year period at a tertiary hospital in northern China. We analysed 4,028 A. baumannii isolates from a single tertiary hospital (2014-2024; first isolate per patient-year), calculating resistance rates, annual CRAB proportion, antibiotic consumption (DDDs/100 patient-days, 2018-2024) and in-hospital mortality; testing used the Cochran-Armitage test and Spearman correlation. The CRAB proportion fell from 62.2% (2014) to 37.8% (2024; p<0.001) while antibiotic consumption rose by 29.2%. Resistance was near-universal, sparing only minocycline (4.6%) and polymyxin (0.3%). No agent's resistance rate was significantly correlated with its consumption (|ρ| ≤ 0.71; all p ≥ 0.09). In 1,811 patient-episodes (35.2% mortality), older age (OR 1.20 per 10 years), intensive-care admission (1.86), mechanical ventilation (1.74) and male sex (1.25) each independently predicted death; empirical therapy covered only 2.6% of isolates. CRAB was predominantly detected in intensive care units and was closely associated with mechanical ventilation, representing a major nosocomial pathogen. Given its high associated mortality, continuous surveillance of its epidemiological characteristics is warranted.

items.title: Lactate-driven protein lactylation contributes to aniline-induced hepatic metabolic dysfunction.
items.abstract: Aniline is a widely distributed aromatic amine pollutant with recognized hepatotoxic potential, but the molecular events linking aniline exposure to hepatic metabolic dysfunction remain incompletely defined. Protein lactylation links lactate metabolism to cell regulation and may participate in exposure-related metabolic remodeling. Here, mouse models and short-term hepatocyte experiments (5 and 10 mmol/L aniline) were integrated with transcriptomics, metabolomics, lactylomics, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate lactate-associated responses. Aniline disrupted hepatic metabolic homeostasis and produced steatotic liver injury accompanied by oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and lipid metabolic abnormalities. In cells, aniline decreased early growth response 1 (EGR1), increased lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA), promoted lactate accumulation, and enhanced global protein lactylation. Nucleoporin 153 (NUP153) showed increased lactylation after aniline treatment. LDHA manipulation altered lactate abundance and the NUP153-associated Pan-Kla signal, and pharmacological activation of PPARγ partially restored lipid-metabolism markers. L-threonine supplementation partially restored EGR1/LDHA-associated responses, reduced lactate-related metabolic signals, and alleviated metabolic injury. These findings implicate LDHA-associated lactate accumulation and protein lactylation in aniline-induced hepatic metabolic dysfunction under the tested exposure conditions.

items.title: In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.
items.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) remains a major public health threat in Africa and South America. Although the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is highly effective, its use is restricted in certain vulnerable populations, emphasizing the need for nonreplicating alternatives. We performed an integrated in silico characterization of two production-optimized recombinant YFV envelope (Env) proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains. Physicochemical, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), electrostatic, and immune simulation analyses were conducted. Both proteins were predicted to be antigenic, hydrophilic, and structurally stable, although allergenicity predictions differed for 17D Env. Epitope mapping identified multiple predicted CD8⁺ and CD4⁺ T-cell epitopes, linear B-cell epitopes, and conformational antibody-accessible regions. T-cell epitopes showed substantial conservation across YFV strains, whereas linear B-cell epitopes exhibited greater variability. Structural comparisons supported conservation of the Env monomeric fold but revealed differences from experimentally determined dimeric assemblies, raising uncertainty regarding native quaternary organization and epitope accessibility. Docking and MD simulations with the neutralizing antibody YD6 identified predicted interactions and persistent intermolecular contacts. Immune simulations predicted coordinated adaptive responses following repeated immunization. Overall, these findings support further experimental evaluation of both recombinant Env proteins as potential nonreplicating vaccine antigens, diagnostic reagents, and tools for investigating YFV antigenicity and immune responses.

items.title: Cervical Cancer Screening Uptake and Associated Behavioral Factors Among Female Primary Health Care Providers in Georgia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Primary health care (PHC) providers are instrumental in promoting cervical cancer screening, yet little is known about their own screening practices. This study assessed screening uptake and associated behavioral factors among female PHC providers in Georgia. A national cross-sectional survey was conducted in December 2023 among 1,613 female PHC providers participating in a state-funded continuing medical education program on cancer screening. A self-administered questionnaire adapted from an International Agency for Research on Cancer screening barriers tool, tailored to the Georgian context, and informed by the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model assessed screening behavior and associated factors. Lifetime screening uptake was examined using multivariable logistic regression. 57% reported ever undergoing cervical cancer screening; among those ever screened, 42% had been screened within the previous three years. In bivariate analysis, recommending/referring ≥6 patients weekly was associated with higher screening uptake (OR=1.49; 95% CI: 1.16-1.90). In multivariable analysis, screening uptake was associated with urban practice (aOR=1.28; 95% CI: 1.02-1.60), screening-frequency knowledge (aOR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.01-1.54), sufficient information (aOR = 1.53; 95% CI: 1.22-1.93), confidence in accessing screening (aOR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.24-2.00), previous screening-related training (aOR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.04-1.69), partner support (aOR = 1.92; 95% CI: 1.24-2.99), family support (aOR = 1.83; 95% CI: 1.34-2.51), perceived importance of screening (aOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.01-1.70), and definite future screening intention (aOR = 2.25; 95% CI: 1.75-2.87). Screening uptake among female PHC providers remains suboptimal and was associated with factors across psychological capability, social opportunity, and reflective motivation. Findings identify screening knowledge, practical guidance, and social support as targets for future interventions to increase eligible female PHC providers' own participation in Georgia's national cervical cancer screening program, with effectiveness requiring prospective evaluation.

items.title: A Tetrahydro-Isoquinoline Derivative as a Novel mGlu2/3 Ago/PAM with Therapeutic Potential in Models of Parkinsonism Models.
items.abstract: Introduction Parkinson's Disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder marked by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons within the dopamine nigrostriatal pathway. Current pharmacological treatments provide only symptomatic relief and are associated with several adverse effects. While indirect evidence strongly supports the therapeutic potential of metabotropic glutamate receptor 3 (mGlu3) in PD, pharmacological limitations have hindered progress in the field. In this study, we present the first functional characterization of a tetrahydroisoquinoline derivative acting as a dual agonist/positive allosteric modulator (Ago/PAM) of mGlu2/3. This compound exhibits slightly higher potency for mGlu3 compared to mGlu2, along with notable neurotrophic properties. Methods The study employed complementary in vitro and in vivo approaches, using a cellular model of PD and healthy male C57BL/6 mice. Results The novel Ago/PAM shows equal affinity for mGlu2 and mGlu3 and greater efficacy at mGlu3 receptors in recombinant cells. Exposure to the mGlu2/3 Ago/PAM protects the human neuroblastoma cell line SH-SY5Y from 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-induced cell death by modulating neurotrophic signaling pathways, including the Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase/Extracellular Signal-Regulated Kinase (MAPK/ERK) and Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinase (PI3K)-AKT pathways. Moreover, this treatment increases the expression of Glial Cell Line-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (GDNF), a key factor for dopaminergic neuron survival. Interestingly, pre-treatment with ML 337, a negative allosteric modulator for mGlu3, abolishes mGlu2/3 Ago/PAM-induced neuroprotective effects. In vivo administration of mGlu2/3 Ago/PAM upregulates GDNF and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) expression, while activating MAPK/ERK and PI3K-AKT pathways in mouse brain regions involved in PD pathophysiology, such as the striatum, the hippocampus, and the prefrontal cortex. Discussion Collectively, these findings identify this tetrahydroisoquinoline-derived compound as a novel mGlu2/3 Ago/PAM with preferential activity at mGlu3 and provide its first functional characterization, demonstrating robust neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects. Conclusion By combining agonist and positive allosteric modulation with mGlu3 selectivity, this compound represents a translationally promising strategy to counteract neurodegeneration and restore neuronal-glial homeostasis in PD. These results, though preliminary, support the therapeutic potential of this compound and, more broadly, of mGlu3-targeted approaches, laying the foundation for future in vivo studies to validate efficacy, safety, and receptor specificity.

items.title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
items.abstract: Objectives Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context. Materials and methods We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing. Postinterview evaluation sessions and researcher observation notes were analyzed to assess the system's feasibility and acceptability and identify usability, accessibility, technical, and implementation considerations. Results Participants reported that the system was easy to use and appreciated its empathetic and nonjudgmental tone. They also rated the system positively for clarity, comfort, and accessibility, indicating that conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be adapted to support qualitative data collection in underserved communities. Identified challenges included intermittent technical errors, limited contextual adaptability, and variations in participants' comfort with digital technology. Discussion Large language model-powered conversational interview systems, when guided by community engagement, ethical design principles, and human support, offer a feasible and acceptable approach to qualitative health research with underserved populations. Hybrid human-AI models may offer a scalable yet inclusive pathway for expanding participation and advancing health equity in qualitative research. Conclusion These findings support further development and evaluation of LLM-powered interview systems for community-engaged qualitative research. Ongoing technical improvement, ethical safeguards, and participatory design will be critical to ensuring these systems are used responsibly and effectively to advance health equity.

items.title: multiVIB: A unified probabilistic contrastive learning framework for atlas-scale integration of single-cell multi-omics data.
items.abstract: Integrating heterogeneous single-cell datasets requires aligning shared biological features while preserving meaningful variation across modalities, studies, and species. Here, we present multiVIB, a unified framework combining the variational information bottleneck with probabilistic contrastive learning for horizontal, vertical, and mosaic integration of single-cell multi-omics data. Across diverse benchmarks, multiVIB achieves competitive integration performance while minimizing spurious alignments. Applied to BRAIN Initiative atlas-scale datasets, multiVIB enables incremental integration of nine molecular modalities in the mouse primary motor cortex and cross-species integration of primate basal ganglia transcriptomes, recovering conserved cell identities and species-specific molecular programs. Together, these results establish multiVIB as a versatile framework for scalable, biologically faithful construction and expansion of comprehensive brain cell atlases.

items.title: An integrated single-cell and epigenomic resource for comparative analysis of the basal ganglia from BICAN.
items.abstract: The basal ganglia regulate motor, cognitive, and affective behaviors, and their dysfunction underlies diverse neurological and psychiatric disorders. Comprehensive, accessible multi-omics resources are needed to understand the regulatory mechanisms governing basal ganglia cell types. Here, we present an open, interactive web-based platform for exploring single-cell multi-omics datasets from basal ganglia, generated using 10X Multiome, single-nucleus methylome and chromatin conformation sequencing (snm3C-seq), and Paired-Tag technologies by the BICAN (NIH BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network) consortium. The platform is available at https://basalganglia.epigenomes.net/and enables integrated visualization of gene expression, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin conformation across cell types and human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse species, with direct genome browser support and comparative epigenomic functionality. Representative analyses demonstrate cell-type-specific regulatory landscapes, conserved and species-specific regulatory elements, and links between epigenomic regulation and transcription. This resource provides a scalable, community-oriented foundation for advancing basal ganglia biology and interpreting regulatory mechanisms relevant to brain function and disease.

items.title: MapMyCells: High-performance mapping of cell-by-gene data to reference brain taxonomies.
items.abstract: Single-cell reference mapping is increasingly central to translating heterogeneous datasets into consistent representations of cell identity. As cell-type atlases expand in scale and complexity, mapping new data to shared references enables reproducible annotation, cross-study integration, and accumulation of biological knowledge. We present MapMyCells, an open-source, high-performance framework for mapping diverse single-cell omics datasets to hierarchical reference taxonomies with minimal preprocessing. MapMyCells currently supports six diverse brain references spanning whole mouse and human brain, Alzheimer's disease and aging cohorts, developing mouse cortex, and a cross-species basal ganglia taxonomy. Across these references, MapMyCells accurately recovers cell identities at broad and intermediate taxonomic levels, remains robust with reduced informative gene panels, and supports transcriptomic, epigenomic, and spatial datasets. Benchmarking shows competitive accuracy with substantially lower computational requirements, enabling datasets and taxonomies containing thousands of cell types to be analyzed on standard workstations. MapMyCells provides a scalable framework for unified, extensible brain cell atlases.

items.title: Enhancer-based AAV approach for selective AADC delivery reduces motor symptoms and dyskinesia in Parkinson's mouse models.
items.abstract: Degeneration of dopamine (DA) neurons and reduced DA levels in the brain is recognized as an underlying cause of Parkinson's Disease (PD). Levodopa (L-DOPA) is the standard treatment, but its effectiveness wanes over time and prolonged use can cause L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID). AAV-mediated aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) expression in the striatum combined with L-DOPA shows promise for symptomatic improvement but requires invasive delivery. Here, we generate enhancer-driven AAVs to drive AADC expression in key cell types and pair them with a blood-brain barrier (BBB)-penetrant capsid. Across two delivery routes and PD mouse models, cell type-specific AADC expression improves survival and ameliorates motor deficits and LID, with similar or greater phenotypic rescue than ubiquitous AADC expression. We further demonstrate the conservation of enhancer-driven AADC specificity in non-human primates (NHP). This viral strategy, combined with L-DOPA, may enable a less invasive and better tolerated approach to alleviate PD motor deficits.

items.title: Sedimentary ancient DNA expands bioarchaeological evidence and interpretation at Roman Harelbeke
items.abstract: Sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) can expand archaeological research by recovering broad biological signals from small amounts of sediment. Here, we apply shotgun sedaDNA metagenomics and target capture (also known as hybridization capture) to disused Roman wells from the vicus of Harelbeke, Belgium, dated to ca. 160-300 CE, and integrate the results with existing bioarchaeological datasets. Moving beyond individual introduced taxa as proxies for Roman influence, we reconstruct community-level profiles spanning consumption-related, synanthropic, and environmental organisms. SedaDNA reproduced most established bioarchaeological signals, including cultivated plants and domestic animals, while also recovering additional environmental taxa that established methods underrepresented. Mitochondrial target capture strengthened selected faunal detections and enabled phylogenetic placement of a pig (Sus scrofa) within the European mitochondrial lineage. The predominance of previously established consumption-related taxa is consistent with subsistence continuity and selective adoption of Roman-introduced resources, although taxon counts alone cannot establish their relative importance. Analytical-effort modeling further indicates that batch-based sedaDNA workflows can provide broad biological profiles at lower cost and time investment than established archaeological methods. Overall, sedaDNA complements conventional bioarchaeology by broadening taxonomic recovery, supporting scalable sampling, and providing a broad-spectrum approach to reconstructing settlement ecology, subsistence, and human-environment interaction.

items.title: Analog Ecology: Capturing Environmental Change Before Remote Sensing Technologies
items.abstract: Historical wildlife monitoring data, often collected as population indices for harvestable species, provide longitudinal trends that can address contemporary conservation ques-tions. However, these data frequently lack corresponding environmental information needed to evaluate drivers of population change. Many long-term harvest monitoring programs predate remote sensing, and their survey protocols rarely included concurrent environmental data collection. Here, we present a generalized workflow for construct-ing ecological covariates to complement historical monitoring data and summarize sources of longitudinal environmental information spanning the pre-1970 era to the present. Using prairie-chickens and sharp-tailed grouse in Nebraska’s Sandhills as a case study, we demonstrate best practices for developing covariates that reflect species bi-ology and ecological scale. Our covariates capture long-term trends in recreation, wild-life populations, land use, grazing pressure, and climate that may influence habitat quality for grassland obligates in one of the largest intact grassland ecosystems in the continental United States. We also introduce a private-land grazing pressure index, the first longitudinal grazing index compiled for the Sandhills, with potential applications beyond ecological modeling. By providing practical guidance and resources for con-structing long-term ecological covariates, we aim to encourage wildlife practitioners to repurpose historical monitoring data to address emerging conservation challenges.

items.title: The efficacy of upgrading rural drinking water treatment in karst areas of Chongqing: simultaneous removal of conventional pollutants and microplastics.
items.abstract: Rural drinking water safety is a critical issue in China's public health sector. This study focused on typical small-scale rural water treatment plants in the karst region of southeastern Chongqing, Southwest China, and systematically compared the treatment performance of the conventional simplified coagulation-natural sedimentation-sand filtration process with that of the upgraded combined grid-flocculation-inclined tube sedimentation-submerged ultrafiltration (GF-TS-SUF) process. The removal efficiency of the processes was quantitatively assessed based on conventional parameters such as turbidity, color, iron, manganese, permanganate index, nitrate (NO 3 - ), as well as microplastics (abundance, morphology, size, polymer type), and correlations among parameters were explored. The results showed that the GF-TS-SUF process achieved substantially higher purification efficiency in this case study, with an effluent turbidity of 0.28 ± 0.02 NTU, a color of 3 ± 1 PCU, iron and manganese levels below detection limits, and a permanganate index of 1.58 ± 0.09 mg L -1 . The GF-TS-SUF process exhibited excellent microplastic retention performance, with only trace amounts of microplastics detected in the final effluent, indicating that the vast majority of influent microplastics were effectively removed. Exploratory analysis showed strong co-variation between microplastic abundance and turbidity, permanganate index and other conventional parameters across treatment stages, indicating that these readily measured indicators may serve as a useful preliminary operational reference for tracking microplastic removal. As these variables decline together along the treatment train, this relationship should nonetheless be regarded as exploratory and remains pending independent validation. This single-site case study suggests the potential feasibility of the GF-TS-SUF process for the simultaneous removal of conventional and emerging pollutants at the studied rural water treatment plant and provides a preliminary reference for other small-scale water plants with similar source-water characteristics and operational conditions.

items.title: The Role of Light in Mediating Physiological Stress in Small Corals Exposed to Elevated Temperature.
items.abstract: Marine heat waves (MHW) are important stressors on coral reefs, and evaluating their implications for the population dynamics of young corals has become a key research need. However, projecting the effects of MHW on the demographics of young corals is made difficult by an incomplete understanding of how their response to high temperature is modulated by light. Here we tested for the interactive effects of temperature and light on genetically identified colonies of the Pacific coral, Pocillopora spp. from 3-m depth in the back reef of Moorea, French Polynesia. The ecological implications of the responses to manipulated temperature and light were strengthened through context provided by long-term in situ records of temperature and light. Two 14-day trials were conducted in which young P. meandrina were exposed to 28°C and 31°C at six light levels ranging from 436 to 1621 μmol photons m -2 s -1 . The probability of bleaching was unaffected by temperature, but it increased across the light gradient, while the probability of partial or full mortality increased with light faster at 31°C compared to 28°C. Mortality was associated with a decline in the photophysiological performance ( F v / F m ) of the symbiotic algae (Symbiodiniaceae) in the corals, notably as light levels increased at 31°C but not at 28°C, and at light levels commonly reached at 3-m depth. Declines in F v / F m revealed impaired PSII functionality, although values remained higher than those usually associated with bleaching (i.e., Pocillopora spp., and show that corals pale enough to be scored as fully bleached on the reef can contain relict algal populations that remain photophysiologically functional at elevated temperature and high light.

items.title: Sequential Sampling from Memory Underlies Perceptual Decisions Unyoked from Actions.
items.abstract: Perceptual decision-making refers to the class of decisions in which sensory evidence is used to categorize percepts and guide actions. Conventionally, categorical decisions are thought to precede motor actions. However, recent studies in nonhuman primates challenge this assumption-when perceptual decisions were uncoupled from the actions they bear upon, animals postponed the decisions until relevant response options were revealed. To determine whether this postponement stems from cognitive limitations unique to nonhuman primates, we conducted a similar experiment with human participants. Naive participants viewed a random dot motion (RDM) stimulus that was difficult to categorize. After a delay period following the RDM, two choice targets were presented and participants decided which target lay closer to the perceived motion direction. Decision accuracy varied across participants, reflecting individual differences in ability to integrate motion evidence. Notably, participants with higher decision accuracy showed prolonged deliberation after choice-target presentation. Furthermore, the time they took to report their decisions depended on the strength of the motion evidence. This pattern of accuracy and decision reporting time could be accounted for by a bounded diffusion model in which participants sequentially sample stored sensory information from memory during the target selection phase. When the RDM was challenging to categorize, the subsequent appearance of the targets provided a framework to interrogate stored evidence and render a decision. Our results reveal a strategic feature of working memory of retaining information based on its future utility. This observation opens new avenues for investigating how memory and decision-making interact.

items.title: Confounds in Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Part III: Auxiliary Data.
items.abstract: In the first part of this series, we reviewed the pathways that bring about confounding nuisance signals in fMRI. Then, in the second part, we considered how human factors can modify these pathways. In this, the third and final part, we review auxiliary data that may allow researchers to identify and perhaps correct for nuisance signals and their modifiers. We consider three broad categories of data: (1) measures that can be collected synchronously with the fMRI, (2) other MRI scans that either capture trait information or attempt to define the state that exists during an fMRI scan in the same session, and (3) non-MRI measures that can be collected before or after the scan and that also capture trait or relevant state factors influencing the fMRI. We conclude with some recommendations on ways to improve fMRI experiments going forward.

items.title: Distributed Neural Dynamics Underlie the Shift from Movement Preparation to Execution.
items.abstract: Understanding how neural population activity supports the transition from movement preparation to execution remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience. Invasive recordings in nonhuman primates indicate that motor preparation and execution occupy orthogonal subspaces within the primary motor cortex (M1), yet how these neural dynamics evolve across broader networks and support skilled, memory-guided action remains poorly understood. We used source-resolved magnetoencephalography during a memory-guided finger-sequence task to track population dynamics across a cortico-hippocampal network. Manifold trajectories and decoding revealed that preparation and execution of movement sequences occupy distinct, yet not fully orthogonal, neural subspaces-a separation that generalized across all regions but was most pronounced in motor regions. Crucially, we identified a hierarchical spatio-temporal transition across the brain: The state shift originated in the hippocampus via theta-band modulations and rippled through the pre-SMA, SMA, and lateral premotor areas before culminating in M1 via broadband activity. This progression follows the functional hierarchy of descending motor pathways, with M1 shifting last, 160 msec before the first button press. Although sequence identity could be decoded from all areas during execution, only the hippocampus and M1 maintained predictive representations of upcoming sequences during preparation. These findings demonstrate that the initiation of complex motor sequences relies on a well-timed integration of hippocampal memory systems with primary motor output, rather than being a process localized to the motor cortices alone.

items.title: Biodiversity conservation and its associations with economic performance, inequality, and peace
items.abstract: Abstract Biodiversity conservation is increasingly recognized as a product of coupled social–ecological systems shaped not only by ecological processes, but also by economic capacity, social inequality, and geopolitical stability. Here, we examined whether national conservation performance is systematically associated with economic prosperity, income inequality, peace, and the importance of natural resources in the national economy across 142 countries. Conservation performance was represented using the Nature Conservation Index (NCI), a composite metric integrating biodiversity threats, land management, governance capacity, and future environmental trends. We analyzed relationships between NCI, Gross National Income per capita, the Gini coefficient, the National Peace Index, and the total nature resources rents using a generalized additive model that accounted for nonlinear relationships and income stratification. Together, these societal variables explained deviance of 52.2% for the NCI model. Economic prosperity was positively associated with NCI, although the relationship was nonlinear across income groups, suggesting that conservation capacity does not increase uniformly with development. Counter to commonly assumed relationships between inequality and biodiversity loss, income inequality showed a positive multivariate association with NCI scores. This result suggests that high national conservation performance can coexist with unequal social conditions, potentially reflecting centralized or exclusionary conservation systems that elevate institutional conservation metrics without necessarily improving equitable biodiversity outcomes. We also found that more peaceful countries consistently exhibited higher conservation performance, supporting the view that geopolitical stability provides enabling conditions for sustained conservation governance and institutional continuity. We further suggest that national conservation indices may partly capture governance capacity, reporting infrastructure, and political commitment rather than ecological condition alone, while telecoupled trade systems may allow wealthier nations to externalize environmental pressures beyond their borders. Although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, our findings highlight the need to interpret global conservation indicators cautiously and to incorporate social equity and externalized environmental impacts more explicitly into international biodiversity assessment frameworks.

items.title: Improving Parental Investments in Children: Experimental Evidence from The Gambia
items.abstract: We study two early childhood programs in The Gambia for children between 0 and 3 years of age. The basic version of the program, called Baby Friendly Community Initiative (BFCI), provides parents with child health and nutrition information delivered through home visits and community meetings. A second version, called BFCI+, is center-based and adds cognitive stimulation to the basic version of the program through activities with children. Villages were randomly assigned to one of two versions of the program or to a control group that received neither. The BFCI+ program had moderate impacts on parental investments in children in terms of resources and time. Child language development improved for well-off parents or parents in the more well-off region. Poorer parents invested more in time spent with the children, whereas those who were more materially well-off spent more financial resources on the children. The basic version of the program, the BFCI, had no detectable impacts.

items.title: The more the merrier? systematic review and meta-analysis of working memory and category learning
items.abstract: The role of working memory capacity (WMC) in category learning (CL) remains theoretically contested. While the COVIS model posits that information-integration (II) learning is WMC-independent, empirical findings are mixed. Through a systematic review and subsequent three-level meta-analysis of 21 articles (164 effect sizes), we synthesized the WMC–CL relationship. Results revealed a significant overall positive correlation (r = 0.258; trim-and-fill adjusted r = 0.118). Notably, category structure (rule-based vs. information-integration) did not significantly moderate this relationship, challenging the COVIS prediction that implicit learning is independent of WMC. However, WMC task-specific moderation revealed significantly weaker correlations for reading span compared to operation span, memory updating, and spatial storage. No moderating effects were found for age, gender, or stimulus modality. These findings suggest that performance across diverse category structures shares a common reliance on WMC.

items.title: Serotonin signaling in the rat prefrontal cortex is required for Retrieval-Induced Forgetting
items.abstract: Forgetting is a ubiquitous phenomenon actively promoted in many species. The act of remembering some experiences can cause forgetting of others in both humans and rats. We previously found that when rats retrieve a memory to guide exploration, it reduces later retention of other competing memories encoded in that environment. As with humans, this retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) relies on prefrontal control processes, is competition-dependent, and cue-independent. RIF is thought to be driven by inhibitory control signals from the prefrontal cortex that target areas where memories are stored. Serotonin plays a crucial role in behaviors requiring high cognitive demand, including memory processes, partly through its modulation of prefrontal cortex activity. However, its potential involvement in regulating active forgetting remains unexplored. Here, in male and female rats performing a task known to induce RIF, we pharmacologically manipulated serotonin 5-HT1A, 5-HT2A, and 5-HT2C receptors and their downstream effectors in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). Our findings reveal a specific role for prefrontal serotonin signaling in RIF. Whereas 5-HT2C receptor manipulation had no effect, activating 5-HT1A or blocking 5-HT2A receptors in the mPFC abolished RIF. By contrast, activating 5-HT2A receptors promotes RIF under conditions in which it is normally reduced. Further analyses identified the PI3K/AKT pathway as a downstream effector of 5-HT2A receptor signaling, suggesting a specific molecular mechanism through which serotonin modulates inhibitory control over memory. These results uncover a previously unrecognized serotonergic modulation of adaptive forgetting, identifying specific receptor subtypes that link prefrontal serotonin signaling to inhibitory control over memory competition. Significance statement Forgetting is an essential, active process that helps the brain stay flexible and focused. In both humans and animals, remembering one thing can lead to forgetting competing memories, a phenomenon called retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF). Our research shows that serotonin, a neurotransmitter best known for its role in mood, also actively regulates which memories are forgotten. In rats, we found that serotonin signaling in the prefrontal cortex regulates adaptive forgetting: 5-HT2A receptor signaling promotes RIF, whereas activation of 5-HT1A receptors disrupts it. We further identified PI3K/AKT signaling as a key downstream effector of 5-HT2A receptor activation in this process. These findings matter because the mechanisms of active forgetting remain poorly understood, and their disruption may contribute to psychopathological conditions.

items.title: Noun-adjective collocations in L2 Portuguese: Exploring the effects of proficiency and native language in a large-scale learner corpus
items.abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the development of phraseological knowledge in Portuguese second language learners, focusing on noun–adjective combinations through the lenses of phrasal frequency, association strength, and accuracy. We analysed essays from 693 learners across five proficiency levels, representing 18 typologically diverse first languages (L1). Learners’ use of noun–adjective combinations was examined using four association measures — phrase frequency, mutual information, log dice, and delta P (ΔP) — as well as the accuracy of use. Findings reveal that phraseological development is not linear; advanced learners produced less frequent and less strongly-associated combinations, suggesting a shift toward more varied or creative expressions. L1 word order typology did not influence phrase frequency or association strength, but learners from noun–adjective dominant L1s produced collocations more accurately, indicating a dissociation between accuracy and idiomaticity. Accuracy followed a U-shaped developmental trajectory. Overall, the results highlight the complex interplay of learner and input-related variables in L2 phraseological development.

items.title: A moderation examination of the effects of a mindfulness-based intervention on primary school students’ symptoms of inattention, depression, and anxiety
items.abstract: Abstract The number of mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) has proliferated in the last decade, as accessible evidence-based practices, to improve children’s mental health in school settings. However, some studies suggest that MBIs do not offer distinct advantages over other mental health promotion interventions. These inconsistent findings may be explained, at least in part, by the lack of a clear definition of what constitutes a MBI, inconsistencies in intervention length and facilitator training, and importantly, the limited examination of moderating variables––particularly dispositional mindfulness, emotional regulation, and social competence––that may influence intervention effectiveness and mental health outcomes (inattention, anxiety, and depression). The present study was therefore interested in the potential benefits associated with a case of this type of intervention and aimed to explore whether dispositional (i.e., trait) mindfulness and mental health indicators evolved over time in primary school children. A secondary objective meant to evaluate whether receiving a MBI could moderate the relationship between changes in mindfulness and changes in mental health indicators. Contrary to our hypothesis, results showed that mindfulness levels were linked with indicators of mental health. Specifically, changes in mindfulness were associated with increases in inattention, anxiety and depression using structural equation modelling. Moreover, the association between changes in mindfulness and inattention differed by intervention group, with greater increases in mindfulness associated with greater increases in inattention in the control group but not in the intervention group. Results thus lend support to exercising caution when aiming to only foster mindfulness abilities, without ensuring that children also learn the emotion regulation skills that are required to deal with the increased awareness of their difficulties. ClinicalTrials.gov trial registration number NCT06346002; trial registration date: April 3rd, 2024.

items.title: Public carry, private fear: empirical evidence on fear and avoidance responses to visible firearms
items.abstract: Introduction The Supreme Court's 2022 New York State Rifle Pistol Association v. Bruen decision recognized a constitutional right to carry firearms in public. Its 2024 United States v. Rahimi decision applied Bruen's historical approach, considering the affrighting tradition's going armed laws prohibiting carrying weapons in a manner that terrorized the public. Little experimental research has examined fear responses to visibly carried firearms in ordinary public encounters. The current preregistered between-subjects experiment examined whether firearm visibility was associated with fear, hostile intent attribution, perceived proximity, and avoidance or reporting intentions. The study also examined hostile intent attribution and perceived proximity as potential mediators of the association between firearm visibility and fear, and rural identity as a potential moderator. Methods Participants were 415 U.S. adults recruited through Prolific in February 2026 (ages 18–81; M = 41.31, SD = 12.46). Of these, 54.0% were male and 44.3% female; 71.6% identified as White, 10.4% Black, 9.2% Asian, and 4.6% Hispanic. Participants were randomly assigned to view one of two 6-second videos showing the same individual in a public setting, either carrying a visible firearm ( n = 205) or no firearm ( n = 210). Welch's t -tests compared conditions, and a bootstrapped parallel mediation model examined indirect effects on fear. Moderated regression and moderated mediation tested rural identity as a moderator. Results Participants who viewed the armed individual reported greater fear ( d = 1.15), hostile intent attribution ( d = 1.47), perceived proximity ( d = 0.87), and avoidance or reporting intentions ( d = 1.86) than those who viewed the unarmed individual. Hostile intent attribution measured judgments about the individual's intentions, while perceived proximity measured felt closeness or intrusion. Together, these variables statistically accounted for approximately 81% of the total effect of firearm visibility on fear. Gun owners and non-owners showed similar differences between conditions, with no significant moderation by firearm ownership. Rural identity did not moderate the proposed pathways in the predicted direction. Discussion The findings provide experimental evidence that viewing a visibly armed individual in the setting studied was associated with greater fear, a response relevant to the historical affrighting tradition.

items.title: Exploring the Value of Diverse LLM Explanations in Introductory Programming
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown the potential to generate code explanations that surpass those of peers in quality, offering promising opportunities for computer science education. While these explanations may not yet match the depth and clarity of instructor-provided explanations, research in computational creativity highlights that the quantity and diversity of ideas can often outweigh a singular focus on quality. Inspired by this, we explore whether combining multiple diverse explanations, each emphasizing distinct aspects (e.g., function, concept, goal), can enhance students' understanding of programming exercises compared to generic explanations that do not emphasize distinct conceptual aspects. In our study 971 first-year computing students were randomly assigned either diverse or generic LLM-generated explanations for two programming exercises. Students completed multiple-choice and open-ended questions for each exercise, followed by Likert-scale questions and open-ended reflections. Our findings outline patterns in student performance and perceived cognitive load across the two explanation conditions. These findings highlight how variation in explanation emphasis may relate to learner engagement and understanding. Across participants, open-ended response accuracy was consistently about 7.7% higher when students received diverse explanations, with no difference in perceived cognitive load.

items.title: Less Deliberate in Teams: Student LLM Use Across Individual and Collaborative Work
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become common in computing courses, we need to understand how the social setting shapes how students use them. This paper reports findings from a semester-long study of 96 undergraduate students who completed six assignments, alternating between individual homework and team project milestones. We tracked LLM usage, prompting habits, and how students verified AI-generated output across all six assignments. LLM usage dropped by 42.7 percentage points when students moved from individual work to their first team milestone, then partly recovered in later team tasks. Students also wrote fewer prompts, used fewer deliberate prompting strategies, and checked LLM output less carefully. The share of students who ran tests on AI-generated code fell by 19.4 percentage points during team assignments and never fully rebounded. A within-student analysis found that 18.9% of students who consistently used LLMs on their own stopped using them entirely in teams, while only 3.2% went the other direction. These results suggest that collaborative context is associated with reduced deliberate LLM engagement beyond what task type alone can explain. The moment students form teams appears to be a critical turning point that may benefit from more explicit instructional support.

items.title: Exploring Mindfulness in the Context of Gambling: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Future Directions
items.abstract: Abstract Background Although researchers have investigated the relationship between mindfulness and gambling, findings across observational and intervention studies remain underdeveloped and inconsistent. Objectives This scoping review synthesised existing literature on mindfulness (state and trait) and gambling by addressing two key research questions: (1) How does mindfulness (state and trait) relate to gambling ? and (2) What areas and gaps in knowledge require further investigation and clarification ?. Method Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, five electronic databases (Academic Search Elite, PsycINFO, PsycProQuest, Scopus, and PubMed Central) were searched from inception to March 2025, with an updated search in November 2025. Independent double-screening and data extraction against a priori eligibility criteria yielded 20 synthesised peer-reviewed articles. Data were synthesised using descriptive and thematic approaches. Results High levels of trait mindfulness were related to lower gambling severity. The mindfulness facets of non-judging and acting with awareness were most consistently associated with lower gambling severity and propensity. Preliminary evidence also associated mindfulness-based interventions with lower levels of gambling severity. Conclusions Lower levels of mindfulness potentially serve as a risk factor for increased gambling propensity. However, the literature surrounding mindfulness and gambling remains underdeveloped, with limited evidence regarding underlying mechanisms or potential bi-directional relationships. Future research adopting randomised controlled trials, qualitative methodologies, multidimensional measurement, and culturally diverse samples is required to address these current gaps in understanding. Preregistration This review was not preregistered.

items.title: The social cure effects of United Voices: a randomized waitlist-controlled pilot trial of an online group-singing intervention for older adults with HIV
items.abstract: Introduction Older adults with HIV experience increasing loneliness and social isolation as they age with the stigma of HIV. Group singing is a promising social identity approach but remains largely understudied among people with stigmatizing health conditions. Based on our conceptual model, we developed United Voices (UV), a group-singing intervention for older adults with HIV to mitigate the impacts of stigma on loneliness and social isolation. Methods We conducted a randomized, waitlist-controlled pilot trial of UV to evaluate its feasibility and acceptability. A total of 23 people with HIV ages 50 years and older were randomized into immediate- (n=13) or delayed-start (n=10) group of 12 weekly 90-minute group-singing sessions via Zoom during COVID-19. Psychosocial and behavioral measures were administered at baseline, 6- and 12-weeks, and semi-structured exit interviews were conducted. Results Of four a priori feasibility thresholds, only enrollment was met (6.8 per week vs. 6). Of 27 enrolled participants, 23 (85%) were randomized (threshold 100%). Of 13 randomized to the immediate-start arm, 9 (69.2%) completed baseline (threshold 80%); of these, 7 (77.8%) attended at least 10 of 12 rehearsals and 7 (77.8%) completed both follow-up assessments (thresholds 80%). Among the 7 participants who completed the acceptability survey, the 80% benchmark was met for staff support (100%), information provided, the study website, rehearsal structure, and confidence in ability to participate (86% each), but not for overall satisfaction with the choir (71%) or the research study (57%). Exit interviews from 4 of the 13 participants randomized to the immediate-start arm indicated that while participants were at first skeptical regarding online group-singing, the experience was enjoyable, providing a social outlet during shelter-in-place. Discussion Participants appreciated getting to know and supporting each other over time. The professionally rendered concert recording was a source of pride. Interviewed participants described pride, belonging, and mutual support, consistent with the social identity processes UV is designed to engage; whether these processes reduce loneliness and social isolation remains to be tested. Findings identify the procedural changes needed before a full-scale randomized controlled trial to test the efficacy of UV among older adults with HIV.

items.title: Development and feasibility of a theory-driven multidomain intervention for community-dwelling older adults with mild cognitive impairment: a quasi-experimental pilot study based on the Multi-Theory Model
items.abstract: Abstract Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a critical stage for dementia prevention, and multidomain interventions are recommended to delay cognitive decline. However, implementing these interventions in community settings remains challenging because of difficulties in initiating health behaviours and maintaining long-term adherence. Theory-based interventions can facilitate the initiation of behaviors and sustained engagement. This study aimed to develop a multidomain intervention guided by the Multi-Theory Model (MTM) for community-dwelling older adults with MCI and to evaluate its feasibility and preliminary effectiveness. Methods This study comprised two sequential phases: intervention development and feasibility evaluation. The intervention was developed through evidence synthesis, semi-structured interviews with older adults with MCI guided by the Multi-Theory Model (MTM), and multidisciplinary expert consultation. A 12-week quasi-experimental pilot study with a historical non-equivalent control group was subsequently conducted. Participants in the control group (n = 20) received a conventional multidomain intervention, whereas those in the intervention group (n = 22) received the MTM-guided multidomain intervention. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment and adherence. The primary outcome was feasibility, assessed by recruitment and adherence. Secondary outcomes included cognitive function, physical performance, frailty, depressive symptoms, instrumental activities of daily living, and social participation. Results Forty participants completed the study (intervention, n = 21; control, n = 19). Recruitment was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (73.3% vs. 40.0%, P = 0.024), and overall adherence was also significantly better (P = 0.007). Compared with the control group, participants receiving the MTM-guided intervention demonstrated significantly greater improvements in global cognitive function, physical performance, instrumental activities of daily living, and social participation (all P < 0.05), together with greater reductions in frailty and depressive symptoms (both P < 0.001). Conclusions The MTM-guided multidomain intervention was feasible and acceptable for community-dwelling older adults with MCI, with higher recruitment and adherence than a conventional programme. These findings suggest that integrating behaviour change strategies that explicitly target behaviour initiation and maintenance may facilitate the implementation of multidomain interventions in community settings. Larger multicentre randomised controlled trials with longer follow-up are warranted to confirm the intervention's effectiveness and scalability. Trial registration This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500112119; registered on 10 November 2025. https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=289572).
