items.title: A scoping review of self-silencing and mental health outcomes in women across three decades
items.abstract: Silencing the Self-theory proposes that women who inhibit self-expression to preserve close relationships are at greater risk of depression. This scoping review maps the empirical literature on self-silencing and women’s mental health published since 1996. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched Scopus, Web of Science and ProQuest (1,761 records) and an AI-assisted search engine (Consensus; 108 records). After deduplication, single-reviewer title/abstract screening and quality-control checks, 184 records (1996–2026) were charted: 154 primary studies, 11 reviews and 19 non-empirical records. Two raters appraised the quantitative studies with the MMAT (κ = 0.98). Depressive symptoms were the most frequently examined outcome (111 of 184 records; 60.3%), followed by anxiety (29; 15.8%), disordered eating (27; 14.7%), self-esteem (19; 10.3%), relationship functioning (18; 9.8%), intimate partner violence (18; 9.8%), trauma/PTSD (9; 4.9%) and suicidality (2; 1.1%). Most studies were cross-sectional, and cultural context, racial identity and partner dynamics are increasingly examined as moderators. Screening and charting were done by one reviewer from abstracts, and effect directions and sizes were not charted, so counts show where research effort has gone, not the strength or consistency of associations. The review maps three decades of research across outcomes, populations, designs and theoretical frameworks, and identifies which outcome areas now have enough primary studies to justify full systematic reviews. Many women learn to quiet their own thoughts, feelings and needs to keep the peace in close relationships. This review looks at “self-silencing” and how it connects to women’s mental health. We searched three academic databases and a supplementary citation-search tool, then screened the results against explicit criteria and cross-checked them against a keyword-network analysis, arriving at 184 records published between 1996 and 2026 that map what is already known about self-silencing and women’s mental health. Of these, 154 were primary empirical studies (original research reporting new data), 11 were reviews of the existing literature, and 19 were commentaries, conceptual papers or book chapters without new data. Most of these studies look at depression; fewer look at eating problems, self-esteem and relationships, and a growing number ask whether the picture differs by culture or racial identity. Most of this evidence comes from single-survey, cross-sectional studies, so they can show that self-silencing and poorer mental health tend to occur together, but not that one causes the other. The review is intended to help clinicians and researchers see which populations and mechanisms have been studied most, and to help researchers identify where more rigorous, longer-term, and more diverse research is still needed.

items.title: Processing speed accounts for the discriminative power of a brief smartphone Go/No-Go task among individuals with multiple sclerosis
items.abstract: Background Identifying and longitudinally measuring cognitive decline remains challenging because traditional assessments rely largely on episodic, in-person administration of analog scales by trained examiners. Smartphone technology offers a scalable alternative for extracting distinct digital biomarkers from continuous sensor and event streams. Following the integration of several cognitive modules into the self-administered Neurological Functions Test Suite (NeuFun-TS), this study evaluates the clinical utility and incremental validity of a final candidate module: a brief (30 s per hand) equiprobable (50/50) Go/No-Go (50/50GNG) choice-reaction task. Methods We analyzed 3,270 quality-controlled 30-s runs from 303 participants, with primary analyses focused on the first run per hand (488 observations; 18,650 stimuli) across 34 healthy donors (HDs) and 213 multiple sclerosis (MS) participants. From the raw event stream, we screened 16 candidate metrics and retained 10 based on their psychometric properties. Using these 10 metrics, we evaluated diagnostic group separation, test–retest reliability, correlations with clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) benchmarks, and incremental validity over existing digital modules: the randomized Symbol Digit Modalities Test (rSDMT) and the Motor Sequencing Test (MST), using paired observations. Results Although nine of the 10 outcomes significantly separated HD from MS and seven separated relapsing–remitting from progressive MS subtypes (all adjusted p < 0.05), discriminative power was driven almost entirely by response latency rather than by commission errors or inhibitory metrics. Response latency accounted for the majority of its full-run separation within the first 12 s. Multi-predictor composite scores offered no diagnostic advantage over reaction time alone. Furthermore, the Go/No-Go task showed poor-to-moderate longitudinal test–retest reliability and did not provide incremental clinical value over existing modules. Conclusion In this brief implementation, the smartphone Go/No-Go task served as a choice-reaction-time measure reflecting processing-speed impairment in MS; however, its discriminative capability was redundant with reaction-time metrics already implemented on the platform, so the module was excluded from NeuFun-TS. These findings do not generalize to longer continuous performance tests, whose error-based measures require many more stimuli than a 30-s run provides.

items.title: Trees on Farms Provide Both Wood Value and Conservation Value in a Tropical Forest System: A Case Study from Western Kenya
items.abstract: The false perception that preserving tropical rainforests must come at the expense of local community need creates an unnecessary dilemma for conservation. In fact, local communities frequently balance subsistence needs with ecosystem integrity. Agroforestry, both cultural and contemporary, is one system that can simultaneously enhance biodiversity and provide for human needs, but interactions between social and natural dimensions are relatively undescribed. In this study, we explore whether agroforestry practices in a moist tropical forest system and their surroundings in western Kenya can provide timber/fuelwood value to smallholder farmers while promoting biodiversity. We described agroforestry attributes on farms around Kakamega Forest, assessed relationships between tree biodiversity and the number and biomass of timber/fuelwood trees, and explored relationships among tree diversity attributes on a landscape scale. We recorded 58 forest- and 66 farm-tree species. There was no significant relationship between overall tree diversity and the number of farm trees used for timber/fuelwood. Complementarity analyses suggest that conservation outcomes for the region cannot occur without including the forest species found on agroforestry farms. Therefore, as agroforestry farms support regional biodiversity conservation, increased recognition must be given to farmers’ perception of tree value and their selection of species to maintain when devising regional biodiversity conservation targets.

items.title: Humans versus machines: artificial intelligence performs similarly to manual analysis in benthic reef monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Tropical reefs are among the most biodiverse and threatened marine ecosystems and face both local and global stressors. Understanding community dynamics and ecosystem functioning under these pressures requires long-term monitoring. Image-based surveys are increasingly used in reef ecology because they enable rapid data acquisition and storage. However, manual identification of benthic organisms is time-consuming and potentially subjective, creating a bottleneck between image collection and ecological analysis. Automated annotation tools represent promising solutions, but few studies have directly compared their performance with that of manual approaches, especially under varying image quality conditions. Here, we assess the usefulness of the CoralNet automated tool for classifying benthic cover in tropical reef images and evaluate how image quality influences both manual and automated annotations. Using expert-validated images, we trained and tested both approaches, measuring performance with Cohen’s Kappa coefficient and modeling the effects of image imperfections. We found that manual and automated annotators achieved similar performance across most taxonomic and morphofunctional groups, and both were similarly affected by image quality. Importantly, although the automated annotator showed a slightly lower performance than the manual annotator, image-quality imperfections had a stronger influence on annotation performance than annotator type itself. Our findings indicate that automated annotation can provide comparable performance to manual methods once appropriately trained, with strong potential to enhance large-scale monitoring, biodiversity assessments, and conservation strategies in reef ecosystems.

items.title: Ant dominance may mask effects of tree diversity on carcass decomposition
items.abstract: Abstract Tree diversity promotes the diversity of organisms at higher trophic levels and associated ecosystem functions. Tree diversity may thus also influence communities of insect decomposers and thereby accelerate the decomposition of animal carcasses. To test this, we placed 864 dead mice and measured their decomposition over two days across 96 plots in a forest biodiversity experiment (BEF-China) during the monsoon season in subtropical China in 2024. We also captured carcass-associated arthropods using mouse-baited traps subsequently. We sampled 8,916 decomposer invertebrates (≥ 60 species, twelve orders). The abundance, richness, and composition of decomposers (ants, flies and other) were indirectly linked to tree diversity through associated changes in canopy cover. Ants were most abundant in traps (55.5% of individuals) and dominated carcasses in over half of cases (55.9%), whereas flies, although common (33.1%), rarely dominated decomposition (7.0%). Carcass decomposition was 30.8% faster in closed forests but was not additionally influenced by tree or decomposer species richness. Decomposition was instead strongly related to ant-fly interactions. It was 66.5% faster when flies, rather than ants, were the primary decomposers. When both groups co-occurred, ants often outcompeted flies, resulting in slower decomposition. This study shows that, in subtropical forests during the monsoon season, ants dominate small vertebrate carcasses, suppress other decomposers and respond little to tree diversity. Consequently, decomposition rates are only weakly linked to the richness of decomposer or tree species. These findings highlight that ecosystem functions mediated by higher trophic interactions can depend more on the identity and interactions of dominant species than on overall biodiversity.

items.title: Detection of zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum in invasive beavers from southern Tierra del Fuego, Chile
items.abstract: Since their introduction to Tierra del Fuego in 1946, invasive beavers ( Castor canadensis ) have expanded their population and caused extensive environmental degradation across the sub-Antarctic region. Beaver dams have profoundly impacted peatlands, mature sub-Antarctic forests, and watercourses. Here, we report a pathogen in invasive beavers in Patagonia and discuss their potential role as a reservoir of waterborne zoonotic pathogens. We detected Cryptosporidium through microscopy using the Ziehl-Neelsen staining technique in beavers collected from southern Tierra del Fuego. Out of the 105 beavers examined, three tested positive to optical microscopy, which were then identified molecularly as Cryptosporidium parvum by sequence analysis of the 18S ribosomal DNA (rDNA), showing a 2.87% infection rate. Given the potential impacts of Cryptosporidium parvum upon native species, wildlife, and human health, this finding highlights the potential risks associated with the ongoing expansion of beavers into other areas of the sub-Antarctic region. A potential role of invasive beavers as reservoirs of zoonotic Cryptosporidium spp. in Patagonia emphasizes the unknown consequences of human-introduced exotic species on pristine ecosystems.

items.title: Ecosystem services in shellfish reef restoration and coastal policy: A global scoping review
items.abstract: Shellfish reefs can contribute to nature-based solutions (NbS) that can support coastal protection, water quality, and biodiversity, yet the extent to which their ecosystem services (ES) are reflected in coastal policy remains unclear. This global scoping review maps the scientific evidence on ES associated with shellfish reefs and examines their relationships with restoration approaches, policy instruments, and governance frameworks. Specifically, we (i) classify reported ES, (ii) examine associations between restoration approaches and reported ES, (iii) assess the representation of policy instruments and governance dimensions in the reviewed literature, and (iv) identify knowledge gaps relevant to coastal management and planning. We used a predefined search strategy, eligibility criteria, and structured full-text coding to map evidence across shellfish taxa, geographic regions, restoration approaches, and policy dimensions, identifying areas of concentrated and limited representation within the retrieved literature. Within the 151 included studies, regulating and supporting services were reported more frequently than provisioning and cultural services. Although approximately three-quarters of studies included explicit policy content, links to operational instruments—such as spatial planning, permitting, and incentive-based mechanisms—were less frequently reported. Monitoring and stakeholder engagement were inconsistently documented, potentially limiting the usability of the published evidence for decision-making. These findings reveal gaps in how connections between ecosystem-service evidence, restoration, and coastal governance are documented in the literature. Greater attention to socio-ecological objectives, consistent restoration monitoring, and the reporting of links between ES outcomes and policy instruments could strengthen the relevance of this evidence for coastal decision-making. Broader documentation from less frequently represented regions, including parts of the Global South, would improve the geographic breadth of the evidence base.

items.title: Transient species can increase resident metapopulation size by modifying local conditions and regional connectivity
items.abstract: Abstract Populations are regulated by processes operating at both local and regional scales. As a result, species can interact not only within local communities but also through regional-scale processes. However, the feedback between local and regional processes of species interactions in shaping metapopulation dynamics have rarely been tested experimentally. Using nectar microbes as a model system, we examine how a bacterial species dispersing to a sink habitat, sustained by external supply, can interact with a resident yeast species directly by modifying local nectar chemistry and indirectly by altering metapopulation connectivity. We show that the external supply of bacteria increases resident yeast densities, potentially through increased local productivity, and that this benefit is enhanced when the dispersal rate of yeast is reduced in patches supplied with bacteria. Analysis of a metapopulation model indicates that the benefit of dispersal modification on metapopulation size occurs only when local productivity differs across patches, consistent with our interpretation that bacterial supply increases local productivity. Taken together, our results underscore the role of dispersal in shaping how metapopulations experience density-dependence across heterogeneous landscapes, highlight the relevance of material flows across ecosystem boundaries, and suggest a plausible mechanism in which transient species may leave lasting impacts on ecological communities.

items.title: Recurrent hybridization between highly divergent paramecium species
items.abstract: The process of speciation, through which two reproductively isolated species emerge from an ancestral population, is often gradual, including a period during which gene flow still occurs, and hence speciation remains reversible. However, if isolation persists, the progressive accumulation of genetic incompatibilities ultimately locks the speciation process, reaching the point where hybrid offspring are inviable or sterile. In plants and animals, the establishment of species barriers is quite rapid: Beyond a net genetic divergence of 0.02 substitutions per synonymous site, interspecific introgressions become extremely rare. Here we report that in ciliates, species barriers can be broken despite huge genetic divergence. We show that the genome of Paramecium sonneborni contains hundreds of DNA segments that were acquired by recurrent horizontal transfers from multiple very distant lineages (synonymous divergence ~1 substitution/site). These segments approach the size of full-length chromosomes, which indicates that they were introgressed by interspecific mating. These data show that in the ancestry of P. sonneborni , hybridization events with highly divergent species occurred repeatedly and led to viable and fertile offspring. We propose that this unexpected promiscuous sexual behavior is made possible by the fact that paramecia separate somatic and germline functions in two types of nuclei: The elimination of non-self-DNA fragments during the development of the somatic genome allows individuals of a species to remain phenotypically the same, despite recurrent genetic flow from distant species into their germline.

items.title: Organic matter composition and origin differ between restored and natural UK saltmarshes up to 100 years after the breach
items.abstract: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. While carbon stocks in restored marshes were found to reach equivalence with natural sites, the shares of autochthonous and allochthonous carbon sources entering these marshes are less well known. This issue is important because allochthonous carbon is usually excluded from stock calculations. To determine if differences do exist, the conventional tools for determining organic matter source – elemental, stable isotope and thermogravimetric analyses – were applied to sediments from four restored saltmarshes of different ages. Comparisons were then made with existing data from nearby natural marshes. Breach depth horizons in individual cores were successfully identified using foraminifera, unicellular marine protists. The OC/N-ratio was persistently lower in restored saltmarshes compared with natural counterparts even 100 years after the creation of a breach. Additionally, δ 13 C signals indicated a mixture of organic matter sources to the restored sites and there was often a higher proportion, based upon thermal sensitivity, of recalcitrant material in the organic matter of the restored marshes. Together, these results indicated that a higher proportion of allochthonous organic matter was entering these restored marshes. Understanding the composition of the organic matter in restored marsh sediment will allow the development of robust and constructive climate change mitigation methods.

items.title: Dormancy stabilizes structured food webs
items.abstract: Theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. This discrepancy motivates enduring interest in ecological mechanisms that limit or counteract instability. Dormancy—reversible metabolic suppression—may be one. Dormancy is a ubiquitous life history trait found in organisms ranging from bacteria to trees. Dormant individuals form “seed banks” that are temporarily disengaged from demographic processes and species interactions, creating a memory of past ecological dynamics. Seed banks can stabilize predator–prey interactions, but whether, when, and how they affect the stability of larger ecological networks is uncertain. We show that dormancy stabilizes oscillatory dynamics in a minimal mathematical model and illustrate how dormancy converts high oscillation frequency into strong restoring force. We find that dormancy can have qualitative stabilizing effects in structured food webs that undergo Hopf bifurcations and exhibit oscillatory instability, but rarely in unstructured networks or networks with symmetric (competitive or mutualistic) interactions. This classification remains accurate when only some species go dormant and drive stabilization. Our results clarify when dormancy can promote stability, indicating that it may be an important but overlooked stabilizing factor in food webs.

items.title: Where are Barn Swallow nesting records most abundant in anthropogenic landscapes? Testing the Goldilocks hypothesis along urban–rural environmental gradients
items.abstract: Abstract Urban and rural environments are often treated as contrasting habitat types, but they can also be interpreted as the two ends of a continuous land-use gradient shaped by human activities. Along such gradients, organisms may experience trade-offs among different ecological resources. Here we introduce the Goldilocks hypothesis, which predicts that breeding activity is maximized under intermediate environmental conditions between urban and rural environments. To test this hypothesis, we investigated the distribution of Barn Swallow (Hirundo rustica) nests along urban–rural gradients in three regions of Kyushu, Japan (Nagasaki, Fukuoka, and Kagoshima). Environmental gradients were quantified using principal component analysis (PCA) based on land-cover composition within 500 m grid cells. Nest abundance showed a consistent unimodal pattern across all regions, peaking at intermediate environmental conditions. Potential nesting sites increased toward the urban end of the gradient, whereas potential foraging habitats increased toward the rural end, indicating a spatial trade-off between key breeding resources. These findings support the Goldilocks hypothesis and highlight the ecological importance of intermediate landscapes where elements of contrasting human-modified environments overlap, providing insights for landscape management and biodiversity conservation under ongoing urbanization.

items.title: Genetic variability within Triatoma sanguisuga complex in North America and the re-description of Triatoma ambigua Neiva, 1911, with specimens from Florida, USA
items.abstract: Triatoma sanguisuga is the most widely distributed triatomine vector in North America, occurring in at least 23 U.S. states and capable of transmitting Trypanosoma cruzi to humans. Historical morphological variability led to the description of several subspecies, but their taxonomic validity has remained unresolved. We integrated molecular (cytochrome b, n = 58; ITS-2, n = 23) and morphometric (18 characters, n = 82 specimens) data to reassess species boundaries within T. sanguisuga sensu lato. Four species-delimitation methods (GMYC, ABGD, mPTP, hierBAPS) consistently identified four divergent mitochondrial lineages; post-hoc K2P distances among these groups ranged from 4.78 to 8.20% (mean pairwise distances). Florida specimens formed a distinct, strongly supported clade (Group 1; mean K2P 7.19–8.20% from other groups) corresponding to T. sanguisuga var. ambigua Neiva, 1911. Linear discriminant analysis discriminated Florida and non-Florida morphotypes (100% resubstitution accuracy; 80–100% accuracy on small held-out random-forest test subsets), with synthlipsis width providing the strongest diagnostic character (AUC > 0.96). Based on concordant mitochondrial and nuclear evidence and geographically congruent morphological evidence, we revalidate Triatoma ambigua Neiva, 1911 stat. rev. as a distinct species within a newly defined T. sanguisuga complex and designate a neotype from the Instituto Oswaldo Cruz collection. Additional triatomine sampling in Florida and adjacent southeastern states is needed to characterize geographic boundaries. These findings have implications for Chagas disease vector surveillance in the southeastern United States.

items.title: Facility-scale quantification and monitoring of ammonia (NH 3 ) emissions using ASTER multispectral thermal infrared observations
items.abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is an important atmospheric pollutant affecting air quality, ecosystems, and climate. Hyperspectral thermal infrared sounders such as IASI and CrIS combine broad coverage with high spectral sensitivity, but their kilometer-scale footprints limit facility-scale source attribution. Here we test whether high-spatial-resolution multispectral thermal infrared imaging can detect NH 3 plumes at facility scale. We develop a physically based retrieval framework for the Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission and Reflection Radiometer (ASTER), combining radiative transfer calculations with lookup table (LUT) inversion. The method exploits the differential sensitivity of ASTER bands 13 and 14 to NH 3 absorption in the ν 2 band near 930–970 cm −1 , retrieving NH 3 column enhancements at 90 m spatial resolution with surface emissivity prescribed from a long-term ASTER emissivity climatology. NH 3 absorption remains measurable after convolution with the ASTER spectral response functions, but retrieval performance depends strongly on thermal contrast between the surface and the NH 3 -bearing layer. The retrieval is applied to three industrial NH 3 point sources: Khor Al Zubair, Tolyatti, and Piesteritz. Khor Al Zubair yields repeated source-connected plumes under favorable arid conditions; Tolyatti and Piesteritz show that detection is also possible in more heterogeneous environments. Source rates derived with the Integrated Mass Enhancement method are instantaneous estimates for individual detected scenes rather than annual mean emissions, with detected-scene medians of 56.6, 27.1, and 6.0 kt yr −1 at the three sites. These agree in order of magnitude with published satellite and airborne estimates, and at Khor Al Zubair to within a few per cent of the CrIS estimate once the differing NH 3 lifetime assumptions are placed on a common basis. The reported uncertainties are dominated by the assumed effective wind speed and are not a complete error budget. Multispectral TIR imagers can therefore resolve NH 3 plume structure and source location, complementing coarse-resolution sounders. Sampling is limited by revisit frequency, cloud cover and thermal contrast, so the approach suits episodic mapping of large, persistent sources and retrospective analysis of the ASTER archive.

items.title: Polymetallic nodules provide a distinct habitat for abyssal meiofauna
items.abstract: Abstract Deep-sea abyssal plains harbour extensive biodiversity, much of which remains undocumented. Polymetallic nodules in the abyssal plains of the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), Central Pacific, harbour diverse meiofaunal communities within their crevices, representing an understudied habitat. Given their high concentrations of nickel, copper, and cobalt, nodules are currently one of the primary targets for the extraction of deep-sea mineral resources. Here, we characterise the physical properties of polymetallic nodules, quantify their meiofaunal crevice communities, and compare them to those from the nearby sediments. We show that nodules contain internal cracks and microfossils, that their crevices harbour meiofaunal communities dominated by nematodes and copepods, and that faunal abundance increases significantly with nodule volume. Foraminifera were also a recurrent component of nodule-crevice assemblages. Nodule-crevice nematode and copepod abundances were equivalent to approximately 10% and 25%, respectively, of those recorded in nearby sediments across the two exploration contract areas in the eastern CCZ. Based on 18S rRNA data, nematode and copepod assemblages recovered from nodule crevices differed from those recovered from nearby sediments collected during the same expedition and within the same exploration contract areas. Our findings, therefore, demonstrate the presence of nodule-associated crevice fauna and the consequent risk of biodiversity loss associated with nodule removal through potential future commercial mining.

items.title: Paleoecological reconstruction by subsurface faunal assemblages of the quaternary deposits in lower Mesopotamia, southern Iraq
items.abstract: Khor Abdullah is a strategically important marine area located between Iraq and Kuwait. Reconstructing the region's paleoenvironments and coastal evolution during the Quaternary period relies heavily on sea-level fluctuations, climatic conditions and neotectonics. This study examined two subbottom sediment cores (Cores 4 and 8), which were recovered from a depth of 40 m within the Grand Al-Faw Port region. Four primary faunal groups were identified foraminifera, ostracoda, mollusca and bryozoa—alongside notable sterile intervals lacking microfauna at multiple core depths. Benthic foraminifera were represented by six species, with the family Milliolidae dominating Core 4, which indicates turbid environments across supratidal, intertidal, and subtidal zones. Twelve ostracod species were identified, mostly corresponding to freshwater habitats. Furthermore, ten pelecypod and five gastropod species were documented, reflecting turbid and lagoonal environments. Bryozoa, meanwhile, occurred sporadically with low diversity. A distinct marine horizon at a depth of 28–30 m in Core 4 marks an Early Holocene marine transgression, which is interlayered with marsh deposits and evidence of subsequent marine regression. Textural analysis revealed that the core sediments predominantly consist of silt, muddy sand and sandy silt. According to the hydrodynamic conditions diagram, most sediment samples fall within the quietest environment. This explains the absence of fauna at most depths, as the soil texture at these depths is unsuitable for habitation by fauna.

items.title: Diversity, ecological patterns, and zoogeography of nematodes (Nematoda) in terrestrial vertebrates in the South of the Middle Volga Region, European Russia (a century-long synthesis)
items.abstract: This paper presents an overview of the nematode fauna in terrestrial vertebrates from the Samara Oblast (Middle Volga region). We analyzed our own and published literature data on the nematodes of amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals covering a research period of over a century. To date, 124 nematode species from 33 families are known to infect vertebrates in the Samara Oblast. A total of 117 recorded nematode species use terrestrial vertebrates solely as definitive hosts, while five (Eustrongylides excisus, Spiroxys contortus, Streptocara crassicauda, Ascarops strongylina, Physocephalus sexalatus) use them only as intermediate and/or paratenic hosts. The remaining two species (Physaloptera clausa and Porrocaecum depressum) parasitise mammals at the larval and adult stages. Forty-one species of nematodes have an indirect life cycle, while 83 develop directly. Geohelminths predominate in the nematode fauna of mammals, reptiles, and amphibians, with the highest ratio observed in reptiles and mammals. Conversely, biohelminths dominate in birds. The ratio of geo- and biohelminths among nematodes of vertebrates strongly depends on the hosts’ lifestyle and diet. The majority of nematode species (70) were recorded in mammals. The nematode fauna associated with the avifauna comprises 36 species. The lower number of nematode species recorded in amphibians (15) and reptiles (11) compared with that in birds and mammals likely reflects the smaller number of host species studied in these groups (nine amphibian and nine reptile species vs. 100 bird and 48 mammal species), rather than an inherently poorer parasite fauna. Most of the nematodes identified in vertebrates of the Samara Oblast belong to the Palearctic faunal complex (61 species). Additionally, 34 species are cosmopolitan. The range of 22 nematode species spans the Holarctic. The geographic distribution of seven species is limited to Europe. Among the 124 nematode species found in terrestrial vertebrates in the Samara Oblast, 30 are of medical and veterinary importance as potential pathogens of dangerous helminthiases. Of these, seven species (Syphacia obvelata, Calodium hepaticum, Ascaris suum, Toxascaris leonina, Toxocara canis, Ancylostoma caninum, and Uncinaria stenocephala) are zoonotic, capable of infecting humans.

items.title: Human-made structures as nesting sites for hummingbirds across the Americas: insights from citizen science
items.abstract: Abstract Urbanization can negatively affect nesting and reproductive behaviors of birds. Even so, certain species can survive in abundance despite its negative impacts, due to their ability to use alternative human-made structures as nesting sites. There are several studies focusing on hummingbirds’ floral resource use in urban environments, however, little is known about their reproduction and nesting in these areas. Here, we used 5,136 nest photographic records from WikiAves and eBird , two widely used crowdsourcing citizen science platforms, to assess hummingbird nest site choice in natural and anthropized environments across the Americas. We found that 74 hummingbird species (32.03% of the sampled and 20.22% of known species) used diverse human-made substrates as nesting sites or built nests in anthropized environments. This use was observed across almost all clades and its detection was related to sampling effort, but not to species’ body mass, a trait often associated with hummingbird occurrence in urban areas. Overall, these results could indicate behavioral plasticity in some hummingbird species reproductive behavior and nesting resource use, besides their ability to incorporate novel floral resources and nectar feeders in their diet across human-modified areas. Because plants were their preferred nesting sites even in anthropized environments, the importance of maintaining vegetation in transformed and urbanized areas to support these pollinator populations is highlighted. Finally, our results also emphasize the potential of citizen science to provide large amounts of data across extensive geographical regions that would otherwise be difficult to obtain.

items.title: Strong on Diagnosis, Weak on Delivery: A Structured Assessment of Urban Nature-based Solutions Frameworks
items.abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly promoted as essential instruments for urban climate adaptation, biodiversity recovery, and sustainable development. Yet their implementation remains slow and insufficiently monitored. Frameworks, including standards, guidelines, tools, and indicator sets, are meant to bridge the gap between NbS ambition and practice, but it is unclear how comprehensively they support cities across the full range of operational tasks. We conducted a structured qualitative content analysis, with dual-reviewer coding, of 30 NbS frameworks relevant to urban contexts. Each framework was assessed across six operational dimensions: baseline assessment and ecological performance; planning and design; implementation; financing and funding mechanisms; monitoring and evaluation; and impacts and co-benefits. We also evaluated the presence of practical “how-to” guidance and classified each framework into one of four functional archetypes: Integrator, Designer, Financier, or Monitor. Results revealed a structural imbalance: approximately two-thirds of frameworks provided guidance on baseline assessment and planning, while only 36.7% addressed implementation, the lowest of any dimension. Gaps in operational guidance, financing, and monitoring co-occurred systematically, consistent with shared structural causes rooted in disciplinary biases. Only five frameworks achieved consistently high coverage across all functional dimensions. The archetype typology offers practitioners a navigation tool for assembling complementary resources matched to their functional dimensions and governance context. Policy implications include requiring comprehensive planning that addresses both diagnostic and delivery dimensions as a condition of NbS funding. These also include embedding comprehensive monitoring and verification requirements and investing in cross-disciplinary institutional capacity to support scaled implementation.

items.title: Water resilience in the high Andean basins of Peru and Ecuador: A synthesis of hydrological modeling, cryosphere dynamics, and ecohydrological approaches under climate change (2011–2025)
items.abstract: The high Andean basins of Peru and Ecuador supply freshwater to approximately 60% and 70% of their respective national populations. However, these systems are increasingly threatened by glacier retreat, land-use transformation, and climate variability, which jeopardize long-term water security. This study presents an integrative narrative review of 58 peer-reviewed scientific publications published between 2011 and 2025, focusing on hydrological modeling, cryospheric dynamics, hydrometeorological monitoring, climate change impacts, and ecohydrological processes in tropical Andean mountain systems. Following a systematic selection process, the reviewed evidence was organized into five thematic areas: advances in hydrological modeling under data-scarce conditions, validation of satellite precipitation products, glacio-hydrological and cryospheric dynamics, hydroclimatic scenario simulation, and ecohydrological approaches. The results reveal a sustained methodological transition from semi-distributed conceptual models (SWAT, HEC-HMS, and GR2M) toward physically based distributed models (MGB, PREVAH, and JULES), integrated with satellite products (GPM-IMERG, SM2RAIN, and ERA5-Land) and machine learning algorithms, significantly reducing the limitations associated with data scarcity. Climate projections under CMIP6 scenarios indicate increases of up to 60% in extreme precipitation intensity and up to 39% in annual runoff in some basins, while glacier mass loss could reduce dry-season water storage by as much as 25% over the coming decades. At the same time, land-use changes, including the conversion of páramo ecosystems to pasturelands and deforestation, have been shown to alter baseflow and infiltration processes independently of climatic forcing. The synthesis further reveals that water resilience in the Andes cannot be fully understood through physical hydrology alone. The conservation of water-regulating ecosystems such as páramos, bofedales, and montane forests plays a critical role in maintaining hydrological regulation and sustaining water availability under changing environmental conditions. The review highlights the importance of integrating hydrological processes, cryospheric dynamics, and ecosystem functions to improve water resilience assessments and support sustainable water resources management in the tropical Andes.

items.title: Continental diatoms (Bacillariophyta) from Paraná state, Brazil: a critical, georeferenced checklist and spatial synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Freshwater diatom diversity remains unevenly documented across the Neotropics, limiting assessments of regional biodiversity and biogeographic patterns. We provide a critical, georeferenced synthesis of continental diatoms from Paraná State, southern Brazil, integrating bibliographic records, herbarium collections, nomenclatural revision, and spatial analyses. The compiled dataset comprises 86,775 occurrence records from 3649 samples collected between 1951 and 2025 at 712 georeferenced sites. After taxonomic and nomenclatural updates, 1525 accepted infrageneric taxa belonging to 190 genera, 71 families, and 35 orders were recognized. However, sampling was strongly spatially biased: Only 11.1% of the state territory was represented by Ottobasins containing confirmed records, and 258 of 399 municipalities lacked documented occurrences. Rarefaction and extrapolation analyses revealed pronounced differences in sampling completeness among hydrographic units, with several poorly sampled basins showing substantial discrepancies between observed and estimated richness. Approximately one quarter of all taxa were recorded from a single sampling locality, a pattern that, combined with the extensive spatial gaps in sampling, indicates that the geographic distributions of many taxa remain poorly characterized. Our synthesis demonstrates that Paraná harbors exceptionally high continental diatom diversity while substantial Linnean and Wallacean shortfalls persist, providing a spatially explicit framework for directing future inventories, biogeographic studies, and freshwater biomonitoring.

items.title: Updated occurrence, habitat associations, and genomic resources of syngnathids in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia
items.abstract: Syngnathid fishes, including seahorses and pipefishes, are ecologically and economically important but remain vulnerable to overfishing, habitat degradation, and trade-driven exploitation. This study documents syngnathid occurrence, habitat associations, body-size observations, and genomic resources in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia, using SCUBA-based visual surveys and high-resolution photographic analysis. Across 32 dives at seven reef sites, we recorded 54 occurrence records belonging to four species: Hippocampus kuda , H. comes , Doryrhamphus janssi , and Trachyrhamphus bicoarctatus . Species differed in their observed habitat associations, while size–depth relationships varied among species. A brooding male and two juvenile seahorses provided evidence of local reproductive activity during the survey period. To establish baseline genomic resources for Malaysian syngnathids, we generated high-quality PacBio HiFi genome assemblies for six individuals from three species, with genome sizes ranging from 0.45–0.61 Gbp and BUSCO completeness scores of 92.3–98.8%. The assemblies were characterized through repeat annotation, protein-coding gene prediction, orthology analysis, and phylogenomics. Complete mitochondrial genomes were generated for all six individuals. These genomic resources provide a foundation for future comparative and population genomic studies of genetic diversity, connectivity, and evolutionary relationships. Together, the ecological observations and genomic resources provide a baseline for future standardized monitoring and conservation research on Malaysian syngnathids.

items.title: Distinct associations of rhizoid-sphere and endophytic bacteria with dominant moss traits along an elevational gradient on Segrila Mountain
items.abstract: Microbial communities associated with alpine mosses remain poorly characterized in southeastern Tibet, particularly the distinction between bacteria at the rhizoid-soil interface and those inside moss tissues. We used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to characterize 36 rhizoid-sphere and 12 endophytic samples from three dominant mosses ( Actinothuidium hookeri , Ptilium crista-castrensis , and Dicranum fuscescens ) across four elevations (3,700–4,300 m) on Segrila Mountain. We combined community analysis, SPIEC-EASI networks, random forests, and path modeling to examine how habitat, elevation, soil properties, and bacterial community attributes were related to moss traits. The endophytic network showed higher clustering (0.665) and modularity (0.84) and a larger proportion of positive partial correlations (94.71%) than rhizoid-sphere’s (0.305, 0.79, and 83.48%). Elevation uniquely explained 25.9% of the variation in rhizoid-sphere bacterial composition ( p = 0.0001), compared with 7.9% for moss species ( p = 0.0093), while neither factor significantly explained endophytic composition (both p > 0.05). Soil properties explained rhizoid-sphere community variation (adjusted R 2 = 0.199, p = 0.001), whereas the endophytic model was nonsignificant (adjusted R 2 = 0.029, p = 0.239). Random-forest models most strongly predicted moss tissue K (LOOCV R 2 = 0.58) and N (LOOCV R 2 = 0.48). In path modeling, rhizoid-sphere Shannon diversity was positively associated with morphology ( β = 0.500, p = 0.0005) and negatively associated with nutrient ( β = −0.263, p = 0.0036). These findings highlight the rhizoid-sphere as an interface linking elevation, soil conditions, bacterial community variation, and moss traits.

items.title: Combined data of two monitoring schemes show four decades of biodiversity change: breeding bird survey in Czechia
items.abstract: Long-term datasets uncover changes that are impossible to find by intensive short-term studies. Collecting such datasets is challenging because their time span usually exceeds individual researchers’ careers. This challenge may be fixed by running long-term citizen science programmes. Here we present a dataset describing more than four decades of biodiversity changes in Czechia, a country in Central Europe, using two common bird monitoring schemes with 351 citizen scientists. The schemes are based on standardized fieldwork of skilled volunteers counting breeding birds. They are coordinated by professionals, aiming at producing bird population indices and trends annually. One scheme operated from 1982 to 2024, another one from 2018 onwards. The period of overlap enables data combination and the production of outputs for a continuous time series spanning 44 years. We publish both count data for all 236 bird species recorded in both schemes, as well as national population indices and trend estimates for 106 bird species that are suitable for this purpose.

items.title: Assessing the range expansion of a generalist carnivore by a novel approach combining questionnaires to experts and dynamic occupancy models
items.abstract: Abstract Despite the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, the geographic ranges of many mesopredators are expanding, largely driven by their generalist life histories and the decline of apex predators. Quantifying these expansions and identifying their underlying drivers remain challenging and require innovative methodological approaches. We aimed at quantifying the factors driving the recent spatial expansion of the Egyptian mongoose ( Herpestes ichneumon ) at the European edge of its range. We combined occurrence data from three periods (2000–2009, 2010–2015 and 2016–2018) in the central Iberian Peninsula (Spain), collected via questionnaires to environmental rangers, with Bayesian dynamic occupancy models. Responses were obtained from 66% of rangers, covering 91.6% of municipalities (93.9% of the total area), ensuring broad spatial representation. Detection probability increased with the proportion of time rangers devoted to field work. Initial mongoose occupancy showed unimodal relationships with elevation and scrubland cover, peaking at low to intermediate elevations and at intermediate scrubland proportions. Colonization probability was highest in warmer areas, near already occupied sites, and in areas with higher scrubland cover. The Egyptian mongoose has undergone substantial expansion in central Spain between 2000 and 2018, with an estimated 262% increase in occupied municipalities (from 6.8 ± 1.5% to 24.6 ± 2.7%). Our study suggests that integrating expert-based questionnaires with dynamic occupancy models may be an effective approach for quantifying range expansions and assessing environmental drivers of colonization.

items.title: Ensemble species distribution modeling and InVEST-based habitat quality assessment for Cupressus funebris under climate change: identifying refugia, ecological security patterns, and conservation priorities in China
items.abstract: Abstract Cupressus funebris , an indigenous and ecologically important conifer in China, is increasingly endangered by climate change and habitat fragmentation. Using an ensemble species distribution model (BIOMOD2), we projected current and future habitat suitability under three climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5) for the 2050s, 2070s, and 2090s. We integrated 355 occurrence records and bioclimatic variables using 12 algorithms. We also used the InVEST Habitat Quality model to assess current habitat quality and degradation, and constructed an ecological security pattern from habitat patches and resistance surfaces. This framework identified climate refugia and priority conservation zones. Random Forest performed best (AUC = 0.92 ± 0.02, TSS = 0.85 ± 0.03). Temperature seasonality (Bio04) and minimum temperature of the coldest month (Bio06) were the main climatic drivers. Results show severe range contractions under all scenarios: habitat loss ranges from − 28.5% (SSP1-2.6) to − 62.4% (SSP5-8.5) by the 2090s, with elevational shifts of 180–310 m. Persistent climate refugia (about 15,200 km²) occur in topographically complex regions like the Hengduan Mountains and Northern Yunnan. InVEST showed that high-quality habitat patches are largely restricted to these refugia, while degradation hotspots overlap with projected climate loss zones. A spatial conservation priority map combining climate suitability and habitat quality guides adaptive management, highlighting areas for immediate protection, assisted migration, ex situ conservation, and ecological restoration. This multi-model framework supports climate-resilient conservation strategies for C. funebris .

items.title: Biotechnology roadmap for native microbial consortia in artisanal mezcal linking fermentation ecology, economic value and biocultural sustainability in Oaxaca, Mexico
items.abstract: Artisanal mezcal produced in Oaxaca, Mexico, relies on native microbial communities that shape its volatile composition, sensory profile, and economic value. This manuscript presents a perspective on indigenous microbial consortia as a biotechnological roadmap for improving mezcal production stability, traceability, and sustainability while preserving regional diversity and the traditional knowledge rooted in artisanal systems. A six-stage framework is proposed (microbial characterization; functional metagenomics and metabolomics; selection of compatible microorganisms; design of native consortia; validation in palenques; and comprehensive evaluation of sensory, economic, environmental, and sociocultural impacts), which aims to put into practice the concept of a “biotechnological roadmap” for mezcal. Native microbial diversity constitutes a form of biocultural capital with direct economic implications, including the potential to reduce production losses, support product differentiation, and strengthen resilience among small-scale producers, subject to technical validation and compliance with the applicable regulatory framework. Biotechnological interventions must avoid homogenization while supporting context-specific solutions that respect the designation of origin and local traditions. By integrating microbiological, economic, and policy perspectives, native microbial consortia can be positioned not only as a substitute for spontaneous fermentation, but rather as a complementary tool for safeguarding the biological memory of mezcal production, improving its competitiveness in global markets, and driving the transition toward sustainability in traditional Mexican agri-food systems.

items.title: From the sky to the deep sea: ecosystem structure and ecological integrity across the National Marine Sanctuaries of Bikar and Bokak, Marshall Islands
items.abstract: Remote oceanic atolls provide increasingly rare opportunities to examine relatively intact tropical marine ecosystems in the Anthropocene. However, most ecological studies remain focused on individual habitats, limiting understanding of cross-habitat linkages across terrestrial, pelagic, mesophotic, and deep-sea systems. We investigated ecosystem structure across the remote atolls of Bikar and Bokak in the northern Republic of the Marshall Islands to characterize biodiversity patterns, ecosystem structure and condition, across terrestrial-to-deep-sea gradients within the recently established National Marine Sanctuaries of Bikar and Bokak. Integrated ecological surveys conducted in 2023 included terrestrial habitats, seabird communities, coral reefs, pelagic ecosystems, mesophotic reefs, and deep-sea environments. Surveys incorporated benthic and reef fish assessments, baited remote underwater video systems, mesophotic submersible observations, deep-sea camera deployments, vegetation surveys, and seabird and sea turtle assessments. Multivariate analyses, generalized linear mixed models, and constrained ordination approaches were used to evaluate ecosystem structure and differences between atolls. Both atolls supported ecosystem characteristics consistent with relatively intact oceanic systems, including extensive seabird colonies, mature native vegetation, predator-rich reef fish assemblages, structurally complex mesophotic habitats, and diverse deep-sea communities. Reef fish assemblages were dominated by herbivores, sharks, and other upper trophic-level predators, while mesophotic and deep-sea surveys documented multiple apparent new regional records and several provisionally identified taxa, highlighting the limited exploration of deeper habitats in the northern Marshall Islands. Despite their proximity, the atolls differed in several ecosystem components. Bokak supported higher reef-fish biomass and more coral-dominated benthic communities, whereas Bikar exhibited greater macroalgal cover, more extensive Pisonia grandis forest, higher Polynesian Rat encounter rates, and concentrated sea turtle nesting activity. These component-specific contrasts demonstrate substantial ecological heterogeneity between neighboring remote atolls. As relatively intact tropical marine ecosystems become increasingly uncommon worldwide, Bikar and Bokak provide complementary ecological baselines for evaluating future change across terrestrial-to-deep-sea gradients.

items.title: A Measurement of CO(3–2) Line Emission from eBOSS Galaxies at z ∼ 0.5 Using Planck Data
items.abstract: Abstract Line intensity mapping (LIM) is a novel observational technique in astrophysics that utilizes the integrated emission from multiple atomic and molecular transition lines from galaxies to probe the complex physics of galaxy formation and evolution, as well as the large-scale structure of the Universe. Modeling multiple line luminosities of galaxies with varying masses or their host halo masses poses significant uncertainty due to the lack of observational data across a wide redshift range and the intricate nature of astrophysical processes, making them challenging to model analytically or in simulations. While future experiments aim to measure multiple line intensities up to z ∼ 8 across a wide volume using tomographic methods, we leverage publicly available datasets from the cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiment Planck and the galaxy survey eBOSS to constrain the CO(3–2) emission from galaxies. We stack galaxies on the Planck CO(2–1) map and measure galaxy-correlated emission at z ∼ 0.5. Its interpretation as CO(3–2) depends on the continuum model, spectral response, and background treatment, which turns into the signal detection confidence between 2.2 σ and 3.4 σ . Our findings demonstrate that stacking methods are already viable with existing observations from CMB experiments and galaxy surveys, and are complementary to traditional LIM experiments.

items.title: Analyzing Fermionic Dark Matter Scenarios with Anomalous Compact Objects
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, we consider three compact objects (HESS J1731-347, PSR J1231-1411, XTE J1814-338) with anomalous mass–radius relations to analyze the possibility of their being dark matter admixed neutron stars. We try to infer the properties of the dark matter particles, under the assumption of their behaving as a free Fermi gas. The main novelty relies on the use of a baryonic equation of state obtained from first principles over the whole density range, which allows the model dependence of the baryonic part of the calculation to be eliminated. Once the possible dark matter admixed neutron star configurations are obtained, we check their stability and whether it is feasible for a neutron star to capture the necessary dark matter fraction. Our analysis shows that our dark matter model favours the dark matter admixed neutron star hypothesis over the pure baryonic neutron star one, with the most favoured dark matter mass of m DM = 1 GeV, although the necessary dark matter content cannot be explained in a standard galactic environment.

items.title: Analytical Modeling of Far-Field Wavefront Error with Beam-Waist and Lateral-Shift Effects in Spaceborne Laser Interferometry
items.abstract: Abstract The coupling between far-field wavefront error (WFE) and laser pointing jitter is an important source of tilt-to-length (TTL) noise in spaceborne laser interferometric links. We extend the Nijboer--Zernike analytical model for far-field WFE of truncated Gaussian beams by incorporating two practical initial-condition parameters, the beam-waist-to-aperture ratio $q$ and the normalized lateral spot-shift ratio $s_r$, to account for realistic beam truncation and alignment conditions. Based on this model, we analyze the influence of $q$ on far-field WFE in addition to the conventional received-power trade-off, showing that decreasing $q$ from 1 to 0.9 and from 0.9 to 0.8 reduces the mean far-field WFE by approximately 10\% and 14\%, respectively, in Monte Carlo simulations of random initial aberrations. We also derive the direct contribution of lateral spot shift and its coupling with transmitted WFE (constrained to $\lambda/20$). For the normalized lateral spot-shift ratio $s_r$, a $2~\mu\mathrm{m}$ entrance-pupil displacement in a Taiji-like telescope corresponds to $s_r=0.001$ and produces a phase-angle coupling coefficient of about $0.0892~\mathrm{pm/nrad}$, close to the typical far-field TTL requirement $0.1~\mathrm{pm/nrad}$, while the spot-shift--aberration coupling terms are much smaller and can be neglected in practical tolerance estimation. These results provide a theoretical basis for beam-parameter optimization and alignment tolerance design in future space-based gravitational-wave detection missions.

items.title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
items.abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.

items.title: Clusters Hiding under Millimeter Sources (CHUMS). I. Extreme CHUMS
items.abstract: Abstract Galaxy cluster abundance provides a powerful probe of the ΛCDM model and enables precise constraints on cosmological parameters. Millimeter-wavelength surveys detect clusters through the Sunyaev–Zeldovich (SZ) effect and are particularly effective at high redshifts. However, the SZ signal can be significantly contaminated by emission from active galactic nuclei (AGN), particularly AGN within the central galaxies (CGs). This contamination reduces the SZ signal strength at the frequencies most accessible from the ground, which reduces detection significances or converts cluster detections to nondetections, thereby diminishing survey completeness and introducing biases in cosmological analyses. In this work, we analyze three clusters that host bright AGN in their CGs using 30 and 90 GHz observations from the Combined Array for Research in Millimeter-wave Astronomy (CARMA). In each case, the AGN emission overwhelms the cluster SZ signal, resulting in nondetections in the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) survey. We present signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimates for the clusters after subtracting the AGN signal from 90 GHz ACT maps using the CARMA measurements, demonstrating high SNR cluster detections once this contaminating emission is removed. Using cluster pressure profiles derived from Chandra X-ray data, we subtract the expected SZ signal from the 150 GHz ACT maps to estimate the flux density of the AGN in that band. Leveraging the time-asynchronous CARMA observations, we also assess temporal variability in the AGN emission and find low fractional variability for our sample. Finally, we discuss the importance of modeling and mitigating AGN contamination in SZ cluster surveys.

items.title: Calibration of CMB Polarisation Using Cross-Experiment Correlations
items.abstract: Parity-violating physics in the Universe can generate correlations between the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) E - and B -modes, but detecting such signals requires extremely accurate calibration of instruments. We describe a data-driven method to calibrate the relative polarisation angle between CMB experiments using cross-correlations of observations over a common sky region. Unlike standard self-calibration approaches, this method does not assume vanishing isotropic cosmic birefringence or primordial E B correlations when estimating the relative misalignment angle, and therefore preserves sensitivity to parity-violating physics. As a proof of concept, we forecast the performance of this method using the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) as a calibrated reference. If they can be calibrated to an uncertainty of 0.08 ∘ , as anticipated from the SO wire grid calibration system, we show that the SO Large Aperture Telescope and Planck could be calibrated to uncertainties of 0.10 ∘ and 0.17 ∘ , respectively, at ∼ 145 GHz. This approach relies on the availability of at least one well-calibrated instrument, and provides a complementary path to improving polarisation calibration across experiments, enabling more robust searches for parity-violating physics in the CMB, such as cosmic birefringence.

items.title: Radio Spectral Imaging and Magnetohydrodynamic Modeling of a Coronal Mass Ejection–driven Shock: Connecting Solar Type II Radio Bursts with Shock-surface Magnetic Geometry
items.abstract: Abstract Solar type II radio bursts are widely regarded as signatures of shock waves propagating in the solar corona and are of particular importance for understanding shock-driven particle acceleration processes. Type II radio bursts often exhibit complex multilane and split-band features. The detailed spectral, temporal, and spatial structures carry key information about the shock properties and evolution. However, the physical origin of the multilane and split-band features remains unclear, largely due to a lack of spatially resolved data and understanding of the concurrent shock morphology and its magnetic-field context. In this work, we combine radio imaging spectroscopy of a multilane, split-band type II burst event with a three-dimensional global magnetohydrodynamic simulation of the associated coronal mass ejection–driven shock using the Alfvén Wave Solar atmosphere Model-Realtime. In this event, the burst intensity evolves from fundamental-emission dominated to harmonic-emission dominated. Meanwhile, the preferential emission source region moves from the Earth-facing side to the limb or farside, coinciding with quasi-perpendicular shock regions with enhanced Mach numbers. The observed spatial offset between the fundamental and harmonic sources is generally aligned with the projected shock-surface magnetic field from the simulation, consistent with anisotropic scattering in a magnetized turbulent plasma. These results establish a physical connection between type II radio sources and coronal shock magnetic geometry, providing new insight into the origin of the multilane features and their diagnostics of coronal shocks.

items.title: Radio and X-Ray Observations of the Transitional Supernova 2019yvr: Insights into the Progenitor Mass-loss History
items.abstract: Abstract The final life stages of the massive star progenitors of stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) remain an open question, especially when it comes to the timing and magnitude of the progenitor stripping. Observing SESNe across the electromagnetic spectrum allows for the most direct constraints on mass loss in the final stages of progenitor evolution. In this work, we present radio (GMRT+VLA) and X-ray (Swift+Chandra) observations of SN 2019yvr obtained from 18 to 1784 days postexplosion. SN 2019yvr was a Type Ib supernova (SN Ib, with strong helium but little or no hydrogen ) that transitioned into a Type IIn supernova (SN IIn, with shock-driven hydrogen features from interaction with circumstellar material, CSM) at ∼100 days postexplosion. The radio evolution is best fit by a synchrotron self-absorbed model with a ρ ∝ r −1.54±0.31 CSM density profile, suggesting a decreasing mass-loss rate from the progenitor in the years leading up to the explosion. The radio-derived shock speed is high, more than 30,000 km s −1 at early times, suggesting a compact progenitor star. The combined radio and X-ray data probe CSM that extends from 1.7 × 10 16 cm up to ∼20 × 10 16 cm and was created by mass loss from ∼(1−3) × 10 −5 M ⊙ yr −1 (assuming a CSM speed of 100 km s −1 ). The combined dataset rules out any dramatic jump in CSM density (which was seen in the optical analog SN 2014C) associated with the emergence of optical hydrogen emission lines. We place SN 2019yvr in context with similar transitional SNe and discuss implications for the progenitor.

items.title: Hydrogen-bond donor–acceptor imbalance in low-frequency terahertz water spectra
items.abstract: The low-frequency dielectric response of liquid water is commonly described by a dominant Debye relaxation together with additional faster contributions whose microscopic origin remains debated. Here, we show that the dielectric function of water between 0.14 and 1.21 THz can be represented by a collective Debye relaxation plus a Drude-Smith term constrained to the zero-dc-conductivity limit. The Drude-Smith spectral weight increases upon heating pure liquid water from 20 to 50 °C and decreases upon isotopic substitution (D2O at 20 °C vs H2O at 20 °C). Among several microscopic measures of electronic polarization and its fluctuations extracted from molecular-dynamics simulations, including path-integral simulations with nuclear quantum effects, the population of water molecules with unequal numbers of donated and accepted hydrogen bonds best tracks the trends of the Drude-Smith spectral weight, changing with the same sign and comparable magnitude. Because such donor-acceptor imbalance is the local condition for net intermolecular charge transfer, it points to fluctuating molecular charges, a degree of freedom that fixed-charge representations lack by construction. Consistently, ab-initio-based dielectric spectra show that the ∼0.1-1 THz response cannot be solely described within a fixed-charge representation. These results support a plausible interpretation of parts of the excess low-frequency THz response of water as electronic-polarization fluctuations associated with transient donor-acceptor imbalance within the aqueous hydrogen-bond network.

items.title: Can Third- and Fourth-order Multipoles plus Radial Variation of Isodensity Ellipses Explain the Observed Flux Ratios in B1422+231? YES, and a Lesson Learned from a TNG100 Lensing Galaxy Sample
items.abstract: Abstract Flux ratio anomalies in multiply imaged quasar lenses are a long-standing issue. Using the classical system B1422+231 as a case study, we investigate how typical nonclumpy perturbations beyond elliptical shapes—multipoles m 3 , m 4 and radial variations in q , ϕ q —can account for the observed image positions and flux ratios under different observational precisions. We extract these perturbations from a preselected strong-lensing galaxy sample from the TNG100 simulation. Smooth macroscopic models ( SIE + γ , EPL + γ ) are then fitted to the observed image positions alone and to both positions and flux ratios, with and without including the extracted perturbations. With an astrometric uncertainty of σ p = 10 mas, both macromodels alone can already successfully fit image positions within 3 σ p . At σ p = 2 mas, however, “astrometric anomalies” appear if smooth macromodels alone are adopted. In this case, adding the extracted perturbations can explain the anomalous image positions. When both positions and flux ratios are adopted, the SIE + γ model family already shows “flux ratio anomalies” at photometric uncertainty σ f ≤ 10% (keeping σ p = 10 mas). When EPL + γ is used, the smooth model alone can simultaneously fit both positions and flux ratios with σ f = 10%, 5% but not with σ f = 2%, where flux ratio anomalies appear. Adding all four types of extracted perturbations can rescue the macromodels and explain the observed anomalous flux ratios. We present important lessons learned regarding model flexibility and degeneracy.

items.title: Probing the High-energy Emission of the Very-high-energy-emitting Changing-look Blazar B2 1420+32
items.abstract: Abstract We present a multiwavelength temporal and spectral study of the changing-look blazar B2 1420+32 using Fermi Large Area Telescope, Swift X-Ray Telescope, and Swift UV Optical Telescope data from MJD 58818–60721. The source reached a peak 0.1–300 GeV photon flux of (4.62 ± 0.29) × 10 −6 ph cm −2 s −1 around MJD 60488, about 60 times the 4FGL-DR4 average, during which the photon index hardened to 2.19 ± 0.14; the flux–index evolution shows only weak evidence for global harder-when-brighter behaviour. The fractional variability is strongly energy dependent, largest in gamma rays, substantial in the optical/UV, and low in X-rays. Strong gamma ray–optical/UV correlations and a moderate gamma ray–X-ray correlation are observed. We identified five activity states for broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) modelling. Their X-ray spectra are described by a log-parabola, with significant negative curvature in four of the five states. The high-energy (X-ray and gamma-ray) components of their SED are modeled using synchrotron self-Compton (SSC), external Compton (EC), and SSC+EC scenarios. The SSC-only and EC-only models either require physically disfavoured parameters or fail to reproduce the very-high-energy (VHE) emission, whereas SSC+EC provides the most self-consistent description, with a seed-photon temperature of ∼10 3 K favouring an infrared torus origin. The brighter states require larger bulk Lorentz factors and higher jet powers, while the magnetic field is comparable across most states but drops sharply in the VHE state. The break energy also changes significantly between outbursts, indicating that the spectral shape evolves between activity episodes. These results suggest that Doppler boosting and jet energetics set the activity level, and the break energy governs the spectral shape between outbursts.

items.title: The GASKAP-H I Survey Toward the Magellanic Clouds: Cold Atomic Gas Survival and Evolution in the Large Magellanic Cloud
items.abstract: Abstract We use atomic hydrogen (H I ) absorption detections from the GASKAP-H I survey to investigate the properties of cold atomic gas in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). Using the radiative transfer method, we decompose 155 sightlines into 330 cold neutral medium (CNM), 2 thermally unstable neutral medium (UNM), and 310 warm neutral medium (WNM) components. We find that the CNM in the LMC exhibits higher optical depths (median 0.46), lower spin temperatures (median ∼37 K), broader linewidths (median ∼4.9 km s −1 ), and slightly lower CNM fractions (median ∼23%) than in the Milky Way. We examine the connection between the CNM, molecular gas, and star formation, finding that CNM correlates more closely with molecular gas than WNM, while molecular gas shows a tighter relation with star formation. Molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) formation begins near N HI,CNM ∼ 10 20 cm −2 , and nearly all sightlines with N HI,CNM > 10 21 cm −2 contain molecular gas. The CNM fraction increases with visual extinction ( A V ), and the LMC maintains CNM fractions comparable to those in the Milky Way at substantially lower A V , likely due to higher local densities and a longer line-of-sight depth. Sightlines near expanding shells tend to show higher CNM fractions, although this is partly driven by higher total H I column densities. Finally, the CNM kinematics generally follow the H I disk rotation, with about 7% of components showing velocity offsets greater than 25 km s −1 , likely tracing inflows or outflows driven by stellar feedback or large-scale interactions within the Magellanic system.

items.title: Revealing the Quantum Signature of Gravity via Gravitational Waves
items.abstract: Can propagating gravitational waves serve as operational probes of the quantum nature of gravity? We address this question by developing a unified theoretical framework that combines spacetime geometry, quantum information, and gravitational-wave physics. Starting from the geodesic deviation equation in linearized General Relativity, we derive the effective detector Hamiltonian directly from spacetime geometry and construct the complete quantum dynamics for detector subsystems interacting with both classical and quantized propagating gravitational-wave fields. This unified formulation enables a direct comparison between classical and quantum descriptions of gravitational radiation within the same physical framework. We demonstrate that classical gravitational-wave backgrounds can induce mixedness in the detector state but cannot generate genuine quantum correlations between the detector subsystems. In contrast, quantized gravitational waves coherently mediate gravity-induced entanglement, quantum coherence, quantum memory, and nonclassical correlations, providing clear operational signatures of the quantum nature of propagating gravitational radiation. We further discuss how mesoscopic quantum mechanical oscillators offer a promising route towards experimentally probing these effects. Our results establish a geometric and quantum-information-based framework for exploring quantum gravity through propagating gravitational waves.

items.title: Why Most Neutron Star Low-mass X-Ray Binaries Accrete Transiently: An Evolutionary Study of Transient and Persistent Phases
items.abstract: Abstract A neutron star (NS) low-mass X-ray binary (LMXB), in which an NS accretes matter from a low-mass donor star, is an ideal source for probing some fundamental aspects of physics and astronomy, such as strong gravity, superdense matter, and the accretion-ejection processes. However, to reliably achieve these goals, one must adequately understand NS LMXBs, including why some accrete persistently and others transiently. Focused models, such as those based on a thermal-viscous instability in the accretion disk, are considered to explain transient accretion. However, broader perspectives, including which LMXB parameter values and phases cause transients and why there are more transients than persistents, remain poorly understood. Here, our computation of the long-term evolution of NS LMXBs addresses these questions, providing insight into LMXB parameters and phases, naturally producing more transients than persistents, and being partially consistent with the known properties of observed sources. For example, we typically find a greater fraction of the persistent phase at lower orbital periods from the LMXB evolution computation, which is somewhat consistent with observations. However, a lack of full consistency calls for improving the aforementioned focused models, and our computations provide a new way to discriminate among these models.

items.title: Coronal Green-line Emission during a Solar Prominence Eruption: Spectroscopic Evidence of Its Correspondence with the Extreme-Ultraviolet Late Phase
items.abstract: Abstract We report spectroscopic observations during a prominence eruption on 2025 October 9 from the Sun’s west limb, associated with an M2.0 flare that commenced at 12:11 UT. The event was captured in sit-and-stare mode by the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) on board Aditya-L1, providing continuous observations of the Fe xiv 5303 Å coronal green line. The spatially averaged green-line emission exhibits a clear correspondence with the EUV late-phase (ELP) emission observed in multiple Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)/Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) channels. In particular, an enhanced 5303 Å emission peak at 15:24 UT coincides with secondary peaks in the AIA 211, 171, 193, and 335 Å passbands, occurring ∼173 minutes after the X-ray peak. The 5303 Å line-width information provides important constraints on the mechanism responsible for the ELP. The line-width decreases progressively by about 28% toward the ELP peak, broadly consistent with the cooling of postflare coronal loops. This behavior suggests that the ELP is predominantly associated with plasma cooling, with relatively weak additional energy input from magnetic reconnection, which does not produce a significant enhancement in line widths. The estimated nonthermal velocity decreases from ∼36 km s −1 during the impulsive phase to ∼21 km s −1 during the gradual phase, indicating a reduction in turbulent plasma motions. And Doppler velocities evolve from predominantly positive values during the eruptive rise phase to negative values during the later gradual phase, implying upward and subsequent downward plasma motions. To our knowledge, this study provides the first space-based spectroscopic evidence linking coronal green-line emission with the ELP and its origin during a solar flare.
