items.title: Analyses on Christoph Clavius’s Reports of Total Solar Eclipses in 1560 and 1567: Key References for the Centennial Variations of the Earth’s Rotation Speed and the Solar Radius
items.abstract: Abstract Variations in solar radius (hereafter R ⊙ ) is a key reference for solar magnetic activity over time. The sunlight amount may have varied with R ⊙ and had an effect on the Earth’s climate in the past. Eclipse observations offer a unique opportunity to measure the absolute R ⊙ value before modern direct observations. The scientific community has discussed a possible long-term R ⊙ variability from 1715 onward. Prior to their coverage, Clavius’s eclipse reports had been subjected to qualitative debates regarding the local eclipse visibility and a possible secular R ⊙ trend. This study leverages the recent dramatic developments of lunar topography data and ephemeris data to provide an effective resolution of this debate. Clavius’s eclipse reports described an explicit totality in 1560 at Coimbra and a “slender circle” around the eclipsing Moon in 1567 at Rome. Our study revised the Δ T constraints of −492 s ≤ Δ T ≤ 200 s in 1560 and 140 s ≤ Δ T ≤ 151 s in 1567 to satisfy Clavius’s descriptions, considering the lunar topography data and assuming Auwers’s canonical R ⊙ . This study constrains the R ⊙ margin of 1567, utilizing three scenarios to interpret Clavius’s account. The local totality requires an upper R ⊙ limit of 1567 as R ⊙ ≤ 696200 km in absolute size (959 . ″ 92 in angular size), indicating no linear secular R ⊙ shrinkage but possible R ⊙ modulations on a centennial timescale. Conversely, the annularity scenario is considered unlikely because it requires a R ⊙ decrease of 4 . ″ 7 within three centuries, even beyond the capacity of Eddy's extreme shrinking-Sun hypotheses.

items.title: Constraining Pulsar Radiative Geometry via Multiwavelength Modeling
items.abstract: Abstract The center of the thermal X-ray emission, which corresponds to the center of the plasma flow within the polar cap, can be constrained by modeling the thermal X-ray pulse profile, while the rotating-vector model (RVM) fitting is widely used to yield the inclination angle of the focus of polarization orientations of the radio coherent emission. Thus, we propose that the consistency between these two measurements would imply that the polarization orientation is focused at the plasma flow center. Conversely, the discrepancy would suggest that these two centers do not necessarily coincide. One possibility is that as the emission propagates, the evolution of wave modes during wave propagation in the magnetosphere depends strongly on magnetic field orientations. Thus, the focus of the polarization finally overlaps with the center of the magnetic field rather than the plasma flow center. If this happens, the discrepancy can range from one to several degrees. In this paper we estimate the uncertainties of these two measurements in the most ideal situation. We find that the uncertainties of these two measurements can be reduced to less than 1 ∘ to distinguish the discrepancy between the two centers.

items.title: Fast and accurate bandpass integration of complex SEDs with neural networks
items.abstract: The paper presents a novel ML-based approach for fast and accurate bandpass integration of spectral energy distributions (SEDs). The non-locality of the integral operator involved guarantees the smoothness of the target function to be approximated, making it an excellent use-case for neural networks. The computational method developed for this work has been wrapped within pyfine (FINE: Fast Function Interpolation via NEural NEtworks). This new Python package makes the relevant code available and easy to use by everyone within the scientific community. The method is demonstrated with two different bandpass integration test cases with 3 and 9 free parameters, respectively, where both accuracy and computational performance are analyzed. The results show that the method is capable of predicting values of the bandpass integral with maximum relative residuals as low as 0.002% and 0.08% respectively, within the sampled region of the parameter space, fast run times, and very little memory overhead. The usage of pyfine is especially effective when the computation of an SED functional form, given a set of values for its free parameters, is expensive. However, already in the first of the two test cases, where a simple modified black body SED was employed, the neural network’s measured run times resulted faster by two orders of magnitudes than an optimized multithreaded version of the ``brute force’’ exact calculation of the integral.

items.title: Using Scattered Near-infrared Light to Map Water Ice in Prestellar Cores with SPHEREx
items.abstract: Abstract We present the first coreshine-derived, spatially resolved maps of the 3 μ m H 2 O ice absorption feature in four prestellar cores, using SPHEREx spectra. Ices are a key component of dense cores in molecular clouds, playing a central role in the chemistry of planet formation around young stars. However, spatially resolved abundance studies remain limited, typically relying on unevenly distributed background star sight lines. Here, we take advantage of the all-sky spectrophotometric capabilities of SPHEREx to construct ice absorption maps with uniform spatial resolution using the illumination of dense cores by scattered Galactic radiation, or coreshine. To demonstrate proof of concept, we analyse the spatially varying H 2 O ice absorption in four nearby (∼140 pc) prestellar cores—L1544, CrA 151, L260 and L1512. Two cores follow the expected spatial trend of ice absorption peaking at the centre, but the two densest cores show a surprising drop in observed ice absorption in the innermost regions. To interpret the absorption maps, we construct analytical and simulated models of a Bonnor–Ebert sphere illuminated by scattering. We study the effects of different geometric configurations, ice mass fractions, and spatial differences in ice composition. None of these can explain the reduced central absorption, pointing to an unexplained physical or chemical effect operating in the densest prestellar regions. Our simulations further show that spectra derived from coreshine provide a robust tracer of spatially varying ice density and composition, establishing SPHEREx scattered-light spectroscopy as a powerful new probe of ice in dense cores.

items.title: Spherically Polarized Alfvén Waves and the Gosling Boost
items.abstract: Abstract Alfvén waves are thought to play critical roles in solar wind acceleration and plasma heating in the solar corona and inner heliosphere. The Parker Solar Probe (PSP) has highlighted the role of large-amplitude spherically polarized Alfvén waves (SPAWs), where the locally constant magnetic field magnitude ∣ B ∣ together with outward propagation explains the observed one-sided radial velocity enhancement—the Gosling Boost. Starting from the MHD equations, we derive the modified wave pressure and Poynting flux under the SPAW condition, and demonstrate both are governed solely by the transverse magnetic fluctuations. Using PSP data from Encounters 6–25, we define an unperturbed velocity baseline from the lower 10th-percentile running average and statistically characterize the radial evolution of Alfvénic fluctuations. The background solar wind velocity shows clear radial acceleration, while the velocity perturbation amplitude δv decreases with heliocentric distance. This decay is anisotropic between the radial and transverse directions, which is a direct consequence of the growing magnetic deflection angle related to the spherical polarization. Our results demonstrate that radial velocity enhancements in the young solar wind arise naturally from SPAWs rather than from localized velocity jets, and provide direct observational evidence for the anisotropic radial evolution of SPAWs below 50 solar radii.

items.title: ATLAS. III. Dust around Little Red Dots: Hydrogen Line Ratios beyond Dust-free Non-Case B Models
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate broad hydrogen line ratios in little red dots (LRDs) using five high-redshift ( z > 2) sources from James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) medium/high-resolution spectra in the DAWN JWST Archive (DJA) and 15 low-redshift sources ( z = 0.1–0.9) from the literature, all with broad H β detected at >5 σ . After carefully measuring the broad-line fluxes while accounting for absorption features and neighboring emission lines, we find that the broad H α /H β ratios are very high, ranging from 6 to 30, well above the Case B recombination value. Using plane-parallel C loudy photoionization models with the total line emission from both sides of the slab, we investigate the physical origin of the broad hydrogen line ratios beyond Case B, jointly modeling the Balmer and Paschen line ratios for the subset of one high- z and two low- z LRDs with detected broad Paschen lines. We find that one low- z LRD is reproduced by a high gas number density ( log ( n H / cm − 3 ) ∼ 10 –11) on the broad-line H α /H β –Pa β /Pa γ plane, whereas the remaining two LRDs additionally require substantial dust extinction of E ( B − V ) ≳ 0.2, even after accounting for non-Case B effects. Since the narrow H α /H β ratios do not indicate such large dust extinction, these results demonstrate that the obscuring dust is spatially associated with the broad-line region. Even without Paschen-line measurements, two and eight LRDs in the high- and low-redshift samples, respectively, exhibit H α /H β > 13, which cannot be reproduced by the non-Case B models, suggesting that dust obscuration might be common among LRDs, occurring in at least about half of the population. Such dust may represent a lower-column-density counterpart of the dusty torus in active galactic nuclei, reconciling the weak hot-dust emission.

items.title: Anisotropic redshift distributions in photometric galaxy clustering and their cosmological impact
items.abstract: Photometric galaxy clustering is a major probe of large-scale structure. Its interpretation rests on an accurate treatment of the redshift distribution, n(z), of the galaxy sample. Standard analyses assume the n(z) of a selected lens galaxy sample to be isotropic, whereas observational systematics imprint a variation of it across the sky. The cosmological impact of this n(z) anisotropy has not yet been studied end-to-end at survey-level realism. We quantified how it biases the angular two-point correlations w(þeta), the internal consistency of a cosmological analysis of these data, and the inferred cosmological parameters. We developed an analytical formalism of angular galaxy clustering under spatially varying n(z) and forward-modeled the full observation chain from realistic maps of observational systematics, a machine-learning emulated galaxy selection function, to tomographic binning. We computed the resulting observed w(þeta) and propagated the impact of anisotropic n(z) to a joint analysis of galaxy clustering and galaxy--galaxy lensing for a KiDS-like survey. We extended the analysis to configurations that adopt the larger DES- and LSST-sized tiles together with each survey's area and number density. For our fiducial magnitude-limited sample, modeling w(þeta) with a single global bar n (z) underestimates the true clustering signal by up to ∼10% at small scales in the highest tomographic bin, falling to a few percent at intermediate redshifts and vanishing at low redshifts. When propagated to cosmology, the parameter shifts remain below 1σ for the KiDS-like and DES-like setups. However, for the LSST-like setup, σ_8 is biased low by 1.7σ and Ω_m is biased high by 1.4σ along their degeneracy. The contamination is preferentially absorbed by the high-redshift galaxy bias, which shifts by up to ∼4σ. The anisotropy also affects whether the probes are consistent enough to combine: a calibrated posterior-predictive internal-consistency test determines the contaminated angular clustering to be improbable given the joint cosmic-shear and galaxy--galaxy-lensing constraints (median calibrated tilde p under LSST-like noise). -4 Anisotropic redshift distributions have a small but non-negligible effect in our KiDS-like and DES-like configurations and a significant effect in our LSST-like configuration, which retains KiDS-like selection and observing-condition variation. Because our forward model is predictive and independent of cosmology, the same machinery that quantifies the effect could be inverted to mitigate it given a realistic selection function and galaxy population model.

items.title: Light-curve Analysis of the Classical Nova YZ Ret: Revisiting with Fully Self-consistent Nova Outburst Models
items.abstract: Abstract YZ Ret is a well-observed nova from the first detection of an X-ray flash phase in classical novae until the end of a supersoft X-ray source phase. We have reanalyzed multiwavelength light curves of YZ Ret over the total duration of the outburst. Our fully self-consistent nova outburst model, a 1.25 M ⊙ white dwarf (WD) with a mass accretion rate of 1 × 10 −9 M ⊙ yr −1 on to the WD, reasonably reproduced V / g light curves as well as the very early X-ray flash and late supersoft X-ray light curves. This model explains the emergence epoch of the GeV gamma-ray emission because a shock naturally arises far outside the nova (WD) photosphere just after the optical maximum. In our model, before optical maximum, later ejected matter has a smaller velocity than that of earlier ejecta, and therefore, the ejecta expands while, after optical maximum, later ejected matter has a larger velocity than that of earlier ejecta, and the collision with the earlier ejecta makes a shock.

items.title: Twisted Pseudodisk and Asymmetric Mass Accretion on the Circumstellar Disk. II. Parameter Survey
items.abstract: Abstract Using three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations accounting for ohmic dissipation, we investigate the long-term evolution of the infalling envelope for ∼100,000 yr after protostar formation. The primary control parameter is the initial misalignment angle θ 0 between the rotation axis and the magnetic field, varied from 0 ∘ to 90 ∘ . In all misaligned models ( θ 0 ≠ 0 ∘ ), the pseudodisk (or infalling envelope) surrounding the circumstellar disk develops a highly distorted and complex morphology. Gas accretion from the envelope proceeds through discrete, channel-like flows, producing asymmetric streams rather than axisymmetric infall. Protostellar outflows are launched even in these complex environments, and inflow and outflow regions are strongly interwoven. Outflows transport angular momentum anisotropically, leading to time-dependent changes in disk orientation and outflow direction, which further enhance envelope asymmetry. We examine the relative orientation between gas flows and magnetic fields and find that, although statistical tendencies exist, accretion streams cannot be uniquely characterized as either parallel or perpendicular to the magnetic field, particularly in strongly misaligned cases. We also show that most infalling gas accretes at nearly the freefall velocity, with only a minor fraction significantly slowed within the pseudodisk. Asymmetric accretion and stream-like structures persist beyond 10,000 au, demonstrating that large-scale asymmetry can arise intrinsically. Our results show that complex streams and asymmetric envelopes naturally emerge from magnetized core physics, even in the absence of initial turbulence or external gas accretion.

items.title: Mapping Gas Accretion and Stellar Kinematics to Subkiloparsec Scales in NGC 4696 with JWST/NIRSpec
items.abstract: Abstract We present JWST/NIRSpec Integral Field Unit spectroscopy of the central 618 × 618 pc 2 (∼3″ × 3″) of NGC 4696, the brightest cluster galaxy in the Centaurus cluster. Leveraging the ∼ 0 . ″ 1 (20.6 pc) pixel size of JWST, we resolve a compact rotating circumnuclear disk (CND) (radius of ∼120 pc) traced by Pa α and H 2 1 − 0 S(1) emission, which allows a reassessment of the active galactic nucleus position based on the kinematic center of this disk. A central Pa α velocity dispersion reaching σ ∼ 449 km s −1 implies an SMBH mass of ∼10 9 M ⊙ , corresponding to a sphere of influence of r inf ∼ 60 pc, resolved by our observations. Position–velocity diagrams reveal an increase from ∼−200 to ∼600 km s −1 on scales of ∼150 pc (a gradient of 4.7 km s −1 pc −1 ) and an accretion rate of ∼18 M ⊙ yr −1 feeding the CND. The Pa α emission shows a double component in the core, with a high-dispersion redshifted component reaching σ ∼ 600 km s −1 . In contrast, MUSE H α observations covering the ∼10 kpc-scale filamentary structure recover only weak velocity gradients (≲150 km s −1 ) within ∼300 × 300 pc 2 and do not resolve the disk due to larger point-spread functions and pixel sizes. Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array CO(2–1) data reveal only compact molecular clumps within a ∼410 × 410 pc 2 region, with no extended counterpart to the structures traced by Pa α and H 2 1 − 0 S(1). Stellar kinematics show a smooth velocity field and broad dispersion profile, clearly decoupled from both the multiphase gas and the hot intracluster medium probed by XRISM. These results provide a direct, spatially resolved view of gas dynamics within the inner few hundred parsecs, demonstrating the power of JWST/NIRSpec to probe SMBH feeding.

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract Rings are ubiquitous among the giant planets in the solar system, yet their presence around exoplanets remains observationally unconstrained. As direct imaging missions such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope approach first light, understanding the influence of circumplanetary rings on reflected light photometry is critical for the accurate interpretation and follow-up of direct imaging observations. We present a hybrid forward model for reflected light phase curves of ringed exoplanets, coupling a ray-casting framework for computing mutual planet–ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra from Cassini observations of Saturn’s rings. We model Jupiter-like planets with opaque, icy rings spanning 1–10× the radial extent of Saturn’s A, B, and C rings across a grid of inclinations and ring obliquities. Our simulations show that rings enhance the flux ratios at favorable ring geometries. Saturn-equivalent rings increase peak flux by a factor of 3.1 in the visible, while more extended rings produce enhanced contrasts exceeding an order of magnitude. The flux contribution of a ring is highly sensitive to obliquity and orbital location. At certain geometries, rings can suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. We highlight multiband observations as a complementary route for diagnosing the presence of an exoring. We also apply the model to υ Andromedae d as an observational test case and discuss the implications for exoring detectability with the Roman Coronagraph. Exorings have the potential to bias inferred planetary properties from direct images and must be properly accounted for in observation preparation and interpretation.

items.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
items.abstract: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions result in the squeezing of the field, which is a quantum characteristic that is beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and it may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.

items.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence of shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
items.abstract: Odd radio circles (ORCs) are recently discovered peculiar extragalactic sources. They are characterised by one or more bright rings extending on scales of hundreds of kiloparsecs, and they are filled with fainter emission. A massive elliptical galaxy lies at the centre of ORCs. While their formation mechanism is debated, a shock is plausibly involved. We constrain the nature of ORC J1555+2726 (ORC4) by analysing its morphological and spectral properties. We used radio data from the Low Frequency ARray (LOFAR), the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT), and MeerKAT at 50-1284 MHz to obtain images and spectral index maps at high resolution and sensitivity. The resolution and observing frequency both affect the observed morphology. In particular, the brightness contrast between the ring and the filling emission becomes progressively smoother from higher to lower frequencies. We measured an integrated spectrum of slope α=1.06± 0.03, a radio power of P_ ̊m 150 = (5.4± 0.5) ; 10^ 25 ̊m W ; -1 at 150 MHz, and a radial spectral flattening down to α at the ring location. However, we inferred a negative (convex) spectral curvature and a peculiar spectral shape in radio colour-colour diagrams, which imply a spectral flattening towards high frequencies. These properties cannot be explained by shock acceleration of thermal particles and standard ageing. The observed features suggest that a mixture of electrons with different spectra coexists within the ORC4 volume, likely associated with shock re-acceleration of a fossil relativistic reservoir. The ring emission is plausibly dominated by higher-energy electrons that are re-accelerated at the shock front, while lower-energy re-accelerated electrons are more uniformly distributed throughout the whole source (possibly ellipsoidal) volume.

items.title: EP241021a as an Off-nuclear Month-duration Transient in a Dwarf Starburst Galaxy
items.abstract: Abstract EP241021a is a peculiar fast X-ray transient (FXT) exhibiting a long X-ray plateau and an optical rebrightening, both challenging the traditional jet afterglow model. Whether its nature is a stellar explosion or a tidal disruption event (TDE) remains debated. Here we present late-time Hubble Space Telescope (HST)/WFC3 and Gemini-N/GMOS observations of its host galaxy at z = 0.748. After ∼300 days posttrigger, the transient emission had faded below detection, revealing a dwarf disk galaxy with an effective radius R e = 1.7 kpc, a stellar mass M ⋆ ∼ 3 × 10 8 M ⊙ , and a high star formation rate of ∼5 M ⊙ yr −1 . Combined with previous very long baseline interferometry measurements, the transient can be located in the galactic disk with a projected physical offset of 0.95 ± 0.13 kpc from the galaxy center. Host-subtracted optical light curves show that the rebrightening ceased at ∼47 days, followed by a sudden drop with a power-law index steeper than −3.3, coincident with a similar drop in the X-ray light curve. This synchronous drop in both bands is consistent with jet shutoff, and the required month-long jet activity suggests a persistently accreting compact object fed by a TDE. Among the TDE scenarios, the off-nuclear location and the starburst host galaxy slightly favor the postsupernova micro-TDE scenario in a binary system, in which a natal kick drives the newborn compact object into a tidal disruption of its companion. Nevertheless, an off-nuclear intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) TDE or a stellar-mass black hole TDE induced by dynamical scattering in a dense stellar cluster cannot yet be excluded.

items.title: Magnetoelastic avalanches in magnetar crusts with plastic islands
items.abstract: High-energy outbursts from magnetars may be associated with crustal failures or quakes. The magnetoelastic modes of the star can be excited to large amplitudes in such a framework, providing a natural explanation for the quasi-periodic oscillations observed in the X-ray tails of some events. However, previous calculations of torsional modes have been carried out assuming an intact crust without accounting for the failure itself. We develop a code in this paper that solves the axial sector of the linearised Einstein-Maxwell-Euler equations in a cavity that hosts inelastic regions or 'plastic islands'. As crustal elements are displaced, shear stresses are tracked as a function of time to allow cells to dynamically switch from elastic to inelastic states. The presence of islands in the crust promotes phase mixing and, when reflected waves mix constructively, large sections fail collectively ('avalanche') if the initial kick is strong enough. Transient spectral features are observed as a result of the progressive loss of elastic support, which may explain the temperamental nature of the oscillations observed following giant flares and magnetar storms.

items.title: Nano-Nb Superconducting 3D Josephson Junction Arrays in Cu-Normal Matrix: Superconducting Phase Coherence and Quantum Fluctuations Properties
items.abstract: We investigate the superconducting behavior, phase coherence and quantum fluctuation properties of three-dimensional arrays of nanometric Nb Josephson junctions embedded in a normal Cu matrix (Cu–x wt% Nb, x = 3, 5, 15 and 20), with emphasis on the Cu10wt%Nb and Cu20wt%Nb compositions. Magnetic properties were measured by dc magnetization as a function of temperature and field in a SQUID magnetometer and by ac susceptibility. Transport properties, including magnetoresistance, V(I) curves and the critical current Ic(H,T), were measured at fields up to 90 kOe. A micro-Hall sensor with ten transverse voltage bridges (5.0 × 0.2 × 0.01 mm³) was used to calibrate the magnetic field actually applied to the sample. Magnetization and transport reveal a double superconducting transition that depends on the applied field and current: Tc(H), with Tc(0)=8.2 K, associated with the intragranular (volumetric) response of the Nb grains, and a lower TcJ(H), associated with Josephson coupling between grains through the Cu matrix. The response combines that of bulk Nb with signatures of weakly coupled grains, consistent with a collection of superconducting grains in a non-superconducting matrix. The characteristic fields Hc1=400.03 Oe and Hc2 = 15 kOe (grains), and Hc1J = 99.93 Oe and Hc2J=199.25 Oe (intergranular coupling), were determined. The critical current Ic(H,T) shows a central maximum at low fields, followed by a long tail and small oscillations of period ΔH≈24 Oe, attributed to quantum interference between coupled grains. At higher fields, magnetic flux gradients destroy phase coherence and randomize the phase θ of the order parameter ψ = |ψ|eiθ, suppressing the oscillations. Magnetic and transport results are correlated and described by an effective-medium theory for superconducting grains in a normal matrix under magnetic field and current, supporting a three-dimensional Josephson junction array in a Cu matrix.

items.title: High-precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
items.abstract: Binary millisecond pulsars (MSPs) serve as exceptional astrophysical laboratories for a wide range of astrophysical studies, all of which rely on precise property measurements allowed by pulsar timing. In this paper, we present high-precision timing solutions for seven binary MSPs monitored by the European Pulsar Timing Array. By combining data collected from the five largest radio telescopes in Europe as well as through their coherently combined form, the Large European Array for Pulsars, we achieved phase-coherent timing solutions for all seven pulsars. We conducted a Bayesian timing and noise analysis on the combined data, yielding measurements of astrometric and orbital parameters either for the first time or with broadly improved precision. For PSRs J0125-2327, J1741+1351, and J2043+1711, we determined their distances and transverse velocities from astrometric measurements, and we inferred their masses via Shapiro delay measurements. Additionally, we examined the various contributions to the secular orbital-period variations for PSRs J0125-2327, J1125+7819, and J1741+1351, and we estimated their kinematic distances. For PSRs J0125–2327 and J1741+1351, we detected the signature of annual-orbital parallax in the timing data. This allowed us to derive a strongly favoured, unique solution for the orbital ascending node and inclination angle for PSR J0125–2327 and a tightly constrained ascending node for PSR J1741+1351. Moreover, we used the orbital periods and their derivatives for several binary MSPs to place upper limits on gravitational-wave strain in both the sub-nanohertz and microhertz frequency regimes. Our results show that the orbits of binary MSPs could provide stringent constraints in the microhertz range, thereby possibly complementing standard pulsar timing array analyses in the future.

items.title: An analytical framework for atmospheric tides on rocky planets. II. Semidiurnal thermotidal torque
items.abstract: The thermodynamic acceleration induced by atmospheric thermal tides has a major impact on the rotation of temperate rocky planets, where gravitational and radiative tidal forcings are of comparable strength. This acceleration drives planets away from synchronous rotation, thereby affecting their climate, large-scale circulation, and surface conditions. These implications underline the need to better constrain the dependence of thermotidal torque on tidal frequency and on the physical parameters characterising a star-planet system, as this relationship remains insufficiently understood. In particular, the role of resonantly excited Lamb waves requires clarification due to its potential impact on Earth's length of day (LOD) during the Precambrian. A LOD length of the day Building on a previous work that provided a fully analytical formulation of the atmospheric tidal response of rocky planets, we applied this framework to isentropic and isothermal atmospheres. We performed a comprehensive functional analysis of the resulting torque and compared the analytical predictions with numerical solutions from earlier general circulation model (GCM) studies. A GCM general circulation model The analytical model reproduces the present-day thermotidal bulge and torque inferred from barometric observations when direct absorption is assumed. It also agrees well with GCM results, accurately capturing the frequency dependence of both surface-pressure oscillation amplitudes and tidal torque for paleo-Earth as well as that of the torque for present-day Earth. More generally, the solutions capture the torque peak near synchronous rotation and the amplification associated with Lamb-wave resonance, although incomplete GCM spectra limit some quantitative comparisons. Near resonance, the GCM results exhibit a braking torque of a larger amplitude than the accelerating torque. This asymmetry was reproduced by allowing tidal heating to lag behind insolation. The agreement with GCM spectra constrains the free parameters of our model. It further suggests that thermal tides in the benchmark simulations are driven predominantly by an indirect thermal forcing characterised by a substantial time delay, in contrast to the direct absorption of sunlight that dominates semidiurnal tides on present-day Earth.

items.title: Unlocking the full potential of gravitational waves as standard sirens with current and future data
items.abstract: As tensions between early- and late-Universe measurements of cosmological parameters remain unresolved, gravitational wave (GW) standard sirens are emerging as promising probes of cosmic expansion. However, several methodological challenges and the need for scalable frameworks capable of exploiting forthcoming datasets, limit their potential. In this thesis, we develop computational and statistical advances to overcome these limitations and enable precision cosmology with current and third-generation (3G) observatories. First, we address the computational limitations of existing standard siren codes - currently limited with only ~100 events - by developing a GPU-accelerated pipeline which scales to datasets three orders of magnitude larger than current catalogs. Leveraging this improved pipeline, validated against other codes in a blinded mock data challenge, we forecast cosmological, population, and modified GW propagation constraints from the O5 observing run and constraints on the cosmic expansion history H(z) from the Einstein Telescope (ET). We find that percent-level measurements of the Hubble constant (H0) may be achievable during O5, while ET will achieve few-percent constraints on H(z) at higher redshifts, providing a probe to address the Hubble tension. Beyond computational advancements, we introduce methodological innovations to enhance the constraining power of current datasets. We develop a Gaussian process-based correction for galaxy catalog incompleteness, reconstructing the galaxy redshift distribution while preserving large-scale structure information, thereby improving dark siren constraints by up to 66%. In addition, we implement a semiparametric population model based on B-splines to infer features of the binary black hole mass distribution without restrictive assumptions. Applied to the GWTC-4.0 catalog, this model yields 12–22% tighter constraints on H0 than standard parametric approaches. By overcoming key computational and methodological limitations, this work advances standard sirens as precision cosmological probes, laying the foundations for next-generation analyses and enabling gravitational waves to shed new light on the fundamental laws governing our Universe.

items.title: Historical Notes on Physics and Integral Calculus (1988–1989): Michele Nardelli's Lecture Notes from Professor Antonio Grablovitz
items.abstract: Historical Notes on Physics and Integral Calculus (1988–1989) This historical collection contains 34 pages of handwritten notes on physics, astronomy, and integral calculus, originating from the lessons of Professor Antonio Grablovitz in Naples during the period 1988–1989. The collection was assembled and preserved by Michele Nardelli, who personally transcribed part of the material during his mathematical studies. Other pages consist of original teaching documents entrusted to him directly by Professor Grablovitz. The subjects include universal equilibrium, lunar and solar phenomena, eclipses, astronomical geometry, integration techniques, definite integrals, and fundamental concepts of mathematical analysis. Professor Grablovitz strongly encouraged Nardelli's independent mathematical education and enthusiastically supported his intention to transform these notes into a book. During a later hospitalisation at the Cardarelli Hospital in Naples, Professor Grablovitz expressed his pleasure at the prospect of Nardelli continuing this project. The documents have been preserved for nearly four decades and subsequently digitised by Michele Nardelli, with the knowledge and authorisation of Professor Grablovitz's children, Annasofia and Vittorio. This publication is intended as a historical and educational testimony, preserving the memory of Professor Grablovitz's teaching and the intellectual relationship between teacher and student. Collection, transcription, preservation and digitisation: Michele Nardelli. Original teaching and educational materials: Professor Antonio Grablovitz. Historical period: Naples, Italy, 1988–1989. First digital publication: 10 November 2026.

items.title: Forecasting the ionospheric propagation environment over lightning-active regions: a non-circular machine-learning formulation using NASA ISS-LIS, GNSS TEC and OMNI data
items.abstract: Abstract Lightning radiates electromagnetic energy over a very wide frequency range, and the low-frequency component travels to global distances inside the Earth–ionosphere waveguide. How far such a signal reaches, and the highest frequency a given path will carry, are set by the state of the ionosphere at the time of the discharge, which varies by the hour. We forecast that propagation environment over lightning-active regions and convert the forecast into the quantities a radio link actually needs: the F2-layer critical frequency (foF2), the maximum usable frequency (MUF), and the one-hop ground range. A central methodological point is addressed explicitly. Deriving foF2 and MUF from Total Electron Content (TEC) and then training a model to predict them from TEC is circular because the label is a closed-form function of an input feature; any model then recovers R² ≈ 1.0 while learning nothing. We therefore pose the problem as a forecast of TEC at t + ∆t, which is genuinely unobservable at t, and apply the physics to the forecast output rather than to the label. Using 381,858 ISS-LIS flashes, 17,665 fifteen-minute global ionosphere maps, and 8,760 hourly solar and geomagnetic records spanning March–August 2018, five models are compared against a persistence benchmark at 1-, 2-, and 6-hour lead times on a strictly chronological split. All five beat persistence at every lead time. Histogram gradient boosting is the best-performing model, reaching RMSE 3.15 TECU, R² = 0.68, and skill = +0.68 at six hours, where persistence attains R² = −2.11. Skill increases with lead time because persistence decays across the diurnal cycle while solar geometry does not. Feature importance shows the model relying on the current ionospheric state at short lead times and switching to solar zenith angle at the target epoch at long lead times, recovering the dominant physical driver without supervision. A case-by-case analysis qualifies the headline figure: at one-hour lead, the model wins only 51.9% of individual cases and acts mainly as a variance-reducer. Lightning activity was found not to predict TEC, and we report that negative result rather than omit it.

items.title: Na exospheric emission in relation to Sun events during the BepiColombo Second Mercury’s Fly-by
items.abstract: Abstract During BepiColombo second Mercury’s flyby on 23 June 2022, a ground-based campaign with the THEMIS solar telescope provided simultaneous observations of the sodium (Na) exosphere while Bepicolombo measured interplanetary and magnetospheric conditions. Between 8:53 and 9:34 UT, the exospheric Na emission abruptly increased in intensity by about 70% across the entire day side, followed by a slow recovery to the preceding level over approximately four hours. BepiColombo did not register neither relevant perturbations of the solar wind nor solar energetic particles during the Na increase. The configuration of Mercury, Earth and Solar Orbiter enabled observations of the solar regions facing Mercury from both sides. They revealed that an active region facing Mercury, but hidden from Earth, produced a flare and an extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) brightening when the Na emission increased, whereas subsequent emissions from post-flare loops produced no further increase. While photon-stimulated desorption is one of the main mechanisms releasing Na from the surface, short-therm Na variability has so far been attributed mainly to plasma precipitation. Our observations suggest that solar flares can trigger rapid Na variability at Mercury, and point to a multi-phase release from a finite reservoir of surface sodium, reminiscent of the steeper than linear dependence on solar EUV reported for the Moon on longer timescales. This result marks a significant step forward in understanding the mechanisms governing the interaction of Mercury and the Moon with the Sun and it was possible thanks to multi-messenger observations highlighting the potential of investigations during BepiColombo nominal mission.

items.title: Same currents, different field: $Δf = 0$ carrier-only stimulation is not temporal interference without the beat
items.abstract: Carrier-only stimulation ($Δf = 0$) is generally considered the most rigorous control for temporal interference (TI) stimulation, assumed to reproduce TI's kilohertz carrier field without its low-frequency beat. We show that this assumption is incorrect: without the frequency difference, the carrier fields interfere coherently, changing the peak strength, power, and direction of the resulting field depending on electrode polarity and montage geometry. Using computational field modeling, we demonstrate that these mismatches can be substantial and widespread. We therefore recommend that TI studies report electrode polarity, model both carrier-field exposures, and choose controls according to their study objectives.

items.title: Mind-wandering preserves word-level coupling while disrupting comprehension
items.abstract: Readers can move their eyes through a page but retain little of its meaning when their minds wander. We tested whether word properties still guide their eyes during these lapses. We analyzed public eye-tracking and electroencephalography (EEG) data from 44 adults who read articles. They marked the text read during each lapse they noticed. We linked these spans to the sentences needed for later comprehension questions. Word frequency, length and surprisal still predicted which words readers skipped and how long they looked at them. Compared with on-task reading, these effects met equivalence bounds of $\pm$10% for skipping and $\pm$20% for gaze duration. Readers spent 14.6% longer on words during lapses. Yet readers answered less accurately when lapses covered sentences needed for a later question. The adjusted difference was 25.7 percentage points for lapses covering all versus none of these sentences. The fixation-related EEG response was 42.7% smaller during lapses. At left posterior-lateral sensor P7, the median increase in alpha power was 10.0%. Occipital sensor Oz showed no reliable increase. These results suggest that word properties can guide the eyes while readers fail to form or retain a useful representation of the text.

items.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
items.abstract: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.

items.title: Earth accreted increasingly oxidized material as it grew constraining Theia to be small and relatively oxidized
items.abstract: Many different Solar System formation scenarios successfully reproduce the main astrophysical properties of the inner Solar System. Here, we use the chemistry of Earth's mantle to determine whether proposed Solar System formation scenarios can produce Earth and to constrain the characteristics of both the Proto-Earth and the Moon-forming impactor, Theia. To do this, we use a coupled N-body accretion and core-mantle differentiation model (Rubie et al., 2011, 2015b) applied to a range of proposed formation scenarios (Classical, Annulus, and Grand Tack scenarios). This model calculates the mantle chemistry of Earth-like planets in Solar System formation simulations and adjusts the initial redox state of the building blocks in a synthetic protoplanetary disk until the mantle of the simulated Earth closely matches the bulk silicate Earth. We find that a strong oxidizing gradient among the initial solids of the protoplanetary disk is favored to reproduce the chemistry of Earth's mantle, in agreement with Rubie et al. (2015b). The Solar System formation scenarios examined here successfully reproduce the composition of Earth if two related conditions are met: 1) there is a strong positive oxidation gradient with distance in the inner protoplanetary disk and 2) Earth accretes increasingly more oxidized material (on average) as it grows. Furthermore, in simulations that successfully reproduce Earth's composition, Proto-Earth and Theia may possess a wide range of mantle compositions and mass ratios. However, because late accretion is oxidizing across all proposed Solar System formation scenarios, Theia and Proto-Earth cannot both possess mantles that are more oxidized than the present-day Earth's mantle. Similarly, Theia's mantle may be significantly more oxidized than present-day Earth's mantle, but only if it is relatively small compared to the Proto-Earth.

items.title: Locating Debunkers for Rumor Mitigation in Directed Networks
items.abstract: Rumors can spread widely through social networks, making the selection of a limited number of debunkers to disseminate corrective information important. Existing centrality-based methods only consider the individual influence of a node on spreading processes. Those individually influential nodes often have heavily overlapping influence ranges, resulting in a limited number of users they can cover. To address this problem, we propose the so-called Hybrid Marginal Influence (HMI) framework, which combines node centrality with additional audience coverage provided by each candidate and adaptively balances these two factors through a greedy selection procedure. We further develop the Debunker-Augmented SIR (DA-SIR) model for the propagation of rumors and corrective information. Experiments on ten real-world directed networks show that HMI generally selects debunkers with broader audience coverage than conventional centrality-based methods, accompanied by a lower final cumulative fraction of users who repost the rumor.

items.title: A Taxonomic Characterization of Targets in the Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt
items.abstract: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) will investigate seven main-belt objects to improve our understanding of the distribution and evolution of water and metal-rich materials within the asteroid population. Understanding asteroid properties prior to the mission helps anticipate potential surface activity or hazards and optimize data acquisition during brief flyby windows, while also providing essential context for interpreting in-situ measurements within the broader asteroid population. We present visible-wavelength spectra (0.40-0.95 um) and corresponding taxonomic classifications for all seven EMA targets using Chi2 comparison with the visible portion of the Bus-DeMeo class templates. Notably, our analysis identifies two B-type asteroids, a relatively rare class, providing opportunities for future compositional comparisons between EMA targets and OSIRIS-REx observations of the organic-rich asteroid Bennu. We identify the remaining targets to be S-/L-, X-/C-, and D-types. The suite of asteroids selected for EMA offers a unique opportunity to investigate both intra-class variability and compositional differences across multiple taxonomic types, advancing our understanding of chemical and mineralogical heterogeneity in the asteroid belt.

items.title: Turbulence Properties of Corotating Interaction Regions at 1 AU: a Comprehensive Superposed Epoch Analysis
items.abstract: We perform a comprehensive superposed epoch analysis (SEA) of more than 200 corotating interaction regions (CIRs) using WIND spacecraft observations at 1 AU. The stream interfaces are identified by Minimum Variance Analysis (MVA), and turbulence properties are evaluated using wavelet transforms over a wide range of temporal scales. The analysis of normalized cross helicity ($σ_c$) and normalized residual energy ($σ_r$) reveals distinct turbulence behaviors across frequencies. The spectral indices of both magnetic and velocity fluctuations smoothly transition from steeper in the slow wind to shallower in the fast wind, while a localized steepening of the velocity spectra near the interface indicates enhanced dissipation due to compression. Across broad frequency bands, $σ_c$ shows a clear dip at the stream interface, signifying increased inward Alfvén wave energy, whereas $σ_r$ displays a peak-valley-peak structure mainly driven by large-scale velocity shear. In lower-frequency ranges, velocity shear artificially enhances velocity fluctuation energy, producing strong peaks in $σ_r$, while higher-frequency ranges show a smooth increase of $σ_r$ from slow wind to fast wind. Nearly half of the analyzed CIRs are accompanied by a heliospheric current sheet (HCS), with many HCSs closely aligned with the stream interface, suggesting an intrinsic link between the two structures. Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.

items.title: Origins of Satellite-System Building Blocks I: Solid Delivery During Jupiter's Growth
items.abstract: Jupiter's satellites formed within a circumplanetary disk (CPD), but the origin and delivery of the solids from which they accreted remain uncertain. Here, we investigate the delivery of planetesimal material to the CPD while consistently accounting for the growth of Jupiter and the evolution of its surrounding planetesimal reservoir. Using N-body simulations coupled to an evolving CPD model, we quantify the solid mass supplied through planetesimal ablation and direct capture. We find that, although proto-Jupiter rapidly opens a gap in the planetesimal disk, planetesimals continue to enter the CPD for more than 1 Myr. Under efficient ablation, the mass deposited in the CPD can reach approximately 1 Me, about one order of magnitude higher than the mass delivered through direct capture. However, the low efficiency of pebble accretion within the CPD implies that forming the Galilean satellites from ablated material alone may require a very large pebble reservoir. Directly captured planetesimals, despite contributing less total mass, can instead provide satellitesimals that grow through mutual collisions and serve as seeds for subsequent pebble accretion. Our results therefore favor a hybrid formation pathway in which the Galilean satellites grow through a combination of satellitesimal and pebble accretion. We further demonstrate that even a planetesimal reservoir containing less solid material than the minimum-mass solar nebula can supply sufficient building blocks to form the Galilean satellites. The balance between the ablation and direct capture depends sensitively on the efficiency of aerodynamic heating: if ablation is weaker than commonly assumed, direct capture can become the dominant source of satellite building blocks. These results connect the formation of Jupiter and its satellites by showing how Jupiter's growth regulates both the duration and form of solid delivery to its CPD.

items.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
items.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

items.title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
items.abstract: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

items.title: Hydrolyzed Hazes on Water-rich Exoplanets: Composition and Prebiotic Chemistry
items.abstract: Although photochemical hazes complicate the spectroscopic analysis of sub-Neptunes, the very presence of hazes can teach us about the habitability of these planets. Aside from affecting a planet's atmospheric and surface dynamics, hazes offer a source of organics potentially including prebiotic molecules like amino acids, nucleobases, and sugars. These organics are particularly compelling for temperate, water-rich planets where hazes may react with liquid water in condensate clouds or surface reservoirs. Hydrolysis reactions drive molecular reorganization and oxygenation, increasing the chemical complexity of the prebiotic inventory. This water-based evolution of hazes in their environment is largely unexplored and will have consequences for their chemical and optical behavior. In this work, we examine the chemical evolution of temperate water-rich exoplanet haze analogs in liquid water. High-resolution mass spectrometry finds thousands of CHNO molecules with bonding behaviors and chemical complexities distinct from the unaltered haze analogs. The oxygen weight percent increases significantly in the soluble fraction and moderately in the insoluble fraction after hydrolysis, with different carbon bonding structures demonstrating the redistribution of functional groups. The hydrolyzed samples exhibit a broader distribution in H/C and O/C ratios, and the molecular formulas suggest complex carbohydrate chemistry that challenges current theories of prebiotic organic delivery.

items.title: Signatures of CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ in the atmosphere of $β$ Pictoris b
items.abstract: $β$ Pictoris is a nearby (19.7 pc), young ($\sim$ 24 Myr), bright ($V = 3.85$) planetary system hosting three directly imaged planets. Previous high-resolution spectroscopy of $β$ Pic b has detected H$_2$O and CO, but not CH$_4$ or NH$_3$. Combining observations across a broad wavelength range has been shown to maximise sensitivity to such weak molecular signals. We searched for previously undetected molecular species in the atmosphere of $β$ Pic b using high-resolution near-infrared spectra. We combined 44 CRIRES+ spectral settings covering the H, K, L, and M bands and cross-correlated the extracted planetary spectra with molecular templates. For species with uncertain detectability, we weighted the observations by their molecular information content and data quality, independent of the measured candidate-species cross-correlation functions. We recover H$_2$O and CO at cross-correlation S/N values of approximately 200 and 50, respectively. We additionally identify tentative CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ signals near the expected radial velocity of $β$ Pic b, with S/N values of approximately 5.3 and 5.7. Equivalent extractions at the same projected separation on the opposite side of the star show no comparable peaks. We classify the CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ signals as tentative because their cross-correlation S/N values do not fully account for possible residual systematics. If confirmed, these would be the first detections of both species in the atmosphere of $β$ Pic b.

items.title: Observational constraints on CO sequestration and disk mass in the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk
items.abstract: Exoplanets accrete gas, dust, and ice from their natal environment, setting the chemical composition of their atmospheres and interiors. The abundance of the major volatiles in disks can be used to possibly link exoplanet atmospheres to their formation location in the disk. In this work, we aim to quantify the peak CO abundance and disk mass of the PDS 70 disk, the first disk with a direct confirmation of two accreting planets in its dust cavity. We present the first detection of N$_2$H$^+$ and C$^{17}$O in this disk. The C$^{17}$O emission shows marginal statistical evidence for an azimuthal asymmetry trailing that previously seen in the continuum emission. We then compare the disk integrated fluxes of N$_2$H$^+$, CO isotopologues, and the continuum to an existing grid of thermochemical models. We find that the derived disk mass drops by a factor of $\sim 3.4$ from $0.039^{+0.067}_{-0.018}$ M$_{\odot}$ to $0.011^{+0.011}_{-0.006}$ M$_{\odot}$ if the C$^{17}$O line flux is included in the fitting procedure; the quoted intervals do not include systematic uncertainties. CO on the other hand is sequestered with an effective abundance of $(4.8^{+4.3}_{-2.7} - 17^{+8}_{-8}) \times 10^{-6}$ relative to H$_2$ in the probed disk layers after accounting for CO freeze-out and isotope selective CO photodissociation for the adopted chemical network and ionization prescription. The range in peak CO abundances reflects the uncertainty in the N$_2$H$^+$ emission, assuming either optically thin emission at 21 K or optically thick emission. Therefore, the PDS 70 planets are possibly accreting the final portion of their atmospheres from the outer disk molecular layer where CO is sequestered. Thus, CO sequestering may need to be considered when interpreting the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres.

items.title: Effective Pest Management and Biodiversity Conservation in Bangladesh
items.abstract: In Bangladesh, rich agro-biodiversity is increasingly threatened by unsustainable pest management practices, environmental degradation, pest resistance, decline of beneficial species, and contamination of food and water. This study evaluates prevailing pest management strategies, their ecological and economic impacts, and opportunities to develop biodiversity- and eco-friendly pest control systems. A cross-sectional mixed-methods approach was applied across five agroecological zones, involving surveys of 500 smallholder farmers, 30 key informant interviews, ecological field assessments, and laboratory analysis of pesticide residues in soil, water, and vegetables. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially, while biodiversity indices measured species richness; qualitative data were thematically analyzed to explore knowledge, institutional barriers, and perceptions. Results show that 87% of farmers rely solely on chemical pesticides, often applying high doses based on visual inspection rather than integrated thresholds. Pesticide residues were detected in 85% of vegetable and 80% of soil samples, with 28% exceeding national maximum residue limits. Ecological assessments revealed lower populations of pollinators and beneficial predators in high pesticide-use areas compared to fields managed under IPM or ecological agriculture. Only 13% of farmers received IPM training, and under 11% practiced it actively. Economic analysis indicated that IPM fields achieved similar yields but lower input costs, generating higher net income. Biodiversity was notably higher in diversified farms with hedgerows, polycultures, and ecological buffer zones.

items.title: Complexity-informed causal modeling of neurodevelopmental trajectories in pediatric high-grade gliomas: divergences from neural stem cell signatures
items.abstract: Abstract Pediatric high-grade gliomas (pHGGs) are lethal evolutionary disorders with stalled developmental pathways and disturbed differentiation hierarchies. We integrate transcriptional and algorithmic network complexity-based perturbation analysis to elucidate gene expression patterns and molecular divergence between Diffuse Midline Gliomas (DMG; previously DIPG) and glioblastoma (GBM), revealing shared developmental programs steering cell fate decision-making. Our complex systems approach supports the emerging paradigm that pHGGs are neurodevelopmental disorders with hybrid lineage identities and disrupted patterning. We identify dysregulated neurodevelopmental and morphogenetic signatures, alongside bioelectric and neurotransmitter signaling programs that alter synaptic organization, neuronal fate commitment, and phenotypic plasticity, regulating glioma phenotypic switching (cell state-transitions). In silico candidate transition-associated network signatures and regulators of plasticity were predicted as possible predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets, reinforcing the view that pediatric gliomas are disorders of cell fate decisions and collective cellular identity. Neuronal and synaptic enrichment is interpreted as a candidate neurodevelopmental network program emerging from disrupted cell fate decision-making. Across validation cohorts, these predictive signatures localized to progenitor-like, NPC/OPC-like, hybrid/ambiguous, immune, and extracellular matrix-associated compartments, supporting recurrence-associated plasticity dynamics. Decoded cell fate transition-associated signatures indicate recurrence-associated remodeling of neural progenitor, OPC-like, neurosynaptic interface, immune, and matrisome-associated programs, as computationally inferred network features. Using graph network-based complexity signatures, our algorithms identified candidate network-associated plasticity markers and interpretable regulatory drivers underlying latent glioma cell fate dynamics. These computational findings may help advance ‘differentiation therapy’ as a systems medicine strategy, discovering plasticity regulators to reprogram malignant fates toward stable lineages, offering complex systems-based targets for cancer reversion and predictive, preventive, and precision oncology.

items.title: Noninvasive Sweat Patch Collection of Neuroinjury Biomarkers in Critically Ill Children: A Feasibility Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Objectives Critically ill children experience neurologic injury that is associated with specific biomarkers. Monitoring of these biomarkers in this population is limited by invasive sampling methods and single timepoint measurements. We sought to evaluate the feasibility of using a novel noninvasive sweat patch to collect cumulative concentrations of neuroinjury-associated biomarkers over time in the PICU. Design Single-center prospective pilot feasibility study conducted across three sequential enrollment cohorts. Setting A tertiary-care PICU. Patients Forty-two children admitted to the PICU 5 weeks to 17 years old. Interventions Sweat patches were placed and worn for 24-96 hours. Sweat samples were analyzed for four neuroinjury-associated biomarkers: glial fibrillary acidic protein, ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1, tau, and neurofilament light chain using single-molecule array assays. Measurement and main results Biomarkers were reported as total cumulative concentrations and concentrations per hour of patch wear. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, safety, protocol adherence, and assay success. All approached families consented, and no patch-related adverse effects were observed. One patch was removed early due to uncertainty regarding MRI compatibility. Adequate sweat volumes required for assay were obtained from all 41 analyzed patches, and biomarker levels were measured successfully in each, with 97% of samples maintaining coefficient of variation (CV) within an acceptable range ( Conclusions Sweat patch collection of neurologic injury biomarkers was feasible, safe, and acceptable to families in a PICU setting. This minimally invasive method yielded consistently adequate and analyzable volumes in infants through adolescents and may support future studies designed to evaluate the relationship between elements of critical care and neurologic injury in children admitted to the PICU.

items.title: Anesthesia Teleconsultation for Pediatric Preoperative Assessment: A Large National Prospective Multicentric Study in Children (TeleCCCAP).
items.abstract: Background While interest in pediatric anesthesia teleconsultation is growing, published data remain scarce. This study evaluated the feasibility of anesthesia teleconsultation in children, providing a comprehensive analysis of failure, quality, dedicated time, and satisfaction. Methods This prospective observational study was performed in 11 major French hospitals. The primary outcome was anesthesia teleconsultation feasibility. Feasibility was defined as the rate of successful anesthesia teleconsultations, i.e ., those performed in the presence of both child and parent, exclusively via the dedicated secure audiovisual platform, and not requiring a complementary in-person appointment. Secondary outcomes included causes and consequences of failure, factors associated with failure, quality of anesthetic preparation, medical time dedicated to preoperative assessment, analysis of parents, and anesthetist satisfaction. Results A total of 830 children aged 6.7 [25th, 75th percentiles, 3.5,12.2] yr were included. Feasibility of anesthesia teleconsultation was 73%. Failure was due to technical (91%), organizational (9%), and medical (1%) issues. Three anesthesia teleconsultations (0.4%) were converted to in-person consultations. Factors associated with technical failure included the use of tablets or smartphones rather than computers (odds ratio, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.40 to 4.26; P = 0.002), the absence of a preconnection test (odds ratio, 6.21; 95% CI, 3.05 to 12.66; P Conclusions This national audit highlights that addressing technical and organizational issues appears essential to transform anesthesia teleconsultations from a mere tool into a robust clinical process, ensuring its reliability and clinical utility in pediatric anesthesia.

items.title: Beyond the Tigers Fixing the Structural Fractures in India’s Biodiversity Conservation Regime
items.abstract: India, a global biodiversity powerhouse, harbours four of the world’s 36 biodiversity hotspots — the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland — along with an estimated 45,000 plant species and over 91,000 animal species. Yet this wealth is eroding: South Asia’s Living Planet Index shows a steep four-decade decline in vertebrate populations, despite India’s ratification of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and its enactment of the Wildlife (Protection) Act (1972), Forest (Conservation) Act (1980), and Biological Diversity Act (2002). This paper argues that the paradox is best understood not as a series of unrelated failures but as six recurring structural disconnects that run through India’s conservation architecture: a jurisdictional disconnect (mandates split across at least fourteen central ministries, epitomized by governance paralysis at Chilika Lake); a species-ecosystem disconnect (a charismatic-species bias, inherited from Project Tiger’s success, that leaves wetlands, grasslands and marine habitats under-resourced); a state-community disconnect (a fortress-conservation model that has displaced over 600,000 Adivasi families since 1947, even where community-managed landscapes out-perform formal Protected Areas); a science-policy disconnect (generalist administration, compromised Environmental Impact Assessments, and the sidelining of the Gadgil Report); an incentive disconnect (revenue-based forest metrics and a Rs. 50,000-crore compensatory-afforestation regime whose plantation-heavy implementation has often fallen short of restoring natural forest); and a temporal disconnect (static, boundary-bound Protected Areas that cannot track climate-driven range shifts). Read together, these disconnects rather than any single failure explain why India’s considerable legal and institutional investment has not translated into commensurate ecological outcomes. The paper is deliberately not a story of uniform failure. Project Tiger’s population recovery, the growth of Community and Conservation Reserves, functioning State Biodiversity Boards such as Kerala’s, a growing number of notified Biodiversity Heritage Sites, and rare but real Access and Benefit-Sharing successes — notably the Kani tribe–TBGRI arrangement — show that India’s architecture can work when incentives, science and community authority are aligned. The paper examines the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation’s (MSSRF) three-decade programme of operationalizing People’s Biodiversity Registers and Biodiversity Management Committees as a case study in bridging these disconnects in practice. It further situates India’s governance debate within emerging global themes — Nature Positive commitments, Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs), large-scale ecosystem restoration, biodiversity finance, digital sequence information (DSI) and AI-enabled biodiversity monitoring, and nature-related business disclosure regimes — that are reshaping international expectations of national biodiversity governance. The paper closes with reforms mapped explicitly onto each of the six disconnects: a strengthened National Biodiversity Authority; full Forest Rights Act implementation; faithful enforcement of existing ecological-expertise and EIA safeguards in decision-making bodies; incentive reform in CAMPA implementation and in forest-service metrics; aquatic parity through expanded marine protection and a Wetlands Authority; and climate-adaptive corridor planning. Together, these can forge governance that finally matches India’s biological wealth with its institutional capacity.

items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
items.abstract: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

items.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. We study this reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward--context conflicts, where compliant task completion remains feasible while some executable shortcuts earn more reward than every compliant strategy. Encoding these conflicts in task dynamics lets us generate diverse interactive environments at scale and derive compliance feedback from execution histories. In resource and reporting workflows, task optimization increases real productivity through unauthorized resource use or raises reported scores while actual work declines. Controlled changes in the training distribution show that minority conflict exposure can still lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, reaching 97.9\% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25\% conflict mixture after 128 updates. The same contextual checks supply a simple binary penalty that supports joint capability and compliance gains and partially mitigates acquired violations. Learned safety adapts to expanded authorization and transfers across mechanisms into workflows with evolving evidence and approval requirements. On 32 unseen changing-evidence tasks, resource-trained safety increases safe completion from 53.1\% to 89.1\% relative to task-only training, while both policies achieve full real work. These results connect a verifiable account of reward-driven misalignment with scalable task construction and safety learning that remains useful under changing execution requirements.

items.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
items.abstract: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data. However, should AI forecasting systems be adopted, human builders will shoulder the work of building and evaluating them. In this paper, we explore what this work looks like with a qualitative interview study with 15 builders of forecasting bots, sampled from among successful participants in a recent AI forecasting competition. Our analysis surfaces the challenges around (1) tuning a bot to acquire factual research, (2) implementing coherent reasoning, and (3) understanding how well one's bot actually does. During their work, builders frequently introduced complexity that did not pay off, and tested in ways that were opportunistic and piecemeal. Our detailed account of their challenges helps clarify what problems should be targeted in upcoming innovations in process, tools, and human-AI teaming for forecasting.

items.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. We introduce MaxIM (Maximally Informative Incremental Memory), a framework that formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem. Grounded in value suboptimality bounds, we show that bounding sequential information loss motivates maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future, task-relevant targets, a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency. We introduce a recursive consistency condition to ensure summaries are grounded by maximizing mutual information (MI) with the observed history. We mitigate credit assignment issues with a parameterized asymmetric critic that computes step-wise variational MI bounds for dense reward shaping. Empirical evaluation on long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks shows that MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, comprehensive autorater metrics, and downstream task utility across strict token budgets and extended horizons, without the need for expensive human preference labels.
