items.title: Exploring remembering through embodied geographies, walking, and culturally relevant third places.
items.abstract: Social reminiscence, or sharing memories in conversation with others, may improve memory recall. When paired with walking, social reminiscence becomes an exercise in collective, place-based memory reconstruction. We explore how culturally relevant third places, and experiences tied to place become embodied, contributing to collective memory-making and remembering among older adults with and without memory loss, and particularly for those living in gentrifying neighborhoods. Drawing from participatory geography methods, the Sharing History through Active Reminiscence and Photo Imagery (SHARP) study in Portland and Seattle engages older Black adults in reminiscence while walking pre-planned routes that pass culturally meaningful locations, revealing how place, walking, and social reminiscence may contribute to remembering. Walking sessions were transcribed and categorized to identify sections constituting distinct memories. During and after the walking intervention, data were collected from 35 focus groups, coded thematically for reflections on memory, remembering, and place. Results suggest that collective remembering and emotion recall occur through social reminiscing while triadic walking. The three proposed pathways eliciting in-place memory and emotion responses through walking are: (1) sensory triggers, specifically visual images (2) recalling social actors associated with places (e.g., clergy, business people), and (3) experiencing feelings of place attachment. Findings also indicate that culturally relevant third places are potential spatial cues for recalling embodied memories of place when physical places no longer exist, given that gentrification can disrupt cognitive maps of place, rendering places harder to recall. Place-based walking methods may support positive cognitive outcomes (e.g., memory-making) facilitated through embodied spatial processes.

items.title: Probing spatiotemporal context reveals differences between true and false memories.
items.abstract: Our memories do not faithfully represent the past, but rather are reconstructive, rendering them susceptible to the intrusion of false memories. However, the nature of the false memories is debated: Do false memories reflect the retrieval of a genuine, erroneous memory trace, or are they the product of semantic associations? This question reflects the fact that although some findings suggest that false memories can be phenomenologically compelling and rich in details, others suggest that there are subtle cues that distinguish true and false memories. Here, we take a novel approach to this question by assessing memory for the spatiotemporal context of false memories - the when and where of those memories. We demonstrate that context memory can provide a probabilistic cue to whether a memory is true or false in the Deese-Roediger-McDermott paradigm. Across participants, the reliability of reported context memory (i.e., the consistency with which people report remembering when or where a false memory occurred) revealed differences between true and false memories. Additionally, confidence in memory for context (both within and across participants) differed between true and false memories - even when controlling for confidence in having encountered the false memory. However, these effects were malleable: Under certain circumstances, false memories appeared to have genuine context traces. Together, these data provide new insights into the circumstances under which true and false memories differ in subtle but meaningful ways, speaking to theories of how false memories may arise from the reconstructive nature of memory.

items.title: Repetition increases belief in implausible statements more than for plausible statements.
items.abstract: The finding that repetition causes increased belief - termed the illusory truth effect - has raised important concerns about the possibility of repetition leading to widespread belief in falsehoods. This concern implies that the illusory truth effect meaningfully impacts statements that are initially thought to be implausible, as is commonly the case for falsehoods. Using a large (N = 933) online experiment, we test the relationship between the illusory truth effect and prior belief in trivia statements. In contrast to previous work, we measure the prior belief that an individual assigns to a specific statement to allow for a precise estimation of this relationship. Concerningly, we find that not only does the illusory truth effect appear meaningful for statements where participants have low prior belief, but the effect is actually stronger for these initially implausible statements. Our findings suggest that repetition can be particularly harmful when statements are initially seen as implausible.

items.title: Loss aversion for time and money: Cross-commodity variation in loss weighting and choice consistency.
items.abstract: Loss aversion is often inferred from a prospect-theory parameter (λ) greater than 1 and interpreted as evidence that losses receive greater psychological weight than equivalent gains. Yet this interpretation depends on the assumptions used to translate observed choices into model estimates. We examined whether λ can be interpreted as a measure of psychological loss weighting by comparing observed choices and model estimates across money and time. A total of 124 participants chose between safe and risky options in separate gain-only and loss-only tasks involving both resources and completed a measure of time perspective. Participants chose the risky option more often for losses than for gains in both resources. However, the primary model yielded population-level λ estimates of 0.77 for money and 0.82 for time, with no reliable difference. Individual estimates showed weak correspondence across resources, although recovery analyses indicated it could arise even when the underlying λ is identical. Time perspective did not predict λ. Across alternative modeling specifications, estimated λ shifted from below to above 1 despite unchanged observed choices. Moreover, different combinations of loss valuation and sensitivity to value differences could produce identical predicted choice probabilities. Thus, behavioral differences between gains and losses, and even an estimated λ greater than 1, do not necessarily demonstrate greater psychological weighting of losses.

items.title: Frequency-tagging SSVEP reveals late-stage sustained attention to sad faces in subthreshold depression.
items.abstract: Attentional bias toward negative information has been regarded as a central cognitive mechanism underlying depression. However, the temporal dynamics of emotional attention in individuals with subthreshold depression (StD) remain insufficiently understood. Conventional measures of attentional bias are generally unable to continuously track the dynamic allocation of attentional resources between competing stimuli. In the present study, a frequency-tagged steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) combined with a dot-probe task was employed to continuously measure visuocortical responses to emotional faces in individuals with StD (n = 25) and healthy controls (HC; n = 28). Participants viewed concurrently presented happy-neutral, sad-neutral, and neutral-neutral stimulus pairs while SSVEP amplitudes were recorded across different stages of attentional processing. The results showed no significant differences in SSVEP amplitudes among happy, sad, and neutral faces in the StD group during early processing (180-500 ms), potentially suggesting reduced early sensitivity to emotional information. During late processing (2000-3000 ms), the StD group exhibited greater sad-neutral difference SSVEP amplitudes than the HC group, whereas no corresponding group difference was detected during earlier stages. Larger late-window sad-neutral difference amplitudes were also associated with greater depressive symptom severity across the full sample. These findings suggest altered late processing of negative emotional information in StD, which may be consistent with, but does not directly establish, impaired attentional disengagement. Frequency-tagged SSVEPs may therefore provide a useful neural measure for characterizing the temporal dynamics of emotional processing in individuals with subthreshold depression.

items.title: Beyond source: The effects of AI's multiple roles in persuasion.
items.abstract: AI is becoming embedded across all aspects of persuasion in business, from segmentation and message creation to conversational exchange. This review and synthesis of the relevant literature argues that the understanding of the psychological effects of AI persuasion should not be reduced to source inferences about machine credibility. It shows that AI can influence persuasion by taking on several roles other than being a perceived source. It can directly influence persuasion by message crafting, recipient tuning and being a contextual influence. Critically, these non-source effects may occur even when AI involvement is undisclosed or undetected. Looking forward, future research should go beyond attitude change as a dependent variable, and also consider attitude strength, metacognitive confidence and resistance to counterpersuasion.

items.title: Assessing Displacement Risk in Relation to Health Outcomes among Black Women Living with HIV Using Spatial Analysis and Zip Code Level Data.
items.abstract: Gentrification results in higher tax revenues, but also the displacement of longstanding residents. Housing insecurity has been associated with medication nonadherence among people with HIV; however, the existing literature does not assess neighborhood level variables (e.g., indicators of gentrification) in tandem with individual level variables to adequately assess the risk of displacement and its association with health outcomes. This study examines estimated displacement risk in relation to mental health symptoms, HIV medication adherence, and HIV viral load among Black women living with HIV (BWLWH). Baseline data was collected (2019-2020) among 151 Black women enrolled in a cohort study in Miami, FL on mental health symptoms, medication adherence, HIV viral load, and sociodemographic variables (e.g., income). We combine changes in zip code level data (2014-2019) on Black individuals, White individuals, bachelor's degree, owner occupied house, median gross rent, and Airbnb fees (2015-2019) for apartment, condominium, and houses to assess estimated displacement risk (dichotomized [0, 1]). Spatial analyses and nonlinear regression models accounting for robust standard errors are used to assess estimated risk of displacement and its association with health outcomes. Results indicate that higher estimated risk of displacement is related to (a) higher depressive symptoms, (b) higher trauma exposure, (c) higher symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder, and (d) lower medication adherence. Our novel findings reiterate the importance of future research examining indicators of gentrification that may impact the risk of displacement for BWLWH and ultimately their well-being and health outcomes.

items.title: Is exercise associated with health-related quality of life in children and adolescents with sickle cell disease using self- and parent proxy-reports?
items.abstract: Purpose This study examined associations between demographics, disease severity indicators, levels of weekly mild, moderate and strenuous intensity exercise and self-reports and parental proxy-reports of health-related quality of life (HRQL) in children and adolescents with sickle cell disease (SCD). Concordance between parental and child/adolescent reports was also examined. Methods This cross-sectional study adopted an interdependent-groups, correlational design. One-hundred and six children and ninety-six adolescents with SCD and one of their parents independently completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory and the Godin-Leisure-Time Exercise Questionnaire. Parents also reported demographics and disease severity indicators. Results Parents underestimated children's/adolescents' HRQL, although the effect was small, but reports of exercise were generally concordant. Fewer days missed from school and higher levels of moderate exercise were associated with better HRQL reported by children and their parent. Fewer days missed from school and fewer vaso-occlusive crises were associated with adolescent and parental reports of better HRQL. Higher levels of strenuous exercise were also associated with parental reports of better HRQL in adolescents. Conclusion Disease severity indicators are associated with self-reports and parental reports of better child and adolescent HRQL but moderate intensity exercise also plays a role for children. Clinical practice should promote daily exercise and help parents understand that balance is needed between taking some precautions but not being overprotective so that exercise levels are insufficient and HRQL is impacted.

items.title: Exploring performance and trust in autonomous surgical robotic systems: the role of visuo-haptic guidance.
items.abstract: Purpose Incorporating task-level autonomy into teleoperation systems for robot assisted laparoscopic surgery requires operators to effectively manage transitions from task-level autonomy to teleoperation control, particularly during system failures. This study investigated the impact of the level of guidance during take-over situations on participants' performance and their trust in the teleoperation system. Methods N = 34 students, unfamiliar with the system and task, performed a ring transfer task under two conditions: visual guidance, where they monitored the system visually, and visuo-haptic guidance, where they also received haptic feedback by holding the input device as the system operated in task-level autonomy. During some trials, system failures occurred, requiring participants to take over control. Results Results showed that participants noticed system failures faster with visuo-haptic guidance compared to visual guidance. Although visuo-haptic guidance did not improve task completion times or accuracy during task completion, it led to significantly higher trust in the teleoperation system and a stronger sense of perceived control. However, participants also reported higher physical demand and effort under visuo-haptic guidance, indicating an increased workload in this condition. Conclusion In conclusion, these findings reveal important trade-offs of the influence of haptic guidance during human oversight of teleoperated autonomous systems.

items.title: Effectiveness of Verbal Fluency Tests for Detecting Cognitive Decline in Adults with Alzheimer's Dementia and Frontotemporal Dementia: A Three-Level Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: As our population ages, the prevalence of dementia, including Alzheimer's dementia (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), is increasing. Early dementia diagnoses facilitate access to interventions when they are most effective for prolonging and improving life. Verbal fluency tests (e.g., FAS and Animal Fluency) can aid in the diagnosis of AD and FTD through detecting declines in executive functioning and language. These tests may be particularly useful for diagnosing the behavioural variant of FTD (bvFTD), which is associated with declines in executive functioning. A systematic search of Embase, PsycINFO, PubMed, MEDLINE, CINHAL, and AgeLine identified 127 peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to July 2024, which compared FAS and Animal Fluency Test performances of people with AD or FTD to cognitively-healthy controls. Hedges' g effect sizes determined the effectiveness of three common score types (Total, Intrusion, Perseveration) for AD/FTD combined, AD and combined FTD subtypes, and AD and FTD subtypes (e.g., bvFTD). FAS and Animal Fluency Total Scores were the most reported and effective for detecting cognitive decline in these dementias combined (g = -1.31 and g = -1.95, respectively), but similar effects were seen for AD and bvFTD. The pattern of effects was not influenced by patient characteristics and remained consistent when only low risk-of-bias studies were analysed. However, significant publication bias may have inflated the effects for AD. Overall, the FAS and Animal Fluency Total Scores can effectively detect cognitive decline in both AD and FTD, although they cannot be recommended for differentiating between AD and bvFTD.

items.title: Patterns and Factors Associated With Contacting a Children and Young People's Mental Health Crisis Service.
items.abstract: BackgroundIn recent years, there has been a notable increase in the number of children and young people (CYP) experiencing mental health crises.ObjectiveThis study aimed to explore the demographic and clinical characteristics of CYP who engaged with a mental health crisis service in Northwest England.MethodA retrospective cohort study was conducted using data collected from CYP accessing the crisis service between January 2022 and December 2023.ResultsA total of 1,940 individuals were identified as having contact with the crisis team. Approximately 75% were female, and nearly half lived in the two most deprived socioeconomic quintiles. The majority were aged between 13 and 15 years. The number of contacts per individual ranged from 1 to 186, totaling 7,711 contacts overall. The primary reasons for contact included self-harm (50%) and suicidality (30%). Notably, 29% were not in education, and 28% were also receiving therapy from CYP mental health services. Contact rates peaked during weekdays and during May, September, October, and November.ConclusionsThe findings highlight the need for multi-agency preventative interventions, particularly targeting females and those from deprived communities, with attention to times of high service demand.

items.title: Two-stage least squares as a mean and covariance structure estimator: Reconciling econometric and psychometric formulations.
items.abstract: Instrumental variables regression is increasingly used in psychology and is the basis of model-implied instrumental variables structural equation modelling (MIIV-SEM), yet econometric and psychometric formulations use different statistical representations and terminology. We develop a general theory of multi-stage weighted least squares estimation for mean and covariance structures and show that classical two-stage least squares (2SLS) is the second stage of a three-stage procedure. The first stage estimates predictive equations for the explanatory variables; the second estimates the structural intercept and regression coefficients; and the third estimates the remaining disturbance variance and covariances, propagating uncertainty from earlier stages. For structural parameters, the normal-theory and asymptotically distribution-free covariance estimators reduce exactly to conventional homoscedastic and heteroscedasticity-robust 2SLS estimators. With model-based covariance matrices, Browne's normal-theory goodness-of-fit statistic equals Sargan's overidentification statistic, and its ADF counterpart equals Wooldridge's heteroscedasticity-robust score statistic. Third-stage disturbance covariances quantify endogeneity and yield Wald tests asymptotically equivalent, under the null, to the Hausman OLS-2SLS contrast and Wooldridge's robust exogeneity test, respectively. The results place MIIV-SEM estimators, standard errors, and tests within a coherent multi-stage statistical theory.

items.title: The Architecture of Wisdom in Interpersonal Conflict: Structure and Trait, State, and Cultural Expression Across World Regions.
items.abstract: Objective How do individuals across diverse cultures navigate interpersonal conflicts, and what drives variation in their use of wisdom-related strategies? Method In two studies spanning eight world regions (N = 4445), we examined the factor structure of five wisdom-related strategies (Intellectual Humility, Others' Perspectives, Acknowledgement of Multiple Outcomes, Search for Compromise, Outsider's View), their individual-difference correlates, and trait-state variance. Results In Study 1 (autobiographical recall), we identified a three-factor structure-Perspectival Metacognition, Conflict Resolution, and Outsider's View-that showed approximate measurement invariance across cultures. In Study 2 (standardized scenarios), we replicated this structure and partitioned trait, state, and cultural variance. Cross-cultural differences accounted for about 4% of variance in expressed wisdom, whereas within-person variation across situations explained the largest share: People expressed less wisdom in reflections on conflicts involving trust betrayal than social rejection, an effect linked to greater emotional reactivity to betrayal. At the individual level, need for cognition and relational-interdependent self-construal showed small-to-moderate positive associations with each wisdom-related feature, whereas a sense of uniqueness was positively related to Conflict Resolution. Conclusions Wisdom in reflections on interpersonal conflict appears organized around three metacognitive themes that replicate broadly across cultures, with situational affordances (vs. cultural or trait dispositions) accounting for most variation in its expression.

items.title: Friendship under ostracism: how informal ties relate to service-oriented citizenship behavior in public organizations.
items.abstract: Informal relationships are widely regarded as important for the effectiveness of public organizations, yet the pathways through which these ties may relate to extra-role behaviors remain underexplored. Drawing on social support and social comparison theories, this study develops and tests a dual-path moderated mediation model linking workplace friendship to service-oriented organizational citizenship behavior (SO-OCB) among civil servants. Using two-wave survey data from 363 respondents in Heilongjiang Province, China, the results show that workplace friendship is positively associated with SO-OCB through two complementary indirect pathways: via social support from coworkers and via social comparison. Moreover, the friendship-social support association is stronger at higher levels of reported ostracism, suggesting that the link between workplace friendship and social support may depend on the relational context. These findings extend understanding of how workplace friendships may act as both resources and motivational cues, offering tentative practical insights for sustaining service quality and employee engagement in public sector organizations.

items.title: Oral Health Knowledge and Lifestyle-Related Factors Among First-Year University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Introduction Oral health knowledge and lifestyle factors play a key role in the prevention of oral diseases, yet their relationship with oral health knowledge in young adult populations remains insufficiently explored. This study aims to assess oral health knowledge and its association with selected lifestyle-related factors among first-year university students in a Spanish academic setting. Methods A cross-sectional exploratory study was conducted with 149 first-year university students recruited through non-probabilistic sampling. Oral health knowledge was evaluated using a validated 20-item questionnaire, and lifestyle behaviours using the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP II). Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p Results Most participants demonstrated medium to high levels of oral health knowledge. Lifestyle profiles were generally favourable. Gender-related differences were observed, with women showing higher oral health knowledge and interpersonal relationships scores, while men reported higher physical activity. Degree-related differences were also observed, with higher oral health knowledge levels among health-related students. No consistent associations were observed between oral health knowledge and lifestyle variables. Conclusion Oral health knowledge was generally adequate but uneven and not consistently reflected in lifestyle behaviours, highlighting a gap between knowledge and practice. These findings suggest that educational approaches alone may be insufficient to promote favourable outcomes. Interventions should therefore incorporate behavioural and contextual components to enhance effectiveness. Regarding its clinical relevance, adequate oral health knowledge alone does not ensure healthy behaviours among young adults. Incorporating lifestyle-tailored strategies into preventive interventions may improve their effectiveness in promoting sustained oral health practices.

items.title: Development and Measurement Invariance Test of the Chinese Social-Emotional Climate Scale from the Social-Relational Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract Background Social-emotional climate refers to individuals' perceptions of the emotional environment within a collective and profoundly shapes emotional experience, interpersonal interaction, and social behavior. However, most existing scales were developed in Western cultural contexts and cannot adapt to the paradigm of indigenous Chinese social psychology. Against this backdrop, this study, grounded in de Rivera's two-dimensional emotional climate framework and adopting the social-relational perspective, developed the Chinese Social-Emotional Climate Scale using the semantic differential scale paradigm and conducted measurement invariance tests. Methods This study adopted a convenience sampling method and collected data via online and offline questionnaires. A total of 500 participants were recruited, with 250 allocated for item analysis and exploratory factor analysis and 250 for confirmatory factor analysis, to examine the scale's factorial structure, reliability, and validity. Measurement invariance was subsequently tested across gender, age, and educational level. Results Exploratory factor analysis yielded three factors—"Relation to others," "Relation to ideals," and "Relation to groups"—explaining 78.60% of the variance, with factor loadings of 0.743–0.861 in the confirmatory three-factor model. Fit indices were satisfactory ( χ ²/ df = 1.418; NFI = 0.976; RFI = 0.964; IFI = 0.993; TLI = 0.989; CFI = 0.993; RMSEA = 0.041). Cronbach's α coefficients of the three dimensions ranged from 0.61 to 0.90, indicating good internal consistency, and measurement invariance was supported across gender, age, and educational level. Conclusions Grounded in the social-relational perspective, this study developed a localized Chinese Social-Emotional Climate Scale with three dimensions—"Relation to others," "Relation to ideals," and "Relation to groups"—demonstrating good reliability, validity, and measurement invariance. Moving beyond emotional content and valence classifications, the scale establishes a three-dimensional structure of Chinese social-emotional climate from a social-relational perspective, offering a new path for measuring emotional climate and enriching the cross-cultural explanatory power of this concept. It provides a useful tool for future research on social mentality.

items.title: 'You've got something to look at and something to achieve': Perspectives of adults with type 2 diabetes on professional-mode glucose monitoring. A GP-OSMOTIC nested qualitative study.
items.abstract: Aims Approximately half of adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) have average glucose levels above the recommended range, increasing the risk of long-term complications. Intermittent (quarterly) use of professional-mode continuous glucose monitoring (Pro-CGM) offers opportunity for greater personalisation of management, collaborative care and targeted education to support behavioural modification. Framed in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study aimed to explore how Pro-CGM was experienced by adults with T2D, and to identify potential mechanisms for behaviour change. Methods This qualitative study was nested within a pragmatic, 12-month randomised controlled trial of quarterly Pro-CGM in primary care. Participants were purposively recruited from the intervention group; 22 individuals from six primary care clinics in Victoria, Australia, took part. An abductive analytic approach was adopted, whereby data-driven themes were subsequently interpreted through the SDT framework. Results Qualitative analyses identified Pro-CGM monitoring and consultation experiences both satisfied and frustrated individual needs. Impacts on motivation and behaviour change were influenced by the degree to which support needs were met by clinicians and individual differences (e.g. regulatory orientation, preferences). This suggests that more sustained changes in behaviour and longer-term improvements in HbA1c may have occurred if Pro-CGM was implemented in a manner that provided appropriate support for psychological needs. Conclusion Pro-CGM has the potential to improve engagement in diabetes self management and health outcomes among people with T2D. Consideration of Pro-CGM-related resource needs for people with T2D, including facilitation of clinical support, is required to optimise the engagement with and sustain behavioural change for people with T2D.

items.title: Mechanobiology in the Brain: Sensing Your Heartbeats via Mechanosensitive Channels.
items.abstract: The brain-heart axis mediates bidirectional communication via neural and humoral pathways and plays a pivotal role in physiological regulation and the pathogenesis of cardiocerebral comorbidities. Mechanobiological studies further suggest that mechanical signaling pathways may serve as the third modality for brain-heart crosstalk. This commentary reviews two distinct mechanical regulatory modalities within the brain-heart axis: periphery-dependent mechanosensation, which acts as an upstream sensory module of classical neural pathways, and central in-situ mechanotransduction, which directly senses mechanical stimuli originating from cardiovascular pulsations in the central nervous system. Cumulative molecular, ex vivo, and in vivo experimental evidence demonstrates that subsets of central neurons can directly respond to arterial pressure pulsations via mechanosensitive ion channels and achieve functional coupling with heartbeat rhythms. Nevertheless, this field faces further evidentiary limitations. This commentary synthesizes current evidence and puts forward a scientific hypothesis that the mechanical microenvironment of brain tissue may modulate central mechanosensation. It also highlights future priorities including verification across broader neuronal cell types and in vivo functional interventions, to further refine the theoretical framework of the brain-heart axis.

items.title: Needs Assessment: Expanding Perinatal Psychiatry Access Programs to Support Infant Care Professionals and Postpartum Individuals.
items.abstract: The Perinatal Psychiatry Access Program model (i.e., Access Program) aims to address mental health (MH) inequities among pregnant and postpartum individuals by providing MH training and support to perinatal care professionals. Despite program expansion, perinatal MH and substance use disorders (SUDs) remain significant contributors to postpartum maternal mortality. Collaborating with infant care professionals may enhance detection and access to MH/SUD treatment. This needs assessment explored infant care professionals' interest in recognizing and responding to the MH/SUD needs of pregnant and postpartum individuals and assessed the degree to which the statewide Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms (MCPAP for Moms), could meet the needs of these professionals. We conducted four focus groups (n = 34) and 20 interviews (n = 22) with public health professionals, MCPAP for Moms staff, and child-focused professionals. Sessions were transcribed and coded using iterative thematic analysis. Although most infant care professionals expressed interest in perinatal MH/SUDs, this interest varied based on their recognition of parental MH as within their purview. Training and systematic support for perinatal MH/SUDs was not common in infant care settings. These findings highlight infant care professionals' interest in supporting postpartum individuals with perinatal MH/SUDs as well as the need for an increased prioritization of workforce development to serve the infant care system and ultimately improve the lives of families. Hiring additional staff, including a liaison from the early childhood community, and leveraging existing networks to improve consultation, resource referrals, and communication with infant care professionals is recommended.

items.title: Lifestyle Psychiatry in Mental Health Care: Knowledge, Practices and Attitudes of Australian Health Practitioners.
items.abstract: This study sought to examine Australian health practitioners' knowledge, practices, and attitudes regarding lifestyle psychiatry to help elucidate factors driving an implementation gap. A convergent parallel mixed methods design was employed using an online survey with closed- and open-ended questions on eight lifestyle interventions. 212 eligible health practitioners working in or referring to mental health settings completed an online survey. Descriptive analyses were used for quantitative data, and conventional content analysis for qualitative data. Results indicated that 73.6% of participants had knowledge of lifestyle psychiatry. Two categories described their understanding of lifestyle psychiatry in mental health care: Lifestyle interventions are non-medical adjuncts that complement current practices; and lifestyle interventions empower behaviour change across a range of domains. Most participants considered all eight lifestyle interventions to be evidence-based. The mean number of lifestyle interventions in which participants had received additional training was 1.65, most commonly in mindfulness and stress reduction. Five categories were constructed from respondents' perceived benefits of lifestyle interventions: psychological health, physical health, self-empowerment, holistic wellbeing, and connection to self, other and the wider context. Perceived risks fell into three categories: psychological distress, physical harm, and social and economic impacts. Incorporation of lifestyle psychiatry into patient care varied across interventions; dietary interventions and smoking cessation had the largest implementation gap. Overall, respondents identified benefits of lifestyle psychiatry for holistic mental health care but limited integration, possibly due to perceived risks and insufficient training. Findings support calls for strengthened professional development and embedded training in lifestyle psychiatry within health degrees.

items.title: Multimodal AI in Oral Cancer: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Oral cancer presents significant diagnostic and prognostic challenges, often due to late-stage detection and tumour heterogeneity. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML), offer promising solutions by integrating multimodal biomedical data. This PRISMA-guided systematic review evaluates over 82 studies from 2015 to 2025 that apply convolutional neural networks, transformers and graph neural networks to oral cancer, using combinations of histopathology, radiology, genomics and clinical data. Results indicate that multimodal AI models consistently outperform unimodal approaches in diagnostic accuracy, AUC and survival prediction. Architectures employing attention mechanisms, graph embedding and fusion transformers demonstrate superior performance in tasks such as early lesion detection and treatment outcome modelling. Despite these advances, challenges persist in generalisability, data standardisation and clinical validation. Multimodal AI thus represents a paradigm shift toward precision oncology in oral cancer, warranting further research focused on interpretability, prospective validation and ethical clinical deployment.

items.title: Epidemiological Profile and Temporal Trends of Exogenous Poisoning in the State of São Paulo and Brazil From 2010 to 2020.
items.abstract: Exogenous poisoning is a compulsorily notifiable condition in Brazil, but analyses of its temporal trends in the state of São Paulo remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological profile of exogenous poisoning in the state of São Paulo from 2010 to 2020 and its distribution across Regional Health Care Networks (Redes Regionais de Atenção à Saúde (RRAS)) and to analyze temporal trends in incidence, mortality, and case fatality compared with Brazil. An observational time-series study was conducted using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)), obtained through the TabNet platform of the Brazilian Ministry of Health, and population estimates from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics. Sociodemographic, exposure, and outcome variables were analyzed. Incidence, mortality, and case fatality rates were calculated, and notifications were stratified by RRAS. Temporal trends were assessed by joinpoint regression, estimating the annual percent change (APC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each segment and for the entire period, with sensitivity analyses. A total of 315,266 notifications and 3,209 deaths were recorded in São Paulo, accounting for 25.7% of notifications and 27.4% of deaths in Brazil. Cases predominated among females (n=169,740; 53.8%), individuals aged 20-39 years (n=142,989; 45.4%), and White individuals (n=166,896; 52.9%). Medications were the main toxic agent (n=144,567; 45.9%), and suicide attempt was the main circumstance (n=125,491; 39.8%). Incidence was 64.7 cases per 100,000 inhabitants per year (Brazil: 54.8), mortality was 6.6 deaths per 1,000,000 inhabitants per year (Brazil: 5.2), and case fatality was 1.02% (Brazil: 0.95%). Incidence (APC=13.9%; p<0.001) and mortality (APC=11.7%; p<0.001) increased over the period, whereas case fatality showed no significant trend over the entire period; a decline between 2016 and 2020 (APC=-14.8%; p=0.031) was not statistically significant in sensitivity analyses. The highest incidence was observed in RRAS 12 (São José do Rio Preto/Araçatuba; 126.2 per 100,000 inhabitants per year), a region of intense agricultural activity. Exogenous poisoning in São Paulo showed increasing incidence and mortality, at levels above the national average, with a decline in case fatality after 2016 that should be interpreted with caution, and marked regional heterogeneity. These findings support strengthening toxicological surveillance and tailoring prevention strategies to regional and epidemiological characteristics.

items.title: The Relationship Between Racism and Suicidal Thoughts Among Asian American Firearm Owners and Non-Owners.
items.abstract: Objective Firearm suicides among Asian Americans rose significantly between 2018 and 2023, outpacing the increase in firearm suicides among Whites over the same period. Despite this rising risk, firearm suicide research and prevention efforts have rarely focused on Asian Americans. Our study compares the relationship between suicidal thoughts and personal experiences of racial discrimination between firearm owners and non-owners among Asian American adults. Methods Our study utilizes a nationwide cross-sectional online survey conducted among Asian Americans in July 2023 using a multi-sourced, non-probabilistic panel of U.S. adults. Eligible participants were aged 21 or older and could read English. A logistic regression model assessed the interaction between experiences of racial discrimination and firearm ownership on suicidal ideation, controlling for mental distress, alcohol use, and demographic variables for 729 survey respondents. Results The interaction between racism and firearm ownership was significant (OR = 2.60, C.I.=1.19-5.66). Simple slope analysis showed a stronger, positive association between experiences of racial discrimination and suicidal ideation among firearm owners (OR = 2.88, C.I.= 1.40-5.90) compared to non-owners (OR = 1.11, C.I.=0.80-1.54). Conclusion Our findings indicate that the combination of racism-related stress and firearm ownership is linked to an elevated likelihood of suicidal ideation among Asian Americans. Attention to these co-occurring risks is critical for informing culturally responsive strategies for firearm suicide prevention within this population.

items.title: Pesticide β-cypermethrin exposure compromises endometrial receptivity during the window of implantation through ERK-MAPK signaling-driven dysregulation of cell-cycle-associated proteins in early-pregnant mice.
items.abstract: Beta-cypermethrin (β-CYP), a widely used type II pyrethroid insecticide, is increasingly recognized as a reproductive toxicant, yet its direct impact on endometrial receptivity and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Endometrial receptivity is critical for embryo implantation, and its impairment is a major cause of pregnancy loss. Here, we investigated whether β-CYP disrupts endometrial receptivity in early pregnant mice by dysregulating the ERK-MAPK signaling pathway and associated cell cycle checkpoints. Pregnant Kunming mice were orally administered β-CYP from gestational day 1 (GD1) to GD4, with or without co-treatment with the selective ERK1/2 inhibitor SCH772984. On GD5, implantation sites, and endometrial receptivity-related molecules were assessed via western blotting, immunofluorescence, and ELISA. β‑CYP exposure significantly reduced implantation sites, downregulated the receptivity markers LIF and HOXA10, upregulated the anti‑adhesion molecule MUC1, and dysregulated G1/S- and G2/M- cell-cycle-associated proteins, as evidenced by reduced E2F1, Cyclin D1, CDK4, CDK2, and CDK1, alongside aberrant Cyclin B1 accumulation. These defects were accompanied by marked ERK1/2 hyperphosphorylation and profound systemic and uterine oxidative stress (elevated ROS, MDA, and LDH; suppressed T‑SOD, CAT, GSH‑Px, and GGT). ERK inhibition rescued implantation rates, restored LIF and HOXA10, normalized Cyclin D1-CDK4/6-E2F1 and CDK1-Cyclin B1 axes, and partially attenuated oxidative stress, although antioxidant enzyme activities remained below baseline. Our findings demonstrated that β-CYP impaired endometrial receptivity through elevated ERK-MAPK signaling, which coordinately disrupted molecular gatekeepers of receptivity, dysregulated G1/S- and G2/M-associated cell-cycle proteins, and potentiated oxidative injury. Pharmacological ERK blockade effectively improved these pathogenic cascades, identifying ERK as a vital mediator and a potential therapeutic target for environmental toxin‑related implantation failure.

items.title: Effects of maternal exposure to 2,6-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone during pregnancy and lactation on the gut microbiota and neurodevelopment in offspring rats.
items.abstract: 2,6-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone (DCBQ), as an emerging drinking water disinfection byproduct, has been widely detected in drinking water and pose potential risks. However, there are relatively few reports on their potential neurodevelopmental toxicity, especially the lack of in vivo studies as the most direct evidence. A rat model was established for the entire gestation and lactation period to study the neurodevelopmental toxicity of DCBQ in offspring rats, through evaluating gut microbiota, neurotransmitters and neurobehaviors. Maternal rats were administered with DCBQ at 0.5, 5, and 50 mg/kg body weight via gavage throughout gestation and lactation. Our results showed that maternal DCBQ exposure induced prolonged neural reflex behavior, decreased motor activity, and increased anxiety-like behavior in offspring rats. And the levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factors and neurotransmitters, especially glutamate and dopamine, in serum and hippocampus were significantly decreased in offspring rats after maternal DCBQ exposure. Maternal DCBQ exposure induced imbalance of intestinal microbiota in a gender-specific way. In addition, maternal DCBQ exposure induced significant changes of 123 metabolites, affecting multiple metabolic pathways, such as mTOR pathway. In particular, the altered gut microbiota showed strong associations with altered metabolites, neurotransmitters and neurobehaviors after maternal DCBQ exposure. Our findings suggest that maternal DCBQ exposure may impair neurodevelopment and disrupt gut microbiota and fecal metabolite profiles of offspring rats, indicating a potential gut microbiota-metabolome-neurochemical link. Our study highlights the importance of evaluating the neurodevelopmental toxicity of disinfection byproducts in future.

items.title: Early circulating cell-free mitochondrial deoxyribonucleic acid and mortality in adults with sepsis: A systematic review and Meta-analysis protocol.
items.abstract: Objectives To assess whether higher circulating cell-free mitochondrial deoxyribonucleic acid concentrations within the first 24 h are associated with higher all-cause mortality at 28-30 days in adults with sepsis. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on October 17, 2026. Eligible observational studies will assess early circulating concentrations and prognosis. At least two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias using Quality In Prognosis Studies or the Joanna Briggs Institute analytical cross-sectional tool. Certainty will be assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Meta-analysis will require at least three independent studies with compatible estimates for the same outcome. Inverse-variance random-effects models will use restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals. Association measures, discrimination, and concentration differences will be synthesized separately. When a cohort reports both mortality horizons, 28-day estimates will be preferred; 30-day-only estimates will remain eligible. Expected results The review will characterize associations with mortality and organ dysfunction, discrimination, and additional prognostic information, accounting for baseline severity, clinical setting, and measurement conditions. Conclusions The synthesis will inform further evaluation of this biomarker for risk assessment in sepsis.

items.title: Nicotine Pouch and Tobacco Use, Nicotine Dependence, and Psychiatric Symptoms Among U.S. Adults.
items.abstract: Introduction Nicotine pouches (NPs), a rapidly growing category of non-combustible oral nicotine products, are frequently used alongside tobacco products. This study examined NP-tobacco co-use and its association with nicotine dependence and high internalizing and externalizing symptoms among U.S. adults. Methods This study analyzed Wave 7 (2022-2023) of the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health (PATH) Study, including 11,514 U.S. adults with past-year tobacco or NP use. Data were analyzed in 2026. Past-year NP and tobacco use were assessed along with nicotine dependence (16-item validated scale) and internalizing and externalizing symptoms (≥4 as high symptoms for each domain). Survey-weighted linear and modified Poisson regression examined associations of NP-tobacco co-use with nicotine dependence and psychiatric symptoms, respectively, adjusting for covariates and the other outcomes. Results Among U.S. adults with past-year tobacco or NP use, 5.4% reported NP use; 95.7% of adults who used NPs also used tobacco. NP-tobacco co-use was associated with the highest adjusted nicotine dependence scores (vs. tobacco-only use: b=7.75, 95% CI=6.29-9.20). NP-tobacco co-use (vs. tobacco-only use) was not significantly associated with high internalizing or externalizing symptoms after adjustment for covariates, including nicotine dependence. Conclusion NP-tobacco co-use is common among adults who use NPs and is associated with greater nicotine dependence, but not significantly associated with psychiatric symptoms after covariate adjustment. Adults with co-use may benefit from nicotine dependence assessment and tailored cessation support. Longitudinal research is needed to clarify the observed associations.

items.title: Quality is in the eye of the beholder: A qualitative description study to explore the perceptions of researchers and practitioners on the quality of implementation science tools.
items.abstract: Objective Implementation science (IS) tools (collectively referring to theories, models, frameworks, and tools that support TMF use) provide guidance for implementing, disseminating, sustaining, and scaling up health interventions, programs, and policies. However, little is known about the quality of IS tools. The study explored how implementation researchers, practitioners, and researcher-practitioners define and perceive quality in relation to IS tools. Study design and setting We employed a qualitative description methodology informed by a pragmatic theoretical worldview. Eligible participants were individuals with experience developing or using IS tools, and who primarily work in Canada, the United States, Australia, or Europe. They were recruited through purposeful and snowball sampling. Data was collected through virtual, semi-structured focus groups and individual interviews on Zoom. They were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and de-identified. An inductive, codebook thematic analysis was used to analyze the data. Three researchers independently coded an initial set of transcripts to develop a coding template. One researcher coded the remaining transcripts, and another audited the coding for consistency and congruence. Three researchers generated themes and sub-themes. The Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research (SRQR) was used to report our findings. Results We conducted 10 focus groups and 11 individual interviews with 35 total participants (19 researchers, 9 researcher-practitioners, and 7 practitioners). Approximately half were from Canada, and most identified as women. Across the roles, the quality of IS tools were perceived to be multidimensional (e.g., scientific rigour, practical utility) and context-dependent (e.g., type of IS tool). Participants' perceptions of quality were influenced by their training and experiences. Other selection factors such as relevance appear to have a greater influence than the perceived quality of an IS tool. Participants described the importance in the quality of IS tool application. They suggested multiple considerations for improving the quality, development, selection, application, and evaluation of IS tools. Conclusion The quality of IS tools was perceived to be multidimensional and context-dependent. Varying perspectives on the role of quality of IS tools in selection and application indicate a need for clearer conceptualization. Our findings highlight the importance of future research aimed at improving the application of IS tools.

items.title: Milu antler powder demonstrates efficacy in mitigating kidney damage induced by the aging process through the modulation of intestinal microbiota.
items.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Aging significantly affects the structure and function of the kidney, leading to profound changes. Ancient texts document that deer antler powder can ameliorate renal damage and aging, but its exact mechanism of action remains unclear. Aim of study To evaluate the renal protective capabilities of Milu antler powder in senescent mice and elucidate its mechanism of action in alleviating renal injury. Materials and methods We prepared and conducted the ultramicro-grade Milu antler powder (UGM) and evaluated its effectiveness in improving kidney function in D-galactose-induced senescent mice through biochemical indices and histological studies. We then employed UPLC-MS/MS and 16S rRNA gene analysis to analyze the changes in intestinal microbiota and metabolites. Finally, the effects of UGM and its metabolites on the aging phenotype and renal function in mice were verified through fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and cell experiments. Results UGM significantly ameliorated brain aging and immune decline in senescent mice. Notably, it significantly reduced renal structural damage and aging phenotype, and improved renal dysfunction. The 16S rRNA gene analysis and its metabolite analyses showed that UGM was able to upregulate Akkermansia, Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and downregulate Desulfobacterota, as well as alter metabolite expression (especially sodium acetate). Furthermore, through FMT and HK-2 cell experiments, we confirmed that Milu antler powder was able to attenuate renal aging by modulating the intestinal microbiota and their metabolites (sodium acetate). Conclusions This study provides a scientific basis for the anti-aging application of Milu antler powder by demonstrating its ability to attenuate renal aging through modulation of the gut-kidney axis.

items.title: Plasma proteomic profiling reveals mediating proteins and preventive targets linking ambient air pollution to type 2 diabetes incidence: a prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Ambient air pollution has been associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D), but the underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. We included 44,917 participants with 2,911 plasma proteins from a large prospective cohort and followed them for incident T2D. Long-term PM 2.5 , NO 2 , NO x , and SO 2 exposures were estimated via bilinear interpolation. Cox regressions assessed air pollutant-T2D associations. Elastic net regression identified air pollution-associated proteins and constructed a protein score. Mediation analyses identified top-mediating proteins. Functional and PPI analyses identified hub proteins. Druggability was screened using two drug databases, with binding potential evaluated by molecular docking across seven small-molecule databases. During 13.64 years of follow-up, 3,193 incident T2D cases occurred. Per IQR increase in PM 2.5 , NO 2 , NO x , and SO 2 was associated with 5%-14% higher T2D risk. We identified 187 proteins mediating the PM 2.5 -T2D association, 61 for NO 2 , 66 for NO x , and 14 for SO 2 . The protein score mediated 31.69% (PM 2.5 ), 18.06% (NO 2 ), 16.81% (NO x ), and 19.71% (SO 2 ) of the associations. Functional and PPI analyses revealed these proteins function through cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, chemokine signaling, leukocyte migration, and inflammation-related pathways. We further identified 13 targeted proteins with approved drugs (4 in DrugBank, 4 in Therapeutic Target Database). Molecular docking indicated 5 have potential small-molecule binders. This study identified potential biological pathways and candidate mediators linking air pollution to T2D, particularly through inflammatory and immune-related pathways mediated by plasma proteins, and identified potential intervention targets, offering opportunities for drug repurposing and precise prevention.

items.title: Liposomal delivery of triptolide fatty acid prodrugs with varied fatty acid chain lengths for breast cancer therapy.
items.abstract: Triptolide is a highly potent natural antitumor agent whose clinical translation has been limited by systemic toxicity, narrow therapeutic window, and insufficient formulation stability. To address these limitations from a formulation-oriented perspective, a liposomal platform based on fatty acid-conjugated triptolide prodrugs was developed to investigate how fatty acid chain length influences formulation and plasma conversion behavior. Triptolide was covalently linked to myristic (C14), palmitic (C16), stearic (C18), eicosanoic (C20), and behenic (C22) acids and subsequently formulated into liposomal systems using a thin-film hydration method. The physicochemical properties were characterized, and plasma conversion, cytotoxicity, local irritation, and in vivo antitumor activity were evaluated. The free TP-FA prodrugs and their corresponding liposomal formulations exhibited distinct plasma conversion profiles. At 48 h, free TP-SA, TP-EA, and TP-BA showed conversion percentages of 97.53%, 97.02%, and 97.21%, respectively, whereas the corresponding liposomal formulations showed conversion percentages of 90.96%, 80.31%, and 41.83%, respectively. The difference between the free and liposomal forms was more persistent for the longer-chain conjugates, although the relationship with fatty acid chain length was not strictly monotonic across all time points. Among the tested formulations, behenic acid-conjugated liposomes showed distinct plasma conversion behavior and were further evaluated in the local irritation and in vivo antitumor studies. These findings suggest that saturated fatty acid chain length represents one structural variable influencing the behavior of TP-FA liposomal formulations.

items.title: Combined exposure of copper and iron induces nerve damage in Caenorhabditis elegans through ROS-induced autophagy/mitophagy.
items.abstract: Copper (Cu) and iron (Fe) are essential trace elements that become biotoxic in excess. Their widespread coexistence in the environment poses a significant risk of co-exposure to human populations. This study aimed to elucidate the combined toxic effects and underlying mechanisms of Cu and Fe using Caenorhabditis elegans as a model organism. Our results demonstrated that combined exposure to Cu and Fe synergistically inhibited motor behaviors, including head thrashes and body bends, to a greater extent than individual metal exposures. Furthermore, this co-exposure exacerbated the degeneration of both dopaminergic (DAergic) and GABAergic neurons, revealing a potent synergistic neurotoxic effect. Mechanistic investigations indicated that the combined exposure group exhibited a significant increase in both cellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), pointing to severe oxidative stress as a primary driver of toxicity. This oxidative stress led to profound mitochondrial damage, characterized by a reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ultrastructural defects, such as rupture and cristae loss, as observed via transmission electron microscopy. Consequently, pathways for mitochondrial quality control and cellular clearance were activated, evidenced by the upregulation of PINK-1 (mitophagy), HSP-6 (mitochondrial stress), LGG-1 (autophagy), and the transcription factor HLH-30. Validation experiments using the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) confirmed this mechanism. While NAC treatment effectively rescued neurodegeneration and motor deficits, it only partially mitigated the molecular damage in the co-exposure group, underscoring the severity of the synergistic interaction. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that Cu and Fe co-exposure induces synergistic neurotoxicity mediated primarily by an oxidative stress-driven autophagy/mitophagy pathway.

items.title: The landscape and characteristics of LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations delivering mental health and alcohol or other drug services in Australia.
items.abstract: Objective Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer/questioning (LGBTQ+) people experience disproportionate mental health and alcohol and other drug (AOD) burdens and have distinct care needs, yet limited evidence on the characteristics of LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations constrains optimal service design and delivery. This study aimed to map the landscape of LGBTQ+ community-controlled mental health and AOD organisations that provide mental health and AOD services across Australia. Methods A mixed-methods study involved 16 LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations, using an online cross-sectional survey and semi-structured interviews. Descriptive and content analyses examined organisational characteristics and service provision. A common practice elements approach integrated both data sources to identify shared organisational and service elements. Results Organisations varied substantially in size, workforce composition, and service models. All organisations provided mental health services, and nine provided AOD services. Eight common practice elements were identified: LGBTQ+ governance and infrastructure, embedded community responsiveness, integrated holistic services, collaborative partnerships, community building, foundational knowledge, relational practice, and safety-oriented approaches. Conclusions LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations provide essential, contextually safe mental health and AOD services and operate through distinctive yet commonly shared practices. Implications for public health Workforce development and integration with mainstream systems are critical to sustain LGBTQ+ community-controlled organisations and meet growing community demand for inclusive care.

items.title: Integrated Prenatal Cardiopulmonary Assessment Using Fetal Echocardiography in Isolated Left-Sided Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia.
items.abstract: Objective Prenatal severity assessment in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) primarily relies on lung-based parameters such as the observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (o/eLHR) and liver position; however, these markers do not fully reflect fetal cardiopulmonary adaptation. We investigated the prognostic significance of fetal echocardiographic parameters and integrated these in prenatal prediction models in left-sided CDH. Methods This nationwide multicenter retrospective study included fetuses with prenatally diagnosed isolated left-sided CDH. Gestational age-adjusted Z-scores were generated for fetal cardiac dimensions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance for survival. Results A total of 363 fetuses were included, with an overall survival rate of 74.9%. Non-survivors demonstrated significantly smaller right pulmonary artery and mitral valve dimensions than survivors. Among fetal echocardiographic parameters, the mitral-to-tricuspid valve ratio (MTR) demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77. In fetuses evaluated at ≤ 29 weeks' gestation, an exploratory model combining MTR with o/eLHR and liver-up status achieved an apparent AUC of 0.827. Conclusion Fetal echocardiographic parameters were associated with survival in CDH. Integrated prenatal cardiopulmonary assessment incorporating MTR may provide complementary prognostic information although independent external validation is required.

items.title: Development and initial content validation of the Vienna post-exertional malaise questionnaire: an iterative mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Objectives Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is a multidimensional exertion-response pattern involving diverse triggers, variable onset, and prolonged recovery. This study developed and content-validated the Vienna Post-Exertional Malaise (VPEM) Questionnaire, a patient-reported outcome measure assessing functional decline, recovery, crash-associated symptoms, and pacing adaptations in ME/CFS. Methods An iterative mixed-methods instrument-development study combined quantitative ratings and qualitative feedback across sequential evaluation cycles. An initial 13-item draft, informed by existing PEM, fatigue, and functional-capacity instruments and consensus literature, was evaluated by individuals with ME/CFS or Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) using Likert ratings, open-ended feedback, and interviews. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively, and qualitative data were analysed using deductive-inductive structuring content analysis. Revisions were documented in revision matrices. The revised instrument was evaluated by an interdisciplinary expert panel using domain-level and item-level ratings of relevance and clarity. Results Twelve individuals with ME/CFS and one individual with PCS fulfilling ME/CFS criteria evaluated the questionnaire. Ratings showed high approval for length (92.3%) and terminology (76.9%), while completeness and clarity were more heterogeneous. Qualitative findings identified ambiguities in distinguishing PEM from non-specific fatigue, missing trigger domains, and insufficient representation of intra-individual variability. After revision, the expert panel (n = 11) rated PEM coverage as complete or largely complete (100%) and the multidimensional structure as suitable or very suitable (90.9%). Item-level ratings showed high relevance (S-CVI/Ave = 0.96), whereas clarity ratings were more variable (S-CVI/Ave = 0.82). Conclusions The VPEM Questionnaire operationalises PEM as multidimensional post-exertional deterioration. Findings support initial content and face validity, warranting further psychometric validation.

items.title: Bioinformatic analysis of ACAD9 genetic variability.
items.abstract: Mitochondrial diseases (MD) are a heterogeneous group of disorders with a diagnostic rate often below 50%, mostly due to the difficulty of interpreting Variants of Unknown Significance (VUS). ACAD9 is a nuclear gene that encodes a mitochondrial protein involved in fatty acid β-oxidation and the assembly of respiratory complex I. This study aimed to refine the classification of ACAD9 missense VUS through an integrative computational approach combining in silico, evolutionary and structural analysis. A gene-specific dataset of missense pathogenic, benign and uncertain significance variants was curated from public databases (HGMD, ClinVar, GnomAD, UniProt or LOVD) and in-house sequencing data. Thirty-five in silico pathogenicity predictors were retrieved from the dbNSFP v5.3 and benchmarked using the datasets. Predictor performance was evaluated using 10 metrics and the top predictors were integrated with evolutionary conservation (ConSurf), structural modelling (PyMOL, HOPE) and thermodynamic stability analysis (FoldX) to re-evaluate 17 VUS. Predictor performance for ACAD9 variants varied significantly. Because no statistically significant differences were detected among the ten highest-ranked predictors, ClinPred, MetaRNN, PHACTboost, MutationTaster and REVEL were selected as the top stability-informed predictors. The integrative predictive and structural analysis reclassified 8 variants as "likely pathogenic" and 5 as "likely benign", while 4 remained classified as VUS due to conflicting evidence. A gene-specific, multi-layered computational strategy substantially improves VUS classification in ACAD9. These in silico findings provide strong, albeit non-definitive, evidence to guide diagnostic efforts. It should be complemented with functional validation, which remains essential to confirm pathogenicity.

items.title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
items.abstract: The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis. Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897). MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms. Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

items.title: Psychometric performance of the OECD Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys Patient Questionnaire (PaRIS-PQ) among adults with chronic conditions in Norway.
items.abstract: Purpose The OECD Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys (PaRIS) initiative aims to provide standardised, internationally comparable patient-reported indicators for people living with chronic conditions receiving primary or generalist ambulatory care. This study evaluated the psychometric performance of the multi-item scales in the Norwegian PaRIS Patient Questionnaire (PaRIS-PQ). Methods Data were drawn from the 2023 Norwegian PaRIS Main Survey. Respondents aged ≥ 45 years with at least one self-reported chronic condition were included. Measures were PROMIS Global Physical Health, PROMIS Global Mental Health, and WHO-5 Well-Being Index as patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs); the Person-Centred Coordinated Care Experience Questionnaire (P3CEQ) as a patient-reported experience measure (PREM); and the Porter-Novelli Scale (PNS) and self-management confidence as capability-related measures. Analyses assessed structural validity, internal consistency reliability, measurement invariance, item functioning, and construct validity. Results Of 8,683 respondents, 6,691 reported at least one chronic condition. PROM scales performed best, with acceptable internal consistency (α = 0.80-0.89) and strongest confirmatory support for PROMIS Global Physical Health (CFI = 0.992, RMSEA = 0.080). The PREM (P3CEQ) showed weaker performance, with suboptimal fit for the total scale (CFI = 0.818, RMSEA = 0.132), limited scalar invariance, and low internal consistency for the care coordination subscale (α = 0.61). Capability-related measures showed mixed performance. Metric invariance was supported across all tested models, whereas scalar invariance was less consistent. Construct validity findings were consistent with expectations. Conclusion PROM scales showed the most consistent psychometric support. PREM and capability-related measures were more heterogeneous and require cautious, scale-specific interpretation, especially in subgroup comparisons and when used as latent measures. Evaluation and refinement of weaker experience- and capability-related measures is warranted.

items.title: Development and Psychometric Evaluation of the Self-Efficacy for Cooking Healthy Meals Scale in the Teaching Kitchen Multisite Trial (TK-MT).
items.abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a scale measuring self-efficacy for overcoming barriers to preparing healthy meals at home. Design Cross-sectional data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis comparing 1 and 2-factor structures. Setting Teaching Kitchen Multisite Trial. Participants Adults with overweight or class I-II obesity (n = 169; mean age, 46 years; 79% female; 38% Hispanic, 10% Black, 23% Asian). Variables measured Self-Efficacy for Cooking Healthy Meals, addressing contextual barriers and resource constraints. Analysis Confirmatory factor analysis was performed using maximum likelihood estimation with robust errors; fit was evaluated with multiple indexes; internal consistency was assessed with Cronbach α. Results The 2-factor model fit better than the 1-factor model; the indexes were borderline (SBχ²[43] = 82.9, root mean squared error of approximation = 0.074, Comparative Fit Index = 0.91, Tucker-Lewis Index = 0.88). Reliability was acceptable for contextual barriers (α = 0.79) but lower for resource constraints (α = 0.68). Conclusions and implications In this preliminary analysis with a predominantly female, educated, higher-income sample, the scale showed borderline-to-adequate psychometric properties; validation in larger, more diverse samples is needed.

items.title: Pesticides and Hypospadias in Southern Brazil: An Ecological Study.
items.abstract: Rio Grande do Sul ranks among the Brazilian states with the highest pesticide consumption and one of the highest prevalences of hypospadias, a congenital anomaly often associated with prenatal exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals. We assessed the relationship between prenatal pesticide exposure and hypospadias risk through an ecological study of 1 776 670 live births in the state from 2010 to 2022. Using a spatial Bayesian hierarchical model, we examined associations between hypospadias and municipal-level indicators: relative crop area, pesticide sales, and probability of pesticide detection in water samples. The prevalence was 4.69 cases per 10 000 live births, with 10 municipalities at high risk and 15 at low risk. Higher risk was associated with tobacco cultivation. Sales of metaflumizone and Melaleuca alternifolia were associated with increased risk, while detection probabilities of alachlor and DDT showed the largest estimated effects, although these estimates were accompanied by substantial uncertainty. While causal inference is not possible in this ecological design, findings generate hypotheses for future research on prenatal pesticide exposure. Considering other environmental risk factors may further clarify hypospadias etiology. Identifying modifiable determinants is key to guiding interventions and public policies to reduce this condition's burden, particularly in rural areas and agricultural populations.

items.title: Colleague-Perpetrated Workplace Bullying Among Nurses: Experiences and Perceived Implications for Mental Health and Professional Functioning-A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Introduction Workplace bullying is a persistent problem in nursing that may adversely affect nurses' mental health, professional functioning and quality of patient care. This study aimed to explore Slovenian nurses' experiences of colleague-perpetrated workplace bullying, its perceived organisational contributors, implications for mental health and professional functioning, and nurses' responses and perspectives on prevention. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 20 nurses employed in different healthcare settings in Slovenia. Study participants were recruited through purposive sampling. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis. Results Through thematic analysis, four main themes were identified: (1) nurses' experiences of workplace bullying; (2) the impact of workplace bullying on mental health; (3) the impact of workplace bullying on professional functioning; and (4) nurses' responses to bullying and prevention strategies. Nurses described workplace bullying as a common and persistent phenomenon characterised by verbal abuse, humiliation, social exclusion and hostile communication. Bullying was perceived to negatively affect psychological well-being through increased stress, anxiety, emotional exhaustion, reduced self-confidence and difficulties detaching from work. Discussion and conclusions Workplace bullying remains an important occupational challenge with substantial implications for nurses' mental health and professional functioning. Healthcare organisations should prioritise comprehensive bullying prevention strategies, supportive leadership and psychologically safe work environments to protect nurses' well-being. Patient or public contribution No patients or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis or interpretation of this study, or in the preparation of this manuscript. As the study population consisted of registered nurses and nursing professionals rather than patients or members of the public, this study aimed to give voice to nurses' own experiences of colleague-perpetrated workplace bullying as the primary contribution to the research process.

items.title: Target Trial Emulation: Considerations for Physical Therapy Research.
items.abstract: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) are considered the ideal method for assessing the effectiveness of physical therapist interventions. However, RCTs are resource-intensive and usually take several years to complete, often providing insights well after they are needed to inform practice. Due to the constantly evolving nature of physical therapy, study designs are needed that can more rapidly generate evidence that can be used to guide clinical care. Target trial emulation (TTE) provides a framework that improves researchers' abilities to draw causal inferences from observational data, by specifying protocol components of a hypothetical RCT and emulating those components with observational data elements. By leveraging data generated through routine care encounters, TTE allows researchers to examine the effectiveness of interventions as they are being used in clinical care - enhancing researchers' abilities to generate evidence when it is most needed. However, TTE has not been used extensively among physical therapy researchers, potentially due to a lack of familiarity with this concept or challenges related to the way physical therapy is delivered or the types of data generated during physical therapist encounters. In this manuscript, the authors provide an introduction to the TTE framework, using an ongoing study examining the effectiveness of remote therapeutic monitoring as a case example. The authors also discuss considerations and challenges associated with TTE studies within the context of physical therapy and recommend strategies for addressing these challenges. They also discuss how TTE studies can be enhanced through the addition of implementation-focused data collection and conclude with a discussion of limitations associated with TTE studies.
