items.title: Anticipatory Cardiac Deceleration Is Related to Cautious Decision-Making after Threat Image Exposure.
items.abstract: Cautious decision-making can be an adaptive tendency in stressful environments and in certain individuals. We hypothesized that cautious decision-making is supported by anticipatory cardiac deceleration (ACD)- a brief cardiac slowing tied to preparation and action readiness. To test this hypothesis, we examined whether individuals with stronger ACD make more economically cautious choices after exposure to threat-depicting images. Participants (N = 97; 65% women, Mean age = 22.4 years) completed a threat priming decision-making task while electrocardiography was collected. To manipulate emotional contexts, every economic lottery choice was preceded by an affective image depicting a neutral, injury threat, or infection threat scene, and choice trials were presented in three separate blocks - one for each image type. Cardiac deceleration was assessed during 10-s countdown periods before each block. Results indicate that individuals with greater ACD before the infection threat block made more cautious choices after exposure to the infection threat images. This association was strongest when the infection block occurred last in the task sequence, i.e., when that image condition was more predictable. No significant relationships emerged for the other image conditions suggesting that anticipatory deceleration might only relate to behavioral caution in certain threat conditions. Results are consistent with the hypothesis that ACD is an autonomic correlate of preparation that is relevant to human performance and fear/anxiety theories.

items.title: Prenatal cocaine exposure alters synaptic plasticity of hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons in postnatal rats.
items.abstract: Prenatal cocaine exposure (PCE) severely affects brain development, psychology, and behavior in exposed offspring, while altering their susceptibility to drug addiction. however, the mechanisms underlying PCE-induced changes in cocaine-conditioned place preference (CPP) remain unclear. This study demonstrates that PCE attenuates cocaine-induced CPP, a process involving spatial memory and drug reward. We also investigated the dorsal hippocampus (dH), which is closely associated with spatial memory, and the ventral hippocampus (vH), which is linked to motivational reward mechanisms. Results indicate that PCE impairs long-term synaptic plasticity in the dH, suggesting that spatial memory deficits contribute to the attenuation of CPP. In contrast, PCE did not significantly inhibit synaptic plasticity in the vH, indicating that while the vH contributes to addiction susceptibility, it is less affected by prenatal exposure. Notably, acute cocaine exposure increased presynaptic plasticity in the vH regardless of prenatal history. These findings suggest that synaptic impairment in the dH drives spatial memory deficits in PCE offspring, while the vH retains sensitivity to acute drug challenge. This study elucidates the cellular mechanisms underlying PCE-induced cognitive changes and guides future molecular investigations.

items.title: Caffeine in Red Bull® selectively sustains the consumption of highly concentrated alcohol in energy drink-alcohol mixtures.
items.abstract: Mixing alcohol with caffeinated energy drinks is common among young people and is associated with heavier drinking. We previously found that rats self-administering Red Bull® consumed more alcohol and reached higher blood alcohol concentrations than rats given an isocaloric sucrose solution, but only when alcohol was highly concentrated. Here, we identified the beverage constituents associated with this effect. One hundred and eight male Wistar rats were trained in oral operant self-administration (30-min sessions, fixed ratio 1) and assigned to an energy-drink-flavoured vehicle, taurine, B vitamins, caffeine, sucrose, a laboratory reconstitution of the beverage (Lab-RB), or commercial Red Bull®. Solution concentration was escalated from 25% to 100%; alcohol was then added and escalated from 3% to 40% v/v in 4-day blocks. Without alcohol, only sucrose and Lab-RB sustained high responding, whereas caffeine, taurine, and B vitamins were indistinguishable from vehicle. With alcohol, sucrose increased alcohol intake only at low concentrations (3-6% v/v), whereas caffeine increased intake only at high concentrations (15-40% v/v), where sucrose was no longer effective (Group × Segment interaction: F(1,22) = 66.30, P 2 p = 0.751). Taurine and B vitamins had no detectable effect. These findings indicate that sucrose and caffeine contribute to alcohol intake at different parts of the concentration range and suggest that palatability alone is insufficient to explain the sustained consumption of highly concentrated alcohol.

items.title: Thermally unfavorable conditions of volatile existence in near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26, the Hayabusa extended mission's target
items.abstract: The near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26, the target of the Hayabusa2# extended mission, has been proposed as a dark comet that may host volatiles, particularly water, owing to an anomalous out-of-plane nongravitational acceleration that may result from outgassing. This asteroid, however, may also belong to a largely anhydrous taxonomic group. Whether outgassing-driven acceleration is possible strongly depends on how the asteroid stores volatiles in its interior and releases them upon heating at the surface. Thus far, the contentious topic of the existence of volatiles on 1998 KY26 that can cause outgassing has not been extensively examined from a thermophysical standpoint. Here, we show that all locations on the surface or in the interior of 1998 KY26 have orbit-averaged temperatures significantly above the sublimation point of volatiles in vacuum. Across 13 thermal characterizations, this observation is found to be consistent despite parameter variations in equivalent diameter, thermal conductivity, Bond albedo, specific heat capacity, and spin pole ecliptic latitude and longitude. Our temperature model results indicate that the water outgassing rate on 1998 KY26 would be too high to maintain buried ice, refining the understanding of the asteroid's composition.

items.title: The deuterium-rich atmosphere of a mature super-Jupiter
items.abstract: The deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio (D/H) has provided key insights into the origin and evolution of the Solar System. Using the James Webb Space Telescope, we detected deuterated methane at $48σ$ in a mature giant exoplanet, $ε$ Ind Ab. We measure the planet's D/H ratio to be $(4.4 \pm 0.7) \times 10^{-5}$, which is similar to those of Uranus and Neptune but about twice those of Jupiter, Saturn, and the protosolar nebula. $ε$ Ind Ab's heavy elements (C, O, N, and S) are uniformly enriched to a level similar to Jupiter's. These measurements require $ε$ Ind Ab to have accreted solids with $\mathrm{D/H} \gtrsim 1\%$, at least 30 times more deuterium-rich than typical Solar System comets. Such D/H values are found in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS and in organic molecules in star-forming regions, indicating that $ε$ Ind Ab accreted pristine solids formed in a very cold environment.

items.title: DMAJOR: A JWST Legacy Survey of Protoplanetary Disks
items.abstract: We propose an infrared imaging survey of resolved protoplanetary disks spanning a range of galactic environments, directly mapping the 3D structure of planet-forming disks across the IR. DMAJOR (Disk Motions and Architectures JWST Observational Reference survey), our legacy survey, will deliver a benchmark sample to reveal structure and connection to environment. The exquisite stability of JWST allows us to probe for variability with a time-scheduled revisit strategy, while its sensitivity and resolution open a window on disks unobservable from the ground. A uniform sample will reveal how small grains and ice are distributed in protoplanetary disks, how scattered light structures relate to large-scale environmental features, and identify new companions. To achieve this, DMAJOR takes advantage of model-based data analysis using telemetry and mutual calibration to enhance processed data products while minimizing telescope overheads.

items.title: Beyond node strengths: the topological content of weighted bipartite networks
items.abstract: Weighted bipartite networks encode the topology and intensity of interactions between two disjoint sets of nodes. However, it is unclear whether the observed pattern of connections is already explained by node interaction volumes or contains additional structural information. Here we introduce a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks that preserves node strengths alone, strengths and global density, or strengths and the complete degree sequence. Across economic, technological, ecological, social and lexical systems, we find that strength constraints alone are generally insufficient to reproduce empirical structures. Yet the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single constraint controlling network density frequently provides the most parsimonious description, whereas networks with stronger residual degree heterogeneity require node-specific constraints. Beyond downstream inference, we also show how the choice of topological resolution changes which interactions and projected relationships are identified as statistically significant. Our results indicate that topology is essential, but often compressible, in the statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and provide a scalable computational framework for fitting, sampling, model selection and validation within a common workflow.

items.title: What is compassion connected to, and does it differ by gender and age? A network analysis of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy and mental health
items.abstract: Abstract Compassion is an emotional state experienced in response to witnessing the suffering of others, accompanied by an internal motivation to help. When directed toward the self, it is referred to as self-compassion. Previous research suggests that compassion and self-compassion are closely related to mindfulness and empathy, contributing to reductions in anxiety and depression and to the enhancement of positive affect. Accordingly, this study employed network analysis to explore the complex structure of interactions among these psychological variables. A total of 1,020 Korean adults completed measures of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy, well-being, and negative affect (depression, anxiety, and stress). An EBICglasso network was estimated in R (version 4.5.1). Centrality indices were computed, and subgroup networks were constructed by gender and age to compare structural differences. The results showed that compassion was closely connected to empathy, whereas self-compassion was more strongly linked to mindfulness and well-being; the capacities to feel, tolerate, and alleviate suffering emerged as central nodes. In the gender-based networks, compassion and self-compassion among men tended to be organized primarily around cognitive factors, whereas women exhibited a pattern in which the behavioral motivation for compassion was activated relatively immediately, even in the absence of emotional responding. In the age-based networks, the influence of suffering tolerance was most pronounced in middle-aged adults, while the role of empathy diminished and the role of mindfulness expanded in older adults. By examining compassion at the level of its constituent elements and visualizing the interaction structure among related variables, this study provides an empirical foundation for extending theoretical understanding and for developing tailored intervention strategies.

items.title: An Image Is Worth K Topics: A Visual Structural Topic Model with Pretrained Image Embeddings
items.abstract: Abstract Political scientists are increasingly interested in analyzing visual content at scale. However, the existing computational toolbox is still in need of methods and models attuned to the specific challenges and goals of social and political inquiry. In this article, we introduce a visual structural topic model (vSTM) that combines continuous image embeddings with a structural topic model. This has important advantages compared to existing approaches. First, continuous embeddings allow the model to capture the semantic complexity of images, which is relevant to the study of politics. A consequence of using continuous embeddings is that we can directly use off-the-shelf pretrained deep learning models, offering state-of-the-art performance in image analysis tasks while saving time, cost and resources. Second, the structural topic model provides the ability to analyze how topics and covariates are related, while maintaining a nuanced representation of images as a mixture of multiple topics. In our experiments, we show that the vSTM is able to identify topics that are interpretable, coherent and relevant to the study of online political communication.

items.title: Childhood Trauma and APOEε4 Are Associated With Patterns of Developmental Frontal Alpha Connectivity, Posttraumatic Stress, and Alcohol‐Related Outcomes
items.abstract: Childhood trauma affects neurodevelopment and lifelong risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD). Changes in brain structures and function are observed in young carriers of APOEε4, the genetic factor most associated with Alzheimer's disease. Longitudinal studies of APOEε4, childhood trauma, and neural connectivity in adolescence have not been explored. We studied 837 trauma-exposed participants (53% female) from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism prospective sample, using latent growth curve models to assess associations of childhood trauma and APOEε4 on repeated measures of frontal alpha EEG coherence (EEGc) throughout adolescence and young adulthood. Young adult AUD and PTSD symptoms were also examined. Results indicate childhood sexual assaultive trauma (CSAT) and APOEε4 are linked to neural connectivity, with effects differing by brain region and direction. CSAT was associated with a higher EEGc baseline but less growth in three EEGc pairs, while APOEε4 associated with lower left frontocentral (LFC) EEGc baseline and higher slope. EEGc patterns and symptoms of PTSD and AUD were robustly associated. A significant interaction between CSAT-by-APOEε4 interaction also emerged, such that among APOEε4 carriers, childhood sexual assaultive trauma was associated with higher baseline PFI and diminished growth in PFI and LFC EEGc. No significant direct links between APOEε4 and PTSD or AUD were observed. Findings highlight how EEGc may help explain connections between genetics, trauma, and psychopathology, guiding at-risk group identification and informing prevention strategies.

items.title: Disentangling cognitive and emotional load in interpreting
items.abstract: Abstract This study employs a multimodal approach to investigate how emotional and cognitive load differentially impact interpreter stress. Twenty student interpreters consecutively interpreted four Turkish-to-English mental healthcare narratives of varying emotionality and difficulty, constructed using a 2×2 factorial design. Stress responses were measured using galvanic skin response (GSR), voice parameters (pitch and voice intensity), and self-report scales (PANAS, STAI, and NASA-TLX). Stimuli were normed for emotional valence and linguistic complexity using readability indices, expert ratings, and natural language processing (NLP) tools. Results showed that primarily cognitive load drove GSR arousal, particularly during later interpreting stages, whereas emotional load was reflected in pitch and self-reported negative affect. A pitch convergence between speaker and interpreter also emerged. None of the stress indicators predicted interpreting accuracy, suggesting a possible role for individual coping strategies.

items.title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
items.abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. However, additional measures may be needed. Fear, disgust, and avoidance of specific foods would likely distinguish an AVI pandemic from COVID-19. The threat of infected food triggers disgust, and so food-related disgust would likely be a prominent emotional reaction during an AVI pandemic. Public messaging from health authorities and others has the potential to either ease or exacerbate public concerns about food safety, depending on how the messages are crafted.

items.title: Philosophy Is Perfect
items.abstract: Abstract Philosophy Is Perfect offers a bold defense of philosophy against its pessimistic and moderate critics. Where “Flagellants” see futility and “Hedgers” see only piecemeal progress, Herman Cappelen advances a model of Hyper-Optimism: the claim that philosophy has been massively successful, foundational to all inquiry, and is flourishing precisely because of its characteristic disagreement. Part I argues that all disciplines ultimately “answer to philosophy” when their core concepts and methods are scrutinized, showing that pessimism about philosophy would undermine confidence in every branch of knowledge. Part II turns the standard critique on its head, arguing that persistent disagreement is not a defect but a structural virtue of philosophical inquiry: convergence would signal decay, not progress. Part III presents the positive thesis—that philosophy has already found the correct answers to the “Very Important Questions.” Cappelen argues that after centuries of systematic exploration, the correct answers are already articulated and defended in the philosophical commons. Part IV addresses objections. The result is a provocative re-evaluation of philosophy’s status. Rather than a discipline in crisis, Cappelen depicts philosophy as uniquely successful: it has discovered foundational truths, thrives on principled disagreement, and sets the terms for all other forms of inquiry. Philosophy Is Perfect is both a challenge to entrenched pessimism and a constructive vision of philosophy’s achievements and future.

items.title: Age-related amplification of spatial contextual influence on visual scene processing.
items.abstract: Older adults rely increasingly on prior knowledge to make sense of their deteriorating representation of the visual world, but how this shapes scene perception and spatial reorientation remains unclear. To address this issue, 28 young and 25 older adults viewed artificially generated rooms either before or after learning the position of a goal hidden in an adjacent room. We manipulated both the number and the eccentricity of navigational affordances (i.e., open doors) to investigate the interaction between bottom-up scene features and top-down spatial knowledge. Consistent with previous findings, younger adults showed decreased performance as the number of open doors increased, but only after learning the goal position, indicating a top-down interaction with the automatic processing of affordances. Door eccentricity did not affect this interaction, suggesting our findings were not due to a distractor effect. In older adults, this interaction between prior spatial information and navigational affordances was markedly amplified: reaction times increased at twice the rate observed in younger adults. These findings show that prior spatial knowledge interacts with the automatic extraction of navigational affordances, and that this influence is markedly amplified with age. While prior knowledge helps stabilize perception when sensory processing becomes less reliable, it can also increase the processing time for complex scenes, particularly when multiple action possibilities are present. By revealing how aging shifts the balance between top-down and bottom-up mechanisms, these results refine models of age-related spatial navigation decline and highlight a trade-off whereby increased reliance on prior knowledge supports perception but can also slow interaction with complex environments.

items.title: Quantifying the impact of groundwater fauna and temperature on the ecosystem service of microbial carbon degradation; a proof-of-principle approach
items.abstract: Abstract Groundwater ecosystems fulfil functions that humankind relies upon, e.g. for sustainable drinking water production. Quantification of these services is lacking so far. Thus, it is not possible to predict scenarios (e.g. future climates). Based on data from a comprehensive groundwater ecosystem study comprising four zones of varying land use and groundwater / surface water exchange, we parameterized a quantitative dynamic food web model (recharged organic carbon, microorganisms using the biodegradable fraction of this carbon, and fauna grazing on the microorganisms). With the model satisfactorily reflecting the field data, we calculated five further scenarios, three of which without fauna (mortality e.g. due to contamination, sudden peaks of temperature etc.). Two of the “fauna” and two of the “no fauna” scenarios were run with temperature elevated by 1.5°C and 3°C, respectively. The ecosystem service of carbon degradation was expressed as the difference in carbon concentration between the beginning of the simulation and the end of the simulation. In most scenarios, remaining carbon increased over time. The remaining carbon in some scenarios was up to 6.6 times as high in the “no fauna” scenarios compared to the reference case. Fauna was thus shown to fulfil a service by promoting microbial carbon degradation that may be substantial. Sustainable drinking water production is more reliable and less costly, the more active the groundwater fauna in the production area is. This model set up can serve to test other cases of varying physical and chemical variations and disturbances.

items.title: Genomic and dietary insights from non-invasive sampling of western capercaillie in Tyresta National Park (Sweden)
items.abstract: Abstract The Western Capercaillie ( Tetrao urogallus ), a boreal forest specialist, has experienced marked declines in southern Sweden due to habitat loss, fragmentation, and isolation. Tyresta National Park and the surrounding forests harbor one of the region’s last remnant southern populations, yet little is known about its genetic health, population structure, and dietary ecology. Here, we used low-coverage whole-genome sequencing of 272 non-invasively collected samples (feathers and faeces) to comprehensively assess the status of this population. Feather samples yielded high-quality genomic data, enabling sex identification, estimation of genome-wide heterozygosity, runs of homozygosity (ROH), and relatedness inference. Heterozygosity levels in Tyresta were comparable to other European Western Capercaillie populations, and inbreeding levels were generally low, although several individuals showed long ROH indicative of recent close-kin mating. Population structure analyses revealed a genetically distinct isolated unit with possible female-biased dispersal. Kinship analysis uncovered a highly interconnected social network, with males having, on average, more relatives than females. Recapture simulations based on genotype matching estimated a current maximum population size of 145–215 individuals. Faecal metagenomic analysis revealed a diverse diet, including key plant species such as blueberry, lingonberry, and alder, and a wide range of invertebrates critical for chick development. Despite its current genetic robustness, the Tyresta population is small, isolated, and at risk of inbreeding depression. Conservation efforts should prioritize maintaining habitat quality, promoting gene flow, e.g., by protecting migration corridors to neighbouring populations and ensuring a rich forest invertebrate community to support population resilience.

items.title: More than Leaves: Phylogenetic and Spatial Dimensions of Ritual Plant use in Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract The Povos e Comunidades Tradicionais de Terreiro e de Matriz Africana in Brazil (Traditional Peoples and Communities of Afro-Brazilian Terreiro and African Matrix religions, henceforth Povos de Terreiro ) are Afro-Brazilian religious communities in which plants play important ritual, therapeutic, and cultural roles. Their communities are organized around terreiros , sacred spaces where religious practices, ceremonies, and plant-related knowledge are maintained and transmitted. We investigated whether variation in the plants reported in Brazilian terreiros was associated with environmental context, geographic proximity, or shared cultural heritage. We compiled 643 species from 32 publications and compared taxonomic and phylogenetic composition across Brazilian biomes, tested spatial autocorrelation, and examined species frequencies and biogeographic status. Taxonomic composition differed among biomes, whereas phylogenetic composition did not. Geographic proximity was not associated with taxonomic or phylogenetic similarity. Ten species occurred in at least half of the analyzed terreiros , and the flora included similar proportions of species native (52%) and non-native (48%) to Brazil. The recurrence of the same species in geographically distant terreiros is consistent with a role for shared plant knowledge in shaping similarities among them. Non-native plants used in Afro-Brazilian religious practices have diverse biogeographic and historical origins.

items.title: Plant invasions in Natura 2000 habitats in Poland are driven primarily by macroclimatic factors
items.abstract: Invasive plants pose an ecological threat around the world. Their influence can also be observed in protected areas such as the European Ecological Network Natura 2000. Although invasions can endanger protected habitats, the specific impact of invasive species in such areas and the factors that determine their spread remain understudied. This study aimed to analyse the factors influencing the probability of plant invasion in five groups of habitat types protected under the EU Habitats Directive, based on Polish State Monitoring of Natura 2000 data. A total of 2,096 monitoring sites, with a balanced distribution across the country, were analysed, belonging to broadleaf forests, riverine habitats, dry grasslands, mesic and wet grasslands, and mires. The study confirmed the presence of 45 invasive species and two potentially invasive species. The most frequently observed species were Impatiens parviflora , Prunus serotina , Solidago gigantea , Erigeron canadensis , Solidago canadensis , and Bidens frondosa . The correlation between the presence of invasive species in monitored Natura 2000 sites and 38 variables was then analysed. The probability of invasion was much higher in regions with milder and wetter winters and, at the same time, in areas with a more continental climate. The importance of large rivers and their valleys and major roads as corridors facilitating plant invasions was also confirmed. Moreover, this study demonstrated the effectiveness of the State Monitoring Programme in detecting invasive species and analysing invasions. The programme could be used to inform the planning of future invasion management and prevention strategies.

items.title: Dynamic instabilities and pattern formation in chemotactic active matter
items.abstract: Collectives of actively-moving particles can spontaneously segregate into dilute and dense phases through a process known as motility-induced phase separation (MIPS). This captivating phenomenon is well-studied for randomly-moving particles with no directional bias. However, many active systems perform collective chemotaxis -- directed motion along a chemical gradient collectively generated by the particles themselves through consumption or production. Here, we use linear stability analysis, amplitude equations, and numerical simulations to study how MIPS is influenced by collective chemotaxis. We find that chemotaxis can either arrest or entirely suppress MIPS, or give rise to novel dynamic instabilities such as traveling waves and spirals. We predict the stability region of the stationary and oscillatory patterns and identify four types of bifurcation that can arise: pitchfork, saddle-node, infinite period, and supercritical Hopf. We also derive analytical expressions for the amplitude of the pattern and traveling wave velocity, yielding excellent quantitative agreement with simulations. Furthermore, we generalize our model to study particles that either consume or produce chemoattractant or chemorepellent, as well as mixtures of particles with different chemotactic behaviors. By establishing quantitative principles describing the competition between MIPS and chemotaxis, our study helps deepen understanding of the rich physics underlying chemically-responsive active matter systems.
